# ChurchAppCLD build to-do list with a prompt for every step

_Generated from `docs/PLAN.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md`; skeleton and step 0.1/1.1 written in session 002 (2026-09-03), the remaining steps drafted, critiqued and revised in session 003 (2026-09-04). Source of truth for build order; tick the boxes as steps land._

## How to use this list

1. Work top to bottom. Every step lists what it depends on; do not start a step before its dependencies are ticked.
2. **Agent steps**: open a fresh Claude Code session in this repository and paste the whole text inside the step's prompt box. Add one line at the top if the session must work on a branch other than `main`. The agent ticks its own checkbox in this file, updates `HANDOFF.md`, commits and pushes.
3. **Founder steps** are manual (Supabase dashboard, Vercel, Stripe, Expo). Follow the checklist, then tick the box yourself. Some founder steps end with a small helper prompt an agent can run to verify your work.
4. After a step fails or an agent reports a deviation, use the reusable fix prompt (step 3.10) with the observations pasted in. Do not skip verification steps.
5. Checkpoints: **A** (step 2.5) you are signed in on Vercel as super admin; **B** (step 3.9) the finished web app is trialled on Vercel; **C** (step 4.5) the Android preview build works. Everything after C completes Phases 2 and 3 of the plan.

Sizes are one agent session each: S under an hour, M a few hours, L most of a session, XL a full long session (may need a follow-up session to finish verification).

## Decisions these prompts assume

Founder answers of 2026-09-03 (recorded in `HANDOFF.md`) and drafting decisions of 2026-09-04 (`Session log/003_2026-09-04/todo-drafts/orchestrator-decisions.md`). Change one of these and the affected prompts must change too.

- App display name **Anacast**; Android package id `com.anacast.app` (founder wrote `com.Anacast.app`; lowercase recommended and immutable after the first Play upload; confirm in step 0.1); deep-link scheme `anacast`; brand colours and production domain deferred (neutral theme, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`).
- Supabase **Free** plan (US East): 50 MB per upload (`NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=50`, `sermon-media` bucket limit 50 MiB until Pro), project pauses after 7 idle days. Vercel **Pro** at launch (cron `*/5 * * * *`).
- Billing: flat **US$50 per church per month** via one Stripe Price (`STRIPE_PRICE_ID`); 30-day trial; only `suspended` blocks writes, `past_due` shows a banner.
- Families may hide from their own congregation (`hide_from_congregation` UI toggle) and from the fellowship; leaders may only make a family more private; fellowship viewers see everything the congregation sees minus birth year, anniversary year and leader notes.
- Each church sets its own youth/adult ages in settings (defaults 13 / 25 / 18; married excluded from youth; men's/women's include youth).
- Share links: password min 8, stream by default, **downloads allowed for uploaded media when `sermon_share_allow_download` is on**, available to `sermons.link` and `sermons.upload` holders.
- Push on every bulletin upload (per-church toggle, default on). Announcements & bulletins UI (3.5) ships before the push dispatcher (3.6): publishing queues notifications, 3.6 delivers them.
- Head of house: at most one `household_role = head` per household (partial unique index in `9999_init.sql`); in Phase 3 the head answers per-person surveys for household members without accounts.
- The 12-toggle permission mapping in `docs/RLS.md` ships as the default (not explicitly confirmed by the founder).
- Monorepo: Vercel Root Directory `apps/web`, `apps/web/vercel.json`, package names `web` / `mobile` / `@church/*`; `@types/react` follows the 19.2 line.
- `9999_init.sql` may still be edited until the founder pastes it into the hosted project (step 2.4); after that every change is a new `9998_*` file.

## Steps and prompts

## M0 — Prerequisites (founder)

### 0.1 — Accounts & access

- **Who:** Founder
- **Depends on:** none
- **Read first:** HANDOFF.md — Environment status, Decisions, Still open for the founder, Brand palette, docs/PLAN.md §13 (founder answers 9 and 10), docs/DESIGN.md §13 risks 4–7 (Supabase Free plan, Expo push prerequisites, Vercel Hobby limits, default SMTP), Orchestrator decisions 5, 17 and 18 (identity, palette, package id) as recorded in HANDOFF.md
- **Size:** S
- **Commit:** `docs: record founder accounts and identity decisions (step 0.1)`

**Goal.** Every third-party account the build needs exists under one founder email with 2FA on, before any agent needs a key: GitHub (repo default branch main, Actions on, Claude connector with write access), Supabase (organization on the Free plan, no project yet), Vercel (team `Anacast` with the Vercel GitHub App installed for ChurchAppCLD and no project imported yet; on Pro now, or on Hobby with a recorded to-do to upgrade before step 2.5), Stripe (test mode), plus Expo, a Google account for Firebase and the Google Play Console developer account (all may be deferred to step 4.5), the Apple Developer Program (deferred to step 6.4) and optionally a domain and a Resend account. The Anacast identity values the code depends on are already decided and only checked here: display name `Anacast`, Android package id `com.anacast.app` (confirmed 2026-09-07), deep-link scheme `anacast`, the five-blue brand palette; the founder confirms or reassigns the palette's token roles and either names the production domain or records it as deferred. A password-manager vault exists so no secret ever lands in git, a prompt, or chat, and HANDOFF.md carries a per-account status line.

**Founder checklist**

## 0.1 — Accounts & access (founder, about 60 minutes, no code)

Use one email for everything below (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`) and turn on two-factor authentication on every account (each block below says where the switch is) — these accounts will hold church members' personal data.

1. **GitHub — repository `RadioDinner/ChurchAppCLD` (already exists).**
   1. github.com → `RadioDinner/ChurchAppCLD` → Settings → General → "Default branch" = `main` (change it if it still points at a `claude/...` branch).
   2. Settings → Branches: no protection rule on `main` (agents push to `main` directly — standing order 6).
   3. Settings → Actions → General → "Allow all actions and reusable workflows" (step 1.1 adds one non-blocking CI workflow; its final Verify item needs Actions on).
   4. claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → GitHub: confirm the Claude GitHub App has read/write access to `ChurchAppCLD`.
   5. 2FA: github.com → your avatar → Settings → Password and authentication → Two-factor authentication → Enable (authenticator app; save the recovery codes in the vault from item 11).
2. **Supabase account (Free plan).**
   1. supabase.com → "Start your project" → sign in with GitHub or `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`.
   2. Create an Organization: name `Anacast`, plan **Free** (founder decision 10).
   3. Do **not** create a project yet — step 2.4 creates it (US East) once `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` exists. A Free project pauses after 7 idle days; creating it early only burns that window.
   4. 2FA: avatar (bottom-left) → Account Settings → Security → Multi-factor authentication → Add authenticator app.
3. **Vercel account + team.**
   1. vercel.com → "Continue with GitHub" (the GitHub identity that owns `RadioDinner`).
   2. Dashboard → team switcher (top-left) → "Create Team" → name `Anacast`. Plan: **Pro** (US$20 per member per month) — recommended now, per founder decision 10 "Vercel PRO at launch". The one hard rule: the team must be on Pro before step 2.5 imports the project, because the repo ships `apps/web/vercel.json` with a `*/5 * * * *` cron that a Hobby deployment rejects at build time, and Hobby forbids commercial use. If you would rather not pay until the first deployment, create the team on **Hobby** today and write "Vercel: upgrade to Pro (Team Settings → Billing → Upgrade) before step 2.5" into HANDOFF.md → Environment status (item 11 below); step 2.5's precondition checks for Pro.
   3. Install the Vercel GitHub App **without importing a project**: github.com/apps/vercel → Configure → choose the `RadioDinner` account → "Only select repositories" → `ChurchAppCLD` → Save. (Alternative from inside Vercel: Add New… → Project → "Continue with GitHub" → "Adjust GitHub App Permissions" → select `ChurchAppCLD` → Save, then close the dialog — stop before clicking Import.)
   4. Check: Vercel → Add New… → Project → "Import Git Repository" lists `ChurchAppCLD`. Do **not** click Import — step 2.5 imports it with Root Directory `apps/web`.
   5. 2FA: avatar → Account Settings → Authentication → Two-Factor Authentication → Enable.
4. **Stripe account (test mode).**
   1. dashboard.stripe.com/register → `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → business name `Anacast` (editable later) → verify the email.
   2. Stay in **Test mode** (toggle top-right / "Sandboxes"). Do not activate live payments until launch; the product, the US$50/month price and the webhook are created in step 3.9.
   3. 2FA: Settings (gear) → Team and security → Your profile → Two-step authentication → Add (authenticator app or SMS; authenticator preferred).
5. **Expo account (needed at step 4.5 — may be created then).** expo.dev/signup → `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → username `anacast` (or similar). The free plan is enough for EAS Build (monthly build quota, lower-priority queue). Record the Expo username in HANDOFF.md → Environment status (item 11): step 4.5's `npx eas-cli init` creates the EAS project under that account and step 4.1's `app.config.ts` may set it as `owner`. 2FA: expo.dev → Account settings → Two-factor authentication.
6. **Google account for Firebase and Play (needed at step 4.5 — may be created then).**
   1. Decide which Google account will own the Firebase project (console.firebase.google.com) for push notifications (step 4.5).
   2. The same account should own the **Google Play Console developer account** (play.google.com/console; US$25 one-time). It is not needed for the sideloaded APK of Checkpoint C, but it *is* on the critical path to the store: identity verification takes days, and a personal developer account created after November 2023 must run a **14-day closed test with at least 12 testers** before Google grants production access (steps 6.5 and 6.8). Create and verify it no later than step 4.5, so the clock starts early; record in HANDOFF.md whether it is done or deferred to 4.5.
   3. 2FA: myaccount.google.com → Security → 2-Step Verification.
7. **Apple Developer Program (needed at step 6.4 — deferred).** US$99/year; enrolment for an individual takes about two days, for an organisation longer (a D-U-N-S number is required). Nothing to do now; record "Apple Developer: deferred to 6.4" in HANDOFF.md.
8. **Optional now, needed by step 3.9 at the latest: domain and Resend.**
   1. If you want a custom domain (`<DOMAIN>`), register it now. Until then `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (web) and `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` (mobile) carry the Vercel URL `<VERCEL_URL>`. Changing the domain later changes invite/share URLs and the Supabase redirect URLs (share links already issued keep the old host), means a new privacy-policy/terms URL in both store listings (steps 6.4–6.6), and — once Android App Links ship in step 5.8 — a new APK, because the host is compiled into the app. So decide the domain before Checkpoint D (step 5.9) at the latest.
   2. resend.com → account with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` (free tier: 3,000 emails/month). Sending from your own address requires a verified domain, so Resend is only useful once the domain exists. Without it the app shows invite links for copy/paste and Supabase's rate-limited default SMTP sends the OTP codes.
9. **Identity values (already decided — check, do not re-decide).**
   1. Android package id: `com.anacast.app` (confirmed 2026-09-07, orchestrator decision 18; immutable after the first Play upload). Check that HANDOFF.md → Decisions lists it; nothing to decide.
   2. Deep-link scheme: `anacast` (orchestrator decision 5). Check that HANDOFF.md → Decisions lists it.
   3. App display name: `Anacast` (given). Same check.
   4. Brand colours: the five-blue palette is recorded in HANDOFF.md → "Brand palette" (Prussian Blue `#00072d`, Deep Navy `#001c55`, Imperial Blue `#0a2472`, Bright Marine `#0e6ba8`, Icy Blue `#a6e1fa`). Confirm or change the suggested token roles — `primary` Imperial Blue, `primaryDark` Deep Navy, `ink` Prussian Blue, `accent` Bright Marine, `tint` Icy Blue. "Keep as suggested" is a valid answer; write the outcome into the table's third column (item 11).
   5. Production domain: `<DOMAIN>` from 8.1, or "deferred (Vercel URL `<VERCEL_URL>`)".
10. **Password manager.** Create a vault or folder "Anacast — infrastructure" with entries for GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Stripe, Expo, Google, Apple, registrar/Resend. Every key produced in steps 2.4, 2.5, 3.9 and 4.5 goes there, together with the 2FA recovery codes. Never paste a key into git, into a Claude Code prompt (`prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim), or into chat.
11. **Record in `HANDOFF.md`.** Under "Environment status" add a first item "0. Accounts (step 0.1)" with one line per account — GitHub, Supabase, Vercel (plan, and "upgrade to Pro before step 2.5" if on Hobby), Stripe, Expo (username), Google/Firebase, Play Console, Apple Developer, domain, Resend — each "done" or "deferred to step N.N". Under "Decisions" confirm `Anacast` / `com.anacast.app` / `anacast` are listed and add the domain (or "deferred — `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` = Vercel URL"). In "Brand palette" fill the token-role column with your decision. In "Still open for the founder" strike item 1 if you gave a domain and item 5 once the token roles are confirmed. Either edit the file yourself and commit, or paste the helper prompt below into a Claude Code session with your values filled in.

**Helper prompt for an agent (optional)**

```text
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is the helper for step 0.1 "Accounts & access" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `HANDOFF.md` (Environment status, Decisions, Still open for the founder, Brand palette) and `docs/PLAN.md` §13 before editing. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Record the outcome of my account set-up and identity checks in `HANDOFF.md`. No code; no files other than `HANDOFF.md`, `docs/TODO.md` and the session log.

## Inputs / prior state
- Ask me for any value that is missing instead of guessing; never invent a status.
- Accounts: GitHub done; Supabase organization (Free) done; Vercel team `Anacast` <Pro | Hobby — upgrade to Pro before step 2.5>; Stripe (test mode) done; Expo <username | deferred to 4.5>; Google/Firebase <done | deferred to 4.5>; Play Console <done | deferred to 4.5>; Apple Developer <deferred to 6.4>; domain <`<DOMAIN>` | deferred>; Resend <done | deferred to 3.9>.
- Identity values already decided (check only): display name `Anacast`, Android package id `com.anacast.app` (confirmed 2026-09-07), deep-link scheme `anacast`.

## Build
1. `supabase/config.toml`: the minimal file `npx supabase init` would generate (`project_id = "churchappcld"`, `[db] major_version = 16`, `[api] schemas = ["public"]`), with a header comment: "used only by `supabase gen types --db-url` and a future `supabase start`; NEVER run `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset` against this project — migrations are pasted by hand (docs/PLAN.md §4)". Do not run `npx supabase init`; write the file.
2. `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` — local-only, applied by `local-up.sh` as the cluster superuser, idempotent (every statement `if not exists` / `create or replace` / `do $$ … $$` guarded), and clearly headed "NOT a migration; never paste into Supabase". It creates:
   - Roles `anon` and `authenticated` as `nologin`; `service_role` as `nologin bypassrls` (Supabase's service role bypasses RLS — the service client in the cron and in Server Actions relies on it to write `notifications`, `storage_deletions`, `stripe_events` and `billing_*` rows, which have no `authenticated` write policies); guard each `create role` with `if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = …)`. `churchapp_owner` as `login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls` with the dev-only password `churchapp` (needed only when the system cluster's `pg_hba.conf` demands a password over TCP): guard the `create role` the same way, then run `alter role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password 'churchapp'` UNCONDITIONALLY so the attributes converge even when `local-up.sh` pre-created the role (see 3.4) or an older shim left it different; likewise `alter role service_role bypassrls` unconditionally. Grant `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role` to `churchapp_owner` so tests can `set role`. This mirrors Supabase's `postgres` role: NOT a superuser, but BYPASSRLS (DESIGN §1 item 1 — "the local shim uses a non-superuser bypassrls owner so parity is real").
   - Schemas `extensions`, `auth`, `storage` (owner `churchapp_owner`); `grant usage on schema extensions, auth, storage to anon, authenticated, service_role`; `alter database churchapp set search_path` is NOT touched.
   - `auth.users` with the columns the migration and tests need: `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()`, `email text unique`, `raw_user_meta_data jsonb not null default '{}'`, `raw_app_meta_data jsonb not null default '{}'`, `created_at timestamptz default now()`, `updated_at timestamptz default now()`, `deleted_at timestamptz`, `last_sign_in_at timestamptz`, owned by `churchapp_owner` (step 1.3a creates triggers on it, which requires ownership). `auth.uid()` returns `coalesce(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''), nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub')::uuid`; `auth.jwt()` returns `coalesce(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim', true), ''), nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), ''))::jsonb`; `auth.role()` returns the `role` claim the same way — all three `language sql stable`. Tests in 1.4 will "log in" with `set local role authenticated; select set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated')::text, true)`.
   - `storage.buckets` (`id text primary key, name text not null unique, owner uuid, public boolean default false, file_size_limit bigint, allowed_mime_types text[], created_at timestamptz default now(), updated_at timestamptz default now()`) and `storage.objects` (`id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(), bucket_id text references storage.buckets(id), name text, owner uuid, owner_id text, metadata jsonb, path_tokens text[] generated always as (string_to_array(name, '/')) stored, version text, created_at, updated_at, last_accessed_at timestamptz`), both owned by `churchapp_owner` (1.4 creates policies on `storage.objects`); functions `storage.foldername(name text) returns text[]` (all path segments but the last), `storage.filename(name text) returns text`, `storage.extension(name text) returns text` — `language sql immutable`.
   - Grant `all` on all tables in `auth`/`storage` to `churchapp_owner`; grant `select` on `storage.buckets` and `storage.objects` to `anon`, and `select, insert, update, delete` on `storage.objects` and `storage.buckets` to `authenticated`, `service_role` (Supabase grants these table privileges; the `ca_storage_*` policies of step 1.4 do the filtering). `alter table storage.objects enable row level security` (guard with `pg_class.relrowsecurity`; RLS is on for `storage.objects` on Supabase, so without it a 1.4 test would see writes the hosted database blocks). Never `force row level security`.
   - A trailing `do $$ … raise notice 'shim applied' $$`. Note in the header that `local-up.sh` re-applies the shim on EVERY run (it is idempotent), so a later tweak reaches an existing local database without dropping it; the only database that never sees the shim is one reached through the `DATABASE_URL` short-circuit in 3.2 (a hosted-style database that already has `auth.uid()`).
3. `scripts/db/local-up.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable, every path quoted). Behaviour, in order:
   1. Resolve `REPO_ROOT` from the script location; `STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg"` (gitignored).
   2. If `DATABASE_URL` is already set and `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'select 1'` succeeds, print it and exit 0 (a hosted-style database that is already prepared — no shim, no role creation).
   3. Decide the superuser access MODE, then define ONE helper used for every superuser statement in every path: `super_sql() { case "$MODE" in url) psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; cluster) sudo -u postgres psql -p "$PORT" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; initdb) psql "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PORT/postgres" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@";; esac; }` (when already running as root use `su postgres -c` / `runuser -u postgres --` instead of `sudo`, whichever exists). Feed SQL FILES to it on stdin, never by path — `super_sql -f - < "$REPO_ROOT/supabase/tests/00_shim.sql"` — because in `cluster` mode the `postgres` OS user usually cannot read files inside the repo (a `700` home or `/root`). The modes, tried in order:
      - **Path 0 (`MODE=url`)** — when `PG_SUPER_URL` is set (CI's `postgres:16` service container, or a Docker / `npx supabase start` database on the founder's machine at `postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres`, DESIGN §12): use it for every superuser statement, skip Paths A and B, and derive `DATABASE_URL` by replacing user, password and database in `PG_SUPER_URL` with `churchapp_owner`, `churchapp`, `churchapp` (keep host, port and query string).
      - **Path A (`MODE=cluster`)**: `pg_ctlcluster 16 main start` (as `postgres` when root; treat "already running" as success). Superuser access is `sudo -u postgres psql` (peer auth); port from `pg_lsclusters`.
      - **Path B (`MODE=initdb`, when A fails — no cluster, no permission)**: `initdb` refuses to run as root, so when root run `initdb`/`pg_ctl` as the `postgres` OS user, otherwise as the current user. Before `initdb`: `mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"`; when root, `chown postgres "$STATE_DIR"`; if `sudo -u postgres test -w "$STATE_DIR"` still fails (untraversable parent directories such as `/root`), use `PGDATA_DIR="${LOCAL_PG_DATA:-/var/lib/postgresql/churchapp-local}"` instead of `$STATE_DIR/pg` and record the path in `$STATE_DIR/PGDATA` (the URL files always stay in `.local-pg/`). Then `initdb -D "$PGDATA_DIR" -A trust -U postgres --no-locale -E UTF8` (skip when the directory exists), pick the first free port from 5433 upward (loop with `pg_isready`/`ss -ltn`), then `pg_ctl -D "$PGDATA_DIR" -o "-p $PORT -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 -k $STATE_DIR" -l "$STATE_DIR/pg.log" start` (skip when already running per `pg_ctl status`). Superuser URL is `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PORT/postgres`.
   4. Create the owner role BEFORE the database, with its FULL attributes, in one guarded statement through `super_sql`: `do $$ begin if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'churchapp_owner') then create role churchapp_owner login nosuperuser nocreaterole bypassrls password 'churchapp'; end if; end $$;` — the shim's own `churchapp_owner` block then runs `alter role …` unconditionally (Build 2), so the attributes converge whichever ran first.
   5. Create the database if missing — `createdb` has no connection parameters for a URL-based superuser, so use the helper: `super_sql -tAc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = 'churchapp'" | grep -q 1 || super_sql -c "create database churchapp owner churchapp_owner"`. Owning the database gives `churchapp_owner` the CREATE privilege that trusted extensions (`pgcrypto`, `citext`) require in PG16. Then apply the full shim against `churchapp` on EVERY run (it is idempotent): `super_sql -d churchapp -f - < "$REPO_ROOT/supabase/tests/00_shim.sql"` (in `url` mode swap the database name inside the URL instead of passing `-d`).
   6. Compute `DATABASE_URL`: Path 0 → derived from `PG_SUPER_URL` as above; Path B → `postgresql://churchapp_owner@127.0.0.1:$PORT/churchapp?sslmode=disable`; Path A → `postgresql://churchapp_owner:churchapp@127.0.0.1:$PORT/churchapp?sslmode=disable` (Debian's default `pg_hba.conf` uses scram over TCP, hence the dev password; document this in `docs/ENV.md` next to the existing `DATABASE_URL` row). Write `$STATE_DIR/DATABASE_URL` always. Write `$STATE_DIR/PG_SUPER_URL` only in Paths 0 and B (where a URL works); in Path A write `$STATE_DIR/SUPER_PSQL` containing `sudo -u postgres psql -p <port>` instead, because peer auth has no URL the current user can use. Print `export DATABASE_URL=…` as the last line (mask any password). Verify with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select current_user || ' ' || current_setting('server_version')"` → `churchapp_owner 16.x`.
   7. Add `scripts/db/_env.sh` (sourced by the other scripts): sets `REPO_ROOT`, and `DATABASE_URL` from the environment or `$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg/DATABASE_URL`, failing with "run scripts/db/local-up.sh first" when neither exists; exposes a `super_psql "$@"` function — `psql "$PG_SUPER_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"` when `PG_SUPER_URL` is in the environment or in `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL`, else the command stored in `.local-pg/SUPER_PSQL` — so later scripts (1.4a's database reset, 1.5's seed) run superuser statements regardless of path.
4. `scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh`: sources `_env.sh`; lists `supabase/migrations/*.sql`; sorts by the 4-digit numeric prefix DESCENDING (9999 first — highest number = oldest = applied first) and, within one number, by the letter suffix ASCENDING (`9998a_enum.sql` before `9998b_use.sql`); applies each with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f "$file"` and prints `applied <file>`; exits non-zero on the first failure. `--single-transaction` matches the SQL editor (one paste = one transaction) and is why enum value additions must live in their own file. Optional `--only <file>` argument for debugging. Print the final line `applied N migration(s) to $DATABASE_URL` (mask the password).
5. `scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh`: a static checker (bash + `grep -nE`/`awk`, or a small Python 3 script invoked from bash — Python 3 is present) over every `supabase/migrations/*.sql`, implementing exactly the rules of DESIGN §12 "Re-runnability guard" and PLAN §12: fail if (a) any `create policy` is not preceded (anywhere earlier in the file) by `drop policy if exists <same name>`; (b) any `create trigger <name> on <table>` lacks a preceding `drop trigger if exists <name> on <table>`; (c) any `create type` appears outside a `do $$ … if not exists … $$` block (approximate: the `create type` line must be inside a `do $$` block whose text contains `if not exists`); (d) any `create table`/`create index`/`create unique index`/`create schema`/`create extension` lacks `if not exists`; (e) any `create function` is neither `create or replace function` nor preceded by `drop function if exists <name>`; (f) any `create view` lacks a preceding `drop view if exists <name>`; (g) any function definition (from `create or replace function` to the end of its body — the closing `$$` tag or `;`) lacks `security definer` OR lacks `set search_path = ''` — report which clause is missing (DESIGN §12 and PLAN §12 require BOTH on every function); (h) any unqualified `crypt(`, `gen_salt(`, `gen_random_bytes(`, `digest(` (i.e. not preceded by `extensions.`); (i) a file containing `add value` also contains that value as a quoted literal elsewhere; (j) any `create policy` whose name does not start with `ca_`; (k) any `force row level security`. Print `OK <file>` or every violation as `file:line: rule (x): message`; exit 1 on any violation. Make rule (g) tolerant of `language sql`/`language plpgsql` order and of line breaks. Add a `--self-test` flag that runs the checker against a few inline bad snippets written to `$REPO_ROOT/.local-pg/rerun-selftest/` (created and emptied by the script; gitignored with the rest of `.local-pg/`) and asserts each rule fires — for (g) include one snippet missing only `security definer` and one missing only `set search_path` (this is the checker's own test).
6. `scripts/db/test.sh` (minimal; step 1.4 extends it): sources `_env.sh`; if `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` exists, applies it first (`ON_ERROR_STOP=1`); then runs every `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`; prints `PASS <file>`/`FAIL <file>`; exits 1 on any failure; when the `rls/` directory is absent or empty prints `no RLS tests yet (step 1.4)` and exits 0. This makes the standing verification sequence runnable from this step on.
7. `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` — sections (0)–(4) of the skeleton in PLAN §4 "Migration skeleton" and DESIGN §4.4. Write the file with a section header comment per section, e.g. `-- ===== (3) tables =====`, and reserve headers for (5)–(11) with a one-line `-- filled in step 1.3a / 1.3b / 1.4` placeholder each so later steps insert in the right place. Content:
   - Header comment: re-runnable; paste into the Supabase SQL editor as many times as needed; frozen after the first production paste (HANDOFF ledger).

Do not create the `extensions` schema in the migration (Supabase owns it; the shim creates it locally).
   - (2) all 21 enums, each in its own `do $$ if not exists … $$` guard (one `do` block per type, so a later `9998a` paste can copy the pattern). Values — copy verbatim where the docs give them, otherwise use these and keep them: `permission_key` (the 12 values in PLAN §4 order); `org_status` (`trial, active, past_due, suspended, cancelled`); `billing_mode` (`stripe, manual, free`); `subscription_status` (`trialing, active, past_due, canceled, unpaid, incomplete, incomplete_expired, paused, none, unknown`); `membership_status` (`pending, active, disabled`); `congregation_status` (`member, attendee, inactive`); `sex` (`male, female`); `marital_status` (`unknown, single, married, widowed, divorced`); `household_role` (`head, spouse, child, other`); `birthdate_visibility` (`full, month_day, hidden`); `media_kind` (`upload, youtube, dropbox, google_drive, url`); `audience_kind` (`everyone, members, attendees, youth, men, women, custom`); `calendar_kind` (`all, youth, men, women, custom`); `event_status` (`pending, approved, rejected, cancelled`); `survey_status` (`draft, open, closed`); `response_mode` (`per_person, per_household`); `question_kind` (`short_text, long_text, single_choice, multi_choice, yes_no, number, date`); `notification_kind` (`announcement, event, survey, bulletin`); `notification_status` (`queued, claimed, sent, failed, cancelled`); `push_platform` (`android, ios`); `join_request_status` (`pending, approved, rejected`).
   - (3) `create table if not exists` for all 38 public tables and 3 private tables, in dependency order, with `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` (unless the docs give another PK), `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` on every table that is ever updated, `org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id) on delete cascade` + `create index if not exists <table>_org_id_idx` on every tenant table, `extensions.citext` for emails and slugs. Copy the column lists and constraints from DESIGN §4.2 and the SQL in §4.4 verbatim for `organizations` (with two additions: `trial_ends_at timestamptz default now() + interval '30 days'` — founder decision 7 — and `cancelled_at timestamptz` with the comment "set by the `organizations_stamp_org_status` trigger (step 1.3a) when status becomes `cancelled`; drives the 30-day purge in `srv_housekeeping`"), `organization_settings` (ADD `sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false` — founder decision 5: "DOWNLOADS ALLOWED when the church allows it → NEW column `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false`"), `households`, `household_leader_notes`, `persons` (+ the partial unique `persons_org_user_unique`, indexes `(org_id, household_id)`, `(org_id, birthdate)`, and the NEW `create unique index if not exists persons_one_head_per_household on public.persons (household_id) where household_role = 'head'` — orchestrator decision 6), `person_leader_notes`, `sermons` (+ `sermons_storage_path_unique`), `billing_subscriptions`. No `anonymous` column on surveys (DESIGN: Phase 4).
   - (4) exactly the drop block from DESIGN §4.4: the `do $$` loop dropping every policy named `ca\_%` in `public` and `storage`, then `drop view if exists public.directory_persons`, `public.directory_households`, `public.org_directory_info`.
   - (5) header, containing only the two trigger functions this step owns, both `language plpgsql security definer set search_path = ''`: `app.touch_updated_at()` (sets `new.updated_at = now()`), and `app.assert_same_org()` taking two trigger arguments `tg_argv[0]` = FK column name and `tg_argv[1]` = parent table name, which does nothing when the FK value is null and otherwise executes `select org_id from public.<parent> where id = $1` via `execute format(…, tg_argv[1]) using <fk value>` and raises `exception 'cross_org_reference' using errcode = '23503', detail = format('%s.%s must reference a row of the same organization', tg_table_name, tg_argv[0])` when the parent's `org_id` differs from `new.org_id` (or the parent row does not exist). Read the FK value dynamically with `fk_value := (to_jsonb(new) ->> tg_argv[0])::uuid` (plpgsql cannot write `new.<variable>`; no `hstore` or any other extension); the parent lookup is `execute format('select org_id from public.%I where id = $1', tg_argv[1]) into parent_org using fk_value`.
   - (6) header placeholder only. (7) `drop trigger if exists` + `create trigger` for: `<table>_touch_updated_at before update … execute function app.touch_updated_at()` on every table with an `updated_at` column (public and private); and `<table>_assert_same_org_<fk_col> before insert or update of <fk_col>` — name the single-FK case `<table>_assert_same_org` as in DESIGN's `persons_assert_same_org` example — on: `persons(household_id→households)`, `household_leader_notes(household_id→households)`, `person_leader_notes(person_id→persons)`, `invitations(person_id→persons)`, `join_requests(join_code_id→join_codes)`, `join_requests(person_id→persons)`, `sermon_share_links(sermon_id→sermons)`, `announcements(audience_group_id→audience_groups)`, `announcements(document_id→documents)`, `documents(audience_group_id→audience_groups)`, `audience_group_members(group_id→audience_groups)`, `audience_group_members(person_id→persons)`, `calendars(view_audience_group_id→audience_groups)`, `calendars(submit_audience_group_id→audience_groups)`, `events(calendar_id→calendars)`, `surveys(audience_group_id→audience_groups)`, `survey_questions(survey_id→surveys)`, `survey_responses(survey_id→surveys)`, `survey_responses(person_id→persons)`, `survey_responses(household_id→households)`, `survey_answers(response_id→survey_responses)`, `notifications(audience_group_id→audience_groups)`. Then run the standing sequence. Keep the job non-blocking as 1.1 left it.

## Constraints
- Migration rules (CLAUDE.md, PLAN §4, DESIGN §12): `9999_init.sql` is not yet frozen (nothing pasted into production — HANDOFF ledger is empty) so it may be edited freely, but every construct must already be re-runnable: `if not exists` on tables/indexes/schemas/extensions, `do $$ if not exists` per enum, `create or replace` for functions, `drop trigger if exists` before `create trigger`. Every function is `security definer set search_path = ''`. pgcrypto/citext calls are schema-qualified (`extensions.…`). No `force row level security`. No enum `add value`. Never run `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`; never run `supabase start` (Docker is down).
- No policies, no grants beyond section (1), no views, no storage buckets, no RPCs, no seed, no RLS tests in this step; do not enable RLS yet (step 1.4 does it in section 8). Do not invent additional tables or columns beyond the lists above; if a column you need is missing, add it and record the addition under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan".
- Scripts: bash with `set -euo pipefail`; every path quoted (the repo has a `Session log/` directory with a space); executable bit set (`chmod +x`); no `sudo` without a root/`postgres` fallback; never write anything under `/tmp` — use `.local-pg/` or the scratchpad; do not modify system `pg_hba.conf` or `postgresql.conf`.
- Do not add npm dependencies. Do not create `packages/*` code. Do not write secrets anywhere; the `churchapp` dev password is local-only and documented as such.
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must stay green (no TS changes are expected).

## Verify
- `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` → last line `export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://churchapp_owner…/churchapp?sslmode=disable`; `.local-pg/DATABASE_URL` exists; running it a second time re-applies the idempotent shim and prints the same URL. Then `export DATABASE_URL="$(cat .local-pg/DATABASE_URL)"` (or `eval "$(bash scripts/db/local-up.sh | tail -n 1)"`) before every psql check below — the script only prints the export line, it cannot set your shell's variable.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select current_user || ' ' || current_setting('server_version')"` → `churchapp_owner 16.x`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select rolbypassrls, rolsuper from pg_roles where rolname = current_user"` → `t|f`; `select rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = 'service_role'` → `t`; `select relrowsecurity from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where n.nspname = 'storage' and c.relname = 'objects'` → `t`.
- `bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh` → both runs print `applied supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and exit 0 (second run proves re-runnability).
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public'"` → `38`; `… where schemaname = 'private'` → `3`; `select count(*) from pg_type t join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.typnamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and t.typtype = 'e'` → `21`; `select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'organization_settings' and column_name = 'sermon_share_allow_download'` → `1`; `select count(*) from pg_indexes where indexname = 'persons_one_head_per_household'` → `1`; `select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and (table_name, column_name) in (('profiles','archived_at'), ('profiles','archive_reason'), ('account_deletion_requests','scheduled_for'), ('organizations','cancelled_at'), ('calendars','members_can_submit'), ('documents','description'))` → `6`; `select is_nullable from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name in ('bulletins','documents') and column_name = 'publish_at'` → `YES` twice; `select column_default from information_schema.columns where table_name = 'organizations' and column_name = 'trial_ends_at'` → contains `30 days`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select c.table_name from information_schema.columns c where c.table_schema = 'public' and c.column_name = 'org_id' and not exists (select 1 from pg_indexes i where i.schemaname = 'public' and i.tablename = c.table_name and i.indexdef ~ '\\(org_id[,)]')"` → no rows (every table with an `org_id` column has an index whose FIRST column is `org_id`; composite indexes such as `(org_id, publish_at desc)` and PKs on `org_id` count; add a `<table>_org_id_idx` wherever the query lists a table — `fellowship_memberships`, the two leader-notes tables, `survey_questions`, `survey_answers`, `audience_group_members`, `notification_preferences` are the usual misses).
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'app' and not p.prosecdef"` → `0`; `select count(*) from pg_trigger where tgname like '%_touch_updated_at'` ≥ 30; `select count(*) from pg_trigger where tgname like '%assert_same_org%'` → `22`.
- Behaviour smoke (run inside `begin; … rollback;`): insert two organizations A and B; insert a household in A; `insert into public.persons (org_id, household_id, first_name, last_name) values (B, <household of A>, 'x', 'y')` → fails with SQLSTATE `23503` and message `cross_org_reference`; the same insert with `org_id = A` succeeds; `update public.organizations set name = 'z' where id = A` then `select updated_at > created_at` → `t`; inserting two persons with `household_role = 'head'` in one household → unique violation `23505`.
- `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` → `OK supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, exit 0; `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh --self-test` → every rule (a)–(k) reported as firing.
- `bash scripts/db/test.sh` → `no RLS tests yet (step 1.4)`, exit 0.
- `pnpm db:up && pnpm db:apply && pnpm db:apply && pnpm db:check && pnpm db:test` (the root scripts from 1.1) → all exit 0.
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm format:check` → clean (add `supabase/**/*.sql` and `.local-pg` to `.prettierignore` if Prettier complains about SQL).
- Push, then confirm the CI `checks` run: the DB steps now execute against the `postgres:16` service and pass.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: tick nothing in "State" yet for the migration line but add a sub-bullet "9999_init.sql sections 0–4 + local harness (step 1.2)"; in the "Founder's feature checklist" leave every `Schema` cell at `planned` but add a footnote line under the table: "Schema column: tables 1.2 ✓, functions/views 1.3a, RPCs 1.3b, RLS/tests 1.4 — marked `done` after 1.4"; list the decision-15/21 columns you added (`profiles.archived_*`, `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for`, `organizations.cancelled_at`, `trial_ends_at` default, nullable `publish_at`, `documents.description`, `calendars.members_can_submit`) under "Decisions" so 1.3a/1.3b/1.4/6.3a find them; record which PostgreSQL start path worked on this machine (DESIGN §11 Phase 1 step 3 asks for this) and the fallback port if any; add the shim/`churchapp` dev password note under "Version pins worth remembering" or a new "Local database" heading; list any column or enum value you had to choose beyond the lists above under "Deviations from plan".
- Tick step 1.2 in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(db): local Postgres harness, shim, and 9999_init.sql sections 0-4`; push `main` (`git push origin main`).
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong (for example `pg_ctlcluster` and `initdb` both unavailable), do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
```

**Done when**

- [ ] `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` succeeds on a machine with PostgreSQL 16 and no Docker (system cluster, `initdb` fallback, or any `PG_SUPER_URL` such as CI's service container), prints `export DATABASE_URL=…`, writes `.local-pg/DATABASE_URL` (plus `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL` or `.local-pg/SUPER_PSQL`), re-applies the idempotent shim on every run, and `select rolbypassrls, rolsuper from pg_roles where rolname = current_user` over that URL returns `t|f`.
- [ ] `bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh` run twice in a row applies `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` with exit 0 both times (files sorted by descending numeric prefix, letter suffix ascending, each in one transaction).
- [ ] The local database has 38 tables in `public`, 3 in `private`, 21 enum types in `public`, the column `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false`, the index `persons_one_head_per_household`, an `org_id`-first index on every table that has an `org_id` column (the Verify query returns no rows), and the orchestrator-decision-15/21 columns: `profiles.archived_at/archived_by/archive_reason`, `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for` (default now() + 30 days), `organizations.cancelled_at`, `organizations.trial_ends_at` defaulting to now() + 30 days, nullable `bulletins.publish_at`/`documents.publish_at`, `documents.description`, `calendars.members_can_submit`.
- [ ] Inside a rolled-back transaction: a cross-org FK insert raises SQLSTATE 23503 with message `cross_org_reference`; an update bumps `updated_at`; two `head` persons in one household raise 23505 — proving the 1.2 trigger functions and triggers work.
- [ ] `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` prints `OK supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and `--self-test` shows every rule (a)–(k) firing, including (g) for a function missing only `security definer` and one missing only `set search_path`; `bash scripts/db/test.sh` exits 0 with `no RLS tests yet (step 1.4)`.

   - `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete()` (after delete on `announcements`, `events`, `surveys`, `bulletins`): `update notifications set status = 'cancelled' where kind = <kind for the table> and ref_id = old.id and status in ('queued','claimed')`.
   - `app.on_content_publish()` (after insert or update on `announcements`, `bulletins`, `events`, `surveys`): enqueue one `notifications` row when the row becomes publish-worthy and none exists yet — announcements: `push` true, `publish_at` not null (`scheduled_for = publish_at`; future dates are fine, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications` in 1.3b only re-checks), `push_enqueued_at` stamped; bulletins: `organization_settings.push_on_bulletin` (founder decision 6) and published; events: `status = 'approved'` and `push`; surveys: `status = 'open'` and `push`. `title`/`body` from the row (bulletin body "New bulletin: <title>"), `audience_group_id` from the row when it has one, `data = jsonb_build_object('url', '/o/' || org slug || '/…')` is NOT computed here — leave `data` to the dispatcher (step 3.6) and store only `kind`, `ref_id`, `org_id`, `title`, `body`, `audience_group_id`, `scheduled_for`. Use `insert … where not exists (select 1 from notifications where kind = … and ref_id = … and status <> 'cancelled')`. Orchestrator decision 21 (G9): when a `queued` (not `claimed`/`sent`) notification already exists for `(kind, ref_id)` and the row's `publish_at` (announcements, bulletins) or `opens_at` (surveys) changed, `update notifications set scheduled_for = <new value>` instead of inserting — an edit that reschedules an announcement moves its push. When a row stops being publish-worthy (announcement `push` set false or `publish_at` set null, survey back to `draft`), set the still-`queued` notification to `cancelled`.
   - `app.mirror_subscription_status()` (after insert or update on `billing_subscriptions`): when the org's `billing_mode = 'stripe'`, map `active`/`trialing` → `organizations.status = 'active'`, `past_due`/`unpaid` → `past_due`, `canceled`/`incomplete_expired` → `suspended`; other statuses leave it unchanged. Never touch orgs in `cancelled`.
   - `app.stamp_org_status()` (before update of `status` on `organizations`): set `new.cancelled_at = now()` when `new.status = 'cancelled' and old.status <> 'cancelled'`, and `new.cancelled_at = null` when the status leaves `cancelled`; `srv_housekeeping` (1.3b) purges orgs with `cancelled_at < now() - interval '30 days'` (PLAN §4: "purged by cron after 30 days" — without this column the age of a cancellation is not computable).
   - `app.guard_system_audience_groups()` (before update or delete on `audience_groups`; orchestrator decision 21 / G13): rows with `kind <> 'custom'` may not be deleted and may not have `kind` or `name` changed (`description` may) → raise `system_group_immutable` (`P0001`); custom rows are untouched by this trigger (their permission rule is 1.4a's policy). No skips — the six system rows are invariants for `app.on_org_created`, `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` in `@church/domain` (1.6) and the join-code flows of 5.6.

The migration still applies twice; smoke checks prove the invitation flow, share-link creation/resolution with rate limiting, the permission-escalation block, the last-manager guard through the RPC, the suspended-org block, the deactivate/restore/deletion-grace flow, the head-of-house swap and the notification claim loop. Grants are still step 1.4 — locally the RPCs are exercised as the owner with impersonated JWT claims in a rollback-only smoke script (they are `security definer`, so no `grant execute` is needed).

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 1.2: sections (0)–(4), scripts under `scripts/db/`, the shim. Step 1.3a: sections (5a) helpers (`app.require_user`, `app.require_writable`, `app.has_perm`, `app.is_directory_admin`, `app.can_edit_household`, `app.my_person_id`, `app.person_in_group`, `app.rate_limit_hit`, `app.rate_limit_check`, …), (5b) trigger functions (with the `auth.uid() is null` and `app.trusted_rpc` skips in `guard_persons_columns`/`guard_household_privacy_columns`, the `account_archived` rule in `require_user`, `stamp_org_status`, `guard_system_audience_groups`), (6) views, (6b) storage helpers, (7) triggers, and the SQLSTATE convention comment at the top of section (5). Read `9999_init.sql` end to end first and reuse the column names it fixed.
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 5 — "Share links: DOWNLOADS ALLOWED when the church allows it … Min password 8; available to `sermons.link` OR `sermons.upload` holders" (`create_share_link` checks the permission pair; `srv_resolve_share_link` returns `allow_download` from `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download` so the share page can decide); decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes" (`app.require_writable`), trial → `past_due` flip after `trial_ends_at` in `srv_housekeeping`; decision 8 is Phase 3 (do NOT implement head-of-house proxy answers here — `submit_survey_response` answers for the caller's own person/household only); decision 4 — the mapping table in DESIGN §5 decides which permission each RPC checks.
- Orchestrator decisions 15 and 21 (2026-09-07/08) change this step because `9999_init.sql` is not yet pasted. Decision 15: the self-service action is **Deactivate** (archive, reversible by a super admin or by the user on next sign-in); real **Delete account** stays because Google Play requires it, but it archives immediately and deletes after a 30-day grace (`ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30`; the user or a super admin cancels in between); the columns exist since 1.2 (`profiles.archived_at/archived_by/archive_reason`, `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for`). Decision 21: `srv_claim_notifications(org_id, max_rows)` (per-org claiming for the synchronous dispatch after publish), `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(link_id)` for cookie-verified share visits (so 3.4b stops re-validating in TypeScript), and the atomic `set_head_of_house(hh, new_head, previous_head_role)` open to directory admins and household adults (founder answer 8 / orchestrator decision 6; the rejected G12 step 5.8 is its specification). Step 6.3a (G14) builds its UI on these exact names; 3.4b, 3.6a and 5.1a call them.
- Token convention (fixed here, used by steps 1.6, 3.2 and 3.4): raw tokens are 32 random bytes from `extensions.gen_random_bytes(32)` encoded as base64url without padding (`translate(encode(bytes, 'base64'), '+/', '-_')` with `=` stripped, 43 chars); the stored hash is `sha256(convert_to(token, 'UTF8'))` (core `sha256(bytea)`, no pgcrypto needed); Node computes the same with `createHash('sha256').update(token).digest()` and passes the 32-byte Buffer as the `bytea` argument. Invitation and share-link tokens use the same scheme.

Every RPC: `language plpgsql security definer set search_path = ''`, `volatile` unless read-only, first statement `perform app.require_user();` (client RPCs — except `my_context()` and `restore_my_account()`, which read `auth.uid()` directly so an archived user can still call them) and `perform app.require_writable(<org>);` for every mutating one, explicit permission checks raising `permission_denied` (`42501`) with the permission key in `detail`. Server-only RPCs (`srv_*`) do NOT call `require_user()` (they run as `service_role`, `auth.uid()` is null) but DO call `app.require_writable` where they mutate org data.

2. `public.my_context() returns jsonb` (stable): `{is_super_admin, orgs: [{org_id, slug, name, status, membership_status, person_id, household_id, permissions: [..]}]}` — memberships of `auth.uid()` in any status except `disabled` (super admin additionally gets every org with `membership_status = null`); `permissions` sorted; `person_id`/`household_id` via `app.my_person_id`. Also return `profile: {display_name, email, last_org_id}` and `archived: null | {archived_at, archive_reason, deletion_scheduled_for}` (decision 15 — the apps show "Restore my account" or the pending-deletion notice from it). Read `auth.uid()` directly (raise `auth_required` when null) instead of `app.require_user()`, so an archived user still gets a context; for an archived caller return `orgs: []` and `is_super_admin: false`.
3. `set_membership_permissions(membership_id uuid, perms public.permission_key[]) returns void`: derive `org_id` from the membership; require `users.edit_permissions` on that org; compute the diff; delete removed rows, insert added rows with `granted_by = auth.uid()`; the `guard_last_org_manager` trigger (1.3a) blocks stripping the last manager — let its `last_org_manager` propagate; audit happens via triggers.
4. `set_membership_status(membership_id uuid, status public.membership_status) returns void`: `disabled` needs `users.delete`; `active` needs `users.create`; `pending` is not settable (raise `invalid_payload`); stamp `disabled_at` / `approved_by`/`approved_at`; `membership_not_found` when absent. `remove_membership(membership_id uuid) returns void`: `users.delete`; hard-delete the membership (cascades permissions), null `persons.user_id` for that user in that org, delete that user's `notification_preferences` for the org and, when the user has no other active membership, that user's `push_devices`.
5. `create_invitation(org uuid, email text, person_id uuid, perms public.permission_key[]) returns text`: `users.create`; **`perms` non-empty requires `users.edit_permissions`** (raise `permission_denied`, detail `users.edit_permissions`) — this is the escalation rule DESIGN §1 item 2 states ("`users.create` can never grant permissions it does not hold"); `person_id`, when given, must belong to `org` (else `person_not_found`); email normalised with `lower(trim(email))`; create the `invitations` row and `private.invitation_secrets` with the token hash; return the raw token once. `revoke_invitation(invitation_id uuid) returns void`: `users.create`; set `revoked_at`.
6. `accept_invitation(token text) returns jsonb`: after the validity checks below and before any insert, `perform set_config('app.trusted_rpc', 'on', true);` — the 1.3a column and privacy guards skip while this transaction-local flag is on, so this RPC is responsible for the rules it enforces (minor check, role `head`, the `created_via = 'invitation'` household stays visible). Look up by hash; `invitation_invalid` when missing/revoked/accepted, `invitation_expired` when past `expires_at`; the caller's `auth.users.email` (via `profiles.email`) must equal the invitation email (`invitation_email_mismatch`); require the org writable; upsert the membership as `active` (`approved_by = invited_by`); grant the recorded permissions ONLY if the inviter still holds `users.edit_permissions` in that org (else grant none and write an `audit_log` row `action = 'invitation_permissions_dropped'`); when `person_id` is null and the caller has no person in the org, create a one-person household (`created_via = 'invitation'`, `name = display_name`) and a person (`congregation_status = 'attendee'`, `household_role = 'head'`, `user_id = auth.uid()`); when `person_id` is set, link it (`user_id = auth.uid()`) unless it is a minor (`minor_cannot_have_account`); for an existing member merge permissions and link the person instead of failing; stamp `accepted_at`/`accepted_by`; return `{org_id, slug, membership_id, person_id}`.
7. Directory RPCs — the caller must satisfy `app.can_edit_household(hh)` for the household concerned (`not_household_editor`), and the column guards from 1.3a still apply to `save_household`/`save_person`/`delete_person` (they do NOT set `app.trusted_rpc`; RPCs run with the caller's `auth.uid()`), so the trigger and the RPC enforce the same rule twice: `save_household(payload jsonb) returns uuid` — `id` optional (insert vs update), whitelisted keys `name, address_line1, address_line2, city, region, postal_code, country, home_phone, photo_path, anniversary, sort_key`; inserts require directory admin (`org_id` in payload); unknown keys → `invalid_payload`. `save_person(payload jsonb) returns uuid` — keys `id, org_id, household_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, sex, birthdate, birthdate_visibility, marital_status, household_role, congregation_status, member_since, youth_override, directory_listed, email, mobile_phone, work_phone, photo_path, deceased_on, user_id`; non-admins may only set `household_role in ('child','other')` on others (`household_role_not_allowed`), may not set `congregation_status`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, and may set `user_id` only to `auth.uid()` or null; a person may always edit their own contact fields (`preferred_name, email, mobile_phone, work_phone, photo_path, birthdate_visibility`) even without being a household adult. `delete_person(person_id uuid) returns void` — directory admin, or household adult when the person is not linked to a user. `set_household_privacy(hh uuid, hide_fell boolean, hide_cong boolean, show_children boolean) returns void` — update the three flags; the 1.3a trigger enforces "household adults any direction (stamps confirmation), directory admins only toward more privacy, super admin any" (founder decision 1). `save_leader_notes(kind text, id uuid, notes text) returns void` — `kind in ('household','person')` else `invalid_payload`; directory admin only; upsert into the leader-notes table with `updated_by`. `set_congregation_status(person_id uuid, status public.congregation_status, member_since date) returns void` — directory admin only. `set_head_of_house(hh uuid, new_head uuid, previous_head_role public.household_role default 'spouse') returns void` (orchestrator decision 21; the rejected G12 step 5.8 is its specification): `require_user()`; resolve `org_id` from `households` (`household_not_found`); `require_writable`; `app.can_edit_household(hh)` else `not_household_editor` — this admits directory admins, household adults and super admins alike (founder answer 8 / orchestrator decision 6: "editable by directory admins and by the household"); `previous_head_role` must be `spouse` or `other` else `invalid_payload`; `new_head` must belong to `hh` (`person_not_found`) and must not be a minor (`household_role_not_allowed`, detail "a minor cannot be head of house"); then `perform set_config('app.trusted_rpc', 'on', true)` and, in one transaction, `update persons set household_role = previous_head_role where household_id = hh and household_role = 'head' and id <> new_head` followed by `update persons set household_role = 'head' where id = new_head` (the 1.2 partial unique index guarantees one head; the `persons` audit trigger records both updates). Idempotent: `new_head` already head → succeeds without changes. `save_person` is NOT relaxed for `head`/`spouse` on others — this RPC is the only way to move the head.
8. `create_share_link(sermon_id uuid, label text, password text, expires_at timestamptz, max_views int) returns jsonb`: org from the sermon; permission `sermons.link` OR `sermons.upload` (`app.has_any_perm`); `organization_settings.sermons_shareable` else `sharing_disabled`; sermon `publish_at <= now()` else `sermon_not_published`; when `sermon_share_requires_password` and `password is null` → `password_required`; when a password is given, `length(password) >= 8` else `password_too_short`, hash with `extensions.crypt(password, extensions.gen_salt('bf', 10))`; insert `sermon_share_links` (`requires_password = password is not null`, `created_by`) and `private.share_link_secrets` (token hash, password hash); return `{link_id, token}` — the raw token is returned exactly once. `revoke_share_link(link_id uuid) returns void`: same permission pair; set `revoked_at`.
9. `srv_resolve_share_link(token_hash bytea, password text, ip_hash text) returns jsonb` (service role only; never raises for expected outcomes): find the secret by `token_hash`; check the limits FIRST without counting: `app.rate_limit_check('share:t:' || encode(token_hash, 'hex'), 10, interval '15 minutes')` and `app.rate_limit_check('share:ip:' || ip_hash, 10, interval '15 minutes')` (helper from 1.3a) → `{status: 'rate_limited'}` when either is true. Count a failure ONLY on a wrong password: call `app.rate_limit_hit(...)` for both keys before returning `wrong_password`; successful unlocks, `needs_password` and every other status never touch the counters. Then in order: missing → `{status:'invalid'}`; `revoked_at` → `revoked`; `expires_at < now()` → `expired`; `max_views` reached → `max_views`; org not `sermons_shareable` or org not writable → `sharing_disabled` (the writability check is a deliberate addition to DESIGN §4.4's list: a suspended or cancelled church stops public sharing, consistent with `fellowship_visible_org_ids` excluding such orgs — record it under "Deviations from plan" so 3.4 shows the same "sharing disabled" page for it); sermon `publish_at` null or future → `unpublished`; org `sermon_share_requires_password` and `password_hash is null` → `needs_password_reset`; `requires_password` and `password is null` → `needs_password`; wrong password (`password_hash <> extensions.crypt(password, password_hash)`) → count a failure and return `wrong_password`; success → increment `view_count` (ONLY here — "increments `view_count` only on successful unlock"), and return `{status:'ok', link_id, sermon: {id, org_id, title, speaker, preached_on, description, media_kind, storage_path, external_url, external_id, mime_type}, allow_download: <settings.sermon_share_allow_download and media_kind = 'upload'>, org: {name, slug, logo_path}}`. A link whose `requires_password` is false unlocks with `password = null`. The `needs_password` and `needs_password_reset` results additionally carry `link_id`, `sermon_title` and `org_name` so the password form can show a title and 3.4 can key the cookie by `link_id` as DESIGN §7 intends.
   `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(link_id uuid) returns jsonb` (service role only; orchestrator decision 21 — the name was chosen there and is flagged in open_issues): for a visitor whose jose cookie already proves an unlock, re-check `revoked_at`, `expires_at`, `max_views`, org `sermons_shareable` and writability, sermon `publish_at`, and return exactly the same `ok` payload as `srv_resolve_share_link` (same `link_id`, `sermon`, `org`, `allow_download` keys) or the matching status; it never checks a password, never touches the rate limiter and never increments `view_count`. Share the payload-building code between the two functions through a private plpgsql helper `app.share_link_payload(link_id uuid) returns jsonb` (count it as an extra `app.*` helper in HANDOFF; no `authenticated` grant).
10. `srv_audience_user_ids(group_id uuid, org uuid) returns setof uuid` (the docs write `group`; it is a reserved word, so the parameter is `group_id` — record this under "Deviations from plan". PostgREST passes arguments BY NAME, so every parameter name in this section is part of the contract that 1.7's `rpc.ts`, 3.2, 3.4, 3.6 and 5.5 must use — list them all verbatim in HANDOFF): `perform app.require_writable(org)`; distinct `persons.user_id` for persons of `org` with `user_id` not null, joined to `org_memberships` with `status = 'active'` (DESIGN: "removed members never receive pushes") and to `profiles` with `archived_at is null` (decision 15: archived users get no push), filtered by `group_id is null or app.person_in_group(persons.id, group_id)`.
11. `srv_enqueue_due_notifications() returns int`: for announcements/events/surveys/bulletins that are publish-worthy now (same predicates as `app.on_content_publish`, restricted to `publish_at`/`opens_at <= now()`) and have no non-cancelled notification, insert one; return the count. It is the safety net for rows created before the trigger existed and for future-dated content whose `scheduled_for` already exists (those need nothing — the dispatcher claims by `scheduled_for <= now()`).
12. `srv_claim_notifications(org_id uuid, max_rows int) returns setof public.notifications` (orchestrator decision 21 / G9 — DESIGN writes `(limit)`; `org_id` null = every org, non-null = only that church's rows, so the synchronous dispatch after publish does not pick up other churches' backlog): `update notifications set status = 'claimed', claimed_at = now(), attempts = attempts + 1 where id in (select n.id from notifications n where n.status = 'queued' and n.scheduled_for <= now() and n.attempts < 5 and (srv_claim_notifications.org_id is null or n.org_id = srv_claim_notifications.org_id) order by n.scheduled_for for update skip locked limit max_rows) returning *` — qualify the parameter with the function name (`srv_claim_notifications.org_id`) to avoid the column-name clash while keeping the PARAMETER name `org_id`, because callers pass `{ org_id, max_rows }`. Also mark rows with `attempts >= 5` as `failed`. Claimed rows older than 10 minutes without `sent_at` are re-queued by `srv_housekeeping`.
13. `srv_attach_user(user_id uuid, org uuid, person_id uuid, display_name text, perms public.permission_key[]) returns jsonb`: used by the Server Action `createUserDirect` after `auth.admin.createUser`; `require_writable`; `perform set_config('app.trusted_rpc', 'on', true)` (it runs as `service_role` with `auth.uid()` null, which the 1.3a guards already trust — the flag makes the intent explicit and keeps working if a future caller has a uid); refuse a `person_id` that is a minor (`minor_cannot_have_account`); a repeat call for the same `(user_id, org)` is idempotent (membership re-activated, permissions merged, no second household); upsert `profiles.display_name`; upsert `org_memberships` as `active`; when `person_id` is null create a one-person household + person (`created_via = 'admin'`, so `hide_from_fellowship = true` by the 1.3a rule, role `head`, status `attendee`) else link it (minor check); insert the permissions (the caller — the Server Action — has already verified `users.edit_permissions` with the user client; document this in the function comment); return `{membership_id, person_id, household_id}`.
14. Account archival and deletion (orchestrator decision 15; the names are the ones step 6.3a builds on — do not rename). An internal helper `app.archive_account(user_id uuid, reason text, actor uuid) returns void` sets `profiles.archived_at = now(), archived_by = actor, archive_reason = reason` (no-op when already archived), deletes the user's `push_devices`, and leaves the audit trail through the `profiles` audit trigger. `deactivate_account() returns void` (client): `require_user()`; raise `deletion_pending` (P0001) when an unprocessed `account_deletion_requests` row exists; `app.archive_account(auth.uid(), 'user', auth.uid())`. `request_account_deletion() returns void` (client — the Google Play deletion path): `require_user()`; `app.archive_account(auth.uid(), 'deletion_request', auth.uid())`; upsert the request row for `auth.uid()` with `requested_at = now()`, `scheduled_for = now() + interval '30 days'` (write the literal with the comment `-- ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30`; `packages/domain/src/limits.ts` (1.6) carries the same constant). `restore_my_account() returns int` (client; reads `auth.uid()` directly, NOT `require_user()`, because the caller is archived): for the caller's own profile with `archive_reason in ('user', 'deletion_request')` clear the three columns, delete any unprocessed request row, and return the count of `active` memberships restored; `archive_reason = 'admin'` → `account_archived_by_admin` (42501 — an admin decision cannot be undone by the user); not archived → return the membership count unchanged. `srv_archive_account(user_id uuid, reason text) returns void` (service): `reason in ('user','deletion_request','admin')` else `invalid_payload`; `app.archive_account(user_id, reason, null)`; when `reason = 'deletion_request'` also upsert the request row with the same 30-day `scheduled_for` (a super admin starting a deletion for a user who asked by email). `srv_restore_account(user_id uuid) returns void` (service): clear the three columns whatever the reason and delete the pending request row (the super admin's Restore / Cancel deletion buttons). `srv_process_account_deletions() returns int` (service): `perform set_config('app.cascade', 'on', true)` once at the top (transaction-local — PostgREST wraps each RPC in its own transaction, so it cannot leak to the pooled connection; never `set app.cascade` session-wide) so `guard_last_org_manager` audits `org_without_manager` instead of blocking; for each row with `processed_at is null and scheduled_for <= now()` (rows inside the grace window are untouched): null `persons.user_id` (the person stays in the directory), delete memberships (cascades permissions), devices, preferences, then `delete from auth.users where id = …` (cascades `profiles`, `notification_deliveries`, `push_devices`), stamp `processed_at`; return the count. Invariant for all of these: an archived account behaves like a disabled membership everywhere — the 1.3a helpers already treat it as a non-member; `persons` rows stay.
15. `srv_housekeeping() returns jsonb`: prune `private.rate_limits` older than 1 day; expire invitations (`revoked_at = now()` where `expires_at < now()` and not accepted/revoked); delete `sermons` with `media_kind = 'upload'`, `publish_at is null`, `created_at < now() - interval '7 days'` and no `storage.objects` row for `storage_path` (the delete trigger enqueues nothing because the object is absent — guard by checking `storage.objects` first); flip `trial → past_due` where `trial_ends_at < now()` and `billing_mode in ('stripe','manual')` (founder decision 7); re-queue stale `claimed` notifications (> 10 min, `attempts < 5`); purge organizations where `status = 'cancelled' and cancelled_at < now() - interval '30 days'` (the 1.3a `stamp_org_status` trigger sets `cancelled_at`) by enqueueing `storage_deletions (bucket_id, object_name = org_id || '/', is_prefix = true)` for each of the five buckets and then deleting the org row (after `perform set_config('app.cascade', 'on', true)`); return counts per action.
16. `submit_survey_response(survey_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid`: `require_user`; survey `open` and inside `[opens_at, closes_at]` else `survey_not_open`; caller in audience (`app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`) else `survey_not_in_audience`; `answers` is an object `{question_id: value}` whose keys all belong to the survey else `invalid_payload`; insert the response (the 1.3a `stamp_response_scope` trigger sets scope), mapping a unique violation on `(survey_id, scope_key)` to `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit`, in which case update the existing response and replace its answers (`survey_edit_not_allowed` when `allow_edit` is false); return the response id.

## Constraints
- Signatures are frozen by DESIGN §4.4's grant lists PLUS the additions and changes of orchestrator decisions 15 and 21 listed above (`srv_claim_notifications(uuid, int)`, `set_head_of_house(uuid, uuid, household_role)`, `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(uuid)`, `deactivate_account()`, `restore_my_account()`, `srv_archive_account(uuid, text)`, `srv_restore_account(uuid)`) — do not add other parameters (use defaults inside the body instead); do not rename. 1.4a grants exactly these signatures, so list them all, with parameter names, in HANDOFF. - Do not write code under `packages/` or `apps/`; do not add dependencies.
