Re-issue `grant select on public.directory_households, public.directory_persons, public.org_directory_info to authenticated;` (views are owned by the migration owner, so they read the base tables with owner privileges; the functions they call — `app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids` — are executed with the CALLER's privileges, which is why section (9) grants them to `authenticated`).
2. **Section (8) policy catalogue** — one `drop policy if exists <name> on <table>;` immediately before each `create policy`, names `ca_<table>_<op>_<who>`, every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org_id)`, and viewer facts always in the InitPlan form `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` / `org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('<perm>')))` (never a correlated call per row). `service_role` gets no policies (BYPASSRLS). Implement DESIGN §6's table:
   - `organizations`: select `ca_orgs_select_fellowship` (verbatim from DESIGN: member or `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids()`); insert/update `ca_organizations_insert_super` / `ca_organizations_update_super` (`app.is_super_admin()`); no delete policy (`cancelled` + purge).
   - `organization_settings`: select member (`ca_organization_settings_select_member`); update `ca_organization_settings_update_org_settings` = `org.settings` ∧ writable; no insert/delete policy (the `on_org_created` trigger inserts as definer).
   - `fellowships` / `fellowship_memberships`: select when the caller is a member of a linked org (`exists (select 1 from public.fellowship_memberships fm where fm.fellowship_id = <id> and fm.org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids())))`) or super admin; insert/update/delete super only.
   - `profiles`: `ca_profiles_select_org_admin` verbatim from DESIGN (own row, or a `users.create`/`users.delete`/`users.edit_permissions` holder of a shared org); insert/update own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no delete.
   - `super_admins`: select super only; no writes (bootstrap INSERT runs as `postgres`).
   - `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`: select own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`, via the membership for the permissions table) or any `users.*` holder of the org; no write policies (RPC-only; the revoke above already removes the privilege — the absence of policies is the second lock).
   - `invitations`, `join_codes`: select `users.create`; `join_requests`: select `users.create` or own (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no write policies.
   - `households` / `persons`: `ca_households_select_visible` / `ca_persons_select_visible` = `exists (select 1 from public.directory_households d where d.id = households.id)` (DESIGN: "base table only through the view's rule"); no write policies. `household_leader_notes` / `person_leader_notes`: select `org_id = any((select app.directory_admin_org_ids()))`; no write policies.
   - `audience_groups`: select member; insert/update/delete `announcements.create` or `org.settings` ∧ writable, and delete additionally `kind = 'custom'` (system rows are never deleted). `audience_group_members`: select, insert, delete for the same manager pair only; no update policy.
   - `calendars`: select member ∧ `app.user_in_group(view_audience_group_id)`; insert/update/delete `org.settings` ∧ writable.
   - `events`: select member ∧ calendar visible (`exists (select 1 from public.calendars c where c.id = events.calendar_id)` — the calendar policy applies inside the subquery) ∧ (`status = 'approved'` ∨ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` ∨ `announcements.edit`); insert member ∧ writable ∧ (`organization_settings.members_can_submit_events` ∨ `announcements.create`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(<calendar's submit_audience_group_id>)` (DESIGN §6 lists only `members_can_submit_events`; the `∨ announcements.create` branch is this step's reading so managers are never blocked by the member toggle — 1.4c tests it; record it under Deviations) ∧ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` (the 1.3a trigger forces `pending`/`push = false` for non-creators); update `using` own-while-pending or `announcements.edit`, `with check` the same plus `status = 'pending'` unless `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` or own pending.
   - `sermons`: `ca_sermons_select_members` and `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` verbatim from DESIGN §4.4; `ca_sermons_update_by_kind` with the same media-kind split in both `using` and `with check`; `ca_sermons_delete_sermons_delete` = `sermons.delete` ∧ writable.
   - `sermon_share_links`: select `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload`; no write policies (RPC-only).
   - `announcements`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()` ∧ (`expires_at is null or expires_at > now()`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` — each ∧ writable.
   - `bulletins`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()`, or `bulletins.upload`; insert/update/delete `bulletins.upload` ∧ writable. `documents`: select member ∧ published ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or `documents.upload`; writes `documents.upload` ∧ writable.
   - `surveys`, `survey_questions`: select member ∧ `status = 'open'` ∧ inside `[opens_at, closes_at]` (nulls open-ended) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete` (DESIGN §6 says `announcements.create` only; the three-key form follows the PLAN §4 / DESIGN §5 survey mapping `announcements.create/edit/delete` — record it under Deviations) (questions via `exists` on the parent survey); insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit` (the 1.3a `freeze_survey_shape` trigger guards the shape); delete `announcements.delete`.
   - `survey_responses`: select own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org_id)` or `household_id = any((select app.my_household_ids()))`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ survey open/in window/in audience (the `stamp_response_scope` trigger overwrites the scope columns); update own ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult of the household through `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers`: select/insert/update through `exists` on the visible/own response with the same conditions; no delete.
   - `push_devices`, `notification_preferences`: one `for all` policy each, `using`/`with check` `user_id = auth.uid()` (preferences additionally `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` in `with check`).
   - `notifications`: select for any `announcements.*` holder; no write policies. `notification_deliveries`, `stripe_events`, `storage_deletions`: select super admin only. `billing_customers`, `billing_subscriptions`: select `org.settings` or super. `audit_log`: select `org.settings` or super; no writes (trigger-fed as definer). `account_deletion_requests`: select own.
   Every public table ends up with at least one select policy.
3. **Section (9) grants** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block verbatim: `revoke execute on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated; revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon, authenticated;` then the three `grant execute` statements: the `app.*` helper list to `authenticated` (add `app.can_read_object(text, text)` and `app.can_write_object(text, text)` because the storage policies call them as the querying role; add `app.person_in_group(uuid, uuid)` only if a policy references it directly), the 17 client RPCs to `authenticated` with DESIGN's exact signatures (`my_context`, `set_membership_permissions`, `set_membership_status`, `remove_membership`, `create_invitation`, `revoke_invitation`, `accept_invitation`, `save_household`, `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_household_privacy`, `save_leader_notes`, `set_congregation_status`, `create_share_link`, `revoke_share_link`, `submit_survey_response`, `request_account_deletion`), and the 7 `srv_*` RPCs to `service_role` only (`srv_resolve_share_link`, `srv_audience_user_ids`, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications`, `srv_claim_notifications`, `srv_attach_user`, `srv_process_account_deletions`, `srv_housekeeping`). If a 1.3b signature differs from DESIGN's, the grant must match the real function (grants on a non-existent signature fail the paste) and the difference goes to HANDOFF. `anon` receives nothing. Trigger functions, `app.require_*`, `app.rate_limit_*`, `app.person_in_kind` and every `srv_*` stay unreachable for `authenticated`.
4. **Section (10) storage** — start with the single constant: a `do $$ declare c_sermon_media_limit bigint := 52428800; -- 50 MiB: Supabase FREE plan cap (founder decision 10). To raise it on Pro: raise the project's global upload limit in the dashboard, then ship a new migration (supabase/migrations/9995_storage_limit.sql) that repeats ONLY this bucket upsert for sermon-media with 2147483648 (2 GiB) — never edit this file once it is in the HANDOFF ledger. Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (docs/ENV.md) in sync. begin … end $$;` block that executes the `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) values … on conflict (id) do update set public = excluded.public, file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types` statement from DESIGN §4.4 with these rows: `sermon-media` (`c_sermon_media_limit`, MIME `audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/wav, audio/x-m4a, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm`), `bulletins` (26214400; `application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png`), `documents` (52428800; the DESIGN allow-list: pdf, jpeg, png, text/plain, msword, docx, xls, xlsx), `directory-photos` (10485760; jpeg, png, webp), `org-assets` (5242880; jpeg, png, webp — no SVG). All `public = false`. Then the two policies: `drop policy if exists ca_storage_select on storage.objects; create policy ca_storage_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated using (app.can_read_object(bucket_id, name));` and `ca_storage_insert … for insert to authenticated with check (app.can_write_object(bucket_id, name));` — NO update/delete policies for `authenticated` (DESIGN §6: deletions only via `storage_deletions` + service role). If you prefer not to touch `local-up.sh`, the fallback is `psql "$(cat .local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL)" -c "drop database churchapp"` then `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` — but then every other machine (the founder's agents at 1.4b/1.4c/1.5) needs the same manual step, so prefer the script change. 7. **`supabase/tests/helpers.sql`** — re-runnable (`create schema if not exists app_test`, `create or replace function`), header "test helpers — apply before `tests/rls/*.sql`; local and hosted SQL editor; never part of a migration". `grant usage on schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` and `grant execute on all functions in schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` at the end. Two families:
   - Fixture builders, `security definer set search_path = ''` (they bypass RLS whatever role the test currently runs as — but NOT the 1.3a trigger guards, see the identity rule below): `app_test.make_user(email text) returns uuid` (insert into `auth.users`; the 1.3a trigger creates the profile), `app_test.make_org(slug text) returns uuid` (insert `organizations` with `name = slug`, `status = 'trial'`, `trial_ends_at = now() + interval '30 days'`; the trigger creates settings, 6 groups, 4 calendars), `app_test.make_member(org uuid, uid uuid, perms public.permission_key[] default '{}', status public.membership_status default 'active') returns uuid` (membership in the given status + permission rows; 1.4c needs `disabled` memberships and 1.5's seed `pending`/`disabled` ones without hand-editing `org_memberships`, which would fire the last-manager trigger (1.3a's name)), `app_test.make_fellowship(slug text, orgs uuid[]) returns uuid`, `app_test.make_household(org uuid, name text, created_via text default 'self') returns uuid`, `app_test.make_person(org uuid, hh uuid, first_name text, opts jsonb default '{}') returns uuid` (opts keys = `persons` column names, applied with `jsonb_populate_record`-style mapping), `app_test.set_setting(org uuid, col text, val text)` (dynamic `update organization_settings`), `app_test.sha256_token(token text) returns bytea` (the 1.3b convention `sha256(convert_to(token, 'UTF8'))`), `app_test.make_super(email text default 'super@example.test') returns uuid` (`make_user` + a `super_admins` row; returns the existing id when the email exists).

Bypassing RLS is not enough: 1.3a's guards (`guard_persons_columns`, `guard_household_privacy_columns`, `force_event_pending`, `stamp_response_scope`, `assert_same_org`, the last-manager trigger (1.3a's name)) fire regardless of role and read `auth.uid()`. Read those functions FIRST. If every guard treats `auth.uid() is null` as a trusted owner/service context, nothing more to do. Otherwise do not weaken the guards — make every builder save `current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true)`, `perform set_config('request.jwt.claims', <claims of a per-run super admin created lazily by app_test.make_super()>, true)` for the duration of the call, and restore the previous value on exit (also on exception). Either way, state the convention in the `helpers.sql` header comment and in HANDOFF, and prove it in 01_tenancy: `make_person(... congregation_status => 'member')` stores `member`, and an `events` row inserted with `status = 'approved'` by the harness stays `approved`.

Every failure raises `test_failed` with the label in `detail`; every pass emits `raise notice 'ok: <label>'`.
8. **`scripts/db/test.sh`** (extend the 1.2 stub): `cd "$REPO_ROOT"` first (test 08 uses a relative `\i`); apply `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`; run each `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f "$f" > "$log" 2>&1` (the `ok:` notices and error text go to stderr — without `2>&1` the failure excerpt is empty; `$log` lives under the session's scratchpad directory or `.local-pg/`, never `/tmp`), print `PASS <file>` / `FAIL <file>` (+ last 20 log lines on failure); optional `--only <name>`; summary `N passed, M failed`; exit 1 on any failure; keep the empty-directory branch. Every test file is plain SQL: it starts with `begin;` and ends with `rollback;` so nothing persists (test.sh supplies `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; never put a psql meta-command such as `\set` in a test — the files must paste unchanged into the hosted SQL editor, DESIGN §12). Acceptance tags: every assertion that realises a PLAN §12 DB sentence gets a label starting with `acceptance:` and a comment line `-- acceptance: <the PLAN §12 sentence>` above it (here: "org A member gets 0 rows from org B" and "no 42P17 on any table"); 1.4b/1.4c continue the convention and 1.5 lists the tags in docs/RLS.md.

## Constraints
- Migration rules (CLAUDE.md, PLAN §4, DESIGN §12): every policy `drop … if exists` then `create`; names start with `ca_`; no `force row level security`; functions untouched unless a signature must change (then drop dependents first in the same file); pgcrypto/citext schema-qualified; the file must apply twice in a row; never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; never `supabase start`.
- Policies are split per operation and use the InitPlan form (`perm_org_ids`, never per-row `app.has_perm`); never derive permissions from `auth.jwt()` claims.
- No policies for `service_role`; no grants to `anon`; no `security_invoker` on views; do not add tables, columns or RPCs (missing pieces → HANDOFF "Deviations from plan", fix in place only when a policy cannot be written otherwise).
- The `sermon-media` limit lives in exactly one place (the `c_sermon_media_limit` constant); do not repeat `2147483648` anywhere except in that comment.
- Tests: plain SQL that pastes unchanged into the hosted SQL editor (no psql meta-commands except the documented `\i` in 08), one rolled-back transaction per file, no `\connect`, no uuids in the seed range `00000000-0000-4000-8000-…` (step 1.5), no real email addresses (`<slug>@example.test`); every shell path quoted; nothing under `/tmp`.
- Do not write `02`–`07` here (steps 1.4b/1.4c), the seed, `gen-types.sh`, `docs/RLS.md` or `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (step 1.5). No npm dependencies. `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must stay green.

## Verify
- A plain `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` on the EXISTING local database (no drop) followed by `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = 'service_role'"` → `t`, and `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select has_table_privilege('authenticated','storage.objects','insert')"` → `t` (proves the shim is re-applied every run).
- `bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh` → both exit 0.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' and not rowsecurity"` → `0`; `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname in ('public','storage') and policyname not like 'ca\_%'` → `0`; `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'storage'` → `2`; `… where schemaname = 'public'` ≥ 90; `select count(*) from storage.buckets` → `5`; `select file_size_limit from storage.buckets where id = 'sermon-media'` → `52428800`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and has_function_privilege('authenticated', p.oid, 'execute')"` → `17`; the same for `service_role` restricted to `proname like 'srv\_%'` → `7`; for `anon` → `0`.
- `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` → `OK supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`. (Checkpoint commit here — see Build.)

3. **`04_sermons_share_links.sql`** — org S with `linker` (`sermons.link`), `uploader` (`sermons.upload`), `member` (none); one published upload sermon `sermon_up` (`storage_path = S/sermons/<id>/a.mp3`), one published youtube sermon `sermon_yt`, one draft. Sequence: `sermons_shareable` false → `create_share_link(sermon_up, 'l', 'password-12', null, null)` by `linker` → `sharing_disabled`; `set_setting(S, 'sermons_shareable', 'true')`; `member` → `permission_denied`; `linker` on the draft → `sermon_not_published`; `linker` with a 7-character password → `password_too_short`; with null password while `sermon_share_requires_password` → `password_required`; `uploader` creates a link with `'password-12'` → returns `{link_id, token}`; the token is 43 characters; `sermon_share_links` shows `requires_password = true`, `view_count = 0`; `member` selects 0 rows from `sermon_share_links`, `linker` 1 row; `private.share_link_secrets` is unreadable for `authenticated` (42501). Then `login_service()` with `h := app_test.sha256_token(token)`, `ip := 'iphash-1'`: `srv_resolve_share_link(h, null, ip) ->> 'status'` = `needs_password`; wrong password → `wrong_password` and `view_count` still 0. Rate limit (acceptance: "10 wrong passwords lock the token"): only calls that return `wrong_password` count as failures (a `needs_password` probe does not) — after 10 wrong passwords the next call (any password, even the correct one) → `rate_limited`; if 1.3b counts the probe as a failure, assert the lock one call earlier and record it in HANDOFF for step 3.4. A fresh token on another link with a different `ip` still works (limits are per token hash and per ip hash). Correct password on an unlocked token → `ok`, `view_count = 1`, `allow_download = false`, and the payload fields as 1.3b documented them in HANDOFF/`9999_init.sql` (at minimum the sermon's media kind and the org slug under whatever keys 1.3b chose — do not rename them); `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_allow_download', 'true')` → `allow_download = true` for the upload link and `false` for a link on `sermon_yt` (founder decision 5: uploaded media only); a link created with `max_views = 1` → second `ok`… → `max_views`; a link with `expires_at = now() - interval '1 minute'` → `expired`; `revoke_share_link` by `linker` → `revoked` (and `member` → `permission_denied`); `set_setting(S, 'sermons_shareable', 'false')` → `sharing_disabled` for a valid link (acceptance: "share link fails after org disables sharing"); re-enable and `update sermons set publish_at = null` → `unpublished`; `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_requires_password', 'false')`, create a passwordless link, then set it back to true → `needs_password_reset`; unknown hash → `invalid`; `login(member)` then `srv_resolve_share_link(...)` → 42501; `login_anon()` → 42501. Assert an `audit_log` row exists for the share-link insert and for the revoke.

   - Surveys: `creator` inserts a `draft` survey (`audience_group_id = everyone`, `per_person`) with two questions; `member` sees 0 surveys while draft; `creator` sets `status = 'open'` → `member` sees it and its questions; `editor` changing `response_mode` after open → `survey_shape_frozen` (P0001), inserting a question → `survey_shape_frozen`; `member` `submit_survey_response(survey, '{"<q1>": "a", "<q2>": 3}')` → uuid, `survey_responses` has `person_id = member's person`, `scope_key = 'p:<person>'`, `submitted_by_user_id`; unknown question key → `invalid_payload`; `outsider` → `survey_not_in_audience` (or 42501 — assert what is raised, note it); with `allow_edit = false` a second submit → `survey_already_responded` or `survey_edit_not_allowed` — assert the key 1.3b's catalogue assigns to this case and record it in HANDOFF for 1.6's `errors.ts`; with `allow_edit = true` a second submit updates in place (still 1 response row, answers replaced); `member2` without a linked person → `no_person_linked`; a `per_household` survey: head submits, spouse of the same household submits → `survey_already_responded` (acceptance: "per-household survey double-response rejected"); `closes_at` in the past → `survey_not_open`; `status = 'closed'` → `survey_not_open`; responses visible to their owner and to `creator`, not to `member2`; a survey with `audience_group_id = men` is invisible to `member_f`; opening a survey with `push = true` enqueues a `notifications` row (`kind = 'survey'`).
4. **`07_storage_billing_audit.sql`** — (a) Storage helpers called directly as roles: org O with `uploader` (`sermons.upload`), `bull` (`bulletins.upload`), `doc` (`documents.upload`), `settings` (`org.settings`), `member` (linked adult female), `head` (household adult of H), `deleter` (`sermons.delete`), `super`. Draft sermon with `storage_path = O/sermons/<id>/x.mp3`: `app.can_write_object('sermon-media', <that path>)` true for `uploader`, false for `member`, false for `uploader` on `O/sermons/<id>/other.mp3` (must equal exactly), false for a path with a malformed uuid, false for a path under another org; `can_read_object` on the draft: `uploader` true, `member` false; after `publish_at = now()`: `member` true, `login_anon()` → 42501 on the function call (no grant). `bulletins`, `documents` (published + `audience_group_id` = `men` → `member` (female) reads false), `directory-photos` (`O/households/<H>/p.jpg`: `head` write true when `households.photo_path` equals it, `member` write false, read true for a congregation member, false when the household is hidden from the congregation; `O/persons/<child>/p.jpg` write by `head` true), `org-assets` (`O/logo/<uuid>.png`: write requires `org.settings` and `organization_settings.logo_path` = path; read true for a member and for a fellowship-visible viewer). (b) Storage policies through the table (the shim grants the table privileges; the policies filter): `login(uploader)` → `insert into storage.objects (bucket_id, name) values ('sermon-media', <exact path>)` → ok; a different name → 42501; `update storage.objects set name = …` and `delete from storage.objects` as `uploader` → 0 rows affected, row still there (no policies); `login_service()` deletes it. Deleting the sermon row as `deleter` → one `storage_deletions` row (`bucket_id = 'sermon-media'`, `object_name = path`, `is_prefix = false`); readable by `super` only (`assert_count` 0 for `settings`, 1 for `super`). (c) Billing (founder decision 7): `make_org(P)` starts `trial`; `login_service()` insert `billing_customers` + `billing_subscriptions (status = 'active')` with `billing_mode = 'manual'` → `organizations.status` unchanged; set `billing_mode = 'stripe'` and update the subscription to `active` → `status = 'active'`; `past_due` → `past_due`, and a `sermons.upload` holder can STILL insert a sermon and call `create_share_link` (past_due = banner only); `canceled` → `suspended`; now (acceptance: "suspended org rejects mutating RPCs") every mutating client RPC raises `organization_suspended` (42501): `set_membership_permissions`, `set_membership_status`, `remove_membership`, `create_invitation`, `revoke_invitation`, `accept_invitation(<token of a pending invitation created in P before the suspension>)`, `save_household`, `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_household_privacy`, `save_leader_notes`, `set_congregation_status`, `create_share_link`, `revoke_share_link`, `submit_survey_response` (plausible arguments; if 1.3b validates arguments before `require_writable`, assert what it raises and note it); `request_account_deletion()` is user-scoped, not org-scoped — it must still succeed for a member of the suspended org (assert a row in `account_deletion_requests`, Play Store requirement); direct `insert into sermons` → 42501, `update organization_settings` → 0 rows; reads still work (`my_context()` returns the org with `status = 'suspended'`, `select` on sermons returns rows); `billing_customers`/`billing_subscriptions` readable by `settings` and `super`, 0 rows for `member`; `stripe_events` 0 rows for everyone but `super`. (e) Server RPCs (DESIGN §4.4 semantics; all as `login_service()`, and each → 42501 as `login(member)`): `srv_attach_user(<new uid>, O, null, 'New Person', '{sermons.upload}')` → active membership, a one-person household (`created_via = 'admin'`, hence `hide_from_fellowship = true`), person linked with `household_role = 'head'`, 1 permission row; calling it again for the same user → idempotent or the 1.3b key (assert what is implemented, note it for 3.2's `createUserDirect`); with a `person_id` of an existing unlinked adult → that person is linked, no new household. `srv_housekeeping()`: an org with `trial_ends_at = now() - interval '1 day'`, `billing_mode = 'manual'` → `status = 'past_due'`; an invitation past `expires_at` → `accept_invitation` → `invitation_invalid`; an upload-kind draft sermon with `created_at = now() - interval '8 days'` and no `storage.objects` row → deleted, while a fresh draft and a draft whose object exists survive; an org set to `cancelled` with the status timestamp 31 days ago (use whatever column 1.3b reads) → the org row is gone and `storage_deletions` has one `is_prefix = true` row per bucket for the `<org_id>/` prefix; `private.rate_limits` rows older than the window are pruned. `request_account_deletion()` as `member` → a row in `account_deletion_requests`; make that member the only `users.edit_permissions` holder of O first; `srv_process_account_deletions()` → the `auth.users` row is gone, `processed_at` set, memberships gone, and an `audit_log` row with `action = 'org_without_manager'` for O exists (the last-manager guard is skipped under `app.cascade = 'on'`).

## Build
1. **`supabase/seed/dev_seed.sql`** — header: "LOCAL / development only. Never paste into the production project. Idempotent: exits when the seed marker exists." Structure: a single `do $$ … $$` block (plpgsql, so it can use variables and `return` early) that (a) returns immediately when `exists (select 1 from public.organizations where slug = 'seed-grace')`; (b) inserts auth users with FIXED uuids in the reserved range `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` … (the RLS tests avoid this range on purpose) into `auth.users (id, email, raw_user_meta_data)` — this works locally against the shim's `auth.users`; on a hosted project users are created through Auth, which is why the seed is local-only; (b2) inserts the `super_admins` row for `seed-super` BEFORE anything else is guarded (`app.is_super_admin()` reads that table); (c) sets the JWT claims to `seed-super` (`perform set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', <super uid>, 'role', 'authenticated')::text, true)`) and asserts `app.is_super_admin()` is true (`raise exception` otherwise) so that every trigger guard (`guard_persons_columns`, privacy guard, `force_event_pending`, `stamp_response_scope`, the last-manager trigger (1.3a's name)) sees a super admin while the block runs (the seed runs as `churchapp_owner`, which bypasses RLS but not triggers). If `helpers.sql` documents that 1.3a's guards trust a null `auth.uid()`, the claims are still set (harmless); if a guard does not honour super admins for some column, run that part of the seed under the per-org `admin` user's claims instead, switching per org, and record it. (d) creates the data below with explicit `id`s where later rows reference them; (e) ends with `raise notice 'seed applied'`.    - Fellowship `seed-fellowship` = {`seed-grace`, `seed-hope`}; `seed-peace` outside it. ## Constraints
- The seed is local-only and must never be applied by `local-up.sh` or CI automatically; it must apply cleanly on a database that has had `9999_init.sql` applied twice and the RLS tests run (tests roll back, so the DB is empty). It must not bypass triggers (no `alter table … disable trigger`) — if a guard rejects seed data, the seed data is wrong or the guard is, and either fix goes to HANDOFF.
- No real email addresses, no real push tokens, no real YouTube/Dropbox content beyond syntactically valid example URLs; the seed share-link password is a local convenience, labelled as such.
- `gen-types.sh` must not require Docker (postgres-meta run directly under Node), must not modify anything but `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`, must leave no server process behind, and must produce byte-identical output on a second run (CI drift check). Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`/`start`.
- Do not write `packages/db/src/{client,rpc,keys}.ts`, queries, `packages/domain/src/*` or any web code (steps 1.6/1.7). Do not edit `9999_init.sql` unless the seed exposes a genuine bug (record it). The only dependency this step may add is the exact-pinned root devDependency `@supabase/postgres-meta` (Build item 3).
- Docs must describe the repo as it is: every policy, RPC, error key and script name copied from the files, not from memory.

## Verify
- Standing sequence `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → exit 0, `9 passed`.
- `pnpm db:seed` → `seed applied` notice with the share token, the invitation token and the notification count; running it again → returns early without error; `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from public.organizations where slug like 'seed-%'"` → `3`; `select count(*) from public.persons` ≥ 30; `select count(*) from public.households h where not exists (select 1 from public.persons p where p.household_id = h.id and p.household_role = 'head')` → `0`; `select count(*) from public.notifications` ≥ 3; `select hide_from_fellowship from public.households where created_via = 'admin'` → all `t`.
- Seed visibility spot-check inside `begin … rollback` using `app_test.login(<grace-member uid>)`: `select count(*) from public.directory_households` > 0 and excludes the `hide_from_congregation` household; as `<hope-member>` `select count(*) from public.directory_persons where org_id = <seed-grace>` > 0 and contains no minors except the `show_children_in_fellowship` family.
- `pnpm db:seed` against a non-local `DATABASE_URL` (e.g. `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://x@db.example.test/x pnpm db:seed`) → refuses with a clear message and exit 1.
- `pnpm db:types` → writes `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` with no Docker daemon running (`docker ps` fails or Docker is absent); `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh` a second time leaves `git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts` clean; `pgrep -f postgres-meta` → nothing left running; `grep -c "sermon_share_allow_download" packages/db/src/database.types.ts` ≥ 1; the Build item 3 `node -e` check prints the 12 `permission_key` members in PLAN §4 order.

Deviations from the skeleton bullet: the generated `database.types.ts` is produced and committed here (the skeleton lists it under 1.7 as well) so the CI drift check activates and 1.7 starts from a real file — G4 (1.7) should regenerate rather than create it. The seed inserts the `super_admins` row before setting the claims to the seed super admin and asserts `app.is_super_admin()`, so every trigger guard passes; if a guard ignores super admins the seed runs that part under the org admin's claims. The share link and invitation are created through `create_share_link` / `create_invitation` (not by hand) so the token/hash convention stays single-sourced; the printed tokens and password are local conveniences. - Follow the standing orders: no model names or secrets in files; never run `supabase db push`/`db reset`; commit only after `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` is green.

## Constraints
- `database.types.ts` is generated output: never hand-edit; regenerate after any migration change; keep it prettier-ignored and committed.
- No elevated keys anywhere in this package; `srv*` wrappers and service-only queries accept `ServiceDbClient` only; the brand is the only cast.
- Directory data only via `directory_households`, `directory_persons`, `org_directory_info`; `grep -rn "from('persons')\|from('households')" packages/db/src` must return nothing.
- Only embed through relationships that exist as FKs in `9999_init.sql`; otherwise use two queries (PostgREST answers "could not find a relationship" at runtime, which no local test catches).
- RPC argument keys = SQL parameter names (from the generated `Args` types); RPC names = `RPC_NAMES`; return shapes parsed with `@church/domain` schemas — do not define duplicate schemas in `@church/db`.
- No `expo-*`, `react-native-*`, `react` or `@tanstack/react-query` imports (keys are plain tuples); no new dependencies beyond what 1.1 declared.
- Do not create `packages/supabase-client` content (step 1.7b), `apps/web` or `apps/mobile` (steps 2.1 / 4.1); do not modify `9999_init.sql` (record anything you needed under "Deviations from plan" for a `9998_*` follow-up); never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- Typecheck must pass with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; no `any` outside the fake clients in tests.

1. `package.json`: `"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts", "./web": "./src/web.ts", "./mobile": "./src/mobile.ts"}`, `"sideEffects": false`; dependencies `@church/db: workspace:*`, `@church/domain: workspace:*`, `@supabase/supabase-js: catalog:`, `@supabase/ssr` `0.12.5` (PLAN §3; exact), `aes-js` `3.1.2` (DESIGN §3; exact — pure JS, no native code, so it may be pinned here) with `@types/aes-js` (matching 3.x) in devDependencies; add `vitest` (catalog/4.1 like the other packages) and a `test: vitest run` script + `vitest.config.ts`. Web imports `@church/supabase-client/web`, mobile imports `@church/supabase-client/mobile`; nothing in `./mobile` imports `@supabase/ssr` and nothing in `./web` imports `aes-js` (Metro and Next only bundle what is imported).
2. `src/index.ts`: shared types and two resolvers that never read `process.env` (apps pass values in): `resolvePublicSupabaseEnv({ url, publishableKey, anonKey }, labels)` → `{ url, key }` accepting both the new `sb_publishable_…` and legacy anon keys (`publishableKey ?? anonKey`), throwing a clear error naming the missing env var (the caller passes the label pair: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` on web, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` on mobile); and its server twin `resolveServiceSupabaseEnv({ url, secretKey, serviceRoleKey })` → `{ url, key }` = `secretKey ?? serviceRoleKey` (DESIGN §8: "`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` (or legacy `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`; code reads `??`)"), naming `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` in its error — step 2.1's `service.ts` calls it and then `brandServiceClient`. Unit tests for both (new key wins, legacy fallback, missing → error text contains the var name). Re-export the adapter interfaces from `large-secure-store.ts`.
3. `src/web.ts`: `createWebBrowserClient({ url, key }): DbClient` = `createBrowserClient<Database>(url, key)` from `@supabase/ssr`, plus `getWebBrowserClient({ url, key })` returning a module-level singleton (create once per browser tab; a second call with different args throws in development). Server-side factories (`createServerClient` with Next 16's async `cookies()`, and the service client) belong to `apps/web/src/lib/supabase/{server,service}.ts` in step 2.1 — say so in a header comment; do not add them here.
4. `src/large-secure-store.ts`: implements the Supabase-documented LargeSecureStore pattern with injected adapters so no Expo import exists in this package: `interface SecureStoreAdapter { getItemAsync(key): Promise<string | null>; setItemAsync(key, value): Promise<void>; deleteItemAsync(key): Promise<void> }` (the `expo-secure-store` surface), `interface KvStoreAdapter { getItem(key): Promise<string | null>; setItem(key, value): Promise<void>; removeItem(key): Promise<void> }` (AsyncStorage-compatible — `expo-sqlite/kv-store` in the app), `type RandomBytes = (n: number) => Uint8Array | Promise<Uint8Array>` (`expo-crypto`'s `getRandomBytesAsync`). `createLargeSecureStore({ secureStore, kvStore, randomBytes })` returns `{ getItem, setItem, removeItem }` for supabase-js: `setItem(key, value)` generates a 32-byte key, encrypts the UTF-8 value with `aes-js` `ModeOfOperation.ctr(key, new Counter(1))`, stores the hex ciphertext in `kvStore` under `key` and the hex AES key in `secureStore` under `key` (64 hex chars — well under SecureStore's 2048-byte limit; the session JSON itself would exceed it, which is the whole point); `getItem` returns `null` when either half is missing; `removeItem` deletes both. Use `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` if present, else `aes-js`'s `utils.utf8`. Tests (`src/large-secure-store.test.ts`) with in-memory fakes and a deterministic `randomBytes`: round trip, `getItem` on unknown key → `null`, `removeItem` clears both stores, two keys do not share ciphertext, corrupted ciphertext throws a `DomainError('unknown')`-wrapped error rather than returning garbage, a value longer than 2048 bytes round-trips (the secure half stays 64 chars).
5. `src/mobile.ts`: `createMobileClient({ url, key, secureStore, kvStore, randomBytes }): DbClient` = `createClient<Database>(url, key, { auth: { storage: createLargeSecureStore(...), lock: processLock, autoRefreshToken: true, persistSession: true, detectSessionInUrl: false } })` (`processLock` is exported by `@supabase/supabase-js`); `bindAutoRefreshToAppState(client, appState: { addEventListener(type: 'change', cb: (state: string) => void): { remove(): void } })` calling `client.auth.startAutoRefresh()` on `active` and `stopAutoRefresh()` otherwise, returning the unsubscribe — the app passes React Native's `AppState`. Header comment: `import 'react-native-url-polyfill/auto'` must be the FIRST import of the app entry (step 4.1), the adapters come from `expo-secure-store`, `expo-sqlite/kv-store` and `expo-crypto` installed with `npx expo install` in `apps/mobile`. Test `src/mobile.test.ts` with a fake `AppState`: `active` → `startAutoRefresh` called once, `background` → `stopAutoRefresh`, unsubscribe removes the listener; and `createMobileClient` passes exactly the documented `auth` options (spy on `createClient` via `vi.mock('@supabase/supabase-js')`).
6. `packages/supabase-client/README.md`: the two subpath exports and why, the env resolvers (new vs legacy keys), the mobile adapter wiring snippet for step 4.1 (`createMobileClient({ url, key, secureStore: SecureStore, kvStore: Storage, randomBytes: Crypto.getRandomBytesAsync })` after `import 'react-native-url-polyfill/auto'`), the web wiring for step 2.1 (`getWebBrowserClient` in `client.ts`; `resolveServiceSupabaseEnv` + `brandServiceClient` in `service.ts`), and the rule that the service client never leaves the server.

## Constraints
- No elevated keys anywhere in this package; it builds user clients only. `resolveServiceSupabaseEnv` only resolves strings for `apps/web` server code.
- No `expo-*`, `react-native-*`, `react` or `@tanstack/react-query` imports; adapters are injected. `aes-js` 3.1.2 and `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.5 are the only additions (exact pins; never bump a major); supabase-js stays on the catalog 2.112.4.
- Nothing in `src/mobile.ts` / `src/large-secure-store.ts` imports `@supabase/ssr`; nothing in `src/web.ts` imports `aes-js`.
- Never read `process.env` in `src/`; apps pass values in. Do not create `apps/web` or `apps/mobile` (steps 2.1 / 4.1); do not touch `packages/db` beyond importing from it; never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- Typecheck must pass with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; no `any` outside test fakes.

## Verify

- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → every task succeeds (now 3 test tasks across the shared packages); `pnpm format:check` clean.
- `grep -rn "^import.*\(expo-\|react-native\|@tanstack\|from 'react'\)\|process\.env" packages/supabase-client/src` → no output (header comments mentioning `react-native-url-polyfill/auto` and `expo-secure-store` are allowed because this pattern matches only import lines and env reads); `grep -n "@supabase/ssr" packages/supabase-client/src/mobile.ts packages/supabase-client/src/large-secure-store.ts` → no output; `grep -n "aes-js" packages/supabase-client/src/web.ts` → no output.
- `node -e "import('@supabase/ssr').then(m=>console.log(typeof m.createBrowserClient))"` run from `packages/supabase-client` → `function`; `node -e "console.log(require('aes-js').ModeOfOperation.ctr ? 'ok' : 'missing')"` → `ok`.
- `node -e "const p=require('./packages/supabase-client/package.json'); console.log(p.dependencies['aes-js'], p.dependencies['@supabase/ssr'])"` → `3.1.2 0.12.5`.

Never match strings in the app: all table/RPC access goes through the `@church/db` wrappers, which already return `DomainError`s (`toDomainError` maps message keys first, then SQLSTATE `42501` → `permission_denied`, `23505` → `duplicate`, `23514`/`22023` → `invalid_payload`). Log the raw error server-side only.
4. **`apps/web/proxy.ts`** (Next 16 middleware file name): create a `createServerClient` with request/response cookie plumbing, call `supabase.auth.getClaims()` (fall back to `getUser()` if the SDK version lacks it) to refresh the session cookie, and redirect unauthenticated requests on protected paths to `/login?next=<encoded original path+query>`. Export `config.matcher` that EXCLUDES `/api/stripe/webhook`, `/api/cron/tick`, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, `_next/static`, `_next/image`, `favicon.ico` and files with image/font extensions (PLAN §7, DESIGN §9). Put the predicates in `src/lib/auth/paths.ts`: `isProtectedPath(p) = p === '/admin' || p.startsWith('/admin/') || p === '/o' || p.startsWith('/o/')` (so `/other` and `/organ` are NOT protected) and `isExcludedFromProxy(pathname)`, both unit-tested.
5. **`next.config.ts`**: `transpilePackages: ['@church/domain', '@church/db', '@church/supabase-client']` (packages are TS source), `outputFileTracingRoot` = the monorepo root computed as in Build 1 (orchestrator decision 1), `experimental.authInterrupts: true` (for `forbidden()`/`unauthorized()`; if 16.3 rejects the flag, drop it, use `notFound()` in the guards and record the fallback in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" — step 3.1 reads that record), `images.remotePatterns` for the Supabase host, and TWO `headers()` entries built from `src/lib/security/csp.ts`, which exports `buildCsp({ supabaseHost, frameAncestors }: { supabaseHost: string; frameAncestors: "'none'" | '*' })` and `securityHeaders({ frameable })`: (a) `source: '/((?!s/|embed/).*)'` → `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and the CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'`; (b) `source: '/(s|embed)/:path*'` → the same CSP built with `frameAncestors: '*'`, NO `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (DESIGN §8/§9: `/s/*` and `/embed/*` must stay frame-able and unindexed; step 3.4 builds those routes and keeps these headers). The CSP body: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (Next inline runtime; a nonce-based CSP is a later hardening item — note it in HANDOFF); `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://<supabase host>; media-src 'self' blob: https://<supabase host>; connect-src 'self' https://<supabase host> wss://<supabase host>; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://drive.google.com; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors <variant>`. A second entry cannot remove a directive set by the first and browsers let `frame-ancestors` override `X-Frame-Options`, which is why the two sources are disjoint.

8. **Guards** (`src/lib/auth/`, server-only, all using the user-scoped server client and `myContext(db)` from `@church/db`; cache per request with `React.cache`). These names and shapes are a contract with G7's steps 3.1/3.2 (drafted against them) — keep them exactly:

## Constraints
- Versions: Next 16.3.4, React 19.2.3 exact (catalog), `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.5, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, Tailwind 4.3, shadcn CLI 4.19.1, TypeScript ~5.9 (never 7), ESLint 9 (never 10), Vitest 4.1. Never bump a major. Do not add `expo-*` or `react-native-*` anything. No `.npmrc`.
- Next 16 specifics: the middleware file is `proxy.ts`, `cookies()`/`headers()`/`params`/`searchParams` are async, Server Components cannot set cookies (hence the try/catch in `setAll`). Do not create a `middleware.ts`.
- Reuse, never re-implement, the shared packages: env fallbacks come from `resolvePublicSupabaseEnv`/`resolveServiceSupabaseEnv`, the upload cap from `readMaxUploadMb`, error mapping from `toDomainError`/`DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`, the scheme from `APP_SCHEME`, the context schema from `myContextSchema`, cache constants from `@church/db/keys`. If a name is missing, add it in the owning package and record it.
- The browser and Server Components use the publishable key only; `service.ts` is created but imported by nothing in this step (standing order: web never holds elevated keys in the client; privileged work runs only in Route Handlers / Server Actions against `srv_*` RPCs). Never expose `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` under a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name.
- Do not build `/login`, `/signup`, `/auth/*`, `/invite/*`, `/admin/*`, `/o/*`, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, `/api/*` or any Stripe/push/share code (2.1b and later). Do not touch `supabase/`, `packages/*` except the additive exports named above, or `apps/web/vercel.json`.
- Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`. No secrets or real email addresses in any file; `.env.local` stays untracked (already gitignored as `.env*`).
- No model identifiers in commits or files.

Behind the guards of step 2.1a a signed-in super admin sees the `/admin` shell (sidebar Churches / Fellowships / Super admins; its pages arrive in 2.2a/2.2b) and any signed-in user sees the `/o` landing that lists their active churches (step 3.1 replaces it). `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` are green; the README documents the Supabase Auth URL configuration the founder needs in steps 2.4/2.5.

## Build
1. **`(auth)` group scaffolding**: `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` (centred card with `APP_NAME`), client forms with RHF + `zodResolver` using the schemas from `@church/domain` `schemas/auth.ts` — do NOT create `src/features/auth/schemas.ts`; Server Actions in `src/features/auth/actions.ts` (`'use server'`, return `ActionResult`, user client only). Read `?error=` codes in `/login` and render messages for `auth` ("Sign-in link invalid — request a new one"), `expired` ("That link has expired — request a new one"), `email_mismatch` ("This invitation was sent to a different email address — sign in with that address").
2. **`/login`** (`app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, `src/features/auth/LoginForm.tsx`): tabs **Password** (`signInWithPassword`) and **Email code** (`signInWithOtp({email, options: {shouldCreateUser: false, emailRedirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=…}})` then a 6-digit code field calling `verifyOtp({email, token, type: 'email'})`). Until the founder adds `{{ .Token }}` to the Magic Link template (step 2.4) the email carries a link instead of a code — the callback route handles that link, so both paths land the user; say so in a help line under the code field. On success go to `safeNext(searchParams.next) ?? landingFor(ctx)` (`searchParams` is a Promise in Next 16). Links to `/signup` and `/auth/reset`. Show the `?error=` messages from Build 1.
3. **`/signup`**: email + password (`emailPasswordSchema`, min 8) + display name (1–80) → `signUp({email, password, options: {data: {display_name}, emailRedirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=<next|/>}})`; show "check your email" when no session is returned, otherwise redirect. The bootstrap path in DESIGN §5 ("sign up at `/login` → run the `super_admins` INSERT") is served by the `/login` → "Create an account" link.
4. **`app/(auth)/auth/callback/route.ts`** (`dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`): reads `code` (PKCE → `exchangeCodeForSession`) or `token_hash` + `type` (→ `verifyOtp`), then redirects to `safeNext(next) ?? landingFor(...)`. Supabase sends expired or already-used links back here with `error`, `error_code` (`otp_expired`, `access_denied`, …) and `error_description` instead of the success parameters: put `callbackErrorToKey(searchParams): 'expired' | 'auth' | null` in `src/features/auth/callback-error.ts` (`otp_expired` → `expired`; any other `error` → `auth`; no error → `null`) and redirect to `/login?error=<key>`; the same `/login?error=auth` is used when the exchange itself fails.
5. **`/auth/reset`**: two states — request (`resetPasswordForEmail(email, {redirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=/auth/reset})`) and, when a session exists, set a new password (`updateUser({password})`, `passwordResetSchema`) then redirect to the landing.
6. **`/invite/[token]`** (`app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`; `params` is a Promise — `await` it; validate the token with `invitationTokenSchema` and render the generic page even when it is malformed — never 500): explains "You have been invited to a church on Anacast. Sign in or create an account with the email address the invitation was sent to." Signed out → buttons "Sign in" (`/login?next=/invite/<token>`) and "Create an account" (`/signup?next=/invite/<token>`). Signed in → a form whose Server Action `acceptInvitation(token)` in `src/features/auth/actions.ts` calls the `@church/db` wrapper `acceptInvitation(db, { token })` with the USER client (never on GET — mail scanners prefetch links), maps `invitation_invalid` / `invitation_expired` / `invitation_email_mismatch` / `organization_suspended` / `minor_cannot_have_account` via `toActionError` (on `invitation_email_mismatch` also offer "Sign out and sign in with the invited address"), and on success calls `setLastOrg(db, userId, org_id)` and redirects to `/o` (the placeholder below; 3.1 upgrades it to `/o/<slug>/dashboard`). Always render an **"Open in app"** button whose `href` is `inviteDeepLink(token)` from `@church/domain` `urls.ts` — do not hard-code the scheme (DESIGN §5 writes `churchapp://`; the scheme is `anacast` per orchestrator decision 5; note the deviation in HANDOFF). The invitation's church name cannot be shown before acceptance (select policy `users.create`); keep the copy generic.
7. **`signOut`** Server Action (`supabase.auth.signOut()` → redirect `/login`) used by both shells.
8. **`(super)` shell**: `app/(super)/admin/layout.tsx` calls `requireSuperAdmin()` and renders `src/features/admin/AdminShell.tsx` (sidebar: Churches `/admin`, Fellowships `/admin/fellowships`, Super admins `/admin/super-admins`; top bar with the signed-in email from `profile` and a Sign out menu). `app/(super)/admin/page.tsx` is a placeholder card "Churches — built in step 2.2a" so the guarded shell can be seen now. Nothing else under `/admin`.
9. **`(org)` placeholder**: `app/(org)/o/page.tsx` — `requireUser()`, then list the user's churches from `orgs` with `membership_status = 'active'` (name, status badge, link to `/o/<slug>/dashboard` — which 404s until step 3.1; label the section "Church admin area arrives in step 3.1") and a "You are not a member of any church yet — ask your church administrator for an invitation" empty state; super admins see a link to `/admin` and, when they hold no membership, the note "Super admins are not church members: use `/admin`, or accept an invitation to a church to open its admin area" (DESIGN §5; proposed step 3.11 lifts this). Step 3.1 replaces this page.
10. **Tests** (reuse the 2.1a harness): `src/features/auth/callback-error.test.ts` (`otp_expired` → `expired`, `access_denied` → `auth`, no params → `null`), `src/features/auth/actions.test.ts` with a mocked user client — `acceptInvitation` never runs on GET (it is a Server Action; assert the page module exports no `GET`), maps `{ code: 'P0001', message: 'invitation_expired' }` to the catalogue message, calls `setLastOrg` on success; `src/features/auth/schemas.test.ts` — a thin import test proving the forms use `@church/domain` (`otpVerifySchema` rejects a 5-digit code, `emailPasswordSchema` rejects a 7-character password); `src/features/auth/invite-link.test.ts` asserting the rendered invite page (`@testing-library/react`, server component rendered via its async function or a small pure `inviteLinks(token)` helper) contains `inviteDeepLink('abc')` and the `/login?next=/invite/abc` link.
11. **README**: add an "Auth configuration" section to `apps/web/README.md`: Supabase Auth → URL Configuration → Site URL = `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`; Redirect URLs `http://localhost:3000/**` and `https://<VERCEL_URL>/**` (the app uses `<APP_URL>/auth/callback` for OTP links, signup confirmation, password reset and invitations); the Magic Link template must contain `{{ .Token }}` for the 6-digit code tab; without it the emailed link still works through the callback.

## Constraints
- Versions unchanged from 2.1a: Next 16.3.4, React 19.2.3 exact, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.5, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (never 7), ESLint 9 (never 10). No new runtime dependency (shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` are fine).
- Reuse the shared packages: auth form schemas from `@church/domain` `schemas/auth.ts`, the invitation token schema and `inviteDeepLink` from `@church/domain`, `acceptInvitation`/`setLastOrg` from `@church/db`; never hand-roll `anacast://` strings or duplicate a schema in the app.
- Every auth operation uses the user-scoped client; `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` is still imported by nothing after this step. Invitation acceptance is a Server Action (POST) — never a GET side effect.
- Do not build `/admin/*` pages beyond the placeholder, `/o/[orgSlug]/*`, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, `/api/*` or any Stripe/push/share code. Do not touch `supabase/`, `packages/*` except the additive exports named above, or `apps/web/vercel.json`. Do not change the 2.1a guards except to fix a bug you can prove with a test.
- Next 16: `params`/`searchParams` are Promises; Server Actions live in `'use server'` files; `revalidatePath` after writes. Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`. No secrets or real email addresses in any file (tests use `example.test` addresses). No model identifiers in commits or files.

Policies (1.4a): `ca_organizations_insert_super` / `ca_organizations_update_super` = `app.is_super_admin()` only (no `org_writable` clause); `ca_organization_settings_update_org_settings` = `org.settings` ∧ `app.org_writable(org_id)` — a super admin passes the permission part because `app.perm_org_ids()` returns every org for super admins, but for a `suspended`/`cancelled` church the update matches ZERO rows and PostgREST reports success with no error; `fellowships`/`fellowship_memberships` insert/update/delete super, select member of a linked org; `billing_subscriptions` select `org.settings` or super; `audit_log` trigger-fed (write no audit code). No delete policy on `organizations` (status `cancelled` + purge by `srv_housekeeping`). `persons`/`households` carry column-level `select` grants (`birthdate`/`anniversary` revoked) — PLAN §5: all directory reads, including counts, go through the `directory_persons` / `directory_households` views, never the base tables.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b) — use these exports, never add parallel schemas: `createOrganizationSchema` (`slug` via `slugSchema` `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` 3–48, `name` 2–120, `contact_email` optional, `billing_mode` default `manual`, `trial_ends_at` optional), `updateOrganizationSchema` (partial + `status`), `fellowshipSchema` (`slug`, `name`, `description`), `orgBillingFormSchema`, `organizationSettingsSchema` (every column except `org_id`/timestamps incl. `logo_path`, with the `youth_range`/`adult_range`/`fellowship_implies_congregation` refinements carrying the constraint name in their `path`/message), `updateSettingsSchema` + `validateSettingsUpdate(current, patch)`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `slugSchema`, `timezoneSchema`, `dates.ts` (`isValidTimeZone`, `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`, `todayInZone`), `errors.ts` (`DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`, keys `duplicate`, `invalid_payload`, `invalid_timezone`, `organization_suspended`, `permission_denied`), `PERMISSION_KEYS`. If an exported name differs, adopt the exported one and record it in HANDOFF.
- `@church/db` (1.7a) — the query modules are `packages/db/src/queries/organizations.ts` (NOT `orgs.ts` — 1.7a recorded the deviation from DESIGN §11) with `listOrganizations(db)` (joins `organization_settings` and the latest `billing_subscriptions` row), `getOrganization(db, id)`, `getOrganizationBySlug`, `insertOrganization(db, { slug, name, contact_email, billing_mode, trial_ends_at })`, `updateOrganization`, `listFellowships`, `getFellowship`, `insertFellowship`, `updateFellowship`, `listFellowshipMemberships(fellowshipId)`, `addOrgToFellowship`, `removeOrgFromFellowship`; `packages/db/src/queries/settings.ts` with `getSettings(db, orgId)`, `updateSettings(db, orgId, patch)` (whitelisted by `updateSettingsSchema`); `queries/directory.ts` (views only); `errors.ts` (`unwrap`, `unwrapMaybe`); `keys.ts` (`queryKeys.orgs.*`, `queryKeys.fellowships.all()`, `queryKeys.settings(orgId)`). Read the files for the exact signatures; add only what is missing (listed in Build 8) and record every added export in HANDOFF.
- No hosted Supabase project yet (2.4): verify with build, unit tests and, optionally, the local Postgres for SQL-level checks.

## Build
1. **Churches list** — replace the placeholder `app/(super)/admin/page.tsx`: server component, `requireSuperAdmin()`, loads `listOrganizations(db)` from `@church/db` `queries/organizations.ts` (already joins settings + latest `billing_subscriptions`), renders `src/features/orgs/ChurchTable.tsx`: columns Name (link to `/admin/churches/[orgId]`), Slug, Status badge (`trial` grey, `active` green, `past_due` amber, `suspended` red, `cancelled` muted), Billing mode (`manual` / `stripe` / `free`), Subscription badge (from `billing_subscriptions.status`, "—" when none), Trial ends (`trial_ends_at` formatted in the org timezone with date-fns + `@date-fns/tz`, using `settings.timezone`; "—" when null; red when in the past and status still `trial`), Created. Client-side search box (name/slug) and a status filter using `searchParams` (async in Next 16). Empty state: "No churches yet" + primary button "Create the first church". Header button "New church" → `/admin/churches/new`.
2. **Create church** `app/(super)/admin/churches/new/page.tsx` + `src/features/orgs/ChurchForm.tsx` (client, RHF + `zodResolver`): fields Name (validated by `createOrganizationSchema`: 2–120 chars), Slug (auto-derived from the name with `slugify` in `src/features/orgs/slug.ts` — lowercase, `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing or double hyphen, trimmed to 48; editable; the slug RULE is `slugSchema` from `@church/domain` (3–48) — the app adds ONLY a `.refine` rejecting the reserved words `admin`, `api`, `o`, `s`, `embed`, `login`, `signup`, `auth`, `invite`, `privacy`, `terms` via `RESERVED_SLUGS`), Contact email (optional), Billing mode (`manual` default, `stripe`, `free`; one-line explanation each: manual = the church pays by check and the super admin tracks status by hand; stripe = card subscription via Stripe, wired in step 2.3; free = no billing, never expires), Trial ends (date, default today + 30 days — founder decision 7: "trial 30 days (`trial_ends_at` default now()+30d on church creation)"; hidden and stored as null when billing mode is `free`, in which case status is inserted as `active`). Server Action `createChurch` in `src/features/orgs/actions.ts`: `requireSuperAdmin()`, Zod parse with `createOrganizationSchema` extended by the reserved-word refinement (`createChurchSchema = createOrganizationSchema.refine(...)` in `src/features/orgs/slug.ts`), then `insertOrganization(db, { slug, name, contact_email, billing_mode, trial_ends_at, status, created_by })` with the USER client (`created_by = auth user id`; `status = 'trial'` unless `free`) — extend `insertOrganization` in `packages/db/src/queries/organizations.ts` with the optional `status` and `created_by` fields if 1.7a did not accept them; map `DomainError` key `duplicate` (SQLSTATE 23505) on the slug to a field error "That slug is already taken", `revalidatePath('/admin')`, redirect to `/admin/churches/<id>`. Do not insert into `organization_settings`, `audience_groups` or `calendars` — the trigger does.
3. **Church page layout** `app/(super)/admin/churches/[orgId]/layout.tsx`: `requireSuperAdmin()`, `await params`, load the org with `getOrganization(db, orgId)` (404 via `notFound()` when missing), render the header (name, slug, status badge, billing mode) and a shadcn `Tabs` navigation implemented as links: Details → `/admin/churches/[orgId]`, Settings → `/settings`, Fellowships → `/fellowships`, Admins → `/admins`, Billing → `/billing`. Create `admins/page.tsx` and `billing/page.tsx` as one-line placeholders ("Built in step 2.2b") so the tabs render; 2.2b replaces them. Put the shared header in `src/features/orgs/ChurchHeader.tsx`.
4. **Details tab** `app/(super)/admin/churches/[orgId]/page.tsx` + `src/features/orgs/ChurchDetailsForm.tsx`: edit Name, Slug (with an inline warning "Changing the slug changes every `/o/<slug>` URL and the links church admins have bookmarked"), Contact email; read-only cards: Status, Billing mode, Trial ends, Created, and counts (active memberships, persons, sermons, announcements) from a new `organizationCounts(db, orgId)` in `queries/organizations.ts`: memberships via `org_memberships` where `status = 'active'`, persons via the `directory_persons` VIEW (never the `persons` base table — PLAN §5), sermons/announcements via their tables; every count uses `select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })`. Server Action `updateChurch` (`updateOrganizationSchema` minus `status` — `.omit({ status: true })` — plus the reserved-word refinement; `updateOrganization(db, id, patch)` with the user client; `duplicate` → slug field error; `revalidatePath`). `ca_organizations_update_super` has no `org_writable` clause, so this update also works for suspended churches — say so in a comment. When the church's `status` is `suspended` or `cancelled`, render the whole form read-only with the note "This church is suspended — the database blocks writes (founder decision 7). ## Constraints
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10). No new runtime dependency except what shadcn adds for `command` (`cmdk`) and `alert-dialog`, generated into `src/components/ui/*`.
- Reuse, never duplicate: schemas from `@church/domain` (`createOrganizationSchema`, `updateOrganizationSchema`, `fellowshipSchema`, `organizationSettingsSchema`, `updateSettingsSchema`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `slugSchema`, `timezoneSchema`); queries from `@church/db` `queries/organizations.ts` and `queries/settings.ts` (extend them; no `orgs.ts`, no `fellowships.ts`, no inline `from('organizations')` in the app). `git grep` verifies.
- User client only — the service client is not imported anywhere in this step (`git grep` verifies). No `srv_*` RPC calls. No Stripe code, no status/billing-mode changes, no Admins tab content, no `/admin/super-admins`, no `/o/*` pages, no migrations. Do not edit `9999_init.sql`.
- Exact column and enum names come from `9999_init.sql` and `database.types.ts` — do not invent columns (for example there is no `organizations.plan`); if a column you need is missing, stop and record it in HANDOFF under "Open questions" instead of adding a migration. Never read `persons`/`households` base tables (views only).
- Never run `supabase db push` / `db reset`. No secrets or real email addresses in files or fixtures (use `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`-style placeholders or `example.test`). No model identifiers in commits.
- Next 16: `params`/`searchParams` are Promises; Server Actions live in files with `'use server'`; use `revalidatePath` after writes.

Checkpoint A's super-admin surface is complete.

## Goal
When you finish, the super admin can give a newly created church its first administrator and manage its billing state, and can see who the super admins are: the **Admins** tab on `/admin/churches/[orgId]` lists the church's memberships with their permissions, invites the first admin with all 12 permissions through the `createInvitation` wrapper (raw token shown once as an `inviteUrl(appUrl, token)` link to copy), or creates the account directly through the Server Action `createUserDirect` in `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` (service `auth.admin.createUser` → `srvAttachUser`; temporary password shown once), lists pending invitations with Revoke, and can disable/enable a membership or grant it all 12 permissions. The **Billing** tab edits `billing_mode` and `trial_ends_at`, changes `organizations.status` (suspend, unsuspend, cancel, reactivate, mark active) with confirmations, shows the mirrored Stripe subscription read-only, and renders the Checkout / Customer-portal buttons disabled with the tooltip "Stripe is wired in step 2.3". `/admin/super-admins` lists the `super_admins` rows and shows the SQL bootstrap instructions. Every payload uses the `@church/domain` schemas and `@church/db` wrappers of steps 1.6b/1.7a, so step 3.2 can reuse `createUserDirect` unchanged. This completes the super-admin half of the founder's Checkpoint A.

## Constraints
- The service client is imported by exactly one file in the web app after this step: `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` (DESIGN §9: "the service client only for Stripe/push/share/cron/direct-create"). Billing status, billing mode, trial, invitations, permissions and membership status all go through the USER client / the `@church/db` client-RPC wrappers.
- Authorisation is checked with the user client BEFORE any service call; never trust `org` from the form without `requireSuperAdmin()` (or the `users.create` check inside `createUserDirect`).
- Reuse, never duplicate: `createInvitationSchema`, `createUserDirectSchema`, `setMembershipStatusSchema`, `orgBillingFormSchema`, `inviteUrl` from `@church/domain`; `createInvitation`, `revokeInvitation`, `setMembershipPermissions`, `setMembershipStatus`, `srvAttachUser`, `listMemberships`, `listInvitations`, `listSuperAdmins`, `getBillingSummary`, `updateOrganization` from `@church/db`. No inline `from('org_memberships')`/`from('invitations')`/`from('super_admins')` in the app; no `profiles(` embed anywhere.
- No Stripe SDK, no `/api/billing/*`, no `/api/stripe/webhook`, no `stripe` dependency — that is step 2.3. No Resend. No `/o/*` pages, no full users grid (3.2), no migrations; do not edit `9999_init.sql`.

The raw string is always stored in `status_raw` (DESIGN §13: "unknown Stripe statuses never fail the insert but the UI keeps a typed badge").
   - `export function shouldApply(storedEventCreated: number, incomingEventCreated: number): boolean` — pure; `incoming >= stored`.
   - `export function subscriptionSnapshot(sub: Stripe.Subscription, eventCreated: number)` — pure; builds the `billing_subscriptions` row: `stripe_subscription_id = sub.id`, `status = mapStripeStatus(sub.status)`, `status_raw = sub.status`, `event_created`, `price_id = sub.items.data[0]?.price.id ?? null`, `quantity`, `current_period_start/end` — read them from `sub.items.data[0]` first (recent Stripe API versions moved the period fields onto subscription items) and fall back to the top-level fields when they exist on the typed object; `cancel_at_period_end`, `trial_end`, `canceled_at` (Unix seconds → ISO strings), `raw = sub` as JSON.
   - **Dependency shape (define once, use everywhere in `sync.ts`, `webhook.ts` and the routes):**

       getCustomerByOrg(orgId: string): Promise<BillingCustomerRow | null>;

       upsertCustomer(row: BillingCustomerInsert): Promise<void>;
       getOrg(orgId: string): Promise<Pick<OrganizationRow, 'id' | 'name' | 'contact_email' | 'billing_mode' | 'status'> | null>;

       upsertSubscription(row: BillingSubscriptionInsert): Promise<void>;

     }
     export type Deps = { stripe: Stripe | null; repo: BillingRepo; webhookSecret: string };

     ```
     The row/insert types are the generated `Database['public']['Tables'][...]['Row' | 'Insert']` aliases from `@church/db`. `export function defaultDeps(): Deps` builds `{ stripe: getStripe(), repo: supabaseBillingRepo(createServiceSupabase()), webhookSecret: stripeConfig().webhookSecret ?? '' }` and THROWS `StripeNotConfiguredError` when `getStripe()` is `null` (used by checkout/portal). `export function defaultWebhookDeps(): Deps` builds the same object but NEVER throws — `stripe` may be `null`; the webhook handler answers 503 itself. Tests pass a Map-backed `BillingRepo` and a fake `stripe`; nothing in this module mocks supabase-js.

   - `export async function resolveOrgId(deps: Deps, { customerId, metadataOrgId })` — first `deps.repo.getCustomerByStripeId(customerId)`, then `metadataOrgId` (from `subscription.metadata.org_id`, `checkout.session.metadata.org_id` or `client_reference_id`); when only metadata resolves it, `deps.repo.upsertCustomer(...)` so future events resolve by customer. Returns `null` when neither resolves.
   - `export async function syncSubscription(deps: Deps, subscriptionId: string, eventCreated: number)` — `deps.stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(subscriptionId)` (the subscription fetched from Stripe is authoritative, never the event payload); resolve the org; `deps.repo.getSubscription(subscriptionId)` for the stored `event_created` (0 when no row); if `!shouldApply(stored, eventCreated)` return `{ applied: false, reason: 'stale' }`; otherwise `deps.repo.upsertSubscription({ ...subscriptionSnapshot(sub, eventCreated), org_id })` and return `{ applied: true }`. 4. **`apps/web/src/lib/stripe/webhook.ts`** (name chosen here because DESIGN §2 lists only `client.ts`/`sync.ts`; keep it) — `export async function handleStripeWebhook(input: { rawBody: string; signature: string | null }, deps: Deps): Promise<{ status: number; body: object }>`, fully testable without `Request`:
   - If `deps.webhookSecret` is empty OR `deps.stripe` is `null` → `{ status: 503, body: { error: 'webhook_not_configured' } }` (DESIGN §8: "503 if secret missing" — never skip verification; without a `stripe` instance `constructEvent` cannot run).
   - If `signature` is null or `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(rawBody, signature, secret)` throws → 400 `invalid_signature`.
   - `deps.repo.insertEvent({ id: event.id, type: event.type, event_created: event.created, received_at: now })`. When it answers `'exists'` read the existing row with `deps.repo.getEvent(event.id)`: `processed_at not null` → return 200 `{ received: true, duplicate: true }` without reprocessing; `processed_at null` → continue (reprocess a previously failed delivery).
   - Dispatch on `event.type`: `checkout.session.completed` → subscription id from `session.subscription` (string or object); `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted` → `event.data.object.id`; `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `invoice.payment_failed` → subscription id from `invoice.parent?.subscription_details?.subscription` with a fallback to the legacy `invoice.subscription` field (both shapes exist across Stripe API versions; write a small `subscriptionIdFromInvoice()` helper and test it). Every other type is recorded and acknowledged with 200 `{ received: true, ignored: true }`.
   - For handled types call `syncSubscription(deps, subscriptionId, event.created)`. A stale result is not an error: set `processed_at`, `error = 'stale_event_ignored'`, return 200.
   - If the org cannot be resolved (no `billing_customers` row and no `org_id` metadata): `deps.repo.markEvent(id, { processed_at: now, error: 'org_not_found' })`, return 200 — retrying cannot fix it, and a permanent 500 would make Stripe disable the endpoint. Record this deviation from the plan's "500 on error" rule in HANDOFF.md.
   - Any other thrown error: update the `stripe_events` row with `error = message` (leave `processed_at` null) and return 500 `{ error: 'handler_error' }` so Stripe retries (PLAN §1 item 7).
   - On success set `processed_at = now()`, `error = null`, return 200 `{ received: true }`.
5. **`apps/web/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`** — `export const runtime = 'nodejs'`, `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`; `POST`: `const rawBody = await req.text()` (never `req.json()` — the signature covers the exact bytes), `signature = req.headers.get('stripe-signature')`, `const { status, body } = await handleStripeWebhook({ rawBody, signature }, defaultWebhookDeps())`, `return NextResponse.json(body, { status })`. `defaultWebhookDeps()` (Build 3) never throws when Stripe is unconfigured — the handler returns 503 itself. Export no other method (GET → 405 by default).
6. **`apps/web/app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts`** — `runtime = 'nodejs'`, `POST` only:
   1. Same-origin check: the `origin` header (or the origin of `referer`) must equal `publicEnv().appUrl` (trailing slash trimmed); otherwise 403 `{ error: 'bad_origin' }`. Note for docs/ENV.md: on Vercel *Preview* deployments this check returns 403 by design because `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is the production URL — billing is exercised on production only.
   2. Authorisation with `getAuthContext()` from `src/lib/auth/context.ts` (2.1, non-redirecting, user-scoped server client): `null` or `!ctx.isSuperAdmin` → 401 JSON `{ error: 'unauthorized' }`. Do not invent a new guard; only if no such helper exists add `getSuperAdminContext()` next to `requireSuperAdmin()` and record it in HANDOFF. Never authorise with the service client.
   3. Body: Zod `{ orgId: z.string().uuid(), attemptId: z.string().uuid() }` → 400 on failure (`attemptId` is generated by the client island with `crypto.randomUUID()` per button press).
   4. `stripeConfig().configured` false → 503 `{ error: 'stripe_not_configured', missing }`.
   5. Load the org with the user client (super admin select policy); `billing_mode !== 'stripe'` → 409 `{ error: 'billing_mode_not_stripe' }` (the super admin switches the mode in the Billing tab first — this is what makes the mirror trigger act); `status === 'cancelled'` → 409.
   6. `const deps = defaultDeps()` (throws only when unconfigured — already excluded by 6.4), `ensureCustomer(deps, orgId)`, then `deps.stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ mode: 'subscription', customer, client_reference_id: orgId, line_items: [{ price: priceId, quantity: 1 }], subscription_data: { metadata: { org_id: orgId } }, metadata: { org_id: orgId }, success_url: `${appUrl}/admin/churches/${orgId}/billing?billing=success`, cancel_url: `${appUrl}/admin/churches/${orgId}/billing?billing=cancelled`, allow_promotion_codes: false }, { idempotencyKey: `checkout:${orgId}:${attemptId}` })` where `appUrl` is the trimmed `publicEnv().appUrl`. Idempotency: DESIGN §8 says "idempotency key = org id" — that holds for the Customer (`customer:${orgId}`, Build 3); the Checkout key is per attempt because a per-org key would return the same (possibly expired, 24 h) Checkout Session on every later click; record this under HANDOFF.md "Deviations from plan". Do not add `trial_period_days` — the 30-day trial is the app's `trial_ends_at`, not a Stripe trial. Respond 200 `{ url: session.url }`; the client navigates with `window.location.assign(url)`.
7. **`apps/web/app/api/billing/portal/route.ts`** — same origin/auth/Zod/config checks (body `{ orgId, attemptId }`); `ensureCustomer(deps, orgId)`; `deps.stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create({ customer, return_url: `${appUrl}/admin/churches/${orgId}/billing` }, { idempotencyKey: `portal:${orgId}:${attemptId}` })` → 200 `{ url }`. If Stripe answers that no portal configuration exists (test mode needs one saved once in the Stripe Dashboard), return 502 `{ error: 'portal_not_configured' }` and show that text in the UI; the founder saves the default portal configuration in step 3.9.

## Constraints
- Never put a Stripe key, webhook secret or price id into the repo, tests (use obvious placeholders), prompts, logs or the client bundle; `stripeConfig()` values never cross to client components — only booleans and variable names. `client.ts`, `sync.ts`, `webhook.ts` start with `import 'server-only'`.
- The service client is used only for the billing tables inside `sync.ts`/`webhook.ts`; authorisation of the checkout/portal routes uses the user client (`my_context()` / `super_admins` via RLS). Web never holds elevated keys client-side (standing order).
- The webhook must stay excluded from `proxy.ts`'s matcher and must not read cookies. Do not weaken CSP or security headers from 2.1; Stripe Checkout and the portal are full-page redirects, so no `frame-src`/`script-src` additions are needed. Do not embed Stripe.js.
- Do not edit `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` or add a migration: if a column you want is missing, adapt the code to the real schema and record it in HANDOFF.md "Deviations from plan" (a `9998_*` migration is a later, founder-approved step). Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`.
- Do not build `/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing` (step 3.1), Resend email (3.2), or the cron (3.6). Do not refactor the 2.2a/2.2b pages beyond the Billing tab wiring, the `/admin` banner and events card; keep `billing-actions.ts`, `status-transitions.ts` and `StripeBanner.tsx` in place (edit, do not replace).
- Pins: `stripe` 22.6.1, Next 16.3, Zod 4.5, Vitest 4, TypeScript ~5.9; `@types/react` on the 19.2 line. No model identifiers in commits or files.

## 2.4 — Supabase project, first paste of `9999_init.sql`, Auth settings (founder, about 45 minutes)

Before you start: step 1.5 must be finished on `main` (HANDOFF.md State ticks "Seed, typegen, DB docs"; `supabase/README.md` exists). 2. **Copy the connection facts into the password manager (not into git, not into a Claude Code prompt — `prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim).**
