## Goal
When you finish, a church leader holding `announcements.create` opens `/o/<slug>/announcements/new`, writes a title and body, picks the audience from the church's `audience_groups` (the six system groups first — All attendees, Members, Non-member attendees, Youth, Men, Women — then custom groups), chooses "Publish now" or a future date and time in the church's timezone, optionally sets an expiry, pins it, leaves "Send a push notification" on or turns it off, and saves. The row lands in `announcements`; the database trigger `app.on_content_publish` (step 1.3a) inserts one `notifications` row (`kind = 'announcement'`, `scheduled_for = publish_at`) when `push` is true — nothing in this step sends anything. The list at `/o/<slug>/announcements` shows every announcement with its state (Scheduled, Active, Expired), the audience name, pinned marker and a Push column that reads the outbox row: "Queued — delivered by the push dispatcher (step 3.6)". `announcements.edit` holders edit at `/o/<slug>/announcements/[id]/edit`; `announcements.delete` holders delete (the trigger `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete` cancels a still-queued push). Members without any `announcements.*` permission can open the list and see only what RLS lets them see (published, not expired, in their audience) with no controls, and every row expands to show the full body — the list is the only web surface for reading an announcement (PLAN §8 has no `/announcements/[id]`). Step 3.5b adds bulletins; step 3.6a replaces the stub `afterContentPublish()` with the real dispatcher; 3.6b adds the cron.

   - `updateAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id, form)` — `announcements.edit`; `getAnnouncement` first (404 → `not_found`); `updateAnnouncement(db, id, { ...input, updated_by })`; 0 rows updated → "You no longer have permission to edit announcements" (RLS refused); `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements')` and `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements/<id>/edit')`; then `afterContentPublish` (turning `push` on after publication enqueues a fresh row via the trigger — the only way an edit causes a push; say so in the form help). Changing `publish_at` of an already-queued push does NOT move the queued `scheduled_for` in this step; show the notice "Push already queued — the dispatcher checks the publish time before sending (step 3.6)" (3.6a rewrites this wording).
   - `deleteAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id)` — `announcements.delete`; `deleteAnnouncement(db, id)`; 0 rows → permission message; `revalidatePath`.
   The Server Actions carry the `…Action` suffix because the `@church/db` queries `updateAnnouncement` / `deleteAnnouncement` own the plain names (same convention as 3.3b's `deleteSermonAction`); never alias imports to make same-named pairs compile.
   Map SQLSTATE 23514 (check violation, e.g. `expires_at` before `publish_at` if the DB has such a check) and 23503 (unknown `audience_group_id`) through `toDomainError` to field errors. Never import `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` here.

Search param `?show=active|scheduled|expired|all` for managers only (default `all`). `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/new/page.tsx` — `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.create')`, `AnnouncementForm` in create mode with the groups. `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/[id]/edit/page.tsx` — `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')`, `getAnnouncement` (→ `notFound()`), form in edit mode prefilled via `instantToZonedLocal`, Delete button (only with `announcements.delete`) opening a confirm dialog that names the title and says "A queued push notification is cancelled; sent notifications cannot be recalled".

## Goal
When you finish, a leader holding `bulletins.upload` opens `/o/<slug>/bulletins`, clicks "Upload bulletin", picks **This Sunday** (the coming Sunday, or today if it is Sunday — `starts_on = ends_on`), **Quarter** (the calendar quarter containing today) or **Custom** (two date inputs), accepts or edits the suggested title, chooses a PDF, JPG or PNG file of at most 25 MiB and watches a resumable upload with progress, pause/resume and cancel. The flow is PLAN §6 exactly: a Server Action inserts the `bulletins` row with `publish_at = null` and the exact planned `storage_path`; the browser uploads to that path with the user's own token through the generic `src/features/uploads/*` from step 3.3b; a second Server Action records size and MIME and sets `publish_at = now()`. At that moment the trigger `app.on_content_publish` inserts a `notifications` row of kind `bulletin` when the church's `push_on_bulletin` setting is on (founder decision 6: "Push on every bulletin upload: yes (`push_on_bulletin` default true, per-church toggle)"). The list shows all bulletins newest first with title, date range, kind (PDF/Image), size, a "Current" badge for the row covering today in the church timezone, a Push column using 3.5a's `PushStatusBadge` (visible to announcement managers — the only role RLS lets read `notifications`; a `bulletins.upload`-only leader sees "Push status is shown to announcement managers"), Open (PDF in a new tab, image in a dialog) and Download via 1-hour signed URLs, and Delete with confirmation. Members without `bulletins.upload` see published bulletins read-only. Step 3.6a makes the push real (3.6b adds the cron that deletes files); step 4.2 renders bulletins in the app.

## Goal
When you finish, publishing an announcement or bulletin on the web sends the push within the same request: the Server Action's `afterContentPublish()` (the 3.5a stub) now runs `dispatchQueued()` with the service client, which claims due `notifications` rows via `srv_claim_notifications`, re-reads the referenced content (cancel when missing or unpublished, reschedule when moved into the future), resolves recipients (`srv_audience_user_ids` ∩ `notification_preferences` ∩ enabled `push_devices`), sends through `expo-server-sdk` in SDK-sized chunks and records one `notification_deliveries` row per device with its Expo ticket. `processReceipts()` exists and is unit-tested (3.6b calls it from the cron); `DeviceNotRegistered` disables the device. Rows the synchronous run could not finish (future-dated, transient errors, other churches) stay `queued` for the cron of step 3.6b. The announcements and bulletins lists replace every "step 3.6" wording with real status ("Sent to 12 devices", "Failed — <reason>") and a permission-gated Retry. There are no mobile devices yet (step 4.3 registers them), so the founder verifies with a fake token that Expo rejects.

- Column names (1.2, in `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` — read them, they are fixed): `notifications (id, org_id, kind, ref_id, title, body, audience_group_id, scheduled_for, status, attempts, claimed_at, sent_at, last_error, created_at, updated_at)`; `notification_deliveries (id, notification_id fk cascade, user_id fk auth.users cascade, device_id fk push_devices set null, expo_ticket_id text, receipt_status text, error text, created_at, updated_at)` — there is NO token column on deliveries, the device is referenced by `device_id`; `push_devices (id, user_id, expo_push_token text not null unique, platform push_platform, device_name, enabled boolean default true, last_seen_at, created_at, updated_at)` — the enable flag is `enabled` (no `disabled_at`, no `is_enabled`), `disablePushDeviceById` sets `enabled = false`; `notification_preferences (user_id, org_id, announcements, bulletins, events, surveys)`. `receipt_status` is free text; this step fixes the vocabulary as `null` (awaiting receipt) | `'ok'` | `'error'` | `'unknown'` and records it in HANDOFF.
- Database semantics you rely on (1.3a/1.3b; read the function bodies in `9999_init.sql`): `srv_claim_notifications(max_rows)` claims `queued` rows with `scheduled_for <= now()` and `attempts < 5` using `for update skip locked`, sets `status = 'claimed'`, `claimed_at = now()`, `attempts + 1`, and marks rows with `attempts >= 5` as `failed`; it has NO org parameter — claiming is global across churches by design (proposed step 3.12 adds an `org` argument); `srv_housekeeping()` (called by the 3.6b cron) re-queues `claimed` rows older than 10 minutes without `sent_at`; `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)` returns distinct `persons.user_id` joined to ACTIVE `org_memberships`, filtered by `group is null or app.person_in_group(...)`, and raises `organization_suspended` when the org is not writable; `app.on_content_publish` enqueues announcements (`push` and `publish_at` not null), bulletins (`push_on_bulletin` and published), events (`status = 'approved'` and `push`), surveys (`status = 'open'` and `push`); `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete` cancels queued/claimed rows on delete.
- `@church/domain`: `schemas/enums.ts` (`notificationKindSchema`, `notificationStatusSchema`), `urls.ts` (1.6b — add `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` additively, see Build 3), `errors.ts`.
- Founder decisions that apply: 6 — bulletin pushes exist because `push_on_bulletin` enqueued them (nothing to decide here); 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes": a suspended church's queued pushes fail with `organization_suspended` and are not retried until Retry. Orchestrator decision 7: "3.6 then adds `src/lib/push/*`, wires the publish Server Actions to call `dispatch()` synchronously after enqueue, and the cron" — this step is everything before "and the cron".

## Build
1. **Transport** `apps/web/src/lib/push/expo.ts`: add `expo-server-sdk` 7.2.0 (DESIGN §3; a newer 7.2.x patch is fine) to `apps/web`. Export `type PushMessage = { to: string; title: string; body: string; data: Record<string, string>; sound: 'default'; channelId: 'announcements'; priority: 'high' }`, `type PushTicket = { id?: string; status: 'ok' | 'error'; message?: string; details?: { error?: string } }`, `type PushReceipt = { status: 'ok' | 'error'; message?: string; details?: { error?: string } }`, and `interface PushTransport { isValidToken(token: string): boolean; sendChunks(messages: PushMessage[]): Promise<{ tickets: PushTicket[]; error?: string }[]>; getReceipts(ids: string[]): Promise<Record<string, PushReceipt>> }`. `createExpoTransport({ accessToken }: { accessToken?: string } = {})` builds `new Expo(accessToken ? { accessToken } : {})` — pass ONLY options present in the installed version's `ExpoClientOptions` (`accessToken`, `httpAgent`, `maxConcurrentRequests`, `retryMinTimeout`); FCM v1 is the only transport in 7.x, so there is no legacy flag to set. `isValidToken` = `Expo.isExpoPushToken`; `sendChunks` = `expo.chunkPushNotifications(messages)` (the chunk size is the static `Expo.pushNotificationChunkSizeLimit` — never a literal 100 anywhere in this step) then `sendPushNotificationsAsync` per chunk, a rejected chunk becoming `{ tickets: [], error: String(e) }` so one bad chunk does not fail the batch; `getReceipts` = `chunkPushNotificationReceiptIds` + `getPushNotificationReceiptsAsync`, merging the maps. The access token comes from `serverEnv().expoAccessToken`; `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` is optional (DESIGN §8) — without it the SDK sends unauthenticated at Expo's public rate limit; say so in `docs/ENV.md` (Build 8).
2. **Dispatcher** `apps/web/src/lib/push/dispatch.ts`: `dispatchQueued(svc: ServiceDbClient, { transport, limit = 50, now = () => new Date(), deadlineMs = 25_000 }): Promise<DispatchSummary>` with `DispatchSummary = { claimed, sent, skipped, cancelled, rescheduled, failed, recipients, devices, errors: string[] }`. There is no org option: `srv_claim_notifications` takes only `max_rows`, so a synchronous run after publish may also deliver other churches' due rows — harmless and documented. Loop: `srvClaimNotifications(svc, { max_rows: Math.min(limit, 20) })` until it returns nothing, the total reaches `limit`, or the deadline passes. Per claimed row:
   - **Re-read** by `kind` (`src/lib/push/refs.ts`, `loadNotificationRef(svc, kind, refId, now)` → `{ state: 'missing' } | { state: 'unpublished' } | { state: 'future', publishAt } | { state: 'ok', orgId, title, body, audienceGroupId }`): `announcement` → `getAnnouncement`: missing → `missing`; `push = false` → `unpublished`; `publish_at > now` → `future`; `expires_at <= now` → `unpublished`; `bulletin` → `getBulletin`: `publish_at null` → `unpublished`; `event` → read `events`: `status = 'approved'` and `push`, else `unpublished` (UI is 5.3); `survey` → read `surveys`: `status = 'open'` and `push`, else `unpublished` (UI is 6.1) — the same predicates the trigger uses. Add tiny read helpers to `packages/db` where the modules do not exist yet (`queries/calendars-events.ts`, `queries/surveys.ts` are deferred to 5.3/6.1 — create them with only the getter, recorded in HANDOFF). `missing`/`unpublished` → `cancelNotification(svc, id, reason)` (additive: status `cancelled`, `last_error = 'ref_missing' | 'ref_unpublished'`); `future` → `rescheduleNotification(svc, id, publishAt)` (additive: status `queued`, `scheduled_for = publishAt`, `claimed_at = null`, `attempts - 1` so a moved date never burns attempts); count `cancelled`/`rescheduled`.
   - **Recipients**: `srvAudienceUserIds(svc, { group_id: row.audience_group_id, org: row.org_id })`; on `organization_suspended` → `markNotificationFailed(svc, id, 'organization_suspended')` (no automatic retry; Retry in the UI re-queues). Load `notification_preferences` for those users in that org (`listPreferencesForUsers(svc, orgId, userIds)` — additive) and keep users whose column for the kind (`announcements` / `bulletins` / `events` / `surveys`) is true or who have no row (defaults on). Load enabled devices for the remaining users (`listEnabledDevicesForUsers(svc, userIds)` — additive: `push_devices where user_id in (…) and enabled`), drop tokens failing `transport.isValidToken`, dedupe by `expo_push_token`. Zero devices → `markNotificationsSent(svc, [id])` with `recipients` counted (nothing to send is success, not failure).
   - **Messages**: one per device: `{ to: device.expo_push_token, title: row.title, body: truncated body, data: { url: notificationTargetPath(kind, refId), org_id, kind, ref_id, notification_id }, sound: 'default', channelId: 'announcements', priority: 'high' }` where the body is cut to 178 characters and an ellipsis is appended ONLY when something was cut. `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` lives in `@church/domain` `src/urls.ts` (additive, tested): `/announcements/<id>`, `/bulletins/<id>`, `/events/<id>`, `/surveys/<id>` — the app-relative route the mobile app (4.3) pushes after switching to `org_id`.
   - **Send**: `transport.sendChunks(messages)` (one call with ALL messages; chunking happens inside the transport). For each chunk result: `error` → insert that chunk's deliveries with `receipt_status: 'error'`, `error: <message>`, `expo_ticket_id: null`, and `requeueNotification` the notification when `attempts < 5` else `markNotificationFailed(svc, id, 'transport_error')`; otherwise `insertDeliveries(svc, rows)` where each row is `{ notification_id, user_id, device_id, expo_ticket_id: ticket.id ?? null, receipt_status: ticket.status === 'ok' ? null : 'error', error: ticket.message ?? null }` — tickets are written IN the insert (one insert per chunk after its send), so 1.7a's `updateDeliveryTicket` is not needed on this path; `null` means "awaiting receipt", which is exactly what `listPendingReceipts` selects. A ticket with `details.error === 'DeviceNotRegistered'` → `disablePushDeviceById(svc, device_id)` immediately. When every chunk succeeded → `markNotificationsSent(svc, [id])`. Any unexpected exception inside a row's processing → catch, `markNotificationFailed` if `attempts >= 5` else `requeueNotification`, push the message into `errors`, continue with the next row — one bad row never blocks the batch.
   - Deadline: stop claiming when `Date.now() - start > deadlineMs`; rows already claimed are always finished. Never claim more than `limit`.
3. **Receipts** `apps/web/src/lib/push/receipts.ts`: `processReceipts(svc, { transport, olderThanMinutes = 15, limit = 1000, now = () => new Date() })` → `listPendingReceipts(svc, { olderThanMinutes })` (ticketed deliveries with `receipt_status is null`), `transport.getReceipts(ids)`; `ok` → `markDeliveryReceipt(svc, id, { receipt_status: 'ok', error: null })`; `error` → `{ receipt_status: 'error', error: details?.error ?? message }` and `DeviceNotRegistered` → `disablePushDeviceById(svc, device_id)`; ids absent from the response whose delivery is older than 24 h → `receipt_status = 'unknown'` (stop asking). Returns `{ checked, ok, error, unknown, devicesDisabled }`. Not called by anything in this step except tests — 3.6b wires it into the cron.

Replace the stub comment with "Synchronous dispatch after publish; whatever this run cannot finish is picked up by the cron tick (step 3.6b)". Export `const maxDuration = 60` from every page whose Server Actions dispatch (PLAN §7: "called on publish (`maxDuration 60`)"; Next applies the segment config of the page that invokes the action): `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/page.tsx` (Retry lives on the list), `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/new/page.tsx`, `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/[id]/edit/page.tsx`, `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/bulletins/page.tsx`.

### 3.6b — Cron tick — route, storage drain, orphan sweep, housekeeping, docs

## Build
1. **Cron route** `apps/web/app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`: `export const runtime = 'nodejs'; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'; export const maxDuration = 60;` `GET(req: Request)`: read `serverEnv().cronSecret`; unset → 503 `{ error: 'cron_not_configured' }` (log once per process); compare the `Authorization` header to `Bearer <secret>` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers → 401 `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` otherwise (Vercel sends this header automatically when the `CRON_SECRET` environment variable exists — document). Then `runTick(createServiceSupabase(), { transport: createExpoTransport({ accessToken: serverEnv().expoAccessToken }), deadlineMs: 50_000 })` and respond with JSON `{ ok, startedAt, durationMs, phases }`; HTTP 200 when every phase succeeded, 500 when any phase threw (all phases still run — Vercel's cron log then shows the failure). Also `export const POST = GET` so a manual trigger from the Vercel dashboard works. Never read the secret from the query string.
2. **Tick phases** `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.ts` — `runTick(svc, { transport, now = () => new Date(), deadlineMs })` runs the phases in this exact order, each wrapped in `phase(name, fn)` that records `{ ok, ms, result | error }` and never stops the chain: (1) `enqueue` → `srvEnqueueDueNotifications(svc)`; (2) `dispatch` → `dispatchQueued(svc, { transport, limit: 200, deadlineMs: 25_000, now })`; (3) `receipts` → `processReceipts(svc, { transport, now })`; (4) `storageDeletions` → `drainStorageDeletions(svc, { limit: 100 })`; (5) `orphanSweep` → `sweepOrphans(svc, { now })`; (6) `housekeeping` → `srvHousekeeping(svc)`; (7) `accountDeletions` → `srvProcessAccountDeletions(svc)`. Stop starting new phases when `deadlineMs` is exhausted and report the skipped ones as `{ ok: false, error: 'deadline' }`. Header comment on idempotency: overlapping ticks are safe because claiming uses `skip locked`, deletions are idempotent (not-found counts as done), receipts are keyed by ticket, the sweep only enqueues, and the `srv_*` functions are re-runnable.
3. **Storage drain** `src/lib/cron/storage-deletions.ts` — `drainStorageDeletions(svc, { limit })`: `listStorageDeletions(svc, limit)` → for `is_prefix = false` remove the single object (`removeObjects(svc, bucket, [name])` — additive in `queries/storage.ts` wrapping `svc.storage.from(bucket).remove(names)`; "object not found" counts as done) → `markStorageDeletionDone`; for `is_prefix = true` list up to 1000 objects under the prefix (`listObjects`; recurse one level for folder entries — Storage lists folders as entries without `id`), remove them, and mark done only when the listing came back empty (large prefixes finish over several ticks); failures → `markStorageDeletionFailed` (`attempts + 1`, `last_error`); rows with `attempts >= 10` are skipped and reported. Returns `{ processed, done, failed, skipped, objectsRemoved }`.
4. **Orphan sweep** `src/lib/cron/orphan-sweep.ts` — `sweepOrphans(svc, { now, bucket? })`: one bucket per tick, rotating over `['sermon-media', 'bulletins', 'documents', 'directory-photos', 'org-assets']` by `Math.floor(now().getTime() / 300_000) % 5` (5-minute epochs — with the Hobby fallback `0 12 * * *` a minute-based rotation would sweep only the first bucket forever); `bucket` overrides the rotation for tests. List objects per org prefix: `listOrganizationIds(svc): Promise<string[]>` (additive in `queries/organizations.ts` — `select id from organizations`; `listOrganizations` joins settings and billing and is not for this) → for each org `listObjects(svc, bucket, '<org_id>/', …)` recursing into the folder entries, capping the total at 1000 objects per tick (continue with the next org on the next tick — keep it stateless: cap and move on); keep objects with `created_at < now - 24 h`; `listReferencedPaths(svc, bucket)` → a `Set` of referenced names (extend it additively with an optional `{ names }` filter only if the full list proves too large; never add a second helper for the same job); every listed name not in the set → `enqueueStorageDeletion(svc, { bucket_id, object_name, is_prefix: false, org_id })` — extend `enqueueStorageDeletion` additively with an optional `org_id` (the object's first path segment) since 1.7a's signature lacks it and the 1.2 table has the column; record it in HANDOFF. The sweep never removes anything itself: the drain deletes on the next tick — two-phase, so a sweep bug can be caught in the table before anything is destroyed. Returns `{ bucket, listed, orphansEnqueued }`.
5. **Docs**: `docs/ENV.md` — the `CRON_SECRET` row (how Vercel injects the header; generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`; Pro `*/5 * * * *`, Hobby `0 12 * * *` fallback; set it in Vercel for Production and Preview) and a "Push & maintenance job" section: what the tick does in order, the retry rules (≤ 5 attempts, re-queue of stale claims after 10 min by `srv_housekeeping`), the two-phase orphan sweep and its bucket rotation, the storage drain's 10-attempt cap, how to trigger manually (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET" https://<VERCEL_URL>/api/cron/tick`), the response shape, and that a Free-plan Supabase project paused after 7 idle days makes every phase fail until restored. Ensure `apps/web/.env.example` contains `CRON_SECRET=` with the comment `# openssl rand -hex 32` (add if missing). `README.md`: one line pointing to that section. If 3.5b's Bulletins paragraph left the question open, state whether incomplete bulletin rows are purged by `srv_housekeeping` (read its body) or persist until discarded.

   - `storage-deletions.test.ts` — single object, prefix in two passes (first listing non-empty → not done; second empty → done), not-found counts as done, `attempts >= 10` skipped and reported, a throwing `removeObjects` → `markStorageDeletionFailed`.

## Build
1. **Dependencies and scripts.** In `apps/web/package.json` add devDependency `@playwright/test` ~1.62 (exact minor from `npm view`). Add scripts: `test:e2e` → `playwright test`, `test:e2e:smoke` → `playwright test --project=smoke`, `test:e2e:full` → `playwright test --project=full` (the `full` project is defined in 3.7b; define the script now so the docs are stable), `test:e2e:report` → `playwright show-report`. Do NOT add Playwright to the `test` script or to Turbo's `test` task — `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must stay fast and network-free. Add a Turbo task `e2e` in `turbo.json` (`cache: false`, `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, `env` list identical to `build` plus `BASE_URL`, `E2E_*`) so `pnpm turbo e2e --filter web` works. Add `apps/web/playwright-report/`, `apps/web/test-results/` and `apps/web/e2e/.auth/` to `.gitignore`.
2. **`apps/web/playwright.config.ts`** (package root; `testDir: './e2e'`; DESIGN §11 step 9 writes `apps/web/e2e/playwright.config.ts` — put the config at the package root so `pnpm --filter web exec playwright test` finds it without flags, and note the wording in HANDOFF). Contents:
   - `const baseURL = process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3100'`; `webServer` only when `BASE_URL` is unset: `command: process.env.CI && existsSync('.next/BUILD_ID') ? 'pnpm start -- --port 3100' : 'pnpm build && pnpm start -- --port 3100'` (in CI the 1.1 web-build step has already built the app with the same mock env — see Build 6 — so do not build twice; `existsSync` from `node:fs`), `cwd` = `apps/web`, `url: baseURL`, `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, `timeout: process.env.CI ? 600_000 : 240_000`, and `env` = the **mock environment** defined in one place, `apps/web/e2e/mock-env.ts` (exported object, also re-used by 3.7b): `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=sb_secret_mock_value_must_never_appear_in_html`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3100`, `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET=<a 44-character base64 literal generated once and committed — it protects nothing>`, `CRON_SECRET=mock-cron-secret`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=50`, and NO `STRIPE_*` / `RESEND_*` (so the Stripe banner, the webhook 503 and the copy-link invitation path are exercised). Build with the mock env too: `next build` must succeed with these values (2.1a designed `serverEnv()` for exactly this).
   - `projects`: `smoke` (`testMatch: /smoke\.spec\.ts/`, Chromium desktop) and `smoke-mobile` (same files, `devices['Pixel 7']`) — the responsive pass costs nothing extra. Leave a commented `full` project placeholder for 3.7b.
   - `use`: `baseURL`, `trace: 'retain-on-failure'`, `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`, `video: 'off'`; `reporter: [['list'], ['html', { open: 'never' }]]`; `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`; `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`; `workers: process.env.CI ? 2 : undefined`; `expect.timeout: 10_000`.
3. **Helpers — `apps/web/e2e/helpers/headers.ts`**. Export a tiny `cspDirective(csp: string, name: string): string[]` parser (split on `;`, find the directive, return its source tokens — never assert on raw string order) and three assertion helpers, one per header variant of `csp.ts`: `expectStrictHeaders(response)` — `content-security-policy` present, `cspDirective(csp, 'frame-ancestors')` equals `["'none'"]`, `cspDirective(csp, 'frame-src')` CONTAINS both `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com` and `https://drive.google.com` (any order; other hosts allowed), `strict-transport-security` present, `referrer-policy` present, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `x-frame-options: DENY`; `expectShareHeaders(response)` (for `/s/*`) — CSP present and its `frame-ancestors` directive is either absent or does NOT contain `'none'` (if present it is `*`), `x-robots-tag` contains `noindex`, `referrer-policy: no-referrer`, `cache-control` contains `no-store`, header `x-frame-options` absent; `expectEmbedHeaders(response)` (for `/embed/*`) — CSP present and its `frame-ancestors` directive is absent or does not contain `'none'`, `x-robots-tag` contains `noindex`, `referrer-policy` equals the value `csp.ts` sets for `/embed/:path*` (3.4b: `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` — read the file and assert that exact value), header `x-frame-options` absent. Never use `expectShareHeaders` on an embed page or vice versa — the two variants differ on purpose. `apps/web/e2e/helpers/routes.ts` exporting `PROTECTED_PATHS` = `['/admin', '/admin/churches/new', '/admin/fellowships', '/admin/super-admins', '/o', '/o/some-church', '/o/some-church/dashboard', '/o/some-church/users', '/o/some-church/invitations', '/o/unknown/announcements', '/o/unknown/bulletins', '/o/some-church/sermons', '/o/some-church/sermons/new', '/o/some-church/settings', '/o/some-church/settings/billing']` and `PUBLIC_PATHS` = `['/', '/privacy', '/terms', '/login', '/signup', '/auth/reset', '/invite/not-a-real-token']` (the invite page renders a generic "you have been invited" page for any token under the mock env — 2.1b — so it belongs in the render checks; PLAN §8 lists it as reachable without a session).
4. **`apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`** — one `test.describe` per area, every test independent, no shared state, no sleeps (use `expect(...).toHaveURL`, `toBeVisible`, `toPass`):
   1. *Public pages render*: for each of `PUBLIC_PATHS`, `page.goto` → status 200, exactly one `h1` visible, `<html lang="en">`, a non-empty `<title>`, no `console.error` entries (collect via `page.on('console')`, ignore the known Next dev-only noise only if the app is running `next dev` — it is not, so expect zero), no failed requests to first-party URLs (`page.on('requestfailed')`; requests to `localhost:54321` may fail and are expected — filter them out and assert they never block rendering). For `/invite/not-a-real-token` additionally assert the body contains the deep link `anacast://invite/not-a-real-token` (the "Open in app" link from 2.1b) and a "Sign in" control.
   2. *Unauthenticated redirects*: for each of `PROTECTED_PATHS`, `page.goto(path)` ends at `/login?next=<encodeURIComponent(path)>`; `request.get(path, { maxRedirects: 0 })` returns 307 or 308 with a `location` header starting with `/login?next=`. Also assert `/other`, `/privacy` and `/s/unknown` are NOT redirected.
   3. *Login form validation*: on `/login` submit empty → the email field shows its error text (find the `aria-describedby` target or the shadcn `FormMessage`); type `not-an-email` → an invalid-email message; type a valid email and a password → the request to `localhost:54321` fails → the page shows the mapped generic error text from `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts` (read that module and assert the exact string, not a regex) and never a raw stack trace. Switch to the **Email code** tab of `/login` (2.1b builds tabs Password / Email code — read `src/features/auth/LoginForm.tsx` for the control name; PLAN §8 defines `/login` as "password + OTP", so the mode MUST exist — do not make this conditional); assert the 6-digit code field appears only after "Send code", and that submitting the email under the mock env shows the mapped generic error, never a stack trace. `/signup` gets the same empty-submit and invalid-email checks.
   4. *Share and embed*: `request.get('/s/unknown')` → 404 with `expectShareHeaders`; `page.goto('/s/unknown')` shows the "link not available" copy from 3.4b (read `app/(public)/s/[token]/page.tsx` for the exact text). `request.post('/api/share/unknown/unlock', { form: { password: 'whatever' } })` → 404 or 400 (read `app/api/share/[token]/unlock/route.ts` and assert the documented code), never 500. `request.get('/embed/yt/dQw4w9WgXcQ')` → 200, `expectEmbedHeaders` (NOT `expectShareHeaders` — the embed page carries `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, not `no-referrer`), body contains `youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ`; `/embed/yt/not-eleven-chars` → 404.
   5. *Security headers*: `expectStrictHeaders` on `/`, `/privacy`, `/login`, `/invite/not-a-real-token` and `/definitely-not-a-route`; for the `/admin` redirect assert only that the 307/308 has a `location` starting with `/login?next=` and — IF the response carries a `content-security-policy` header at all — that it satisfies `expectStrictHeaders` (redirects produced by `proxy.ts` do not reliably carry `next.config.ts` `headers()` entries; record in `e2e/README.md` whether they do on this build); `expectShareHeaders` on `/s/unknown`; `expectEmbedHeaders` on `/embed/yt/dQw4w9WgXcQ`. Assert `/privacy` HTML contains no `<script src=` pointing at a host other than the app itself (CSP `script-src` sanity).
   6. *Operational routes refuse strangers*: `GET /api/cron/tick` without header → 401 (mock `CRON_SECRET` is set); with `Authorization: Bearer wrong` → 401; `GET /api/cron/tick?secret=mock-cron-secret` → 401 (query string never accepted — 3.6b). `POST /api/stripe/webhook` with any body → 503 (no `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and the body says Stripe is not configured (read 2.3's route for the exact text). `POST /api/billing/checkout` and `POST /api/billing/portal`: read `app/api/billing/{checkout,portal}/route.ts` (2.3) first — the routes run a same-origin check BEFORE authentication and export `POST` only. Assert: `request.post(path, { data: {} })` with NO `Origin` header → 403 with JSON `{ error: 'bad_origin' }`; with header `Origin: <baseURL>` while signed out → 401 `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` (under the mock env the Stripe-configured check may instead answer 503 `{ error: 'stripe_not_configured' }` if it runs before auth — assert whichever order the route implements and say so in a comment); in every case the JSON `error` key is one of `bad_origin` / `unauthorized` / `stripe_not_configured`, never a 500 and never a redirect to `/login` (`proxy.ts` redirects only `/admin*` and `/o*` — API routes answer JSON themselves). `GET /auth/callback` without `code`/`token_hash` → 3xx to `/login` (2.1b redirects to `/login?error=auth` or the landing — read `app/(auth)/auth/callback/route.ts` and assert the documented target), never 500. `GET /api/cron/tick` response has `cache-control: no-store` if 3.6b set it (read the route; assert what it does).
   7. *No secret in HTML*: for `/`, `/login`, `/privacy`, `/invite/not-a-real-token`, `/s/unknown`, `/embed/yt/dQw4w9WgXcQ` the response body does not contain `sb_secret_`, `service_role`, `mock-cron-secret`, or the `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET` literal. Also fetch every `<script src>` of `/login` that is same-origin and assert the same on those chunks (the mock `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` value is unique enough to grep for).
   8. *Not found*: `/definitely-not-a-route` → 404 rendered by `app/not-found.tsx` (assert the copy), `expectStrictHeaders`.
5. **`apps/web/e2e/README.md`**: how to run (`pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke`; against a deployment `BASE_URL=https://<VERCEL_URL> pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke`), what the mock env is and why it is safe to commit, how to open the report, where 3.7b's full suite plugs in (`E2E_*` variables from `docs/ENV.md`), and the rule "a failing smoke test blocks a push; fix the app or the test in the same commit".
6. **CI.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` first change the 1.1 web-build step's mock env to EXACTLY the values in `apps/web/e2e/mock-env.ts` (in particular `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3100`, plus `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET`, `CRON_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=50` — `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are baked in at build time, so the build the smoke run reuses must have been made with the same values; put a comment in both files pointing at the other). Then add, after the web build step and guarded with `if: hashFiles('apps/web/playwright.config.ts') != ''`: `pnpm --filter web exec playwright install --with-deps chromium` (cache `~/.cache/ms-playwright` keyed on the Playwright version), then `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` with `CI=true`, then `actions/upload-artifact@v4` of `apps/web/playwright-report` with `if: failure()` and `retention-days: 7`. The workflow stays `continue-on-error: true` (step 1.1's decision) — do not make it blocking here; 3.8 documents the policy.
7. **Warning-free build.** Run `pnpm --filter web build` with the mock env and fix every warning the build prints (unused exports, `next/image` hints, `metadata` warnings, edge/node runtime notices, dynamic-server-usage messages caused by reading cookies in a static page). Fix the cause, never suppress with `eslint-disable` or `// @ts-expect-error`. Record the list of warnings you removed in `session_log.md`.
8. **Smoke-test hooks in the app, only where needed.** If an assertion needs a stable selector, prefer accessible roles and labels (`getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })`, `getByLabel('Email')`); add `data-testid` only when no accessible handle exists, named `<feature>-<element>` (for example `share-unavailable`). Never change behaviour to make a test pass; if a test exposes a real defect (a protected page not redirecting, a header missing, a 500 on an anonymous API call) fix the defect in the owning module and add a Vitest unit test next to the existing ones.

## Constraints
- Mock env only: no Supabase project, no Stripe key, no Resend key, no network. If a test needs a real backend it belongs in 3.7b's `full` project, not here.
- Do not add Playwright to Turbo's `test` task, do not run it in `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, and do not introduce `sleep`/`waitForTimeout` calls.
- Pins: `@playwright/test` 1.62 line; no other new runtime dependency. Chromium only (Firefox/WebKit are not installed on the founder's machines and add nothing for this app).
- Do not refactor pages, guards, headers or API routes beyond fixing a defect a test proved. Do not touch `supabase/`, `packages/*` behaviour, or mobile. Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- No real email address, key, token or domain in tests or docs — use the mock values and `<VERCEL_URL>`.
- Keep `continue-on-error: true` on the CI job (1.1 decided the workflow is informational).

- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (the e2e files are type-checked by `apps/web/tsconfig.json` — include `e2e/**/*.ts` and `playwright.config.ts` in it; exclude them from Vitest's `include`).

- `BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` with the server already running from `pnpm --filter web start -- --port 3100` → passes without starting a second server.
- After pushing, the GitHub Actions run shows the Playwright step executed (green) and no artifact was uploaded.

### 3.7b — Web QA — env-gated full E2E and security spec

## Constraints
- The full suite must be idempotent and self-cleaning: unique `tag` per run, `example.invalid` emails only, `afterAll` cleanup even when a step fails. Never touch rows whose slug or email lacks the run tag; `docs/QA_WEB.md` warns that it creates and deletes churches and auth users on whichever project `E2E_*` points at.
- Mock env and smoke tests stay network-free. `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must not run Playwright.
- Pins: `@playwright/test` 1.62 (already present). No new dependency in this step (`@axe-core/playwright` arrives in 3.7c); no `ffmpeg` requirement for anyone but the one-time fixture generation.
- Do not change RLS, migrations or `packages/*` behaviour; if the suite exposes a data-layer defect, describe it in HANDOFF under "Deviations from plan"/"Known issues" for a `9998_*` migration and mark the step as `test.fixme` with the reason — never `supabase db push`/`db reset`. Do not touch accessibility, loading/error files or empty states — that is 3.7c.
- Never write a real email, key or token into a spec, `.env.example`, docs or `prompt_history.txt`. If I have not given you `E2E_*` values, write and type-check the suite, run it only in its skipped mode, and tell me exactly what to export to run it.

7. **Needs-decision items**: build nothing; in the final message list each with (a) what I asked for, (b) the recorded decision it conflicts with (quote HANDOFF), (c) the cost of changing (schema? migration? mobile impact?), (d) your recommendation. If I decide in a later round, that round implements it and updates HANDOFF "Decisions".
8. **Docs.** For every fixed item update the doc that described the old behaviour (`docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`, `docs/QA_WEB.md`, `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `docs/BILLING.md`, `docs/RLS.md`, `docs/ENV.md`, `README.md`) — no orphaned descriptions. Add a `HANDOFF.md` section "Founder feedback rounds" (create if absent) with one entry per round: date, deployment, counts per class, list of fixed observation numbers with commit hashes, open `needs-decision` items, migrations pending paste.
9. **Commits.** One commit per coherent fix or per small group of polish items, each with a message `fix(web): <symptom> (founder feedback round <N>, #<observation numbers>)` (or `fix(db):` / `docs:` as appropriate), each pushed after green checks — I may stop you between commits. If the round is large (more than ~8 fixes), stop after the blockers and bugs, report, and let me start a "round <N>b" with the polish items.
10. **Regression sweep.** Re-run the relevant acceptance rows yourself where possible (mock env or local hosted `.env.local`), and add any new manual check to `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` so the next round covers it.
11. **Close the loop on the deployment.** After the last push, wait for the Vercel production deployment of `main` (ask me to confirm it shows Ready — you cannot see the dashboard), run `BASE_URL=https://<VERCEL_URL> pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` against it, and end your final message with the exact `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` row numbers I should re-run to confirm each fix — a fix that never reached the deployment I test is not done.

## Constraints
- Only the observations in scope; no refactors, no new features, no dependency upgrades, no theme redesign. If a fix genuinely requires a new dependency, say why in the commit body and pin it (PLAN §3 majors: TypeScript ~5.9, ESLint 9, Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, Playwright 1.62).
- Never weaken security to fix a symptom: no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secret, no service client in a page that a user-scoped client can serve, no permission check removed, no policy loosened without a SQL test proving the intended scope, no header dropped. Web never holds elevated Supabase keys; `srv_*` stays service-role only.
- Frozen `9999_init.sql`; new migrations re-runnable and hand-pasted; never `supabase db push`/`db reset`. Mobile untouched (M4). Do not edit `new_session_instructions.md`.
- No real email, key, token or domain in code, tests, docs or `prompt_history.txt`; if an observation I pasted contains one, redact it in `triage.md` (`<redacted>`) — `prompt_history.txt` keeps my prompt verbatim as the standing orders require, so warn me in the final message if I pasted a secret so I can rotate it.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm --filter web build` → zero warnings; `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green; `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full` → green if `E2E_*` is exported in this shell (say whether it ran).
- If a migration was added: `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → green, and `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh && git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts` → clean after committing the regenerated types.
- Each fixed observation has a test that fails on the previous commit and passes now (show the test name per observation in the triage table); `git log --oneline` shows one commit per fix with the observation numbers.
- `Session log/<this session>/triage.md` has a row for every observation I pasted with a final class and outcome; no row says "TODO".
- `grep -rn -E 'sk_test_[A-Za-z0-9]{8}|whsec_[A-Za-z0-9]{8}|price_[A-Za-z0-9]{8}|sb_secret_[A-Za-z0-9]{8}' apps packages docs 'Session log/<this session>/triage.md'` → nothing except the committed mock literal from 3.7a (the docs' format hints `whsec_…`, `price_…` use an ellipsis and never eight alphanumerics, so they do not match); `grep -rn -E '@(gmail|outlook|yahoo)\.' apps packages docs` → nothing.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: "Founder feedback rounds" entry for round <N>; Known issues updated (add unresolved items, remove fixed ones); ledger row(s) for any migration pending paste; State unchanged (3.10 is repeatable — tick it in `docs/TODO.md` after the first round and leave it ticked; later rounds only add HANDOFF entries).
- Write `session_log.md` (include the triage table), commit the final docs with `docs: founder feedback round <N> — triage and handoff`, push `main` (`git push origin main`) unless another branch was named.
- Final message: the triage table, the list of commits, the result of the post-deploy smoke run (Build 11), the acceptance rows to re-run, the migrations I must paste (if any), the `needs-decision` items with your recommendation, the observations you could not reproduce and what you need from me, and a warning if any pasted observation contained a secret.
````

- [ ] Every fixed observation has a regression test (Vitest, Playwright smoke or full, or SQL RLS test) that fails on the previous commit and passes on the fixing commit, and its commit message has the form `fix(web|db): <symptom> (founder feedback round <N>, #<numbers>)`.

- **Who:** Agent

- **Read first:** docs/PLAN.md §9 (auth screens, createMobileClient bullet), docs/DESIGN.md §5 (Supabase Auth, Tenancy, Getting accounts — invitation path), §10 (screen map, `no-church` wording, Auth bullet), §13 risk 7 (OTP template), packages/domain/src/schemas/{auth,invitation,context}.ts, src/urls.ts, src/errors.ts (1.6b); packages/db/src/rpc.ts and queries (1.7a) for `myContext`, `acceptInvitation`, `setLastOrg`, apps/web/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx and src/features/auth/LoginForm.tsx (2.1b) — the web counterparts to mirror, HANDOFF.md — Decisions, founder to-dos, apps/mobile (4.1a): src/lib/kv.ts, src/lib/query-client.ts, app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
- **Size:** M

**Goal.** A member can sign in to Anacast on Android: `(auth)/sign-in` asks for an email and sends a 6-digit code (`signInWithOtp`) with a password alternative, `(auth)/verify-otp` verifies it (`verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email' })`), `(auth)/invite/[token]` handles `anacast://invite/<token>` deep links (and `<APP_URL>/invite/<token>` once App Links land in 5.7) by storing the token, signing the person in and calling `accept_invitation`, `(auth)/no-church` tells users without an active membership to ask their church, and `(app)/_layout.tsx` gates every app screen on a session plus at least one `active` membership from `my_context()`, chooses the active organization (stored choice → `profile.last_org_id` → first active), persists switches with `setLastOrg`, and offers an org switcher when the user belongs to more than one church. The session gate in `app/index.tsx` routes signed-out users to sign-in, members to the tabs. Everything is verified by typecheck, unit tests of the pure pieces, `expo-doctor` and `expo export`.

## Goal
When you finish, the Expo app from 4.1a has a complete sign-in flow and a tenancy gate. A person opens the app, enters the email their church has on file, receives a 6-digit code (the founder edits the Supabase Magic Link template to include `{{ .Token }}` in step 2.4 — DESIGN §5: "otherwise `signInWithOtp` sends a link"), types the code and lands in the tabs of their church. People with a password can use it instead. A tap on an invitation deep link `anacast://invite/<token>` (from the web invite page's "Open in app" button built in 2.1b) carries the token through sign-in and accepts the invitation with `accept_invitation`. Users with an account but no active membership see the `no-church` screen. Members of several churches get a switcher; the choice persists locally and in `profiles.last_org_id`. No feed, no players, no push yet (4.2a, 4.2b, 4.3).

## Build
1. **Session provider** `src/features/auth/SessionProvider.tsx`: on mount `supabase.auth.getSession()`, then `onAuthStateChange((event, session) => …)`; expose `useSession()` → `{ session, userId, status: 'loading' | 'signed_out' | 'signed_in' }`. On `SIGNED_OUT` clear `active_org_id` from kv and call `queryClient.clear()` (the persisted cache must not leak one account's feed to the next). Mount it inside `app/_layout.tsx` under `AppQueryProvider`. Keep the splash screen up until `status !== 'loading'`.
2. **Context query** `src/features/auth/useMyContext.ts`: `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.context(), queryFn: () => myContext(supabase), enabled: status === 'signed_in', staleTime: 60_000 })`; export `activeOrgs(ctx)` = orgs with `membership_status === 'active'` (pure, tested); `refreshContext()` = `invalidateQueries(queryKeys.context())`.
3. **`(auth)/sign-in`** (`app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx`, `src/features/auth/SignInForm.tsx`, react-native-paper inputs, `react-hook-form` is NOT used on mobile — keep plain controlled inputs validated with the Zod schemas): title "Sign in to Anacast"; email field; primary button "Email me a code" → validate with `otpRequestSchema` → `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: <see rule> } })` → on success `router.push({ pathname: '/(auth)/verify-otp', params: { email } })`. Rule for `shouldCreateUser` (a 4.1b decision — the docs are silent): `true` when a `pending_invite_token` exists in kv (an invited person may have no auth account yet — DESIGN §5 "Getting accounts" item 1 sends the invitation to an email address, `accept_invitation` creates the household/person on first acceptance, and PLAN §9 gives mobile no signup screen, so the invite is the only way an account can be born on the phone), otherwise `false`, and the resulting Supabase error ("Signups not allowed for otp") is mapped to "No Anacast account uses this email yet. Ask your church for an invitation." Secondary link "Use a password instead" reveals a password field and swaps the button to "Sign in" → `emailPasswordSchema` → `signInWithPassword`; wrong credentials → "Email or password is incorrect" (never leak which). Link "Forgot password?" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${publicEnv().webUrl}/auth/reset`)` (password reset stays on the web, DESIGN §5). Footer: "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" linking to `${webUrl}/terms` and `${webUrl}/privacy`. Disable buttons while pending; show `DomainError`/auth messages inline, never raw error objects. Rate-limit friendliness: after a successful send, disable "Email me a code" for 60 s (Supabase default OTP throttle) and say so.
4. **`(auth)/verify-otp`** (`app/(auth)/verify-otp.tsx`, `src/features/auth/OtpForm.tsx`): reads `email` from `useLocalSearchParams`; a single 6-digit numeric field (`keyboardType: 'number-pad'`, `autoComplete: 'one-time-code'`, `textContentType: 'oneTimeCode'`); auto-submits at 6 digits → `otpVerifySchema` → `supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email' })`; on success the session provider fires and `app/index.tsx` routes on; expired/invalid → "That code is wrong or has expired" with a "Send a new code" button (60 s cooldown, same `signInWithOtp` call). Help text: "Look for an email from your church's Anacast service. The code expires in a few minutes." (the exact expiry is set by the founder in 2.4 — do not hard-code minutes). "Use a different email" → back.
5. **`(auth)/invite/[token]`** (`app/(auth)/invite/[token].tsx`, `src/features/auth/useAcceptInvitation.ts`): reached by `anacast://invite/<token>` (expo-router maps the scheme URL to this route automatically; verify with `npx uri-scheme open "anacast://invite/abc" --android` in the docs, and with a unit test of the pure parser below). Validate with `invitationTokenSchema`; malformed → friendly "This invitation link is not valid" + "Go to sign in" (never crash). Signed out → `setKv('pending_invite_token', token)` and `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')` with an inline notice "Sign in with the email address the invitation was sent to". Signed in → call `acceptInvitation(supabase, { token })`: success → `deleteKv('pending_invite_token')`, `refreshContext()`, set active org to the returned `org_id` (Build 7's `switchOrg`), `router.replace('/(app)/(tabs)/home')`, toast "Welcome to <org name>"; `invitation_email_mismatch` → explain that the signed-in email differs, offer "Sign out and try again"; `invitation_expired`/`invitation_invalid` → message from `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES` + "Ask your church for a new invitation"; `organization_suspended` → its message. The same hook runs once from `app/index.tsx` when a session appears and `pending_invite_token` exists (the post-sign-in resume path).
6. **`(auth)/no-church`** (`app/(auth)/no-church.tsx`): "You are signed in as <email>. Your account is not linked to a church yet." (two sentences added here) followed by the DESIGN §10 sentence verbatim: "Ask your church to invite you or create your account"; buttons "Check again" (`refreshContext()`), "Sign out". If `ctx.is_super_admin` is true (the founder at Checkpoint C has an auth account but no membership until he adds himself), append: "You are a super admin. To use the app, make yourself a member of a church on the web: `/o/<slug>/users` → Invite → your own email → open the link in the browser where you are signed in → Accept, then tap Check again." (Invite, not Create account — his email already has an auth account, so `createUserDirect` would fail.) If any org has `membership_status === 'pending'`, add "Your request to join <name> is waiting for approval" (Phase 2 join requests, 5.6, will add join-code entry here — leave a `TODO(5.6)` comment, no UI).
7. **Active organization** `src/features/org/ActiveOrgProvider.tsx` + `useActiveOrg()`: input = `activeOrgs(ctx)`; resolution order: kv `active_org_id` if still active → `ctx.profile.last_org_id` if active → first active org (sorted by name). Exposes `{ org: { org_id, slug, name, status }, permissions, personId, householdId, orgs, switchOrg(orgId) }`. `switchOrg` sets kv, updates state, calls `setLastOrg(supabase, userId, orgId)` (fire-and-forget with error toast), invalidates every query key that is org-scoped (`queryClient.invalidateQueries()` is acceptable here). `status === 'suspended'` → render a persistent read-only banner "This church's Anacast account is suspended; content may be out of date" (reads still work — DESIGN §5 "reads stay available"). The provider is mounted in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` only.
8. **Gate** with `Stack.Protected` (expo-router ~57.0.18, PLAN §3, always has it — do not build a second `Redirect`-based gate): `app/(app)/_layout.tsx`: `useSession()` + `useMyContext()`; while loading → `LoadingState`; then `<Stack.Protected guard={status === 'signed_in' && activeOrgs(ctx).length > 0}>` wrapping `(tabs)` and the stack screens (`sermons/[id]`, `announcements/[id]`, `bulletins/index`, `bulletins/[id]`, `settings/notifications`, headers titled by the org name where sensible), inside `ActiveOrgProvider`; when the guard is false expo-router redirects to the anchor, which is `app/index.tsx`. `app/(auth)/_layout.tsx`: a `Stack` with a plain header whose screens are guarded by the inverse (`status !== 'signed_in' || activeOrgs(ctx).length === 0`) EXCEPT `invite/[token]`, which stays reachable when signed in (Build 5). `app/index.tsx` only: shows the splash while `status === 'loading'` or the context query is pending; runs Build 5's pending-invite resume once when a session exists and `pending_invite_token` is set; then `<Redirect>`s — signed out → `/(auth)/sign-in`; signed in without an active org → `/(auth)/no-church`; signed in with one → `/(app)/(tabs)/home`. Routing logic lives in the two guards and `app/index.tsx`, nowhere else.

10. **Sign-out helper** `src/features/auth/signOut.ts`: `signOutEverywhere()` → placeholder call `await beforeSignOut()` (4.3 registers push-device deletion here — export a `registerBeforeSignOut(fn)` hook so 4.3 does not edit this file's logic), `supabase.auth.signOut()`, kv cleanup (`active_org_id`, `pending_invite_token`), `queryClient.clear()`, `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')`. Used by `no-church` now and by More/sign-out in 4.3.
11. **Deep-link parsing (pure, tested)** `src/lib/links.ts`: `parseAppLink(url)` → `{ kind: 'invite', token } | { kind: 'unknown' }` for `anacast://invite/<token>` and `https://<any host>/invite/<token>` (App Links arrive in 5.7 — the parser is ready now), using `invitationTokenSchema`; used by an `Linking.useURL()` effect in `app/_layout.tsx` only for the https form (expo-router already routes the scheme form). `src/lib/links.test.ts` covers both forms, a malformed token, and an unrelated URL.

No component tests (no jsdom for RN in this step).

### 4.2a — Mobile feed — home (announcements + current bulletin), announcement detail, bulletins list/detail with Android PDF open, signed-URL hook

- **Who:** Agent
- **Depends on:** 4.1b, 3.5b

**Goal.** The signed-in member sees their church's content: `(tabs)/home` lists pinned then recent published announcements (`listFeed`) with a 'This week's bulletin' card (`getCurrentBulletin` for today in the church's timezone), `announcements/[id]` shows the full text, `bulletins/index` lists published bulletins and `bulletins/[id]` opens the file — PDFs are downloaded to the cache and handed to Android with `expo-intent-launcher` ACTION_VIEW, images render inline with `expo-image`. A shared `useSignedUrl(bucket, path)` hook mints 1-hour signed URLs, caches them 50 minutes, never persists them, and re-mints on demand — the same hook 4.2b's players use. Pull-to-refresh, offline (persisted cache) rendering and empty/error states are in place; verified by unit tests, typecheck, `expo-doctor` and `expo export`.

## Goal
When you finish, a member who signs in on Android (4.1b) lands on a Home tab that shows their church's pinned and recent announcements and the current bulletin, can open any announcement, can browse the bulletin archive from the stack route `bulletins/index` (linked from Home now and from the More tab in 4.3), and can open a bulletin file: PDFs download to the app cache and open in the phone's PDF viewer through an Android intent; JPG/PNG bulletins display inline. The `useSignedUrl` hook created here is the single way the app turns a `storage_path` into a playable/downloadable URL (1 h signed URL, 50 min cache, never persisted to disk, re-mint on 403 or expiry) and is reused by 4.2b's sermon players. Content is read-only; everything is scoped to the active org from 4.1b and RLS decides what the member may see (only published rows reach a member — `publish_at <= now()` is enforced in policies, PLAN §1 item 6).

6. **Bulletin detail + open** `app/(app)/bulletins/[id].tsx` + `src/features/bulletins/BulletinDetail.tsx` + `src/features/bulletins/OpenPdf.ts` (name fixed by DESIGN §11 step 10): shows title, range, size, and a primary button "Open bulletin". `openBulletinFile({ bucket: 'bulletins', path, mimeType, fileName })`: (a) `getSignedUrl('bulletins', path)`; (b) download with `import * as FileSystem from 'expo-file-system/legacy'` — use the legacy API for the WHOLE flow: `FileSystem.downloadAsync(url, FileSystem.cacheDirectory + fileName)` then (c) `FileSystem.getContentUriAsync(uri)` for the intent (the SDK 54+ object API `File`/`Paths` has no `getContentUriAsync`; do not mix the two APIs; if the installed version has no `/legacy` subpath — SDK < 54 only — import from `expo-file-system` directly); overwrite an existing cached file; Android: `IntentLauncher.startActivityAsync('android.intent.action.VIEW', { data: contentUri, flags: 1 /* FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION */, type: mimeType })`; when no activity can handle it (`ActivityNotFoundException`) → toast "No PDF viewer is installed. Opening in the browser instead." and `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl)`; (d) iOS (untested until Phase 3, DESIGN §7 "iOS renders natively"): `expo-sharing` `shareAsync(localUri)` or `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl)` — pick one, comment it `Phase 3 (6.4) verifies`. Images (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`): render inline with `expo-image` (`contentFit: 'contain'`, pinch-zoom not required) plus a "Share" button using `expo-sharing`. Show a progress indicator during download (files are ≤ 25 MiB, `BUCKETS.bulletins`); on 403/expired → `remint()` once and retry, then a friendly error. Files stay in `cacheDirectory` (OS may purge); delete the previous file for the same bulletin before downloading a new one.
7. **No analytics or tracking** in the app (privacy; the Play Data Safety worksheet in 6.3 must be able to say so). **Accessibility**: cards are `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"` and labels; text sizes respect the system font scale.

Mock `@church/db` queries and `expo-*` modules in tests (`vi.mock`), no jsdom.
9. **Docs**: add a "Mobile playback and files" section to `apps/mobile/README.md` (signed URL lifetime, cache, PDF intent) — `docs/MEDIA.md` itself is written in 4.4.

## Goal
When you finish, the Sermons tab lists the active church's published sermons and a sermon page plays them. The player has exactly four strategies, chosen by the shared parser and the sermon's `media_kind`: (1) `expo-audio` for uploaded audio and audio streams — plays in the background with lock-screen/notification controls; (2) `expo-video` for uploaded video and video streams — fullscreen and picture-in-picture; (3) `react-native-webview` loading OUR hosted page `/embed/yt/[id]` (built on the web in 3.4b) for YouTube, because YouTube's embed player needs a valid referer that a bare WebView cannot supply (PLAN §1 item 5), with an "Open in YouTube" button; (4) `expo-web-browser` for Google Drive and any link the parser marks `open_external`. Uploaded media never leaves Supabase Storage: the app mints a signed URL with 4.2a's hook and re-mints once when the URL expires or the server answers 403. No downloads for offline listening (Phase 4 idea), no share links (web only), no upload (web only).

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a/4.1b/4.2a produced: `supabase`, `useActiveOrg()`, `useSignedUrl(bucket, path)` → `{ url, expiresAt, isExpired, remint }` (never persisted), `Screen`/`LoadingState`/`ErrorState`/`EmptyState`, `LinkifiedText`, `publicEnv().webUrl`, the tabs layout, placeholders `app/(app)/(tabs)/sermons.tsx` and `app/(app)/sermons/[id].tsx`. 4.1a already installed with `npx expo install`: `expo-audio`, `expo-video`, `react-native-webview`, `expo-web-browser`, `expo-image`; `app.config.ts` has the plugins `['expo-video', { supportsBackgroundPlayback: true }]` and `['expo-audio', { recordAudioAndroid: false, enableBackgroundPlayback: true }]` (DESIGN §10).
- `@church/domain` (1.6a): `parseMediaLink(url, platform: 'web' | 'mobile')` → `{ ok: true, kind, externalId?, canonicalUrl, embedUrl?, streamUrl?, strategy: 'youtube_hosted_embed' | 'native_stream' | 'webview' | 'open_external' } | { ok: false, reason }` (DESIGN §7: YouTube on mobile → `youtube_hosted_embed`; Dropbox `raw=1` mp3/m4a/aac/mp4/m4v → `native_stream` else `open_external`; Google Drive on mobile → `open_external`; other https mp3/m4a/mp4/m3u8 → `native_stream` else `open_external`). The hosted-embed URL builders are fixed by 1.6a/1.6b: `youtubeHostedEmbedPath(id)` → `/embed/yt/<id>` in `packages/domain/src/media-links.ts` and `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(appUrl, id)` = `appUrl + youtubeHostedEmbedPath(id)` (trailing slash of `appUrl` trimmed) in `packages/domain/src/urls.ts` — 1.6b names 4.2's WebView as its consumer and 3.4b builds the same URL on the web. The WebView `source.uri` is therefore `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(publicEnv().webUrl, videoId)`; never hand-write the `/embed/yt/` path and never add a second builder.
- `@church/db` (1.7a): `queries/sermons.ts` — `listSermons(db, orgId, { drafts, query, limit, offset })`, `getSermon(db, id)`; sermon columns (1.2, read `database.types.ts`; `media_kind` is the enum `'upload' | 'youtube' | 'dropbox' | 'google_drive' | 'url'` from PLAN §4 / DESIGN §4.1 — there is no `gdrive` or `other`): `title, speaker, preached_on, series, scripture_refs, description, media_kind, storage_path, mime_type, file_size_bytes, duration_seconds, external_url, external_id, publish_at`; `queryKeys.sermons.list(orgId, filters)`, `.sermons.detail(id)`; bucket `sermon-media` (paths `{org_id}/sermons/{sermon_id}/{uuid}.{ext}`).
- Web 3.3a's `SermonPlayer` (`apps/web/src/features/sermons/SermonPlayer.tsx`) implements the same dispatch for the web — read it for the prop shape (`{ sermon, media, onRemint, variant }`) and mirror the naming; 3.4b's hosted page `apps/web/app/(public)/embed/yt/[id]/page.tsx` — or `apps/web/app/(share)/embed/yt/[id]/page.tsx` if 3.4b had to move it out of a `(public)` layout with chrome; find it with `git ls-files 'apps/web/app/*/embed/yt/*'` and HANDOFF records the group name — renders a `youtube-nocookie` iframe on a black full-viewport page and validates the 11-character id; this is the page the WebView loads (the URL is `/embed/yt/<id>` either way).

## Build
1. **Sermons list** `app/(app)/(tabs)/sermons.tsx` + `src/features/sermons/SermonList.tsx` + `src/features/sermons/useSermons.ts`: `useInfiniteQuery` over `listSermons(supabase, orgId, { drafts: false, query, limit: 25, offset })` keyed `queryKeys.sermons.list(orgId, { query })` (RLS already hides drafts and future `publish_at` from members; pass `drafts: false` anyway); a search field (debounced 300 ms, `title`/`speaker`/`series` as the helper supports — do not add client-side filtering over the whole table); rows show title, speaker, `preached_on` (org date helpers from `@church/domain` `dates.ts`), series, a kind icon (audio / video / YouTube / link), `duration_seconds` as `mm:ss` when present; pull-to-refresh; empty state "No sermons yet"; load-more footer. Tap → `sermons/[id]`.
2. **Sermon detail** `app/(app)/sermons/[id].tsx` + `src/features/sermons/SermonDetail.tsx`: `getSermon(supabase, id)` (`queryKeys.sermons.detail(id)`, `initialData` from the list cache); title, speaker, date, series, `scripture_refs`, description via `LinkifiedText`; the player area at the top; 404/RLS → "This sermon is not available". Cold-start safe (only `id`).
3. **Dispatcher (pure, tested)** `src/features/sermons/playerStrategy.ts`: `resolvePlayer(sermon)` → `{ kind: 'audio', source: { bucket: 'sermon-media', path } } | { kind: 'video', source: { bucket, path } } | { kind: 'audio_url' | 'video_url', url } | { kind: 'youtube', videoId, canonicalUrl } | { kind: 'webview', url, canonicalUrl } | { kind: 'external', url } | { kind: 'unsupported', reason }`. Rules: `media_kind === 'upload'` → audio when `mime_type` starts with `audio/`, video when `video/` (fallback by `storage_path` extension: mp3/m4a/aac/ogg/wav → audio; mp4/mov/webm/m4v → video); every other `media_kind` (`youtube`, `dropbox`, `google_drive`, `url`) → `parseMediaLink(external_url, 'mobile')` (the parser, not `media_kind`, decides the strategy — `media_kind` only labels the provider for icons and the External card): `youtube_hosted_embed` → `youtube` (`externalId`); `native_stream` → `audio_url`/`video_url` by the `streamUrl` extension (m3u8 → video); `webview` → `webview` (`embedUrl`); `open_external` → `external` (`canonicalUrl`); `ok: false` or missing URL → `unsupported`. Table-driven Vitest with rows using the real enum values: `youtube` + a watch URL, `youtube` + `youtu.be`, `dropbox` + a `dl=0` mp3, `dropbox` + a pdf, `google_drive` + a `/file/d/<id>/view` URL, `url` + an https m4a, `url` + an https m3u8, `url` + an https html page, `upload` mp3, `upload` mp4, and a row with neither path nor URL.
4. **`SermonPlayer`** `src/features/sermons/SermonPlayer.tsx`: takes `{ sermon }`, calls `resolvePlayer`, and renders one of `src/features/sermons/players/Audio.tsx`, `players/Video.tsx`, `players/YouTubeWebView.tsx`, `players/External.tsx` (exact basenames from DESIGN §11 step 10 — no `AudioPlayer.tsx`/`VideoPlayer.tsx` variants). For `audio`/`video` (uploads) wrap the player in `SignedMedia` (`src/features/sermons/SignedMedia.tsx`): `useSignedUrl(bucket, path)` → passes `url` down and an `onSourceError()` callback; on the first error (expo-audio/expo-video status error, or a probe `fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD' })` returning 403) it calls `remint()` and re-renders the player with the new URL once; a second failure shows "Playback failed — pull to refresh or try again later". Never store the signed URL anywhere but component state/query cache.
5. **`players/Audio.tsx`** (`expo-audio`): on mount `setAudioModeAsync({ shouldPlayInBackground: true, playsInSilentMode: true, interruptionMode: 'doNotMix', shouldRouteThroughEarpiece: false })` (DESIGN §10 wording: `shouldPlayInBackground: true, playsInSilentMode: true`); `const player = useAudioPlayer({ uri })`, `useAudioPlayerStatus(player)`; controls: play/pause, −15 s / +30 s, a seek slider (`react-native-paper`'s or a plain `Slider` from a package already installed — do NOT add `@react-native-community/slider` unless you `npx expo install` it and record it), current time / duration, playback rate (1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2× via `player.setPlaybackRate(rate, 'high')`), buffering indicator. Lock-screen and notification controls: use the API that the installed `expo-audio` 57 typings expose for now-playing metadata (search the package's `build/*.d.ts` for `setActiveForLockScreen` / `NowPlaying` / `metadata`); set title = sermon title, artist = speaker, album = org name. If the installed version has no such API, keep background playback (already enabled by the config plugin) and record "lock-screen controls pending expo-audio API" under Deviations. Release the player on unmount (`player.remove()` or the hook's cleanup) — only one sermon plays at a time; navigating to another sermon stops the previous one.
6. **`players/Video.tsx`** (`expo-video`): `const player = useVideoPlayer({ uri }, p => { p.staysActiveInBackground = true; p.showNowPlayingNotification = true })`; `<VideoView player={player} nativeControls allowsFullscreen allowsPictureInPicture contentFit="contain" style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />`; `useEvent(player, 'statusChange')` to surface errors to `SignedMedia`. Add `startsPictureInPictureAutomatically` only if the installed typings have it.
7. **`players/YouTubeWebView.tsx`**: `<WebView source={{ uri: hostedEmbedUrl }} allowsInlineMediaPlayback mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false} javaScriptEnabled domStorageEnabled allowsFullscreenVideo originWhitelist={[webOrigin, 'https://www.youtube-nocookie.com', 'https://www.youtube.com']} onShouldStartLoadWithRequest={(req) => req.url.startsWith(webOrigin) || req.url.includes('youtube')} style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />` where `const hostedEmbedUrl = youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(publicEnv().webUrl, videoId)` and `webOrigin = new URL(publicEnv().webUrl).origin` (this page supplies the referer YouTube requires — PLAN §1 item 5; do NOT load `youtube.com/embed` directly and do NOT add `react-native-youtube-iframe`, DESIGN §3); below it a button "Open in YouTube" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(canonicalUrl)`; helper text "Unlisted videos work; private videos and videos with embedding disabled do not" (DESIGN §7). YouTube playback stops when the app is backgrounded (YouTube ToS, DESIGN §7): the WebView player requests no background mode and no lock-screen controls, and shows no caption about it.
8. **`players/External.tsx`**: card with provider name (from `media_kind`: `google_drive` → "Google Drive", `dropbox` → "Dropbox", `youtube` → "YouTube", `url` → the host), the host, and a primary button "Open" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(url, { presentationStyle: 'fullScreen' })`; for Google Drive add "Google Drive may ask you to sign in" (DESIGN §7 mobile → `open_external`). `webview` strategy (reserved by the parser for future providers) renders a plain `WebView` on `embedUrl` with the same origin guard.
9. **`unsupported`**: an `ErrorState` "This sermon cannot be played on this device" with the canonical URL as a fallback link when one exists.
10. **Screen behaviour**: keep the screen awake while audio/video plays (`expo-keep-awake` is bundled with `expo` — `useKeepAwake()` only while playing; skip if it is not in the installed `expo` package); stop playback when the user signs out (subscribe to the 4.1b `registerBeforeSignOut` hook to `player.pause()`); Android back from fullscreen video returns to the page, not the tab.
11. **Tests**: `playerStrategy.test.ts` (table above), `formatDuration.test.ts` (`mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`), and a one-case `YouTubeWebView.source.test.ts` asserting the WebView `source.uri` equals `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(webUrl, id)` for a `webUrl` with and without a trailing slash (the builder itself is tested in 1.6b — do not re-test it). Mock Expo modules with `vi.mock`.
12. **README**: extend `apps/mobile/README.md` "Mobile playback and files" with the four strategies and the referer explanation; `docs/MEDIA.md` proper is 4.4.

### 4.3 — Push & deep links

- **Who:** Agent
- **Depends on:** 4.2b, 3.6b
- **Read first:** docs/PLAN.md §1 item 6 (fan-out), §7 (Push row), §9 (Push bullet), docs/DESIGN.md §4 (Notifications & devices), §6 (push_devices / notification_preferences policies), §8 (Push fan-out row), §10 (Push bullet, More tab contents), §13 risk 5, apps/web/src/lib/push/dispatch.ts (3.6a) — the message/data contract; packages/domain/src/urls.ts `notificationTargetPath` (added by 3.6a) and schemas/notifications.ts (1.6b); packages/db/src/queries/notifications.ts and keys.ts (1.7a); packages/db/src/database.types.ts (push_devices, notification_preferences), HANDOFF.md — Decisions, founder to-dos, apps/mobile/src/features/auth/signOut.ts (`registerBeforeSignOut`, 4.1b) and apps/mobile/src/lib/kv.ts (4.1a)
- **Size:** M
- **Commit:** `feat(mobile): push registration, notification deep links, notification settings, More tab`

**Goal.** The app registers for push and reacts to it: after the first sign-in an explainer asks permission, the Android channel `announcements` (importance high) is created, `requestPermissionsAsync` runs (POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+), `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` obtains the Expo token and the device is upserted into `push_devices` (deleted again on sign-out); a notification tap or cold start with a notification response reads `data.url` + `data.org_id` written by the web dispatcher (3.6a), switches the active org when needed and routes to `/announcements/<id>` or `/bulletins/<id>`; `settings/notifications` edits the per-church `notification_preferences` (announcements, bulletins) and shows device/permission status; the More tab gets its real rows (Bulletins, Notification settings, Switch church, Sign out, privacy/terms, version). Registration is skipped gracefully on emulators and in Expo Go, errors never block the app, and the pure pieces are unit-tested.

Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a member who signs in on a real Android device built with EAS (step 4.5) is asked once whether Anacast may notify them; if they agree, the device appears in `public.push_devices` and, when a leader publishes an announcement or uploads a bulletin on the web, the dispatcher from 3.6a sends a push that lands on the phone; tapping it opens the right announcement or bulletin in the right church, even from a cold start. Members control which kinds they receive per church on `settings/notifications`, and signing out removes the device row so a shared phone never keeps receiving another person's church news. The More tab becomes the real menu (Bulletins, Notification settings, Switch church, Sign out, Privacy / Terms links, app version). DESIGN §10: "Android push requires the dev client / EAS build (not Expo Go)" — the code must detect and explain that, never crash.

Policies (DESIGN §6): both tables `user_id = auth.uid()` for all ops — the app writes its own rows directly through the query helpers; `remove_membership` deletes the user's `push_devices`/`notification_preferences` for that org server-side.

Check whether `upsertPushDevice` sets `enabled: true` on conflict (a device that receipts disabled must come back on re-registration — Build 3); if it only writes the three columns, extend it additively in `packages/db/src/queries/notifications.ts` (`enabled: true, last_seen_at: now`) with a unit test and record it in HANDOFF.
- `@church/domain` (1.6b): `schemas/notifications.ts` — `registerPushDeviceSchema` (`expo_push_token` matching `^Expo(nent)?PushToken\[.+\]$`, `platform`, `device_name` optional) and `notificationPreferencesSchema` (`org_id`, `announcements`, `bulletins`, `events`, `surveys`); `urls.ts` — `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` → `/announcements/<id>`, `/bulletins/<id>`, `/events/<id>`, `/surveys/<id>` (added to `urls.ts` additively by 3.6a, not by 1.6b: "the app-relative route the mobile app (4.3) pushes after switching to `org_id`").
