## Build
1. **Notification handler & channel** `src/lib/push.ts`: at module load `Notifications.setNotificationHandler({ handleNotification: async () => ({ shouldShowBanner: true, shouldShowList: true, shouldPlaySound: true, shouldSetBadge: false }) })` (use the property names the installed `expo-notifications` typings expose — `shouldShowAlert` on older ones). `ensureAndroidChannel()`: `Platform.OS === 'android'` → `setNotificationChannelAsync('announcements', { name: 'Announcements', importance: AndroidImportance.HIGH, sound: 'default', vibrationPattern: [0, 250, 250, 250] })` — the id must equal the dispatcher's `channelId: 'announcements'`.
2. **Capability check (pure, tested)** `src/lib/push-capability.ts` (a sibling FILE — do not create a `src/lib/push/` directory next to `src/lib/push.ts`, which DESIGN §11 step 10 names; UI hooks live under `src/features/push/*`): `pushCapability({ isDevice, appOwnership, executionEnvironment, projectId, platform })` → `'ok' | 'emulator' | 'expo_go' | 'missing_project_id' | 'unsupported_platform'` from `Platform.OS` (anything other than `'android'` or `'ios'` — web, windows, macos — is `unsupported_platform`, because `push_platform` is exactly `android | ios` and `registerPushDeviceSchema` would otherwise reject the row at runtime with an opaque validation error), `Device.isDevice`, `Constants.appOwnership === 'expo'` / `Constants.executionEnvironment === 'storeClient'`, and `projectId = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId ?? Constants.easConfig?.projectId` (DESIGN §10). Messages: emulator → "Push notifications need a physical device"; expo_go → "Push needs the Anacast app build (not Expo Go)"; missing_project_id → "This build has no EAS project id — see docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md" (developer-facing, shown only in dev builds; in production log it and stay silent); unsupported_platform → silent skip.
3. **Registration** in `src/lib/push.ts`, written as a pure state machine over injected dependencies so the unit tests need no native mocks: `registerForPush(deps, { userId })` where `deps: PushDeps = { notifications: { getPermissionsAsync, requestPermissionsAsync, getExpoPushTokenAsync, setNotificationChannelAsync }, device: { isDevice, modelName }, constants: { appOwnership, executionEnvironment, projectId }, platform: 'android' | 'ios' | string, upsertDevice(row), deleteDevice(token), kv: { get, set, delete }, now(): number }`; export `defaultPushDeps()` that binds the real `expo-notifications`, `expo-device`, `expo-constants`, `Platform.OS`, `upsertPushDevice(supabase, userId, …)`, `deletePushDevice(supabase, …)` and `src/lib/kv.ts` — screens call `registerForPush(defaultPushDeps(), { userId })`. Flow: capability check (`unsupported_platform`/`emulator`/`expo_go`/`missing_project_id` → `{ status: 'unsupported', reason }`) → `ensureAndroidChannel()` → `getPermissionsAsync()`; if `undetermined` (or `canAskAgain`) → `requestPermissionsAsync()` (this is the Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt); `denied` → return `{ status: 'denied' }`; `granted` → `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` → validate `{ expo_push_token: token.data, platform, device_name: modelName ?? undefined }` (with `platform` typed `'android' | 'ios'` — the capability check already excluded everything else) with `registerPushDeviceSchema` → `upsertDevice(row)` (the upsert must set `enabled: true` and `last_seen_at = now()` on conflict — see Inputs) → if kv `push_token` holds a DIFFERENT old token, `deleteDevice(oldToken)` (Expo push tokens rotate; a stale row would otherwise keep receiving `DeviceNotRegistered`) → `kv.set('push_token', token.data)` → return `{ status: 'registered', token }`. Errors (network, RLS, invalid token) → `{ status: 'error', message }` — never throw into the UI tree. `refreshPushDevice(deps, { userId })`: on every signed-in app start and foreground (`AppState` → `active`), throttled to once per 24 h via the kv timestamp `push_last_seen_sync`: if permission is `granted`, call `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` AGAIN (do not trust the stored token); if it differs from kv `push_token`, `deleteDevice(oldToken)` then upsert the new one; always upsert with `enabled: true` and `last_seen_at = now()` so a device that receipts disabled (`DeviceNotRegistered` after a reinstall) is re-enabled and the row stays fresh; then `kv.set('push_last_seen_sync', String(now()))`. Both functions are what makes Checkpoint C items "the row comes back" and "reinstall re-enables" true.
4. **Explainer** `app/(app)/push-explainer.tsx` (modal presentation in the `(app)` stack) + `src/features/push/usePushOnboarding.ts`: after the org gate passes and `push_explainer_seen` is unset and capability is `ok`, present once: "Get notified when <org name> posts an announcement or a bulletin" with "Turn on notifications" (→ `registerForPush`; on `denied` show how to enable in system settings via `Linking.openSettings()`) and "Not now" — both set `push_explainer_seen = 'true'`. Never show it in Expo Go or on emulators (capability ≠ ok → mark seen and skip). Silent path, independent of the explainer: whenever a session exists, capability is `ok`, permission is already `granted` and kv `push_token` is EMPTY (fresh install with a previously granted permission, after a sign-out, or a second account on a shared phone — `push_explainer_seen` is already set in those cases, so the modal alone would never bring the device back), call `registerForPush` silently — no modal. When a session exists and kv `push_token` is set, run `refreshPushDevice` instead (Build 3).
5. **Sign-out cleanup** `src/features/push/signOutCleanup.ts`: export `installPushSignOutCleanup(deps = defaultPushDeps())` which calls `registerBeforeSignOut(async () => { const token = await deps.kv.get('push_token'); if (token) { await deps.deleteDevice(token).catch(noop); await deps.kv.delete('push_token'); } await deps.kv.delete('push_last_seen_sync'); await Notifications.dismissAllNotificationsAsync().catch(noop); })` — the delete runs BEFORE `auth.signOut()` (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()` needs the session). A module-level side effect would run only if something imported the module, so the install is EXPLICIT: call `installPushSignOutCleanup()` exactly once from the mount effect of `useNotificationNavigation` (Build 7, mounted in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` after the org gate), guarded by a module flag so re-mounts do not register twice. The unit test asserts `registerBeforeSignOut` was called with a function that calls `deleteDevice(token)` and clears the kv keys before `auth.signOut()` would run.
6. **Deep-link resolution (pure, tested)** `src/lib/deep-links.ts` (file name from DESIGN §11 step 10): `resolveNotificationTarget(data: unknown, ctx: { activeOrgId, orgIds })` → `{ kind: 'navigate', orgId, path } | { kind: 'ignore', reason }`: accept only `data.url` matching `^/(announcements|bulletins|events|surveys)/[0-9a-f-]{36}$` (the four shapes of `notificationTargetPath`) and `data.org_id` a uuid the user actively belongs to (`orgIds`); `events`/`surveys` → for now `ignore` with reason `not_built` (5.3 / 6.1 lift this); anything else → `ignore` (`bad_payload`, `not_member`). Never navigate on attacker-controlled arbitrary URLs.
7. **Response handling** `src/features/push/useNotificationNavigation.ts`, mounted once in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` after the org gate (its mount effect also calls `installPushSignOutCleanup()` from Build 5 and kicks off Build 4's silent-registration / `refreshPushDevice` decision): (a) `Notifications.addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` (warm taps); (b) cold start — `Notifications.getLastNotificationResponseAsync()` (or the `useLastNotificationResponse` hook) once per app launch, deduplicated by `notification.request.identifier` stored in memory; for each → `resolveNotificationTarget(response.notification.request.content.data, …)`; on `navigate`: if `orgId !== activeOrgId` → `await switchOrg(orgId)`; then `router.push(path)` (expo-router maps `/announcements/<id>` to `app/(app)/announcements/[id].tsx`). Foreground receipt (`addNotificationReceivedListener`): invalidate the feed and bulletins queries so Home refreshes; no in-app banner beyond the system one.
8. **Notification settings** `app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx` + `src/features/push/NotificationSettings.tsx`: section "This device" — permission status (`granted` / `denied` with "Open system settings" → `Linking.openSettings()`), registration status from kv (`Registered` / `Not registered` + "Register again" → `registerForPush`), the capability message when not `ok`; section "<org name>" — switches for **Announcements** and **Bulletins** bound to `notification_preferences` via `getNotificationPreferences(supabase, userId, orgId)` (treat a missing row as all-true defaults, matching the column defaults) and `upsertNotificationPreferences` validated by `notificationPreferencesSchema` (send all four booleans; keep `events`/`surveys` at their current/default values and do NOT show their switches until 5.3/6.1 — comment `TODO(5.3)`, `TODO(6.1)`); optimistic update with rollback + toast on error; note "Preferences are per church; switch church to change another one". Explain that turning everything off keeps the device registered (the server intersects preferences — DESIGN §8).
9. **More tab** `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` + `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx`: rows Bulletins → `/bulletins`, Notification settings → `/settings/notifications`, Change password → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${webUrl}/auth/reset`)` with helper text "Password changes happen on the web" (members created with a temporary password — DESIGN §5 path 2 — have no other way to change it), Switch church (only when `orgs.length > 1`, opens `useOrgSwitcher().open()`), Sign out (confirm dialog → `signOutEverywhere()`), a footer with "Anacast", `Application.nativeApplicationVersion`/`Constants.expoConfig?.version`, and links Privacy Policy → `${webUrl}/privacy`, Terms → `${webUrl}/terms` (`WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync`); header shows the signed-in email (`useMyContext().profile.email`) and org name. Leave `TODO(5.x)` comments where Directory, Calendar, Documents, My household, Surveys and Delete account rows will go (DESIGN §10).
10. **Tests** (Vitest, node; because `registerForPush`/`refreshPushDevice`/`installPushSignOutCleanup` take injected `PushDeps`, they are tested with plain fake objects — no `vi.mock('react-native')` needed; only `defaultPushDeps()` touches Expo modules and `src/lib/supabase.ts`, and it is not unit-tested; if any test still imports a file that reaches `react-native`, add `vi.mock('react-native', () => ({ Platform: { OS: 'android' }, AppState: { addEventListener: () => ({ remove() {} }) } }))` and `vi.mock('@/lib/supabase')`): `pushCapability` (five outcomes incl. `platform: 'web'` → `unsupported_platform`), `resolveNotificationTarget` (valid announcement, valid bulletin, event → `not_built`, foreign org → `not_member`, external URL → `bad_payload`, missing data), `registerForPush` state machine (`undetermined → granted → upsertDevice called with a schema-valid row with `platform: 'android'` and kv set`, `denied → no upsert`, `getExpoPushTokenAsync` throwing → `error`, `platform: 'web'` → `unsupported` before any permission call, stored old token ≠ new token → `deleteDevice(old)` then upsert(new)), `refreshPushDevice` (within 24 h → no calls; after 24 h with a rotated token → delete old + upsert new with `enabled: true`; same token → upsert only), and `installPushSignOutCleanup` (registers a function that deletes the device and clears `push_token`/`push_last_seen_sync`).

## Constraints
- All writes through `@church/db` helpers with the user client (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()`); never `supabase.from('push_devices')` in screens; never a service key; never call `srv_*`.
- Payload trust: only `data.url` shapes produced by `notificationTargetPath` and only orgs the user is an active member of; no `Linking.openURL(data.url)`.
- Channel id `announcements`, `projectId` from `Constants.expoConfig.extra.eas.projectId`, token via `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` — exactly as DESIGN §10; never `getDevicePushTokenAsync` for the server.
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` (nothing new should be needed; `expo-application` is bundled with `expo` if you want the native version — otherwise use `Constants.expoConfig.version`).
- Do not build directory, events, surveys, join codes, account deletion (later phases). Do not touch `apps/web` (the dispatcher contract is fixed by 3.6a), migrations (never `supabase db push`), or shared packages except the additive `upsertPushDevice` `enabled: true` on-conflict change if 1.7a lacks it (with a test, recorded in HANDOFF).
- No secrets, no real tokens in tests (use `ExponentPushToken[test-token]`), no model identifiers.

- `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) → no issues; with the 4.1a mock env `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`).

**Notes.** Not split: ~11 new files. `depends_on` 3.6b (G9 split) so the whole dispatcher + receipts + cron exist when the app registers devices; the payload contract itself comes from 3.6a (which also added `notificationTargetPath` to `urls.ts`). Decisions made here because the docs are silent: `data.url` is validated against the four `notificationTargetPath` shapes and `data.org_id` against active memberships before navigating; `events`/`surveys` targets are ignored until 5.3/6.1; events/surveys preference switches are hidden until their features exist; the explainer is skipped (and marked seen) on emulators/Expo Go. Revision after critique (push reliability — PLAN §10 'never cut push registration'): `refreshPushDevice` re-fetches the Expo token every 24 h, deletes a rotated token's old row and always upserts `enabled: true` + `last_seen_at` (if 1.7a's `upsertPushDevice` does not set `enabled: true` on conflict the agent extends it additively — flagged in open_issues for G4); registration also runs silently whenever permission is granted and no `push_token` is stored (fresh install, after sign-out, second account) instead of relying on the one-time explainer; `Platform.OS` values other than android/ios return `unsupported_platform` before touching `registerPushDeviceSchema` (`push_platform` is `android | ios`); the sign-out cleanup is an explicitly installed `installPushSignOutCleanup()` (called from `useNotificationNavigation`'s mount effect) instead of a module side effect nobody imports; the pure capability check lives in `src/lib/push-capability.ts` so `src/lib/push.ts` (DESIGN §11) has no sibling directory; `registerForPush`/`refreshPushDevice` take injected `PushDeps` so Vitest needs no `react-native` mocks; the More tab gains a 'Change password' row → web `/auth/reset` for members created with a temporary password (DESIGN §5 path 2). `expo-notifications` handler property names changed across SDKs (`shouldShowBanner`/`shouldShowList` vs `shouldShowAlert`) — the prompt tells the agent to follow the installed typings. Real delivery cannot be tested in an agent session (needs the EAS build with `google-services.json` and the FCM v1 key — DESIGN §13 risk 5); Checkpoint C (4.5) is the verification.

## 4.5 — Expo / EAS / Firebase + Checkpoint C (founder, about 2–3 hours including build waits; a physical Android phone is required)

Follow `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (step 4.4) for screenshots-level detail; this checklist is the ordered summary. Never paste a key, the `google-services.json` contents or a service-account JSON into git, a Claude Code prompt (`prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim) or chat — everything goes to the password-manager vault from step 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. Checkpoint B is done: the web app is deployed on Vercel (`<VERCEL_URL>`), the Supabase project exists, `9999_init.sql` is pasted (HANDOFF ledger), and BOTH the Magic Link AND the Confirm signup email templates contain `{{ .Token }}` (Supabase → Authentication → Email Templates → Magic Link, then Confirm signup; 2.4 made the second optional — it is required here because an invited person without an account receives the Confirm signup email on their first code) — without them the app sends a link instead of a code and cannot sign in (DESIGN §13 risk 7).
2. You must be an **ACTIVE member** of the first church with the email you will type into the phone. As super admin your email already has an auth account (you signed up in 2.5), so use **Invite, not Create account** (Create account calls `auth.admin.createUser` and fails for an existing email; an invitation is not a membership until accepted): `/o/<slug>/users` → **Invite** → your email (no permissions needed) → if Resend is not configured, copy the link → open it in the same browser where you are signed in → **Accept**. Check that `/o/<slug>/users` now lists you as active (if the app shows the "no church" screen later, this is the item to redo). A second person with a fresh email can instead be created with Create account. The Supabase Free project must not be paused (dashboard shows "Active"; restore it if it says paused).
3. Accounts from step 0.1: Expo (expo.dev) and a Google account for Firebase. If deferred, create them now with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and turn on two-factor authentication.
4. On your computer: `git pull`, `pnpm install`, `cd apps/mobile`.

**A. EAS project**
5. `npx eas-cli login` → sign in with the Expo account.
6. `npx eas-cli init` → confirm creating the project under your account (slug `anacast`). Because `app.config.ts` is dynamic, EAS prints the project id instead of writing it: copy the `Project ID` (a UUID). If the command ends with an error telling you to add `extra.eas.projectId` yourself, that is expected: take the id from the message or from expo.dev → project → Overview. Record it in HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)" (it is not a secret) and put it in `apps/mobile/.env` as `EAS_PROJECT_ID=<id>` (the file is gitignored; eas-cli and Expo CLI read `.env` from `apps/mobile`, so `project:info` and `build` only work after this line exists).
7. Confirm with `npx eas-cli project:info` → shows `anacast` and the id.

**B. EAS environment variables (preview environment; repeat later for production)**
8. expo.dev → your project → **Environment variables** → environment **preview** → Add variable, one at a time (or use the `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview …` commands in MOBILE_BUILD.md §4):
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` = your Supabase project URL (Supabase → Project Settings → API → Project URL) — plaintext.
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = the publishable key (`sb_publishable_…`; or the legacy anon key) — plaintext (it is a public key).
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<VERCEL_URL>` (the same value as Vercel's `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, no trailing slash) — plaintext.
   - `EAS_PROJECT_ID` = the id from A.6 — plaintext. If EAS refuses the name because it reserves the `EAS_` prefix, create `ANACAST_EAS_PROJECT_ID` instead and ask an agent (helper prompt below) to make `app.config.ts` read `process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID ?? process.env.ANACAST_EAS_PROJECT_ID` — one line, recorded in HANDOFF (docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md §4 describes it).
   - `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` — type **File**, visibility **Secret** — added in C.11 after you have the file.
9. Also create the same five variables in the **development** environment if you or an agent will run development builds.

**C. Firebase project and Android app**
10. console.firebase.google.com → **Add project** → name `Anacast` → disable Google Analytics → Create. Project settings (gear) → **Your apps** → **Add app** → Android → *Android package name* = exactly the `android.package` value from `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` (print it: `npx expo config --type public | grep '"package"'` — normally `com.anacast.app`; it is immutable after the first Play upload, step 6.5) → nickname `Anacast` → Register app → **Download google-services.json** → skip the remaining SDK steps.
11. Save the downloaded file as `apps/mobile/google-services.json` (gitignored — check with `git status`, it must NOT appear) and upload it to EAS: expo.dev → Environment variables → preview → Add → name `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON`, type **File**, visibility **Secret**, choose the file → Save (or `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview --name GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON --type file --value ./google-services.json --visibility secret`). Store a copy in the vault.
12. FCM v1 key: Firebase → Project settings → **Service accounts** → **Generate new private key** → Generate → a JSON file downloads (treat it as a password). Then `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → select the `preview` build profile (or "All") → **Google Service Account** → **Manage your Google Service Account Key for Push Notifications (FCM V1)** → **Set up a Google Service Account Key** → Upload a new key → pick the downloaded JSON → confirm. Afterwards move the JSON into the vault and delete it from Downloads.

**D. Build and install the preview APK**
13. `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` → answer **Yes** to "Generate a new Android Keystore?" (EAS stores it; you never see it) → wait (10–25 minutes on the free queue). The terminal prints a build page URL.
14. On the phone: open the build page (QR code or link) → **Install** → download the APK → if Android blocks it, allow "Install unknown apps" for your browser → install → open **Anacast**.
15. Record in HANDOFF.md "Mobile (Phase 1)" → builds ledger: `preview | <build id> | <version from app.config.ts> | <date>`.

**E. Checkpoint C — Android trial (tick every line)**
16. Sign-in: enter the email from item 2 → "Email me a code" → a 6-digit code arrives → enter it → the Home tab of your church opens. (If a link arrives instead of a code, fix the templates from item 1 and retry. If the app lands on the "no church" screen, redo item 2 — the screen tells super admins exactly that.)
17. Notifications: the explainer appears → **Turn on notifications** → Android asks for permission → Allow. Verify on the server: Supabase → SQL Editor → `select platform, enabled, device_name, created_at from public.push_devices;` → one row for your phone.
18. Push from an announcement: on the web (`/o/<slug>/announcements/new`) publish an announcement to **All attendees** with push on → the phone shows a notification within seconds → tap it → the announcement opens in the app. Then repeat with the app fully closed (swipe it away first) → the tap opens the announcement from cold start.
19. Push from a bulletin (founder decision 6, push on by default): upload a bulletin PDF on the web (`/o/<slug>/bulletins`) → notification → tap → the bulletin screen → **Open bulletin** → the phone's PDF viewer shows it.
20. Sermons: play an **uploaded mp3** → lock the phone → audio keeps playing (required); the lock screen also shows the sermon title unless HANDOFF's 4.2b "Deviations from plan" says lock-screen controls are pending the `expo-audio` API (then only continued playback counts); play a **YouTube-linked** sermon → it plays inline; open a **Google Drive-linked** sermon → the browser opens (expected, DESIGN §7). If there are no such sermons yet, create them on the web first (`/o/<slug>/sermons/new`, Upload | Link).
21. Notification settings: More → Notification settings → switch **Bulletins** off → upload another bulletin on the web → no push arrives; switch it back on.
22. Session: kill the app and reopen → still signed in. More → Sign out → SQL Editor: the `push_devices` row is gone. Sign in again (the explainer does not reappear if permission is already granted; the row comes back).
23. Optional: a second family member's phone with a second invited account — both receive the same announcement (a brand-new invited account signs in through the Confirm signup email, so this needs the Confirm signup template edit from item 1).

**F. Record**
24. HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)": tick the Checkpoint C items, note the EAS project id, build id, version, date, phone model + Android version, and every failure verbatim (screenshots' text, `npx eas-cli build:view` errors). Also add under "Environment status" that the EAS `preview` environment is configured. Commit and push (or hand the notes to the helper prompt below).

**Done when**: an APK built by EAS from `main` is installed on your phone; you signed in with a 6-digit code as an active member (invited and accepted on the web); `push_devices` shows your phone; an announcement and a bulletin published on the web produced notifications that opened the right screens (including from a cold start); an uploaded sermon played in the background and a YouTube-linked sermon played inline; a bulletin PDF opened; sign-out removed the device row; HANDOFF.md holds the build ledger and the Checkpoint C results.

Prerequisites that are easy to miss and therefore repeated at the top: the `{{ .Token }}` edit in BOTH the Magic Link and the Confirm signup templates (2.4 made the second optional; a brand-new invited account receives Confirm signup), the founder being an active member of the first church — via Invite + accept in the browser, because his super-admin email already has an auth account and `createUserDirect` would fail — and the Supabase Free project not being paused. `eas init` on a dynamic config may exit asking the founder to add `extra.eas.projectId` himself; the checklist says that is expected and routes the id through `apps/mobile/.env`. Costs: EAS free tier builds queue slowly (10–25 min); Firebase and FCM are free. Verification of pushes requires the web dispatcher to be live on Vercel with `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` optional (3.6a). ## Build
1. **Classify first, then act.** Copy my list into `Session log/<this session>/triage.md` and give every item a class: `bug` (behaviour differs from the TODO step's Done-when or from PLAN §9), `copy` (wording, punctuation, capitalisation, unclear message), `ux` (layout, spacing, touch target, loading/empty/error state, ordering), `config` (EAS environment, Firebase, Supabase template/SMTP, paused project, wrong `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` in the build), `limitation` (documented gap or platform behaviour we accept), `later` (Phase 2+ feature or PLAN §10 cut-list item). Write the class and the owning file(s) next to each item before changing anything; ask me only when an item is ambiguous between `bug` and `later`.
2. **One commit per observation group.** Group related items (e.g. three copy fixes on the sign-in screen) and make one commit per group with a message that lists the item numbers (`fix(mobile): sign-in copy (#3, #7)`). Never mix a behaviour fix with unrelated copy changes in one commit, so a bad fix can be reverted alone.
3. **Regression test first for pure functions.** For `bug` items in `resolvePlayer`, `resolveNotificationTarget`, `pushCapability`, `registerForPush`/`refreshPushDevice` (injected `PushDeps`), `resolveActiveOrg`, `sortFeed`, `bulletinRangeLabel`, `pickOpener`, `isSignedUrlExpired`, `parseAppLink`, `otpOptions`, `authErrors`: add the failing case to the existing Vitest table, watch it fail, then fix. Component-level bugs (layout, state) get a fix plus a static-review note in the commit body, since the mobile package has no jsdom/RN test renderer.
4. **Shared-package changes are rare and symmetrical.** If a fix truly belongs in `packages/domain` (a link shape `parseMediaLink` misparses) or `packages/db` (a query filter), change it there with a test AND run the web tests — the web `SermonPlayer` and share page use the same parser; never change the parser's strategy names, `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl`, `notificationTargetPath` shapes or `queryKeys` without updating both consumers' tests in the same commit and recording it in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan". Never touch `apps/web` otherwise.
5. **Copy and UX rules.** Keep the neutral theme: colours only in `src/theme/tokens.ts`. Copy stays plain, never blames the user, and names the actor ("Ask your church to…", "Open the web app to…"). Every message that comes from an error keeps using `DomainError`/`authErrors` mapping — no raw error text on screen. Respect the system font scale and keep `accessibilityLabel`s when you restructure a screen.
6. **Config items.** For each `config` item write the exact fix for me: dashboard click path or `npx eas-cli …` command, which EAS environment (`preview`/`production`), and whether a rebuild is needed (any `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` change or `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` change → rebuild; a Supabase template or SMTP change → no rebuild). Add the symptom → cause → fix line to `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 if it is not there.
7. **Limitations and later items.** `limitation` → one sentence in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 or `docs/MEDIA.md` (whichever the user would look at) and a line under HANDOFF "Mobile (Phase 1) known gaps"; `later` → a line under the relevant TODO step (5.x/6.x) in `docs/TODO.md` notes or HANDOFF "Phase 4 ideas", with my item number so I can find it.
8. **Rebuild list.** Keep a running list of which commits change anything under `apps/mobile` (they need `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` to reach the phone) versus web/docs-only commits (live after the Vercel deploy). Put the list in your final message and in `session_log.md`.
9. **Do not** add features, redesign screens, upgrade Expo or any dependency, or start Phase 2 work in this round. A dependency bump is a `later` item unless a pasted crash proves it is required — then `npx expo install` it and record the pin in HANDOFF.

## Constraints
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` (record any addition in HANDOFF "Version pins"); never `expo-av`, never `react-native-youtube-iframe`, never a `youtube.com/embed` `source.uri`.
- No elevated Supabase key, no `srv_*` calls, no `supabase.from(` in screens; all reads/writes through `@church/db` helpers with the user client; schemas only from `@church/domain`.
- Migrations are out of scope (never `supabase db push`); if an observation needs a schema change, file it as `later` with the proposed `9998_*` file name and stop.
- Never write a real email, key, token, build log with secrets, or my phone's identifiers beyond model + Android version into the repo or `prompt_history.txt`.
- Do not modify the 3.6a dispatcher contract or the 4.3 payload validation unless a test on both sides proves the bug; record such a change under "Deviations from plan".

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm --filter mobile test` shows every new regression case passing (list them in the commit body).
- `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) → no issues; with the mock env (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321 EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3000`) `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`). `pnpm --filter web build` after any change under `apps/web` or `packages/*`.
- The guard greps from 4.1b–4.3 still return nothing: `git grep -n "z.object" apps/mobile/src`; `git grep -n "anacast://" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app -- ':!*.test.ts'`; `git grep -n "supabase.from(" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app`; `git grep -n "SUPABASE_SECRET\|service_role\|auth.admin" apps/mobile`; `git grep -n "expo-av\|react-native-youtube-iframe" apps/mobile`; `git grep -n "/embed/yt" apps/mobile/src` → tests only; `git grep -n "3600\|50 \* 60" apps/mobile/src` → nothing; `git grep -n "getDevicePushTokenAsync\|openURL(data" apps/mobile` → nothing.
- `Session log/<this session>/triage.md` has a class and an owning file for every pasted item, and every `bug` item points at a commit hash.
- If a development build is on my phone, I re-test the fixed items myself after the rebuild; tell me which items to re-test.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: "Mobile (Phase 1)" — update the known-gaps list (add limitations, remove anything you fixed), append a row to the builds ledger placeholder for the rebuild I must run (`preview | <pending> | <version> | <date>` — I fill in the build id), and add the Checkpoint C follow-up status; "Deviations from plan" — any shared-package or contract change; "Phase 4 ideas" / the relevant 5.x/6.x TODO notes — the `later` items with my item numbers; "Version pins" — any `expo install`.
- `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 and `docs/MEDIA.md` — the symptom → cause → fix lines and limitations from Build 6–7.
- Tick step 4.6 in `docs/TODO.md` only if every pasted item is closed (fixed, configured, documented or filed) — otherwise leave it unticked and list what is open; write `session_log.md` (include the triage table and the rebuild list); commit per group as in Build 2 with the final one `fix(mobile): post-Checkpoint-C polish — <one-line summary>`; push (`git push origin main` unless another branch was named). If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

**Goal.** A directory administrator (any member holding `users.create` or `org.settings`) opens `/o/<slug>/directory`, searches the church's households, creates a household, edits its address/phone/anniversary, uploads a household photo to the `directory-photos` bucket, reads and writes the household's leader notes, designates the head of house, and flips the three privacy toggles (`hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`) subject to the direction rule (admins only toward more privacy) with the family-confirmation state visible. Persons CRUD, congregation status and account linking are step 5.1b.

4. **Household page** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/directory/households/[householdId]/page.tsx` + `src/features/directory/HouseholdPage.tsx`: `getHouseholdWithPersons(householdId)`; `notFound()` when the view returns nothing (a household outside the org or invisible to the actor looks identical to a missing one — never leak existence), and ALSO `notFound()` when the returned row's `view_level !== 'admin'` — a directory admin always gets `admin` for own-org households, so anything else is a fellowship-visible row of another church in the same fellowship that this page must never edit (the RPCs would refuse anyway, but the editing surface and the masked values must not render). Edit mode prefills `anniversary` from `anniversary_display`, which is the full `YYYY-MM-DD` at `admin` level; never read `anniversary` from `households` (42501). Sections with ids for anchors: `#details` (the `HouseholdForm` in edit mode → `updateHouseholdAction(orgSlug, householdId, input)` which sends `{ id, ...fields }` to `saveHousehold`; never send `org_id` on update), `#photo`, `#people`, `#privacy`, `#notes`. Header: name, badges as in the list, `view_level` chip shown only in development builds.
5. **Photo upload** `src/features/directory/HouseholdPhoto.tsx` (client) + actions `prepareHouseholdPhotoAction(orgSlug, householdId, { contentType, size })` and `revertHouseholdPhotoAction(orgSlug, householdId, previousPath)`. Flow (DESIGN §6/§7: the storage insert policy requires "a row exists whose `photo_path` equals `name` exactly and the caller … `can_edit_household`"): the action validates `BUCKETS['directory-photos'].allowedMimeTypes.includes(contentType)` and `size <= BUCKETS['directory-photos'].fileSizeLimitBytes` (10 MiB; 1.6a's `BUCKETS` is keyed by bucket id with `.fileSizeLimitBytes` / `.allowedMimeTypes` copied from `9999_init.sql` section (10) and asserted by `limits.test.ts` — do NOT add a `DIRECTORY_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES` constant or a hard-coded MIME list), computes `path = householdPhotoPath(orgId, householdId, crypto.randomUUID())` (keep the `.jpg` extension the helper produces — the client re-encodes to JPEG below, and the DB check only constrains the prefix anyway), calls `saveHousehold(db, { payload: { id: householdId, photo_path: path } })`, returns `{ path, previousPath }`. The browser then uploads with the user client: `supabase.storage.from('directory-photos').upload(path, blob, { contentType: 'image/jpeg', upsert: false, cacheControl: '3600' })` for the re-encoded Blob; only when the canvas fallback keeps the original file pass that file with `contentType: file.type` (a plain upload — 10 MiB does not need tus). On storage failure call `revertHouseholdPhotoAction` (sets `photo_path` back to `previousPath`) and show `mapStorageErrorMessage(error)`; on success invalidate `queryKeys.directory.household(id)` and show the new signed URL. Client-side: downscale with a canvas to max 1600 px on the long edge and re-encode as JPEG quality 0.85 before upload (keeps photos small and normalises HEIC-converted files); keep the original if canvas decoding fails. "Remove photo" = `saveHousehold({ id, photo_path: null })`. Old objects have no delete policy for `authenticated`; they become orphans that the 3.6b cron sweep (> 24 h) removes — write that in a code comment and in `docs/RLS.md`'s known consequences.
6. **People section** `#people`: cards from `directory_persons` for this household — photo, preferred/first + last name, `household_role` label (Head of house / Spouse / Child / Other), `congregation_status` badge, `birthday_display`, `directory_listed = false` → "Unlisted" badge, `deceased_on` → "Deceased" badge; each card links to `/o/<slug>/directory/persons/<id>` (5.1b). Buttons "Add person" → `/directory/persons/new?household=<id>` (5.1b). **Head of house** control (decision 6): a select listing the household's persons whose `household_role in ('head','spouse')` or for whom 1.6a's `isAdult(p, settings, asOf)` from `@church/domain` `audiences.ts` is true (`settings` = `getSettings(orgId)`, `asOf` = `todayInZone(settings.timezone)` from `@church/domain` `dates.ts`), current head preselected. Server Action `setHeadOfHouseAction(orgSlug, householdId, personId, previousHeadNewRole: 'spouse' | 'other')`: `requireDirectoryAdmin`, `requireWritable`; if another person is currently `head`, first `savePerson({ id: currentHead, household_role: previousHeadNewRole })`, then `savePerson({ id: personId, household_role: 'head' })`. Two RPC calls are not atomic — if the second fails, re-run the first with `household_role: 'head'` to restore, surface the error, and leave a `TODO(5.8): replace with the atomic set_head_of_house RPC (proposed follow-up migration)` comment. A `duplicate` (23505) `DomainError` from the partial index (if the demotion did not happen) must map to "This household already has a head of house" — 1.6b's `toDomainError` already maps 23505 to the `duplicate` key; add only the directory-specific message (additive, with a unit test).
7. **Privacy section** `#privacy` `src/features/directory/PrivacyPanel.tsx` (client) fed by `getPrivacyState(householdId)`: three switches with helper text — `hide_from_congregation`: "Hide this family from the congregation directory (they still see themselves)" (decision 1); `hide_from_fellowship`: "Hide this family from other churches in the fellowship"; `show_children_in_fellowship`: "Show this family's children to the fellowship (default: adults only)". Direction rule for admins: compute `allowedForAdmin(current, next)` in `src/features/directory/privacy-rules.ts` (pure, unit-tested) — an admin may set `hide_*` from false → true and `show_children_in_fellowship` from true → false, never the reverse; a super admin (`ctx.isSuperAdmin`) may do anything. Disabled switches carry the tooltip "Only a household adult can make the family less private (from the Anacast app)". Confirmation state: `privacy_confirmed_at` null → amber "Awaiting family confirmation — a household adult has not reviewed these settings yet"; otherwise "Confirmed <date>" in the org timezone. Server Action `setHouseholdPrivacyAction(orgSlug, householdId, flags)`: `requireDirectoryAdmin`, `requireWritable`, re-check `allowedForAdmin` server-side (belt and braces — the DB trigger is the real guard), call `setHouseholdPrivacy(db, { hh, hide_fell, hide_cong, show_children })`; map `privacy_direction_not_allowed` (42501, raised by 1.3a's `app.guard_household_privacy_columns`; in `errors.ts`) to the tooltip sentence and `not_household_editor` (42501) to "You cannot edit this household" — write the mapping test up front with those two keys. Also show the org-level context: when `organization_settings.directory_share_with_fellowship` is false, a note "Your church does not share its directory with the fellowship (Settings → Directory), so the fellowship toggles have no effect today"; when `directory_share_in_congregation` is false, the same for the congregation toggle.
8. **Leader notes** `#notes` `src/features/directory/LeaderNotes.tsx` (client, reused by 5.1b with `kind='person'`): textarea prefilled from `getHouseholdLeaderNotes(householdId)`, "Save notes" → Server Action `saveLeaderNotesAction(orgSlug, kind, id, notes)` → `saveLeaderNotes(db, { kind, id, notes })`; shows `updated_at` and helper text "Visible only to directory administrators of this church. Never shown to the congregation, the fellowship or the audit log." Max 4000 characters — parse with 1.6b's `saveLeaderNotesSchema` (`kind: 'household' | 'person'`, `id`, `notes` ≤ 4000) from `@church/domain/schemas/directory.ts`; do not add a second schema.
9. **Queries and keys (additive only).** If `queries/directory.ts` lacks `listPersonsForHouseholds(householdIds)` or `countHouseholds(orgId, query)`, add them with explicit column lists from the views only; extend `queryKeys.directory` with `.count(orgId, query)` if used. Update `packages/db/README.md` accordingly. No SQL changes: if a needed RPC behaviour is missing (for example a non-directory-admin path), record it in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" rather than editing `9999_init.sql` (frozen once pasted — check the ledger).
10. **Docs.** `docs/RLS.md`: add a "Directory admin UI (5.1a)" paragraph — which RPC each control calls, the direction rule as implemented, the orphaned-photo consequence, and that `hide_from_congregation` now has a UI (decision 1). Update `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` (3.8) with a short directory click-through: create household → upload photo → set head → toggle privacy toward private (works) → toward public (blocked with tooltip) → write leader notes.
11. **Tests.** Vitest: `privacy-rules.test.ts` (every transition × admin/super), `HouseholdForm` schema mapping (sort_key prefill, empty strings → null), `setHeadOfHouseAction` ordering with a mocked `@church/db` (demote → promote → restore on failure). Playwright smoke (`apps/web/e2e/directory.smoke.spec.ts`, `smoke` project, mock env from 3.7a): unauthenticated `/o/any/directory` redirects to `/login?next=…`; `/o/any/directory/households/new` likewise; the strict security headers hold on those URLs (`expectStrictHeaders`). Add an env-gated scenario to `e2e/full/01-acceptance.spec.ts` only if the 3.7b harness makes it a small addition (create household → appears in list → open it → set `hide_from_fellowship` on → the reverse is disabled); otherwise leave a `test.fixme` with those exact steps and write in HANDOFF that step 5.7 owns the directory Playwright + RLS-matrix coverage (PLAN §11: "add RLS tests for the directory matrix and Playwright coverage as UI lands").

## Constraints
- Reads only through `directory_households` / `directory_persons` / `org_directory_info` and the two leader-notes tables; never `select` from `persons` or `households` base tables (the 1.7a spy test enforces this in `@church/db` — keep web code on the query modules, no ad-hoc `.from('households')`). Writes only through the RPC wrappers; the service client is never used in this step.
- Every page and action: `requireOrgMember` → `requireDirectoryAdmin`; mutations also `requireWritable`. Server Actions receive `orgSlug` and never trust a client-supplied org id; `householdId`/`personId` are validated as uuids with Zod before use.
- Do not build persons CRUD, congregation status, account linking, CSV import, the member web directory or mobile screens (5.1b, 5.2a/5.2b, 5.7). Do not add columns, RPCs or policies; do not touch `supabase/migrations/`. Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, RHF + `zodResolver`, TanStack Query, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62 — add no new dependency (canvas downscaling uses the browser API). No model identifiers in commits or files; no secrets; `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`-style placeholders only.
- Neutral theme tokens from 2.1's `brand.ts`/`@theme` only; no hard-coded brand colours.

- Founder decision 3: "Each church sets its own youth age" — thresholds come from `organization_settings`, never constants. Decision 6: one `head` per household (5.1a's head-of-house control; this step's role select must not create a second head).

## Build
1. **Person form** `src/features/directory/PersonForm.tsx` (client, RHF + `zodResolver(savePersonSchema)` minus the admin-only keys handled by dedicated controls): first_name*, last_name*, preferred_name, sex (Male / Female / not set), birthdate (date input) + `birthdate_visibility` radio ("Full date — congregation sees the year", "Month and day only" (default), "Hidden") with helper "The fellowship never sees years regardless of this setting" (decision 2); marital_status select from the enum; `household_role` select (Head of house / Spouse / Child / Other) — if the household already has a `head` and the admin picks Head here, block with "Use 'Set head of house' on the household page" (link) so the partial unique index never fires; `directory_listed` switch ("Unlisted people never appear to the congregation or fellowship; admins and the household still see them"); `deceased_on` date (collapsed under "More"); contacts: email, mobile_phone, work_phone (light normalisation: trim, keep digits/+ for phones; Zod already validates email). Empty strings become `null`. Server Actions in `src/features/directory/person-actions.ts`: `createPersonAction(orgSlug, householdId, input)` (`requireDirectoryAdmin`, `requireWritable`, `household_id` from the route param validated as uuid, `org_id = ctx.org.orgId`, `savePerson(db, { payload })`, redirect to the person page) and `updatePersonAction(orgSlug, personId, input)` (`{ id, ...fields }` — never `org_id`/`household_id` on update unless the admin uses the explicit "Move to another household" control below).
2. **Routes.** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/directory/persons/new/page.tsx` — requires `?household=<uuid>`; loads the household via `getHousehold` (404 when invisible) and renders `PersonForm` under the heading "Add a person to <household name>". `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/directory/persons/[personId]/page.tsx` + `src/features/directory/PersonPage.tsx` — `getPerson(personId)` from `directory_persons` (404 when missing/invisible; also 404 when `view_level !== 'admin'` — a directory admin always gets `admin` for own-org persons, so anything else means a fellowship row that must not be edited here). Sections with anchors: `#details` (PersonForm in edit mode), `#status` (congregation status), `#groups` (derived badges), `#photo`, `#account`, `#notes`, `#danger` (move/delete). Breadcrumb: Directory → household name → person.
3. **Congregation status** `src/features/directory/CongregationStatus.tsx`: radio Member / Attendee / Inactive with `member_since` date shown when Member (prefilled from the view's `member_since`); Server Action `setCongregationStatusAction(orgSlug, personId, status, member_since)` → `setCongregationStatus(db, { person_id, status, member_since })`. Helper text: "Inactive people stay in the directory for leaders but are hidden from the congregation, the fellowship and every audience group" (base predicate). The `@church/domain` `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` labels are: All attendees = everyone who attends, members included (HANDOFF decision).
4. **Derived groups panel** `src/features/directory/DerivedGroups.tsx` (server component): load `getSettings(orgId)` and compute with `personInKind(p, kind, { settings, asOf })` / `isMinor` / `isAdult` / `isYouth` from `@church/domain` `audiences.ts` for `asOf = todayInZone(settings.timezone)`: badges Youth / Men / Women / Members / Attendees, grey when not in the kind; the "add birthdate or role" amber badge when `household_role = 'other'` and `birthdate` is null (DESIGN §4.3); "Excluded: deceased" / "Excluded: inactive" when the base predicate fails. **Youth override** control (`youth_override`: Automatic / Always youth / Never youth) → `updatePersonAction` with `youth_override: null | true | false`; helper: "Automatic uses the church's youth ages (<youth_min_age>–<youth_max_age>, married excluded: <yes/no>) from Settings". Add a Vitest that renders the panel's pure helper (`deriveBadges(person, settings, asOf)` in `src/features/directory/derive-badges.ts`) against three fixtures from `packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json` so UI and SQL agree.
5. **Photo** — reuse 5.1a's component generalised to `DirectoryPhoto` with `kind: 'household' | 'person'`: for persons the prepare action calls `savePerson({ id, photo_path: personPhotoPath(orgId, personId, uuid) })`, uploads to `directory-photos` within `BUCKETS['directory-photos'].fileSizeLimitBytes` (10 MiB) and `.allowedMimeTypes` (client-side downscale and JPEG re-encode as in 5.1a; no new constant), reverts on failure; "Remove photo" nulls the path. Refactor 5.1a's `HouseholdPhoto` to the shared component (keep its tests passing).
6. **Account section** `src/features/directory/AccountLink.tsx`: four states, chosen by a pure `accountLinkState(person, settings, asOf)` in `src/features/directory/account-link-state.ts` returning `'linked' | 'adult' | 'minor' | 'unknown_age'`. (a) Linked — `user_id` present: show the membership (find it in `listMemberships(orgId)` by `user_id`; link to `/o/<slug>/users/<membershipId>`; status badge) and "Unlink account" → `updatePersonAction({ id, user_id: null })` with a confirm dialog ("The person stays in the directory; the account keeps its access to the church until you disable it under Users"). (b) `adult` — not linked and `isAdult(person, settings, asOf)` is true: buttons "Invite by email" → `/o/<slug>/users?invite=<personId>` (3.2b preselects the person and prefills the display name from `listLinkablePersons`; pass `&email=<encoded>` only if the Invite dialog already accepts such a param — otherwise leave it and do not modify 3.2b), "Create account" → `/o/<slug>/users?create=<personId>`, and "Link existing user": a picker of active memberships whose `person` is null (from `listMemberships`) → `updatePersonAction({ id, user_id })`; the partial unique index refuses a user already linked to another person in this org — map the `duplicate` (23505) `DomainError` to "That account is already linked to <name>" (find the name via `listMemberships`). (c) `minor` — `isMinor(person, settings, asOf)` is true (role `child`, or birthdate present and age < `adult_min_age`): the section reads "Accounts cannot be linked to minors (COPPA). Add a birthdate or set the role to Head/Spouse/Other adult first"; the DB refuses too — map `minor_cannot_have_account` (P0001) to the same sentence if it is forced. (d) `unknown_age` — role `other` with no birthdate (DESIGN §4.3: neither minor nor adult): show the amber "Add a birthdate or role to place this person in audience groups" badge and STILL offer the three linking actions, because `app.is_minor` is false for this person and the database allows the link — the UI must not be stricter than the DB here; say so in a code comment and in `docs/RLS.md`. Map `field_not_editable` (42501) — impossible for an admin, but surface it generically — to "You may not change that field".
7. **Move and delete** `#danger`: "Move to another household" — a household picker (search via 1.7a's `searchHouseholds(orgId, { query, limit: 20, offset: 0 })`) → `updatePersonAction({ id, household_id })`; if this person is the household's `head`, warn that the old household will have no head. "Delete person" → confirm dialog naming the consequences from `delete_person`'s body (read it: whether it refuses when `user_id` is set — if so the UI says "Unlink the account first" and disables the button while linked; whether it deletes the person's photo via `storage_deletions` — if not, note the 3.6b orphan sweep). Server Action `deletePersonAction(orgSlug, personId)` → `deletePerson(db, { person_id })` → redirect to the household page. Refuse in the UI to delete the last person of a household? No — allow it (a household may be empty while being set up), but show "This household will have no people".
8. **Person leader notes** `#notes`: 5.1a's `LeaderNotes` with `kind='person'` fed by `getPersonLeaderNotes(personId)` → `saveLeaderNotes(db, { kind: 'person', id, notes })`.
9. **Household page hooks** (5.1a files, small edits only): the person cards now link to real pages; "Add person" links to `/directory/persons/new?household=<id>`; after any person mutation `revalidatePath` both the person page and the household page.
10. **Queries (additive only).** If missing in `@church/db`: `queries/directory.ts` `getPerson(id)` returning every `directory_persons` column with an explicit list; `queryKeys.directory.person(id)`; a `findMembershipByUserId(orgId, userId)` in `queries/memberships.ts` only if `listMemberships` is too heavy for the account section (prefer reusing `listMemberships`). No `select *`, no base-table reads, no embeds of `profiles(`.
11. **Docs and tests.** `docs/RLS.md`: extend the "Directory admin UI" paragraph with persons (which control calls which RPC; the COPPA rule; the `other` + no birthdate badge; that `delete_person` is the only delete path). `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`: add person → set status Member with `member_since` → badges update → link to an existing user → unlink → delete. Vitest: `derive-badges.test.ts` (fixtures), `PersonForm` empty-string→null mapping and the "second head" block, `accountLinkState(person, settings, asOf)` for all four states (linked / adult / minor / unknown_age — the child fixture, an adult fixture, the `other`-without-birthdate fixture from `persons.json`), and the error-key mapping (`minor_cannot_have_account`, `duplicate`, `field_not_editable`). Playwright smoke `apps/web/e2e/directory.smoke.spec.ts`: add unauth redirects for `/o/any/directory/persons/new?household=<uuid>` and `/o/any/directory/persons/<uuid>`. Playwright full (env-gated `full` project, `E2E_MODE=full`): extend `e2e/full/01-acceptance.spec.ts` with: create household → add an adult person → set status Member with `member_since` → Members badge shown → link to the E2E admin user → the Users grid shows the person → unlink → delete person. If the 3.7b harness cannot support it in one small addition, leave a `test.fixme` with these exact steps and write in HANDOFF that step 5.7 owns the directory Playwright + RLS-matrix coverage (PLAN §11).

## Constraints
- Directory admin guard on every page and action (`requireOrgMember` → `requireDirectoryAdmin`; mutations `requireWritable`). Reads only from `directory_persons` / `directory_households`; writes only via `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_congregation_status`, `save_leader_notes`. Never select `birthdate` from `persons`. No service client.
- The admin `save_person` payload may contain any whitelisted key, but this UI never sends `congregation_status` / `member_since` through `save_person` — those go through `set_congregation_status` so the audit trail is uniform. Never send `org_id` on update.
- Do not build self-service (mobile, 5.2a/5.2b), CSV import (5.7), the member web directory, join requests (5.6) or any migration change. If `delete_person` or the COPPA rule behaves differently from the docs, follow the migration and record the deviation. Error keys come from 1.3b's catalogue via `@church/domain` `errors.ts` — never invent a key or match on message text. Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- No new dependencies; pins as in 5.1a. No model identifiers, no secrets.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → all tasks succeed; the new Vitest files pass, including the fixture-driven `derive-badges.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds; routes `/o/[orgSlug]/directory/persons/new` and `/o/[orgSlug]/directory/persons/[personId]` are listed.
- `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green.
- `grep -rn "from('persons')\|from('households')\|birthdate" packages/db/src/queries/directory.ts` → the only `birthdate` hits are columns selected from `directory_persons`.
- Manual (hosted project): add a child (role Child, birthdate 8 years ago) → Account section shows the COPPA text; add a person with role Other and no birthdate → amber badge, linking still offered; set an adult to Member with `member_since` → Members badge on; toggle `youth_override` Always → Youth badge on regardless of age; link an existing unlinked user → the Users grid shows "first last · household" for that membership (3.2a); unlink → grid shows "Not linked"; delete the person → gone from the household page; as a plain member, `directory_persons` for that household shows no `member_since`/`youth_override` (null) and `birthday_display` without the year unless visibility is `full`.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: feature table "Directory" Web UI → done (5.1a + 5.1b); State checklist; "Deviations from plan" for anything `delete_person`/COPPA-related you had to adapt and for additive helpers you added (names).
- Tick step 5.1b in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): directory admin — persons CRUD, congregation status, account linking, leader notes`; push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

Nothing else — the view already withheld what the viewer may not see; never fetch `birthdate` or the notes tables.

Deep-link paths `/directory`, `/directory/household/<id>` and `/directory/person/<id>` must work through expo-router; add them to the `parseAppLink` allow-list (4.1b) if it filters paths. Write the DESIGN §10 `person/*` → `directory/person/[id]` deviation in a code comment at the route file and in HANDOFF.

## Constraints
- Reads only through `directory_households`, `directory_persons`, `org_directory_info`, `organization_settings`; never the `persons`/`households` base tables, never `household_leader_notes`/`person_leader_notes` (RLS would return nothing for members, but do not even query them), never `select birthdate`. No writes at all in this step. The mobile app holds only the `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`) — no elevated keys, no server code.

- Never persist signed URLs in the query cache; never log personal data. No model identifiers, no secrets.

Context lines when `settings.directory_share_with_fellowship === false` ("Your church does not share with a fellowship, so this switch has no effect today") or `directory_share_in_congregation === false`. "Save" → `setHouseholdPrivacy(db, { hh: householdId, hide_fell, hide_cong, show_children })` — household adults may move any direction; the RPC stamps `privacy_confirmed_*`. Non-adults see the switches read-only with "Only a household adult (head of house or spouse) can change these". Map `privacy_direction_not_allowed` (cannot happen for an adult; surface generically) and `not_household_editor`. Success toast "Saved — your privacy choices are confirmed". Last line: "Changes are recorded in your church's audit log".
8. **Confirmation flow for admin-created households**: `usePrivacyState(householdId)` (`getPrivacyState`, key `.directory.household(id)` suffixed `'privacy'` — additive `queryKeys.directory.privacy(householdId)` if you prefer); when `privacy_confirmed_at` is null and the member is a household adult, show a persistent banner on Home (`(tabs)/home.tsx`, small edit) and on My household: "A leader added your family to the directory. Your family is hidden from other churches until you review your privacy choices" → "Review" opens `/household/privacy?confirm=1` in confirm mode: the current values are preselected and the primary button reads "Confirm these choices" (calls `set_household_privacy` with the same values — stamping the confirmation). Remember dismissal for 7 days in kv (`privacy_banner_dismissed_at`) but never hide it permanently until confirmed.
9. **Photos (ArrayBuffer)** `src/lib/photo-upload.ts` + `src/features/household/PhotoPicker.tsx`: `ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({ mediaTypes: ['images'], quality: 1, allowsEditing: true, aspect: [1, 1] })` (or `launchCameraAsync`), then `ImageManipulator` to resize the long edge to 1200 px and export JPEG at 0.85 (use the `ImageManipulator.manipulate(uri).resize(...).renderAsync()` / `saveAsync({ format: SaveFormat.JPEG, compress: 0.85 })` API of the installed version — read its typings), then read bytes with `fetch(uri).then(r => r.arrayBuffer())` (DESIGN §7 allows it; this avoids mixing 4.2a's `expo-file-system/legacy` usage with the new `File` API) — **never a Blob on React Native**. Flow: `savePerson`/`saveHousehold` with the planned `photo_path` (`personPhotoPath(orgId, personId, randomUUID())` / `householdPhotoPath(...)` with `expo-crypto` `randomUUID()`) → `supabase.storage.from('directory-photos').upload(path, arrayBuffer, { contentType: 'image/jpeg', upsert: false })` → on failure revert the path with the same RPC (previous value) and show `mapStorageErrorMessage`. Enforce `BUCKETS['directory-photos'].fileSizeLimitBytes` after compression (retry at 0.7 once, then refuse with "This photo is too large"). Invalidate `queryKeys.signedUrl('directory-photos', oldPath)` and the household/person queries. A non-adult may set only their OWN person's photo (own-row rule). Unit-test the pure `planPhotoUpload(kind, ids)` and `pickCompression(bytes)` helpers.
10. **Navigation**: More tab row "My household" (→ `/household`) next to 5.2a's "Directory" row (DESIGN §10); register `household/index`, `household/edit`, `household/person/[id]`, `household/privacy` in the `(app)` stack layout with titles. Add `/household` and `/household/privacy` to the `parseAppLink` allow-list (4.1b) if it filters paths.
11. **Docs**: `docs/MEDIA.md` — a "Directory photos (mobile)" section (picker → manipulator → ArrayBuffer → upload; 10 MiB from `BUCKETS`; orphan sweep). `docs/RLS.md` — "Mobile self-service (5.2b)" paragraph listing which screen calls which RPC, the own-row contacts rule, and the head-of-house conflict if you hit it. `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` — the new photo permission strings AND a "My household" section in the founder's device checklist containing the Manual verify steps below verbatim.

## Constraints
- Reads only through `directory_households`, `directory_persons`, `org_directory_info`, `organization_settings`; never the `persons`/`households` base tables, never the leader-notes tables. Writes only via `save_household`, `save_person`, `set_household_privacy`. The mobile app holds only the `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`) — no elevated keys, no server code.
- Mobile native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install`; `react` stays `catalog:` (19.2.3). Do not add `react-hook-form` or web-only packages. Do not import from `apps/web`.
- Do not build calendars/events (5.3b), join codes (5.6), CSV import, delete-person on mobile, or any migration. Do not change `9999_init.sql`; never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- Never persist signed URLs or photo bytes in the query cache; never log personal data. No model identifiers, no secrets.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → every task succeeds; `rules.test.ts` (`canEditHousehold`, `editableFieldsFor`, `allowedRolesForNonAdmin`) and `photo-upload.test.ts` pass.
- `cd apps/mobile && npx expo-doctor` → all checks pass (or the same known exclusions 4.1a recorded); `npx expo export --platform android` → bundle written with no errors; `pnpm --filter mobile typecheck` clean.
- `grep -rn "new Blob\|from('persons')\|from('households')\|leader_notes\|react-hook-form\|DIRECTORY_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app apps/mobile/package.json` → no output.
- `grep -n "expo-image-picker\|expo-image-manipulator" apps/mobile/package.json` → versions present, matching `npx expo install --check` (no drift reported).
- Manual (founder's device with a preview build, or after 4.5): sign in as a household head of an admin-created household → Home shows the review banner → Privacy → "Confirm these choices" → banner gone and `households.privacy_confirmed_at` set (SQL Editor); turn "Hide from our congregation" on → another member no longer sees the household in Our congregation but the family still sees itself under My household; edit the household address → visible to the congregation; add a child (role Child) → appears under People; upload a person photo (row in `storage.objects` under `<org>/persons/<id>/`); as a non-adult member of the household, open My household → only the own row is editable and only its contact fields; try the head-of-house picker as a household adult → either it works or the "ask your church" message appears (record which in HANDOFF).

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: feature table "Directory (households, persons, photos, privacy override)" Mobile UI → done (5.2a + 5.2b); State checklist; "Version pins worth remembering" with the `expo-image-picker` / `expo-image-manipulator` versions installed; "Deviations from plan" for the head-of-house conflict (whether `save_person` refused a household adult — 5.8 input) and any additive `@church/db` helper (`queryKeys.directory.privacy`).
- Tick step 5.2b in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(mobile): household self-service, privacy confirmation, directory photos`; push `main` (or the branch I named).
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

### 5.3a — Calendars & events (web) — calendars CRUD, events list/create/edit/delete, pending approval queue with push

- **Who:** Agent
- **Depends on:** 5.1b, 3.8

- **Size:** L
- **Commit:** `feat(web): calendars CRUD, events list/create/edit, pending approval queue with push`

**Goal.** Church leaders manage calendars and events on the web: `/o/<slug>/calendars` lists the four default calendars (All / Youth / Men / Women, created by `app.on_org_created`) plus custom ones and lets `org.settings` holders rename, colour, set the view and submit audience groups, create and delete custom calendars; `/o/<slug>/events` lists upcoming events per calendar with create/edit/delete for `announcements.create` / `announcements.edit` / `announcements.delete` holders (leader-created events are approved immediately and may push); `/o/<slug>/events/pending` is the approval queue where `announcements.edit` holders approve (→ `status = 'approved'`, the `app.on_content_publish` trigger enqueues the push, the 3.6a dispatcher sends it) or reject with a reason. Everything writes directly to `calendars` / `events` under RLS with the user client; no RPC or migration is added.

## Goal
When you finish, an `org.settings` holder opens `/o/<slug>/calendars`, sees the church's calendars (`kind` all/youth/men/women plus custom), edits a calendar's name, colour, "Who can see it" (`view_audience_group_id`) and "Who can submit events" (`submit_audience_group_id`) from the church's `audience_groups`, adds a custom calendar and deletes a custom one (with its events). An `announcements.create` holder opens `/o/<slug>/events`, filters by calendar and month, creates an event (calendar, title, description, location, start/end in the church timezone, all-day, push) that is approved at once, edits it (`announcements.edit`), deletes it (`announcements.delete`). `/o/<slug>/events/pending` shows member-submitted events awaiting approval with Approve (push is enqueued by the trigger and dispatched by 3.6a's `afterContentPublish`) and Reject (reason stored in `rejection_reason`). Members without those permissions see 403 on these pages (the member experience is mobile, 5.3b). Lint, typecheck, tests, the web build and the Playwright smoke project are green.

Pull-to-refresh; offline hint from the 4.2a pattern. Buttons: "Suggest an event" (when `useCanSubmit`) and "Your submissions" (badge with count when > 0). Empty state: "No upcoming events in the next 90 days". When `listCalendars` returns nothing (all calendars restricted): "No calendars are shared with you".

Submit → `insertEvent(orgId, { calendar_id, title, description, location, starts_at, ends_at, all_day, submitted_by: session.user.id, status: 'pending', push: false })` with the user client; success → `/events/submitted?id=<id>` confirmation screen ("Sent to your church for approval — a leader will review it"); errors: `42501` → "Your church does not accept event suggestions for this calendar" (also when `members_can_submit_events` is off — check `useSettings` first and hide the button; a suspended org also yields a bare 42501 from the `writable` predicate, so check `org.status` client-side first and hide the button when not writable — treat every 42501 as the calendar/submissions refusal), `23514` (`ends_at >= starts_at`) → "End must be after start". There is NO `on_content_publish` trigger on `documents` (`notification_kind` = `announcement, event, survey, bulletin`): documents never enqueue a push. `app.user_in_group(null)` is true (DESIGN §4.3): a null audience means every member.
- Founder decision 10 (Supabase Free): the project-wide upload limit is 50 MB, the `documents` bucket cap is 50 MiB and `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` defaults to 50 — the effective cap is `Math.min(BUCKETS.documents.fileSizeLimitBytes, readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB) * 1024 * 1024)`; map the storage "exceeds plan limit" error exactly as 3.3b does (its `UploadErrorKey`). Decision 7: only `suspended` blocks writes.

## Goal
When you finish, a member opens **Documents** from the More tab of the Anacast app and sees the documents published to an audience they belong to, grouped by category with a chip filter, each row showing kind, title, size and date. Tapping a row opens a detail screen whose "Open document" button downloads the file over a one-hour signed URL and hands it to an installed viewer — PDF, Word, Excel and text through an Android `ACTION_VIEW` intent with the exact MIME type, images inline — and falls back to the system Share sheet when no app can open the type. An announcement that carries a linked document shows a document card in `announcements/[id]` (replacing 4.2a's `TODO(5.4)` comment), and a document the member may not see (audience mismatch, unpublished, deleted) is simply absent — never an error that hints it exists. Nothing changes in the database, the web app or the push pipeline: documents have no notification kind.

## Build
1. **Data hooks** `src/features/documents/useDocuments.ts`: `useDocuments(orgId)` = `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.documents.list(orgId), queryFn: () => listPublishedDocuments(supabase, orgId, {}), staleTime: 5 * 60_000 })` — filter by category in memory (one query, persisted for offline reading); `useDocument(id)` = `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.documents.detail(id), queryFn: () => getDocument(supabase, id) })` with `initialData` taken from the list cache when the row is present; pure helpers in `src/features/documents/format.ts`: `groupByCategory(rows)` → `{ category: string | null; items }[]` sorted by category name, `null` ("Other") last, items `publish_at desc`; `categoriesOf(rows)` → sorted distinct categories; `documentSizeLabel(bytes)` (KB under 1 MB, otherwise MB with one decimal); `documentFileName(row)` → `<title slug>.<ext from mime via extensionForMime>` (safe for the file system, never the storage uuid). Pull-to-refresh invalidates `queryKeys.documents.list(orgId)`.
2. **List** `app/(app)/documents/index.tsx` + `src/features/documents/DocumentList.tsx`: header "Documents"; a horizontal chip row built from `categoriesOf(rows)` with "All" first (no second query — comment why); `SectionList` from `groupByCategory` (a section header per category; a flat list when no row has a category); row = kind icon by `documentKind`, title, `category · size · <published date>` through the domain date helpers; tap → `documents/[id]`; `RefreshControl`; empty state "Your church has not shared any documents yet"; error state with Retry; when the persisted cache serves rows and the refetch fails, keep them with the 4.2a offline bar (reuse the component; do not copy it).
3. **Detail and open** `app/(app)/documents/[id].tsx` + `src/features/documents/DocumentDetail.tsx`: title, description (when present in the row type), category, `DOCUMENT_KIND_LABELS[kind]`, size, published date; primary button "Open document"; secondary "Share". Open logic: do NOT copy `openBulletinFile` — generalise it: move the download → content-URI → intent → fallback body from `src/features/bulletins/OpenPdf.ts` into `src/lib/open-file.ts` as `openStoredFile({ bucket, path, mimeType, fileName, cacheKey, expectedSize })`, keep `openBulletinFile` as a thin wrapper so 4.2a's callers and tests stay untouched, and call `openStoredFile({ bucket: 'documents', path: row.storage_path, mimeType: row.mime_type, fileName: documentFileName(row), cacheKey: row.id, expectedSize: row.file_size_bytes })` here. Extend `pickOpener(mimeType, platform)` (table-tested): Android → `application/pdf`, the two Word types, the two Excel types and `text/plain` → `'intent'` (ACTION_VIEW with the exact MIME type; Google Docs/Sheets, WPS, Drive PDF viewer or the system viewer pick it up), `image/jpeg` / `image/png` → `'inline_image'`; iOS (untested until 6.4) → `'share'` for everything but images. Fallback chain inside `openStoredFile`: when no activity handles the intent (`ActivityNotFoundException` or `startActivityAsync` rejecting) → `expo-sharing` `shareAsync(localUri, { mimeType })` with the toast "No app can open this file. Choose an app to share it with."; only when `Sharing.isAvailableAsync()` is false → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(signedUrl)`. Cache: `FileSystem.cacheDirectory + 'anacast-files/' + cacheKey + '.' + ext`; before downloading, `getInfoAsync` — reuse the cached file when it exists and its `size` equals `expectedSize`, otherwise delete and re-download; on a 403 or an expired signed URL → `remint()` once and retry, then the friendly error "This file could not be opened. Pull to refresh and try again."; show a progress indicator (`createDownloadResumable` progress callback) during download.
4. **Images**: `image/jpeg` / `image/png` render inline on the detail screen with `expo-image` (`contentFit: 'contain'`), same "Share" button — the 4.2a bulletin pattern.
5. **Linked document on announcements**: in `src/features/feed/AnnouncementDetail.tsx` replace the `TODO(5.4)` comment with `LinkedDocumentCard` (`src/features/documents/LinkedDocumentCard.tsx`): when `announcement.document_id` is set, `useDocument(document_id)`; while loading render a small skeleton; when the query returns a row render a card (kind icon, title, size, chevron) that navigates to `documents/[id]`; when it returns no row (RLS-hidden, scheduled, deleted) render nothing — no "not available" text, because the member must not learn that a restricted document exists. In `src/features/feed/AnnouncementCard.tsx` show a paper-clip icon when `document_id` is set (presence of the id only — no query per card). If `getAnnouncement` / `listFeed` do not select `document_id`, add the column to their explicit column lists additively (with a test) and record it.
6. **More tab**: in `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx` add the row Documents → `/documents` in the DESIGN §10 order ("Phase 2/3 add Directory, Calendar, Documents, Surveys, My household …"): after Directory and Calendar when 5.2a/5.3b already added them, otherwise directly under Bulletins. Keep the remaining rows and the footer untouched.
7. **Routing**: register `documents/index` and `documents/[id]` in the stack layout where 4.x declares `bulletins/[id]` (titles "Documents" / "Document"); `documents/[id]` must work when opened cold with only an id (same rule as `announcements/[id]`), because the announcement card may be the first screen a member reaches after a push tap.
8. **Accessibility and copy**: rows are `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"` and `accessibilityLabel` "<title>, <kind label>, <size>"; text sizes respect the system font scale; all strings English, sentence case; the empty state, the no-viewer toast and the open-failure message are the only new copy.
9. **Tests** (Vitest, node; `vi.mock` for `@church/db` and every `expo-*` module; use whichever renderer 4.x already uses — add no test library): `format.test.ts` (`groupByCategory` puts `null` last and sorts items newest first; `categoriesOf` dedupes; `documentSizeLabel` 512 KB / 1.5 MB; `documentFileName` slug + extension for a docx row), the extended `pickOpener` table (every MIME in `BUCKETS.documents.allowedMimeTypes` yields a defined opener on `android` and on `ios`), `open-file.test.ts` (intent rejection → `Sharing.shareAsync` called once; sharing unavailable → `openBrowserAsync`; cached file with matching size → no download; size mismatch → re-download; 403 → `remint` called once then success), `LinkedDocumentCard.test.tsx` (renders nothing when the query resolves to `null`; renders the title when a row exists), `openBulletinFile` still passes its 4.2a tests unchanged.
10. **Docs**: `docs/MEDIA.md` (4.4) — a "Documents" section: which app opens each type on Android, the share fallback, the cache path and size check, the egress note; `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` device checklist — a "Documents (5.4b)" block holding the manual checks from Verify; `apps/mobile/README.md` "Mobile playback and files" — one line for documents.

## Constraints
- Mobile native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install <pkg>`; this step needs no new native module — if you believe one is required, stop and ask. `react` stays `catalog:` (19.2.3).
- No elevated key on the device; the app reads `documents` and signs URLs with the member's session under RLS. Never persist signed URLs (`queryKeys.signedUrl` + `meta.persist: false`).
- Do not touch `supabase/`, `apps/web`, `src/lib/deep-links.ts`, push registration, or `settings/notifications`. Additive changes to `@church/db` / `@church/domain` only if 5.4a missed something you need, each with a test and a HANDOFF note.
- Do not build directory, events, join-code or survey screens; do not add a documents push preference (there is no such kind); do not add a documents web view.
- No model identifiers in commits or files; no secrets; never `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`.
