## Goal
When you finish, a leader holding `announcements.create` **or** `org.settings` (PLAN §4: "custom groups = `announcements.create` or `org.settings`") sees a **Groups** entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/groups`, the six system audience groups (All attendees, Members, Non-member attendees, Youth, Men, Women — read-only, each with a plain-English explanation of who is in it computed from the church's settings) followed by the church's custom groups. They can create a custom group (name, optional description), rename it, edit its description, delete it after a confirmation that spells out what happens to the announcements, documents and calendars that target it, and manage its members on `/o/<slug>/groups/<groupId>` with a searchable picker fed by the directory views. Every existing audience select (announcements 3.5a, documents 5.4a, calendars 5.3a — and surveys in 6.1) lists the custom groups under a separator with a "Manage groups" link, so a custom group can be the audience of an announcement the moment it exists. Members without the permission pair see nothing new: `/groups` is 403 for them, and the mobile app is untouched (custom groups only change which announcements, documents and calendar entries a member sees and which pushes reach them; there is no member-facing UI).

## Inputs / prior state
- Schema (1.2/1.3, `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, sections (3), (5), (7), (8)) — read it, do not change it: `audience_groups` (`id, org_id, kind audience_kind not null, name text not null, description, created_by, created_at, updated_at`; `unique (org_id, name)`; partial unique `(org_id, kind) where kind <> 'custom'`), `audience_group_members` (`group_id fk audience_groups on delete cascade, person_id fk persons on delete cascade, org_id, added_by, created_at`; PK `(group_id, person_id)`; index `(person_id)`); `assert_same_org` triggers on both FKs (a person from another church raises `23514`/the trigger's errcode — read `app.assert_same_org`); `app.on_org_created()` inserts the six system rows per org (`kind` in `everyone, members, attendees, youth, men, women`). Derivation (DESIGN §4.3): `custom` = **base ∧ row in `audience_group_members`**, where base = `congregation_status in ('member','attendee') and deceased_on is null` — so adding an inactive or deceased person to a group has no effect, and `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)` only returns persons whose `user_id` has an **active** `org_memberships` row, so a member without an account is reached by content but never by push. `app.user_in_group(null)` is true.

Every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org)` (suspended orgs are read-only). Nothing in the schema stops a manager from renaming or deleting a **system** row — the UI and Server Actions must refuse it (Build 4).
- FK actions on the referencing tables, as 1.2 created them: `announcements.audience_group_id` and `documents.audience_group_id` `on delete set null`; `calendars.view_audience_group_id` / `submit_audience_group_id` `on delete set null`; `surveys.audience_group_id` `on delete no action` (DESIGN §4.2) — deleting a group a survey targets raises `23503`. ## Goal
When you finish, the database knows how a person joins a church with a code: a leader holding `users.create` mints an 8-character code (optionally labelled, expiring, limited to N uses, or auto-approving), a signed-in person redeems it with `redeem_join_code` and either becomes an active member at once (auto-approve) or gets a `pending` membership plus a `join_requests` row that a `users.create` holder approves (linking or creating a directory person) or rejects; the requester can cancel. All of it lives in a NEW re-runnable migration `supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` that the founder pastes after `9999_init.sql`, is covered by a new RLS test file, is exposed through typed wrappers in `@church/db`, validated by Zod schemas and error keys in `@church/domain`, and documented in `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`, `docs/RLS.md`, `supabase/README.md` and the HANDOFF ledger. No web or mobile UI changes in this step. PLAN §11 item (6): "join codes + join requests (RPCs `redeem_join_code`/`approve_join_request`, pages, mobile `join`/`pending`)" — this step is the RPC half.

## Constraints
- Migration rules (CLAUDE.md, PLAN §4 "Migration skeleton", DESIGN §13 risks 1–3): descending numbering, re-runnable per construct (`drop … if exists` before every policy/trigger, `if not exists` on tables/indexes/columns, `create or replace` for functions — `drop function if exists` only on a signature change), every function `security definer set search_path = ''`, schema-qualified extension calls, policy names `ca_`, no `force row level security`, no enum value additions, never `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`. **Do not edit `9999_init.sql`** — even if it is not yet in the ledger, all of this step's SQL goes into the new file.
- Every RPC starts with `app.require_user()`; every mutating RPC except `cancel_join_request` calls `app.require_writable(org)`; permission checks are explicit `app.has_perm(org, 'users.create')` (or `app.is_super_admin()`); no `srv_*` function is added.
- Additive changes only in `@church/domain` / `@church/db`; no web or mobile code (5.6b/5.6c); no new dependency; no model identifiers or secrets in files or commits; `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`-style placeholders in docs. Do not build the UI, the printable page, or App Links; do not touch `apps/`.

## Goal
When you finish, a leader holding `users.create` sees **Join codes** and **Join requests** in the org navigation. At `/o/<slug>/join-codes` they create a code (label, auto-approve, optional expiry and use limit), see every code with its state (active, expired, used up, revoked) and use count, revoke one, and open `/o/<slug>/join-codes/<codeId>/print` — a clean printable sheet (church name, the code as `ABCD-EFGH`, three steps for the congregation, expiry) for the bulletin board or the Sunday hand-out. At `/o/<slug>/join-requests` they see who asked to join (name, email, code label, message, when), a "Possible directory match" hint when an unlinked person with the same email exists, and approve (linking the requester to an existing directory person through the 3.2b `PersonPicker`, or creating a new one-person household) or reject with a note; a badge on the nav item shows the pending count. `/users` shows pending memberships as "Awaiting approval" pointing at the queue. ## Goal
When you finish, an `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` link tapped on an Android phone with Anacast installed opens the app directly (Android App Links) instead of the browser: `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` declares a verified `intentFilters` entry for the web host, and the web app serves the Digital Asset Links statement at `https://<DOMAIN>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` from an env-driven Route Handler that lists the founder's signing-certificate fingerprints for package `com.anacast.app`. Separately, a leader editing a YouTube sermon on `/o/<slug>/sermons/<id>` (and the Link tab of `/sermons/new`) has a **Re-check link** button that asks YouTube's oEmbed endpoint, server-side, whether the video is still available and embeddable, and shows the answer (title, channel, or "private / removed / embedding disabled"). `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, `docs/MEDIA.md`, `docs/ENV.md` and HANDOFF.md tell the founder how to collect the fingerprints, set the variable, rebuild the APK and verify on a device. No schema change; no new native dependency.

If `app.config.ts` cannot import `@church/domain` at config-evaluation time (Metro is not involved here — Expo evaluates the config with Node/ts-node; check how 4.1a imports things and whether the domain package's `exports` resolve), copy the two constants into the config file with a comment naming `packages/domain/src/urls.ts` as the source and add a Vitest in `apps/mobile` that imports both and asserts equality (`app-config-parity.test.ts`). Body: `[{ "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], "target": { "namespace": "android_app", "package_name": ANDROID_PACKAGE_ID, "sha256_cert_fingerprints": [...] } }]`. Fingerprints come from the new **server** env var `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` (comma-separated, uppercase hex pairs separated by colons — validate each with `/^([0-9A-F]{2}:){31}[0-9A-F]{2}$/`; trim, uppercase, drop empties; reject invalid entries with a 500 and a server log line naming the position, never the value). When the variable is unset or empty return `200 []` (an empty statement list makes Android fall back to the browser, which is the correct pre-launch behaviour and keeps the route valid JSON). Put the parsing in `apps/web/src/lib/app-links/assetlinks.ts` (`buildAssetLinks(fingerprintsEnv)`, `parseFingerprints`) with Vitest: unset → `[]`; one and two fingerprints; lowercase input normalised; malformed → throws. If Next refuses the dot-directory under `app/`, fall back to `app/api/assetlinks/route.ts` plus a `rewrites()` entry in `next.config.ts` mapping `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` to it, and record the deviation.
5. **Proxy and headers** — add `/.well-known/:path*` to the `proxy.ts` matcher exclusions (no session refresh, no redirect on this path). Confirm `next.config.ts` still sends the strict headers on it (harmless for JSON); do not loosen CSP or `X-Frame-Options`. `robots`: leave the `X-Robots-Tag` behaviour as the other public routes have it.
6. **Env plumbing** — `src/lib/env.ts`: add `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` to `serverEnv()` as optional (follow the pattern used for `RESEND_API_KEY`). `apps/web/.env.example`: add the variable with an explanatory comment and no value. `docs/ENV.md`: new row — owner founder, location Vercel (server), set in step 5.7a / updated in 6.5 (Play App Signing adds a second fingerprint), behaviour when absent "assetlinks returns `[]`; invite links open in the browser".
7. **YouTube oEmbed client** — `apps/web/src/lib/media/youtube-oembed.ts`: `recheckYouTube(videoId, deps = { fetch: globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs: 5000 })` → GET `https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3D<id>&format=json` with an `AbortController` timeout and `cache: 'no-store'`. Map: 200 with JSON → `{ status: 'ok', title, authorName, thumbnailUrl }` (only these three fields; ignore the rest); 401 or 403 → `{ status: 'not_embeddable' }` (YouTube answers 401 for embedding-disabled and private videos, 403 for some private/region cases — do not try to tell them apart); 404 → `{ status: 'not_found' }`; anything else, a non-JSON body, a network error or the timeout → `{ status: 'error', detail: 'timeout' | 'network' | `http_${code}` }`. Validate `videoId` with the same 11-character rule `parseMediaLink` uses; throw on anything else. Pure and fully unit-tested with a stubbed `fetch` (200, 401, 403, 404, 500, malformed JSON, abort). Never log the URL or the response body. Copy for each status lives in `src/features/sermons/recheck-copy.ts` (`RECHECK_MESSAGES`): ok → "Available: <title> — <channel>"; not_embeddable → "YouTube reports this video is private or has embedding disabled. Members will not be able to play it in the app."; not_found → "YouTube reports this video was removed or the id is wrong."; error → "Could not reach YouTube right now; try again later." Reuse DESIGN §7's helper text ("unlisted works; private and embedding-disabled videos do not").
8. **Server Action** — in `src/features/sermons/actions.ts` add `recheckYouTubeLinkAction(orgSlug, input)` (`'use server'`): `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requirePerm(ctx, ['sermons.link', 'sermons.upload'])` (the share-link permission pair; read-only, so no `requireWritable`) → Zod-validate `input` as `{ sermonId: uuid } | { url: https string ≤ 2048 }` → for `sermonId` load the sermon with the user client (RLS) and use `external_url`; run `parseMediaLink(url, 'web')`; if `kind !== 'youtube'` return `{ ok: true, result: { status: 'not_applicable' } }` (Dropbox, Drive and other https links are not re-checked — say so in the UI: "Re-check is available for YouTube links only"); otherwise return `recheckYouTube(externalId)`. Nothing is written to the database — the check is informational (recording it would need a column; see notes). Per-user throttle: keep an in-memory `Map<userId, timestamps[]>` allowing 10 checks per minute per user in this server instance and return `{ ok: false, error: { key: 'rate_limited' } }` beyond it (best effort on Vercel; documented as such — the DB `private.rate_limits` helper is for share-link passwords and stays untouched).
9. **UI** — `src/features/sermons/RecheckLinkButton.tsx` (client): renders on `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]` next to the external link when `media_kind = 'youtube'` and the viewer holds `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload`, and inside `LinkPreview` (3.3a) when the parsed kind is `youtube` (pass the current URL instead of a sermon id). ## Constraints
- Web and mobile never hold elevated Supabase keys; the Server Action uses the user client under RLS; the oEmbed call is a plain outbound fetch with no credentials. `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` is a server variable (fingerprints are public information, but keep the single pattern: config lives in `serverEnv()`), never `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`.
- No new native dependency: `expo-linking` is already present through expo-router; do not add `react-native-youtube-iframe` or any oEmbed library. Mobile versions only via `npx expo install` if you must touch a package at all (you should not). `react` stays `catalog:` 19.2.3.
- Do not change `9999_init.sql` or add a migration — nothing here needs the database. Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`.
- Do not claim `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, `/join/*` (proposed 5.9) or `/` as App Link paths; do not remove the `anacast://` scheme handling; do not change the invite page's behaviour beyond what the tests above need.
- Do not call YouTube from the browser (referer/CORS issues and it would leak member IPs to Google on page load); the check runs only when a leader clicks the button, server-side. Do not persist oEmbed results.
- Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Expo 57, TypeScript ~5.9, ESLint 9, Playwright 1.62. No model identifiers, no secrets, no real fingerprints in tests or docs (use `AA:BB:…` style dummies).

**Goal.** A directory administrator (`users.create` or `org.settings`) at `/o/<slug>/directory/import` downloads a CSV template, uploads or pastes a file of up to 2,000 rows grouped into households by `household_key`, and gets a server-side dry run listing what would be created plus every error by row and column (bad dates, unknown enum values, two heads in one household, conflicting household fields, missing names, ragged rows, caps) and 'possible duplicate' warnings against `directory_persons`; with zero errors, Import creates the rows in batches of 20 households through `save_household`, `save_person` and `set_congregation_status` under RLS with a progress bar, a final report and safe re-runs. Imported households keep the admin-created privacy default (hidden from the fellowship until a family adult confirms) and the page says so. The parser/validator/template live in `@church/domain` with sample and error fixtures; the CSV is never stored; `docs/DIRECTORY_IMPORT.md` documents columns and rules. No schema change.

## Build
1. **Column spec and parser** — `packages/domain/src/directory-import.ts` (pure, no Node APIs):
   - `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_COLUMNS`: ordered list of `{ key, required, kind, help }` — `household_key`* (free text; rows with the same key form one household), `household_name`* (taken from the first row of the group; other rows must be empty or identical), `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `region`, `postal_code`, `country` (default `US`), `home_phone`, `anniversary`, `first_name`*, `last_name`*, `preferred_name`, `sex` (`male`/`female`), `birthdate`, `birthdate_visibility` (`full`/`month_day`/`hidden`; default `month_day`), `marital_status` (the enum's values; default `unknown`), `household_role` (`head`/`spouse`/`child`/`other`; default `other`), `congregation_status` (`member`/`attendee`/`inactive`; default `attendee`), `member_since`, `email`, `mobile_phone`, `work_phone`, `directory_listed` (`yes`/`no`/`true`/`false`; default yes). Column order in the file is free; matching is by header name, case- and whitespace-insensitive; unknown headers are a warning, not an error; a missing required header is a file-level error.
   - `parseCsv(text)`: a small RFC 4180 parser (quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded commas and newlines, CRLF/LF, optional UTF-8 BOM, trailing empty line ignored, ragged rows → row error `ragged_row`). No dependency (a dependency needs founder approval; say so in a comment). Reject input over `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000` or more than `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 2000` data rows with a file-level error before parsing further.
   - `validateDirectoryImport(rows, ctx: { settings: { adult_min_age, timezone }, today })` → `{ households: PlannedHousehold[], errors: ImportIssue[], warnings: ImportIssue[], counts }` where `ImportIssue = { row: number (1-based data row, 0 = file), column?: string, code: ImportIssueCode, message: string }`. Codes (exhaustive union, each with a message in `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_MESSAGES`): `missing_required`, `unknown_value` (enum), `bad_date` (accept `YYYY-MM-DD` and `MM/DD/YYYY` only; normalise to ISO), `future_date`, `household_conflict` (differing household fields within one key), `multiple_heads`, `too_long` (names ≤ 120, address lines ≤ 200, phones ≤ 40, emails ≤ 254 — align with `savePersonSchema`/`saveHouseholdSchema` limits; reuse those Zod schemas per planned row so the RPC never sees a payload the UI could not send), `bad_email`, `ragged_row`, `too_many_rows`, `file_too_large`, `missing_header`, and warnings `unknown_header`, `child_without_birthdate` (role `child` and no birthdate — the age rules will treat the person by role alone, PLAN §4 derivation), `possible_duplicate` (filled in server-side, Build 4). Normalise enums case-insensitively (`Male` → `male`), trim every cell, treat empty as null, `preferred_name` empty → null.
   - `PlannedHousehold = { key, payload: SaveHouseholdInput, persons: { rowIndex, payload: SavePersonInput (without household_id), congregation_status, member_since }[] }`. Household field payload comes from the first row of the group; `sort_key` is not importable (the RPC/5.1a default applies).
   - `buildTemplateCsv()` → header row + two example rows (a two-adult household with a child, and a one-person household) built from `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_COLUMNS` — the same function feeds the download button and the docs.
   - Fixture `packages/domain/fixtures/directory-import.sample.csv` (12 rows, 4 households, every optional column used at least once, one intentional error per error code in a sibling `directory-import.errors.csv`). Vitest `directory-import.test.ts`: parser cases (quotes, BOM, CRLF, embedded newline, ragged), header matching, every issue code fires exactly where expected against the errors fixture, the sample fixture produces zero errors and the expected counts, template round-trips through the parser with zero errors, date normalisation, 2,001 rows → `too_many_rows`. Export everything from the package index.
2. **Page and navigation** — `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/directory/import/page.tsx` (server component: `requireOrgMember` → `requireDirectoryAdmin`; renders `src/features/directory/import/ImportPage.tsx`). Add an "Import CSV" button to the households toolbar in `HouseholdsPage.tsx` (directory admins only) and change 5.1a's empty-state text to a link "import a CSV" → `directory/import`. No `NAV_ITEMS` entry (it is a sub-page of Directory). A suspended church (`!isWritable(ctx)`) shows the 3.1 banner and the Import button stays disabled while dry run still works.
3. **Client flow** — `ImportPage.tsx` (client, three panels):
   - **Prepare**: `TemplateDownloadButton` (builds a Blob from `buildTemplateCsv()`, file name `anacast-directory-template.csv`), a file input (`accept=".csv,text/csv"`, read with `File.text()`; refuse > 1 MB client-side with the `file_too_large` message) and a textarea for pasting; a privacy note: "The file is checked on our server and discarded; nothing is stored until you click Import."
   - **Dry run**: on "Check file" call the Server Action `dryRunDirectoryImportAction(orgSlug, { csv })` (Build 4). Render `ImportSummary` (households to create, persons by role and status, warnings count), `ImportIssuesTable` (errors first, then warnings; columns row / column / message; "Download issues as CSV" via Blob), and `ImportPreview` (accordion per household: name, address line, persons with role/status badges, "possible duplicate" badge with the matched existing name). Checkbox "Skip rows flagged as possible duplicates" (default off).
   - **Import**: enabled only when `errors.length === 0` and the church is writable. Clicking shows a confirm dialog with the counts and the sentence "Imported households are hidden from the fellowship directory until a family adult confirms their privacy settings in the app; leaders can only make a family more private (founder decision)." Then the client loops over household batches calling `commitDirectoryImportBatchAction(orgSlug, { csv, householdKeys, skipDuplicates })` with `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE = 20` household keys per call, showing a progress bar (households done / total) and stopping at the first failed batch. Final report: created households/persons, skipped duplicates, and — on failure — the failing row, the domain error message, and the advice "Remove the rows already imported (they now appear in the directory) and check the file again; re-running is safe because imported people are flagged as possible duplicates."
4. **Server Actions** — `src/features/directory/import/actions.ts` (`'use server'`; both: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requireDirectoryAdmin(ctx)`; Zod-validate input with `directoryImportRequestSchema` = `{ csv: string.max(1_000_000), householdKeys?: string[].max(20), skipDuplicates?: boolean }`; never trust a client-supplied plan — the server re-parses and re-validates the CSV on every call):
   - `dryRunDirectoryImportAction`: `getSettings(orgId)` for `adult_min_age`/`timezone`, run `parseCsv` + `validateDirectoryImport`, then **duplicate detection** with the user client (RLS; directory admins see everything through the views): one query through a new additive helper `listPersonsForDuplicateCheck(db, orgId)` in `packages/db/src/queries/directory.ts` (view `directory_persons` only, filtered `org_id = orgId`, explicit columns `id, first_name, last_name, birthdate, household_id` — birthdate is visible at admin level; mocked-client test asserting the filter and columns; no ad-hoc `.from(...)` in web code) and match planned persons by lower-cased `first_name` + `last_name` and equal `birthdate` when both have one (name-only match when either birthdate is missing) → `possible_duplicate` warnings carrying `{ existingPersonId, existingName }`. Return the plan (households with persons), issues and counts. Cap the response: when errors exceed 500 return the first 500 plus `truncated: true`.
   - `commitDirectoryImportBatchAction`: `requireWritable(ctx)`; re-run the dry run server-side; refuse with `{ ok: false, error: { key: 'import_has_errors' } }` if any error remains (the client should never get here, but a second admin may have changed settings between calls); then, for each requested `householdKey` in file order: skip if every person is a flagged duplicate and `skipDuplicates`; `saveHousehold(db, { payload: { org_id, ...householdPayload } })` → household id; for each person `savePerson(db, { payload: { org_id, household_id, ...personPayload } })` (skip flagged duplicates when `skipDuplicates`) → person id; when `congregation_status !== 'attendee'` or `member_since` is set call `setCongregationStatus(db, { person_id, status, member_since })` — 5.1b's rule: status and `member_since` never travel through `save_person`, so the audit trail stays uniform. Sequential awaits (no `Promise.all` — RLS-scoped RPCs and the one-head index make ordering matter: import the `head` row first within each household so a `multiple_heads` race is impossible). `export const maxDuration = 60` on the page's segment config for the action. On a thrown domain error return `{ ok: false, error: { key, row, householdKey }, progress: { households, persons } }`; map error keys through `toDomainError` and the domain's `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`. Return `{ ok: true, created: { households, persons }, skipped }` otherwise.
   - Idempotency across retries: a household whose persons all match existing people is reported, not re-created, when `skipDuplicates` is on; document that with the checkbox off a retry can create duplicates and that the dry run shows them first.
   - Add error keys `import_has_errors` and `import_batch_failed` to the web-side message map (not to `@church/domain` `errors.ts`, which mirrors DB errcodes only).
5. **What the import deliberately does not do** (state it in the UI help panel and docs): no photos, no leader notes, no `hide_from_*` flags (privacy flags come only from the family or from admins moving toward more privacy; imports use the defaults so every imported household is hidden from the fellowship until confirmed), no `youth_override`, no `deceased_on`, no account linking (use `/users` Create account or Invite afterwards), no update of existing people (the import creates only; edits go through the person page). `created_via` stays whatever `save_household` sets for an admin call (`'admin'` — DESIGN §4.2 documents `admin | invitation | self`; do not add an `'import'` value here, see notes).
6. **Tests** — Vitest in `apps/web`: `import/plan.test.ts` for the duplicate matcher (`matchDuplicates(planned, existing)` extracted as a pure function in `src/features/directory/import/match-duplicates.ts`: same name + same birthdate → match, same name + one birthdate missing → match, same name + different birthdates → no match, case/whitespace differences → match) and for the batcher (`splitHouseholdKeys(keys, 20)`); `actions.test.ts` with a mocked `@church/db` asserting call order per household (household → head person → other persons → `setCongregationStatus` only when needed), skip-duplicates behaviour, and the `import_has_errors` refusal. Playwright smoke: unauth redirect for `/o/any/directory/import` with `expectStrictHeaders` (from `apps/web/e2e/helpers/headers.ts`). First run `pnpm --filter web exec playwright test --list --project=smoke | grep -c directory`: if 5.1a's `apps/web/e2e/directory.smoke.spec.ts` is listed (an earlier step widened `testMatch`), add the check there; if it is NOT listed (3.7a's `testMatch: /smoke\.spec\.ts/` still in force), put the check in `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` under a `test.describe('directory import')` block instead, do not widen `testMatch` yourself (5.7c owns that and will pick up `directory.smoke.spec.ts`), and note in HANDOFF that `directory.smoke.spec.ts` is currently uncollected. Playwright full (env-gated `full` project): a new chapter in `e2e/full/01-acceptance.spec.ts` (or `e2e/full/04-directory-import.spec.ts` if the file is already long): sign in as the org admin → Directory → Import CSV → upload `packages/domain/fixtures/directory-import.sample.csv` → dry run shows 4 households / 12 persons / 0 errors → Import → progress completes → the households list shows the four names with "Hidden from fellowship" and "Awaiting family confirmation" badges → re-upload the same file → dry run shows 12 `possible_duplicate` warnings → with "Skip" on, Import creates 0 households; then upload `directory-import.errors.csv` → Import button stays disabled and the issues table lists every code.
7. **Docs** — `docs/DIRECTORY_IMPORT.md` (new): purpose, who can import, the column table generated from `DIRECTORY_IMPORT_COLUMNS` (keep it in sync by hand; add a Vitest that reads the doc and checks every column key appears), accepted date formats, enum values, household grouping rule, one-head rule, limits (2,000 rows / 1 MB / 20 households per batch), privacy defaults (hidden from fellowship until confirmed; leaders cannot un-hide), duplicate detection and re-run safety, what is not imported, and a "Preparing the file in Excel/Google Sheets" paragraph (save as CSV UTF-8; keep leading zeros in postal codes by formatting the column as text). Link it from `docs/RLS.md` (Directory section: "Bulk import uses the same RPCs and therefore the same audit rows and privacy defaults"), `README.md` docs index and `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` (new chapter "Directory import" with the click path above). `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` (3.8; PLAN §12's manual gate) — new row "CSV import: file discarded after each request, no cell values in logs (`grep -n 'console\.' apps/web/src/features/directory/import/` shows only row numbers and issue codes), writes only through `save_household` / `save_person` / `set_congregation_status` under RLS, imported households hidden from the fellowship by default". Update HANDOFF.md feature table: "Directory CSV import" → Schema n/a / Web done / Mobile —.

## Constraints
- Every write goes through the existing client RPCs with the user-scoped client under RLS — no service client, no direct table inserts, no `srv_*` call, no new RPC or migration (an atomic `srv_import_directory(jsonb)` would be better engineering but needs a migration and a decision; it is recorded as an open issue, not built here). Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; do not touch `supabase/migrations/`.
- Never store the CSV (no bucket, no table, no log line containing a cell value); do not log names, emails or phones on failure — log only row numbers and issue codes. Server Action payloads are ≤ 1 MB; if Next's default `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` rejects a file near the cap, raise it to `2mb` in `next.config.ts` and record it.
- Reuse `saveHouseholdSchema` / `savePersonSchema` for the per-row payloads so the import can never send a field the person form could not; do not widen those schemas. Do not send `hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, `photo_path`, `youth_override` or `deceased_on`.
- Directory reads only through `directory_persons` / `directory_households` (DESIGN §13 risk 14 — `select *` on the base tables fails for clients).
- No new runtime dependency (no papaparse, no csv-parse); the parser lives in `@church/domain`. Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9, Playwright 1.62. No model identifiers, no secrets, `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in fixtures and tests.
- Do not build updates of existing people, photo import, mobile UI, or the member web directory; do not change 5.1a/5.1b behaviour beyond the toolbar button and the empty-state link.

- `pnpm --filter web build` → zero warnings; `/o/[orgSlug]/directory/import` appears in the route list.
- `pnpm --filter web exec playwright test --list --project=smoke` lists the file that holds the import-route check (`directory.smoke.spec.ts` if collected, else `smoke.spec.ts`); `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` → green (unauth redirect + headers for the import route). With `E2E_MODE=full` and the 3.7b env: `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full` → the directory-import chapter passes (or, without the env, the chapter is skipped with the documented reason).
- Local manual check against the local DB seed (`scripts/db/local-up.sh` and a dev web env pointing at it, as 5.1a documented): download the template, open it in a spreadsheet, add three households, save as CSV, upload → dry run counts match; introduce `head` twice in one household → `multiple_heads` on the right row; `13/45/2020` → `bad_date`; import → households appear with the two privacy badges; open a person → `member_since` and `congregation_status` show what the file said; `audit_log` has rows for every `save_household`/`save_person`/`set_congregation_status` call (`select count(*) from audit_log where …` in psql). Re-upload → duplicates flagged; Skip on → nothing created.
- Suspended check: set the org `status = 'suspended'` in psql → the import page shows the banner and Import is disabled; dry run still works; reset the status.

**Notes.** Second part of the 5.7 split (orchestrator decision 13). `depends_on` = 5.1b (persons CRUD, `requireDirectoryAdmin`, `PersonForm` limits) and 5.2b (the mobile privacy-confirm flow must exist before a church bulk-imports hidden households, otherwise families have no way to confirm and the fellowship directory stays empty — DESIGN §13 risk 15). Design choices because the docs say only 'CSV directory import (web, dry-run + errors)': one row per person with a `household_key` grouping column; a small in-repo RFC 4180 parser instead of a dependency; import through the existing client RPCs in 20-household batches from the browser (stateless server: the CSV is re-sent and re-validated per batch), which is non-atomic — the dry run, head-first ordering and duplicate flagging make re-runs safe. An atomic `srv_import_directory(jsonb)` service RPC would need a migration and is listed as an open issue. `created_via` stays `'admin'` (DESIGN §4.2 lists `admin | invitation | self` only); an `'import'` value is an open issue. Limits (2,000 rows, 1 MB, 500 reported errors) are constants the founder may change. Names chosen: `packages/domain/src/directory-import.ts` API, fixtures `directory-import.sample.csv` / `directory-import.errors.csv`, route `/o/[orgSlug]/directory/import`, `src/features/directory/import/{ImportPage,ImportSummary,ImportIssuesTable,ImportPreview,TemplateDownloadButton,actions,match-duplicates}`, actions `dryRunDirectoryImportAction` / `commitDirectoryImportBatchAction`, web error keys `import_has_errors` / `import_batch_failed`, `docs/DIRECTORY_IMPORT.md`. Revised after review: duplicate detection reads through an additive `@church/db` helper (`listPersonsForDuplicateCheck`) rather than an ad-hoc view query in the action; the Playwright check is placed wherever the `smoke` project actually collects it (3.7a's `testMatch: /smoke\.spec\.ts/` does not collect 5.1a's `directory.smoke.spec.ts` until 5.7c widens it); `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` gains a CSV-import row. Risk: if 1.3's `save_person` requires fields the CSV lacks (for example `birthdate_visibility` non-null without a default in the RPC), fill defaults in the planned payload rather than changing the RPC.

1. **Performance fixture** — `supabase/tests/perf/directory_5k.sql`, one transaction ending in `rollback`, parameterised by psql variables with defaults (`\set` guarded by `\if`): `:persons_a` 5000, `:persons_b` 2000, `:budget_ms` 250. **psql variables are invisible inside `do $$ … $$` bodies** (psql never interpolates `:var` inside quoted or dollar-quoted literals), so right after the `\set` defaults run `select set_config('perf.budget_ms', :'budget_ms', true), set_config('perf.persons_a', :'persons_a', true), set_config('perf.persons_b', :'persons_b', true);` and read them inside plpgsql with `current_setting('perf.budget_ms')::numeric`; capture generated ids the same way (`select set_config('perf.org_a', id::text, true) from …`) or with `\gset` outside the block (`select id as org_a from … \gset` then `:'org_a'` in plain SQL statements only). Every `:var` that appears inside a `do` block is a bug — grep the file for it before finishing. Build: one fellowship; org A (`directory_share_in_congregation` true, `directory_share_with_fellowship` true), org B (same, in the fellowship), org C (in the fellowship but `directory_share_with_fellowship` false); `organization_settings` defaults otherwise; households of 1–6 persons generated with `generate_series` and deterministic pseudo-random values (`setseed(0.42)` then `random()` so runs are reproducible): 10% `hide_from_fellowship`, 5% `hide_from_congregation`, 15% `show_children_in_fellowship`, roles head/spouse/child/other with one head per household, birthdates spread so ~20% are minors under `adult_min_age`, 3% `congregation_status = 'inactive'`, 2% `deceased_on` set, 1% `directory_listed = false`, `birthdate_visibility` mixed, `sort_key` set; insert as `churchapp_owner` (bypasses RLS) with `insert … select` statements, never row-by-row PL/pgSQL. Users: `auth.users` rows for a plain org A member (linked person, household adult), an org A directory admin (`users.create`), an org B member (fellowship viewer of A), and an org C member; `org_memberships` + `org_membership_permissions` accordingly. Then `analyze public.persons, public.households, public.org_memberships, public.fellowship_memberships, public.organization_settings`.
2. **Measured queries** (copy from `queries/directory.ts`; run each twice and keep the second timing to exclude cold cache): Q1 households first page as the org A member (`select … from directory_households where org_id = :orgA order by sort_key, name limit 50`); Q2 the same with the search filter `searchHouseholds` uses (`name ilike '%yo%'` or whatever the query layer does); Q3 persons for 50 household ids (`listPersonsForHouseholds`); Q4 one person (`getPerson`); Q5 the fellowship tab as the org B member (`directory_households where org_id = :orgA …` and `org_directory_info`); Q6 the admin's households page (level admin sees hidden households too); Q7 the household adult's own household (`app.my_household_ids()` path); Q8 `listPersonsForPicker` for the admin (5.5). For each, `explain (analyze, buffers, format json)` into a temp table `perf_results(query text, role text, rows bigint, ms numeric, plan jsonb)` using a `do $$` block with `execute format('explain (analyze, buffers, format json) %s', q)` capturing the JSON, extracting `Plan.Actual Rows` and `Execution Time`. Assertions (inside the `do` block, reading `current_setting('perf.budget_ms')::numeric` — never `:budget_ms`): every `ms <= budget` (raise with the query name, ms and budget otherwise); Q1–Q3 return the expected row counts (member excludes hidden-from-congregation households; admin includes them; fellowship viewer excludes minors from households without `show_children_in_fellowship`, hidden-from-fellowship households, and every org C row); no plan node of type `Seq Scan` on `public.persons` for Q3/Q4 (warning via `raise notice`, not a failure — index choice varies with table size). Print a table (`select query, role, rows, ms from perf_results order by query`) and the top three plan nodes by `Actual Total Time` for the slowest query so the numbers land in the console and can be pasted into docs.
3. **Runner** — `scripts/db/perf.sh` (mirrors `test.sh`: sources `scripts/db/_env.sh` for `DATABASE_URL` exactly as `test.sh` does — 1.2 centralised the lookup there; do not write a second one — then `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v budget_ms=${PERF_BUDGET_MS:-250} -f supabase/tests/perf/directory_5k.sql`, exit code = psql's). Root script `db:perf` in `package.json`. Not part of `test.sh` (keeps the RLS suite fast and deterministic) but added to CI as a separate non-blocking job step behind the same file guard 1.1 used, running after `db:test`. Document the budget's meaning: local Postgres 16 on a developer laptop, warm cache, 5k persons — a generous upper bound whose purpose is to catch a per-row `organization_settings` lookup regressing into something quadratic (DESIGN §13 risk 11), not to predict hosted latency.

## Goal
When you finish, a newcomer no longer has to type anything. The printable sheet from 5.6b carries a QR code that encodes `https://<APP_URL>/join/<CODE>`, and that URL — scanned from the sheet, tapped in a text message, or shared by a leader with a new **Copy link** action — opens a public page at `/join/[code]` that shows the code as `ABCD-EFGH`, explains which app to install, offers **Open in Anacast** (the `anacast://join/<code>` deep link) and a Google Play button, and repeats the QR so a desktop visitor can scan it with a phone. On an Android phone with Anacast installed the same https URL is an Android App Link — `/join/*` joins `/invite/*` in 5.7a's claimed path prefixes — so it opens the app directly on 5.6c's `join` screen with the code prefilled, or, for a signed-out person, parks the code in kv and sends them through the "I have a join code" sign-in. The landing page never touches the database: it cannot and must not reveal whether a code is valid, expired or revoked — that answer comes only from `redeem_join_code` inside the app. The QR is produced by a small in-repo encoder, so the web app gains no runtime dependency.

## Build
1. **Shared URL helpers** — `packages/domain/src/urls.ts` (append; rename nothing): `joinDeepLink(code)` → `anacast://join/<normalized code>` (built from `APP_SCHEME` and `normalizeJoinCode`); `joinUrl(appUrl, code)` → `<appUrl without trailing slash>/join/<normalized code>` (mirror `inviteUrl`); `playStoreUrl(packageId = ANDROID_PACKAGE_ID)` → `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=<packageId>`; change `APP_LINK_PATH_PREFIXES` to `['/invite', '/join'] as const` and keep the comment that `/s/*` and `/embed/*` are never claimed. Extend `urls.test.ts`: `isAppLinkPath('/join/ABCDEFGH')` true, `'/joiner'` false, `'/join'` alone false (a prefix with nothing after it is not a code; make `'/invite'` alone behave the same and test it), `joinUrl('https://x.test/', 'abcd-efgh')` → `'https://x.test/join/ABCDEFGH'`, `joinDeepLink('abcd efgh')` → `'anacast://join/ABCDEFGH'`. Export everything from the package index.
2. **QR encoder — in-repo, no runtime dependency** — `apps/web/src/lib/qr/encode.ts`: a byte-mode QR encoder returning a module matrix, `encodeQr(text: string, opts?: { ecLevel?: 'M' }): { version: number; size: number; modules: boolean[][] }`. Scope: byte mode only (UTF-8 bytes), error-correction level M, versions 1–10 chosen automatically (version 10-M holds 213 data bytes; a join URL is under 80), Reed–Solomon over GF(256) with the standard generator polynomials and block structure per version, the eight mask patterns scored with the four penalty rules, the standard 15-bit format information (BCH) and, for versions 7–10, the 18-bit version information. Throw `RangeError` for inputs over 213 bytes. One file of plain TypeScript, no `any`, with a header comment naming ISO/IEC 18004 and the supported range. `apps/web/src/lib/qr/svg.ts`: `qrToSvg(matrix, { moduleSize = 4, quietZone = 4, foreground = '#000', background = '#fff', title })` → an SVG string with one `<path>` (all dark modules merged into a single `d`), `shape-rendering="crispEdges"`, a `viewBox`, and an escaped `<title>`. `apps/web/src/components/QrCode.tsx`: a server component `QrCode({ value, sizePx, title })` that calls both and inlines the SVG (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is acceptable for a string we generate ourselves from booleans; the only text that reaches the SVG is the escaped `<title>`), wrapped in a `<div role="img" aria-label={title}>`. Tests `apps/web/src/lib/qr/encode.test.ts`: (a) structure — `encodeQr('https://x.test/join/ABCDEFGH')` picks version 3 or 4 (size 29 or 33), finder and timing patterns sit where the standard puts them, the format bits decode to level M and the chosen mask; (b) round trip with the dev-only decoder **`jsqr`** (add it as a `devDependency` of `apps/web` with an exact version, never imported outside tests): scale the matrix to 4 px per module plus the quiet zone into an RGBA `Uint8ClampedArray`, call `jsQR(data, width, height)` and assert `.data` equals the input for five inputs (a short string, the join URL, 100 bytes of ASCII, a UTF-8 string containing `ä`, the 213-byte maximum) and that 214 bytes throw `RangeError`. If installing `jsqr` fails in this environment, keep test (a), record the gap in HANDOFF and tell me in the final message. `svg.test.ts`: the `<title>` escapes `<` and `&`; the path has as many `M` commands as dark modules (or fewer after merging — assert ≥ 1 and that the output parses as XML).
3. **`/join/[code]` public page** — `apps/web/app/(public)/join/[code]/page.tsx` (server component; `await params`; **no Supabase import anywhere under this route** — add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` override for `apps/web/app/(public)/join/**` that forbids `@/lib/supabase/*` and `@church/db`, so the rule survives later edits). Normalise with `normalizeJoinCode`, compute `valid = isValidJoinCode(code)`, and render 200 in every case. Content: title "Join your church on Anacast"; the copy is generic (no lookup): "Someone from your church shared this code with you. Anacast is the app your church uses for sermons, announcements and its directory." The code as `formatJoinCode(code)` in large monospace type with a **Copy code** button (client component `src/features/join/CopyButton.tsx`: `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, a two-second "Copied" state, keyboard accessible, falls back to selecting the text when the clipboard API is unavailable). When `!valid` (wrong length or a character outside the alphabet) show the normalised text as typed — do not call `formatJoinCode` on it — with the hint "This code doesn't look complete — check it with your church. Codes have 8 letters and numbers and never use 0 or 1." and keep the buttons. Steps under the code: "1. Install Anacast" with the button **Get it on Google Play** (`playStoreUrl()`; see Build 5 for the not-yet-listed state), "2. Open the app and sign in with your email address", "3. Enter the code — or tap **Open in Anacast**" with an `<a href={joinDeepLink(code)}>` (inert on desktop — add the caption "Have the app? Open it on your phone"). Below: `<QrCode value={joinUrl(appUrl, code)} title="Join link as a QR code" />` with the caption "On a computer? Scan this with your phone." ## Constraints
- No runtime dependency for the QR code: the encoder is in-repo; `jsqr` is a test-only `devDependency` of `apps/web` with an exact version (no `^`). No other new dependency, web or mobile. Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Tailwind 4, Expo 57, TypeScript ~5.9, ESLint 9, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62.
- The landing page and the QR carry only the code and the public app URL. No Supabase client, no service key, no lookup, no "valid / expired / revoked / church name" anywhere under `/join/*`; the route is `noindex`. Web and mobile never hold elevated Supabase keys; redemption stays the `redeem_join_code` RPC under the member's session on the phone.
- Never claim `/s/*`, `/embed/*` or `/` as App Link paths; keep the `anacast://` scheme handling and the `/invite` behaviour unchanged. Do not edit `apps/web/app/.well-known/assetlinks.json/route.ts`, `supabase/` (no SQL in this step), `proxy.ts` beyond a matcher exclusion if it is truly needed, or the redemption logic in `JoinScreen.tsx` / `useRedeemJoinCode.ts`.
- Mobile native versions only via `npx expo install` (you should need none). Brand colours only through the token files (decision 17). No model identifiers, no secrets, no real domains in tests (`example.test`). Never `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`.
- Do not build a web redemption flow, a church-name lookup, or the `(me)` member routes; do not change 5.6b's approval queue or 5.6c's pending screen.

## 5.9 — Checkpoint D: Phase 2 trial (founder, about 2 hours plus build waits; an Android phone with USB debugging (`adb`) or the ability to sideload, and a second email address — ideally a second phone — for the join flow)

Do this after 5.7c and 5.8 are ticked in `docs/TODO.md` and pushed. It has three parts that must happen in this order: paste the Phase 2 migration into the hosted database (the web and the app call RPCs that do not exist there yet), rebuild the Android app (5.7a and 5.8 changed native config), then run the two Phase 2 acceptance documents. Keep `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` and `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` open beside this list; where they differ from it, the documents (written by the agents that built the features) win.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. Checkpoint C (4.5) is done: the 4.5 preview APK signed in on your phone and received a push. `HANDOFF.md` → "Applied migrations (hosted Supabase)" lists `9999_init.sql` with a date (if it does not, finish step 2.4 first).
2. The Supabase project shows **Active** (dashboard → project; a Free project pauses after 7 idle days — click Restore and wait). Vercel → the web project → Deployments → the latest **Production** deployment is the commit that includes step 5.8 (compare the commit message with `git log --oneline -5` after `git pull origin main`).
3. In your local clone: `git pull origin main`, then `ls supabase/migrations/` and compare with the ledger. Every file the ledger does not list must be pasted in part A, **highest number first**. Normally that is only `9998_join_codes.sql`; if 5.7c shipped an index migration it is numbered `9995` or lower (never 9997/9996 — those are reserved for Phase 3) and comes after 9998.

**A. Paste `9998_join_codes.sql` and record it (about 10 minutes)**
4. Supabase dashboard → your project → **SQL Editor** → "New query". Open `supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql` in your editor → select all → copy → paste into the SQL Editor → **Run**. Expected result: "Success. No rows returned". The file creates six RPCs (`create_join_code`, `revoke_join_code`, `redeem_join_code`, `approve_join_request`, `reject_join_request`, `cancel_join_request`), adds the column `join_requests.review_note` and an index, sets grants and possibly one policy — it never touches data. If the editor shows an error, stop: copy the exact message into the helper prompt below (item 21) and let the agent fix the file; do not edit the SQL by hand.
5. Paste and **Run** the same file a second time → the same "Success" (every migration is re-runnable; this proves it on the hosted project and is harmless).
6. Verify with a new query: `select proname from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and proname in ('create_join_code','revoke_join_code','redeem_join_code','approve_join_request','reject_join_request','cancel_join_request') order by 1;` → **6 rows**. Then `select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'join_requests' and column_name = 'review_note';` → **1 row**.
7. Optional proof (recommended, 1 minute): paste `supabase/tests/rls/11_join_codes.sql` verbatim → Run → it ends with a rollback and prints no error (its assertions raise when they fail; it changes nothing).
8. Paste any other unlisted file from item 3 the same way (run, run again, no error).
9. Remember the rule from `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`: if you ever paste `9999_init.sql` again, paste `9998_join_codes.sql` (and every later file) again right after it — 9999's section (4) drops every `ca_%` policy.
10. Ledger: in `HANDOFF.md` → "Applied migrations (hosted Supabase)" add the row `9998_join_codes.sql (<short hash>) | <YYYY-MM-DD> | founder` under the 9999 row, where `<short hash>` is `git log -1 --format=%h -- supabase/migrations/9998_join_codes.sql`; one row per other file pasted. Commit `docs: ledger — pasted 9998_join_codes.sql` and push — or leave the recording to the helper prompt (item 21) and just keep the date.

**B. Signing fingerprints → Vercel → `assetlinks.json` (about 15 minutes)**
11. Repo root: `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → choose the project → the `preview` build profile → Keystore → copy the line "SHA256 Fingerprint" (32 colon-separated hex pairs). If a `production` profile with its own keystore exists, repeat and keep both. Fingerprints are not secret, but never paste them into a Claude Code prompt or chat — `prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim; type them into Vercel only.
12. vercel.com → team `Anacast` → the web project → Settings → Environment Variables → Add `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` = the fingerprint(s), comma-separated, uppercase, for the **Production** and **Preview** environments → Save → Deployments → ⋯ on the latest Production deployment → **Redeploy** (environment changes take effect only on a new deployment).
13. In a terminal: `curl -s https://<DOMAIN>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` → a JSON array with one statement whose `package_name` is `com.anacast.app` and whose `sha256_cert_fingerprints` lists what you entered. An empty `[]` means the variable is missing or the redeploy has not finished. Then `curl -si https://<DOMAIN>/join/ABCDEFGH | head -20` → `200` and a header `x-robots-tag: noindex` (proves 5.8 is deployed).

**C. New preview APK with App Links (about 30 minutes, mostly waiting)**
14. `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` → wait for the build → download the APK from the EAS build page → install it on the phone (the keystore is unchanged, so it updates the 4.5 install in place; if Android complains about signatures, uninstall the old APK first). Write down the EAS build id and the date.
15. With the phone connected: `adb shell pm get-app-links com.anacast.app` → your web host shows `verified`. If it shows `none` or `1024`: `adb shell pm verify-app-links --re-verify com.anacast.app`, wait a minute, repeat. Usual causes: a fingerprint typo in Vercel, the redeploy not finished, or a network that blocks Google's verifier — `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` "Android App Links (5.7a)" has the troubleshooting list.
16. Invite link: `/o/<slug>/users` → Invite a test email address → open that email on the phone in a mail app (not by pasting into Chrome's address bar) → tap the link → Anacast opens on the invite screen.
17. Join link and QR: `/o/<slug>/join-codes` → Create join code (label `Checkpoint D`, auto-approve off, 3 uses) → **Copy link** → send the link to the phone (SMS, WhatsApp or email) → tap → Anacast opens on **Join** with the code filled in (if you are signed out on the phone, the sign-in screen shows the code instead). Then open the code's **Print** page on the computer → the sheet shows a QR square → scan it with the phone camera → the same join screen. On a phone without Anacast (or in a desktop browser) the same link shows the public landing page with the code, "Open in Anacast" and the Google Play text.

**D. Web acceptance — `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`, chapter "Phase 2 trial (Checkpoint D)" (about 45 minutes)**
18. Click through the chapter once as the super admin (you reach `/o/<slug>/*` directly — orchestrator decision 20) and once as the first church admin, in the chapter's order: directory — a household with two adults and a child, the privacy toggles, head of house, a leader note (5.1a/5.1b); CSV import — the sample file, then a small fictional list: the dry run reports errors, the commit imports (5.7b); calendars — an event submitted from the phone, approved on the web, the push arrives (5.3a/5.3b); a document uploaded and attached to an announcement (5.4a); a custom group with three members and an announcement targeted at it — a member of the group sees it on the phone, someone outside it does not (5.5); join codes — the request from item 17 (after the phone redeemed it) shows the Join requests badge → approve linking a directory person → `/users` lists the new active member (5.6b); a YouTube sermon → **Re-check link** (5.7a). Tick each item or write the observation as `<where> — <what I did> — <what I saw> — <what I expected>`.
19. The join flow needs an account that is not yet a member: use a fresh email address (a `+test` alias works) on a second phone, or sign out on yours: Sign in → "I have a join code" → the code → a 6-digit code arrives by email (this needs the **Confirm signup** template to contain `{{ .Token }}` — Supabase → Authentication → Email Templates; a 4.1b/5.6c to-do) → Join → "waiting for approval" → approve on the web → Check again → the feed opens. Also try a revoked code and Cancel request.

**E. Android acceptance — `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`, section "Phase 2 device checklist (consolidated)" (about 30 minutes)**
20. Run every block on the new APK: directory tabs and household self-service including the privacy confirmation and a photo (5.2a/5.2b); events by calendar and member submission (5.3b); documents open in the phone's viewer (5.4b); join with a code, cancel, revoked code (5.6c); App Links for `/invite` and `/join` (5.7a/5.8). Tick or note.

**F. Record**
21. `HANDOFF.md` → "Environment status": the EAS build id and date, the number of fingerprints entered (not the values), "Checkpoint D run on <date>"; the ledger rows from item 10 if you skipped the commit; a new heading "Checkpoint D observations" with one line per item that did not pass. Tick step 5.9 in `docs/TODO.md`. Or paste the helper prompt below with your observations and let the agent record everything and run the fix round (it cannot touch the hosted database or your phone, so it needs the pasted results).

Header comment: purpose, founder decision 8 quoted, "re-runnable; paste after 9999_init.sql (and 9998 if present)", and the list of objects it (re)defines. Sections:
   - (0) the same owner `rolbypassrls` assertion as 9999.
   - (3) `alter table public.survey_responses add column if not exists answered_on_behalf boolean not null default false;` — true when the response was submitted by someone other than the person it is for; lets results, CSV and the mobile list say "answered by head of house" without joining `persons.user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function app.can_answer_for(target_person uuid) returns boolean` (stable, definer): true iff the caller has a person in the same org as the target (`app.my_person_id(target.org_id)`), that caller person has `household_role = 'head'` and `household_id = target.household_id`, and the target has **no usable account** — `user_id is null`, OR the linked account is archived per orchestrator decision 15 (`profiles.archived_at is not null`, or whatever archival column/helper the G2/G3 fixers put into `9999_init.sql` — `grep -n archived_at supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`; if no such column exists yet, skip this branch and say so in `docs/RLS.md`), OR the linked user has no `active` row in `org_memberships` for the survey's org — and additionally `deceased_on is null`, `congregation_status in ('member','attendee')` and is not the caller. The `detail` reason `person_has_account` is raised only when the account is usable (active membership, not archived). Record this reading ('a deactivated or disabled family member may be answered for by the head') in `docs/RLS.md` and under HANDOFF Decisions. Super admins do not get a bypass here (answering surveys is a member act).
   - (5) `create or replace function app.stamp_response_scope()` — keep 1.3a's behaviour for the normal path byte-for-byte and add the proxy path: when `current_setting('app.answer_for', true)` is a non-empty uuid, require `app.can_answer_for(that uuid)` (else raise `survey_proxy_not_allowed` with errcode `42501` and a `detail` naming the reason: `not_head_of_house` / `different_household` / `person_has_account` / `person_not_active`), require the survey's `response_mode = 'per_person'` (else `survey_not_per_person`, `22023`), then stamp `person_id = target`, `household_id = target.household_id`, `scope_key` in the same format 1.3a uses for a person scope, `submitted_by_user_id = auth.uid()`, `answered_on_behalf = true`. On UPDATE with the setting, the proxy path applies only when the existing row's `person_id` equals the target. On UPDATE **without** the setting: if `old.answered_on_behalf` is true, keep `old.person_id`, `old.household_id`, `old.scope_key` and `old.answered_on_behalf` unchanged (the update policy already proved `app.can_answer_for(old.person_id)`) and refresh only `submitted_by_user_id = auth.uid()` — never re-stamp a proxied row to the head's own person, which would silently re-attribute the child's answers or collide with the head's own `(survey_id, scope_key)` row; otherwise apply 1.3a's normal re-stamp and set `answered_on_behalf = false`. On INSERT without the setting always stamp the self path with `answered_on_behalf = false`. The setting is read with `current_setting(name, true)` and is only ever set transaction-locally (`set_config(…, …, true)`) by the RPC below; a direct table insert from PostgREST can never carry it, so client inserts stay self-only.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.submit_survey_response_for(survey_id uuid, person_id uuid, answers jsonb) returns uuid` (definer, `search_path = ''`): `perform app.require_user()`; load the survey (raise `survey_not_found`/`P0002` when missing — reuse an existing key if 1.3b has one); `app.require_writable(org_id)`; `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` else `survey_proxy_not_allowed` (42501); `response_mode = 'per_person'` else `survey_not_per_person` (22023); open + in window else `survey_not_open`; **the target person** in the audience via `app.person_in_group(person_id, audience_group_id)` else `survey_not_in_audience` (the head's own membership in the audience is irrelevant — a men's survey may be answered by a father for a son without an account); validate `answers` keys exactly as `submit_survey_response` does (factor the shared validation into `app.validate_survey_answers(survey_id, answers)` if 1.3b did not already, and have both RPCs call it — `create or replace` of `submit_survey_response` is allowed because the signature does not change); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', person_id::text, true)`; insert the response (the trigger stamps scope) mapping the `(survey_id, scope_key)` unique violation to `survey_already_responded` unless `allow_edit`, in which case update the existing row for that person and replace its answers (`survey_edit_not_allowed` when `allow_edit` is false); `perform set_config('app.answer_for', '', true)` in every exit path (use a nested block with `exception when others then … raise`); return the response id. Audit: if `app.audit_row` is trigger-only, do not add rows by hand — record in `docs/RLS.md` that proxy responses are identifiable by `answered_on_behalf` + `submitted_by_user_id`.
   - (5) `create or replace function public.list_survey_proxy_targets(survey_id uuid) returns jsonb` (definer): `require_user`; returns `[]` unless the caller's person is `head` of a household in the survey's org; otherwise a JSON array of `{ person_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, household_role, in_audience boolean, response_id uuid|null, submitted_at timestamptz|null }` for every household member for whom `app.can_answer_for(person_id)` is true, ordered by `household_role` then `last_name, first_name`. Reads `persons` directly inside the definer function (directory reads from clients must go through `directory_persons` — DESIGN §5/§6; the definer RPC reads `persons` only for the caller's own household, which `directory_persons` already shows them, and it is an RPC rather than a view because it also evaluates `app.can_answer_for` per row); it exposes only names and role of the caller's own household.
   - (7) `drop trigger if exists … ; create trigger` for `stamp_response_scope` on `survey_responses` only if 1.3a's trigger name must change — otherwise leave 9999's trigger in place (the function body was replaced in place).
   - (8) `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` for the `survey_responses` and `survey_answers` policies you must widen (re-create only those, with their 1.4a names): select — add the branch "the caller is head of a household and the response's `person_id` is a member of that household with `answered_on_behalf`" — in practice `household_id = any(app.my_household_ids())` from 1.4a already covers it; verify and keep as is if so; update — add `or (answered_on_behalf and app.can_answer_for(person_id))` alongside the existing own/adult branch, still ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit`; `survey_answers` select/insert/update mirror through the `exists` on the parent response. No delete policies. Every policy keeps the `app.org_writable` requirement on writes.
   - (9) `revoke execute on function public.submit_survey_response_for(uuid, uuid, jsonb), public.list_survey_proxy_targets(uuid), app.can_answer_for(uuid) from public;` then `grant execute … to authenticated` (and `app.can_answer_for` to `authenticated` because a policy calls it, like 1.4a did for the other `app.*` helpers referenced in policies). `service_role` gets nothing new.
   - Error catalogue: add to the comment block (or wherever 1.3b keeps the catalogue) `survey_proxy_not_allowed 42501`, `survey_not_per_person 22023`, plus `survey_not_found P0002` if new. Keep `raise … using errcode = …, message = '<key>', detail = '<reason>'` in the same style as 1.3b so `toDomainError` maps them.

**Goal.** Church leaders holding `announcements.create` build surveys at `/o/<slug>/surveys/new` (title, description, audience group from `audience_groups` incl. custom groups, per person / per household, window, allow edits, push, up to N questions of the seven `question_kind`s with reorder), `announcements.edit` holders open them (the existing `on_content_publish` trigger + 3.6a dispatcher push a `survey` notification whose `data.url` is `/surveys/<id>`), edit non-frozen fields, and close them; `announcements.delete` holders delete. `/o/<slug>/surveys/<surveyId>` shows per-question summaries and a response table that names respondents through the directory views (with the documented 'Hidden household' fallback and an 'answered by head of house' badge from `answered_on_behalf`), and `/surveys/<surveyId>/export` streams an RFC 4180 CSV with one column per question. Playwright smoke and one full-E2E scenario cover it; `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` gains a Surveys section.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader with `announcements.create` can build a survey at `/o/<slug>/surveys/new` (title, description, audience group, response mode per person / per household, window, allow edits, push), add and reorder questions of the seven kinds, open it (which enqueues a push of kind `survey` through the existing trigger and dispatcher), watch responses arrive at `/o/<slug>/surveys/<surveyId>` with per-question summaries and a response table that names people through the directory views, close it, and download a CSV. `announcements.edit` holders edit/open/close, `announcements.delete` holders delete. Members do not answer on the web (mobile, 6.1c); the response table already marks rows answered by a head of house on behalf of a family member. Playwright smoke covers the pages; the full E2E gets one survey scenario.

Per household: one answer per family", `allow_edit` switch "Members may change their answer while the survey is open", `push` switch "Notify the audience when the survey opens", `window_mode: 'open_ended' | 'window'`, `opens_at_local` / `closes_at_local` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, converted with `zonedLocalToInstant(…, tz)` where `tz` is the `timezone` read with `getSettings(db, ctx.org.org_id)` from `packages/db/src/queries/settings.ts` exactly as 3.5a does — `OrgContext` carries no timezone, and its org-id field is `org.org_id` (read `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts`); `closes_at > opens_at` mirrored from the DB check), `questions: surveyQuestionFormSchema[]` (`kind`, `prompt`, `required`, `options` string[] for `single_choice`/`multi_choice` — at least 2 non-empty, unique after trim)) and `toSurveyInput(form, tz, now)` → validated with `surveySchema` + `surveyQuestionSchema` from `@church/domain` (single source of truth). Questions editor `src/features/surveys/QuestionEditor.tsx`: `useFieldArray`, add question (kind select), move up/down (buttons — no drag library), remove, per-kind option editor; `position` = array index on save. When the survey is not `draft`, the form renders `response_mode`, `audience_group_id` and the entire questions editor **read-only** with the notice "Questions and audience are locked once a survey is open (answers already refer to them)"; only title, description, window, `allow_edit` and `push` remain editable — this mirrors `freeze_survey_shape`; if the DB still raises `survey_shape_frozen` map it to a form-level error.
5. **Server Actions** `src/features/surveys/actions.ts` (`'use server'`; each receives `orgSlug`, re-runs `requireOrgMember` + `requirePerm` + `requireWritable`, validates with Zod, writes with the USER client, returns `ActionResult`): `createSurvey(orgSlug, input)` → `insertSurvey` (`created_by = ctx.userId` via `getAuthContext()`), then `replaceSurveyQuestions`; on a question insert failure delete the survey row again (draft, no answers) and return the error — no partial surveys; `updateSurvey(orgSlug, surveyId, input)` → `updateSurvey` + `replaceSurveyQuestions` only while `draft`; `openSurvey(orgSlug, surveyId, { opens_at?, closes_at? })` → `canTransitionSurvey('draft','open')`, requires ≥ 1 question (else `fail('Add at least one question before opening')`), `setSurveyStatus(db, id, 'open', { opens_at: opens_at ?? now })`, then — exactly as 3.5a's `createAnnouncementAction` does (read it) — call `afterContentPublish({ orgId: ctx.org.org_id })` from `src/lib/push/after-publish.ts` so the queued `survey` notification is dispatched within the request (`maxDuration = 60` on the page/route that hosts the action, matching 3.5a). Future `opens_at`: read `app.on_content_publish`'s survey branch in `9999_init.sql` first — if it sets `notifications.scheduled_for = opens_at`, allow a future `opens_at`, show the list badge "Scheduled — opens <date>" (reuse 6.2b's `pushStatusLabel` extension if 6.2b ran, else add the label additively) and refuse to edit `opens_at` once open unless you also move the queued push through 6.2b's `rescheduleQueuedNotification` (import it if 6.2b ran; otherwise refuse the edit with the message "Reopen as a new survey"); if it sets `scheduled_for = now()`, force `opens_at <= now` in `openSurvey` (field error "Open the survey when it should start") so a push never announces a survey members cannot open yet; `closeSurvey(orgSlug, surveyId)` → `open → closed` (`closes_at = now` when null or in the future); `deleteSurvey(orgSlug, surveyId)` → `announcements.delete`; confirm dialog states the response count that will be deleted (cascade). Errors through `toActionError`/`toDomainError`: `survey_shape_frozen`, `organization_suspended`, 23514 (`closes_at > opens_at` → field error on `closes_at_local`), `permission_denied`/0-rows → "You no longer have permission".

Response table: one row per response — respondent (person "First Last" or household name; for `per_household` rows the household name; "Hidden household" when the directory view returns nothing because the manager is not a directory admin and the household is private — DESIGN §5's known consequence, state it in a footnote), `answered_on_behalf` → badge "answered by head of house", `submitted_at`, then one column per question (multi_choice joined with `; `, booleans Yes/No, dates `formatDateOnly`). Keep the table inside an `overflow-x-auto` container.
7. **CSV export** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/surveys/[surveyId]/export/route.ts` (`GET`, Node runtime, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`): same guards as the page (`requireOrgMember`, `requirePerm` any of the three), user client, builds the CSV with `src/features/surveys/csv.ts` (pure, unit-tested `buildSurveyCsv(questions, responses, names)`): UTF-8 with BOM, RFC 4180 quoting (double quotes doubled; fields containing `,` `"` `\n` quoted; values starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` prefixed with `'` to defuse spreadsheet formula injection), header `response_id,scope,respondent,household,answered_on_behalf,submitted_at,<question prompt 1>,…` (prompts deduplicated with ` (2)` suffixes), `submitted_at` ISO in the org timezone, multi_choice joined with `; `. Headers `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<slug>-survey-<surveyId>-<YYYYMMDD>.csv"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Guard pattern in the Route Handler (`requirePerm` is written for pages/actions and renders or throws, so do not call it here): `const ctx = await requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` then `if (!hasAnyPerm(ctx, ['announcements.create', 'announcements.edit', 'announcements.delete'])) return Response.json({ error: 'permission_denied' }, { status: 403 })` (use the permission helper 2.1b/3.1 exported — read `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` for its name); anonymous callers are already redirected by `proxy.ts` because the route sits under `(org)`.

## Constraints
- Reads of people and households only through `directory_persons` / `directory_households` (DESIGN §13 risk 14); no service client anywhere in this step except the existing push dispatcher path. Never `select *` on `persons`.
- Do not change `9999_init.sql` or `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql`; if a DB change is unavoidable, write the next free descending number recorded in the HANDOFF ledger (9996 is proposed for 5.8 — ask me if the ledger does not say which number is free), re-runnable per `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`, and record it.
- No member-facing web responder (members answer in the app — 6.1c); no anonymous surveys (Phase 4); no charts library (plain bars); no drag-and-drop dependency. No new dependencies at all.
- Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, RHF + `zodResolver`, `sonner`. Keep 2.1's security headers and CSP. No model identifiers, no secrets, no real email addresses.

- [ ] `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `pnpm --filter web build` and `pnpm --filter web test:e2e:smoke` are green; the `full` project has `05-surveys.spec.ts` (create → open → CSV → close → member gets 403 JSON from the export route); the smoke suite covers unauthenticated redirects for the list, new, results and export URLs; `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` has a Surveys section; HANDOFF.md and docs/TODO.md are updated.

**Notes.** Revised after critique: uses G9's real names (`afterContentPublish({ orgId })`, `getDeliveryCounts(orgSlug, notificationIds[])`), reads the org timezone through `getSettings` (OrgContext has none) and the org id as `ctx.org.org_id`, settles the future-`opens_at` push behaviour by reading `on_content_publish`, gives the export Route Handler an explicit 403-JSON guard, and moves the manual check to the hosted project. Second part of the 6.1 split. Route names chosen because PLAN §8 only says `/surveys/*`: list, `new`, `[surveyId]` (results + manage), `[surveyId]/edit`, `[surveyId]/export` (Route Handler). Web has no member responder — DESIGN §10 puts Surveys in the mobile More tab and DESIGN §11 calls a member web view optional; if the founder wants leaders to answer on the web, that is a new step. The CSV route lives inside the `(org)` tree so `proxy.ts` and the org guards apply; a spreadsheet-formula defusal rule is included because survey answers are free text typed by members. The push after opening reuses 3.5a/3.6a's synchronous `dispatch()` wiring; the agent must read the real function name. The 'Hidden household' consequence (DESIGN §5) is surfaced in a footnote rather than hidden. Depends on 6.1a only (6.1a already depends on 5.2b and 5.5); the hosted trial additionally requires the founder to paste 9997.

## Constraints
- Native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install <pkg>`; this step should need no new native module (masked date field). No `react-hook-form` on mobile (G11 convention). No elevated keys; the mobile client only ever holds the publishable key.
- Reads of people only via `directory_persons` / `list_survey_proxy_targets`; never `select` on `persons`. Do not persist answers in the query cache. No anonymous surveys; no survey management on mobile (leaders use the web, 6.1b).
- Do not change `9999_init.sql` or `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql`; if a DB change is unavoidable, write the next free descending number recorded in the HANDOFF ledger, re-runnable, and record it. Do not touch web code except `@church/domain`/`@church/db` additive helpers with tests.
- Expo 57 / RN 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 exact; TanStack Query 5. No model identifiers, no secrets, no real email addresses.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader holding `org.settings` opens `/o/<slug>/audit` and sees, newest first, who changed what in their church: permission grants and revocations, membership status changes, invitation activity, settings edits, household privacy changes, person status/link changes, share-link creation and revocation, sermon deletions — each row naming the actor (or "System" for trigger/cron work), the table in plain words, the action, the affected row and a readable before/after diff. Filters for table, actor, action, date range (in the church's timezone) and row id live in the URL, pages load with a keyset cursor, and "Download CSV" exports the filtered result. Nothing in the UI can write to `audit_log`; the pages read through RLS with the user client only. `docs/RLS.md` documents what is audited and what is never rendered, and the Playwright suites cover both pages.
