Every helper takes the client first and uses explicit column lists.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `permissions.ts` (`PERMISSION_KEYS`, `PERMISSION_LABELS`, the three role groups), `schemas/enums.ts`, `errors.ts` (`permission_denied`, `not_found`, `invalid_payload`), `dates.ts`.
- Web (2.1–3.8, 5.x, 6.1b): `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext`; read the file for the org-id field name), `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` (`hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm`), `src/lib/auth/require-super.ts` (`requireSuperAdmin()`), `src/lib/dates.ts` (`formatInstantInZone(iso, tz)`, `zonedLocalToInstant(datetimeLocal, tz)`, `instantToZonedLocal`, `todayInZone` — the ONLY date helpers; do not add another module), `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`NAV_ITEMS` with `requires` any-of), the `AdminShell` sidebar (2.2a) and its breadcrumb pattern, `src/features/orgs/StatusBadge.tsx`, the list-page house style of `src/features/announcements/AnnouncementsTable.tsx` (3.5a) and its `?show=` search-param filter, `src/lib/actions/result.ts` (`ActionResult`), `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` and the env-gated full E2E from 3.7 (`pnpm --filter web test:e2e:full`), `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` (3.8). 6.1b shipped a CSV export for survey results — find its writer with `git grep -n "text/csv" apps/web` and reuse it; if 6.1b inlined the CSV code, extract it to `src/lib/csv.ts` (`toCsv(rows: string[][]): string`, RFC 4180 quoting, cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` prefixed with `'` against spreadsheet formula injection) and re-point 6.1b's route at it.
- Routes that audit rows can link to (link only when the route exists in the repo at build time — check with `ls apps/web/app`): `/o/[orgSlug]/users/[membershipId]` (3.2), `/o/[orgSlug]/invitations` (3.2), `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]` (3.3a; share links live on it), `/o/[orgSlug]/settings` (3.1), the 5.1 directory household route (read HANDOFF for its exact shape — DESIGN §9 says `/directory/*`), `/admin/churches/[orgId]` (2.2a), `/admin/super-admins` (2.2b).
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 4 — "Permission mapping (docs/DESIGN.md §5 table) ships as the default": audit log viewing is `org.settings`; nothing else unlocks `/o/<slug>/audit`. Decision 1 and 2 — household privacy changes are audited (`hide_from_fellowship`, `hide_from_congregation`, `show_children_in_fellowship`, `privacy_confirmed_at`) and must be readable in the diff. Decision 7 — reading the audit log is not a write; the page works for `past_due` and `suspended` churches alike (no `requireWritable`).

## Build
1. **`@church/db` `packages/db/src/queries/audit.ts`** (user client; explicit columns `id, org_id, actor_user_id, table_name, row_id, action, old_data, new_data, created_at`): `listAuditLog(db, filters: AuditFilters): Promise<{ rows: AuditRow[]; nextCursor: string | null }>` where `AuditFilters = { orgId?: string | null; table?: string; actorUserId?: string | 'system'; action?: string; rowId?: string; from?: string; to?: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number }` — `orgId` undefined = no org filter (super admin page), `null` = platform rows (`org_id is null`); `'system'` → `actor_user_id is null`; `from`/`to` are ISO instants on `created_at`; order `created_at desc, id desc`; keyset cursor = base64url of `{ created_at, id }` decoded with a Zod schema (an invalid cursor → `invalid_payload`), applied as `(created_at, id) < (cursor.created_at, cursor.id)` using `.or()` with the two-clause expansion (`created_at.lt.X,and(created_at.eq.X,id.lt.Y)`); `limit` default 50, max 200; fetch `limit + 1` rows to compute `nextCursor`. `listAuditActors(db, orgId)` → distinct `actor_user_id` values for the org in the last 90 days merged with display names from the profiles two-query helper (`{ userId, displayName | null }`; null name → "(profile not visible)"). `countAuditSince(db, orgId, sinceIso)` (`{ count: 'exact', head: true }`) for a dashboard tile. Export `AUDITED_TABLES` — the ten table names above with labels ("Church", "Church settings", "Memberships", "Permissions", "Household privacy", "Person status & links", "Share links", "Sermon deletions", "Invitations", "Super admins") and `AUDIT_ACTIONS = ['INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE','invitation_permissions_dropped','org_without_manager']` with labels ("Created", "Changed", "Deleted", "Invitation permissions dropped", "Church left without a manager") — but derive both lists from the real triggers and `insert into public.audit_log` / synthetic-action sites in `9999_init.sql` (`grep -n audit_log supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`) rather than trusting this paragraph: orchestrator decision 15 added account archive/restore/deletion-request RPCs (`deactivate_account`, `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account`, the cancel path) that act on `profiles` / `account_deletion_requests`; if the G2/G3 fixers audit them, add that table and its actions with the labels "Account archived", "Account restored", "Deletion requested", "Deletion cancelled" and a `Platform`-scoped row link to the `/admin` users list (6.3a); if they did not audit archive/restore, record it under HANDOFF "Open questions" as a gap for the next migration. Vitest in `packages/db` with the mocked client: cursor encode/decode round trip, invalid cursor → `invalid_payload`, `limit + 1` fetch and `nextCursor` derivation, `orgId: null` → `is('org_id', null)`, `'system'` actor → `is('actor_user_id', null)`.
2. **Filter parsing** `apps/web/src/features/audit/filters.ts`: `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz, allowOrg }): AuditFilters` — reads `table` (must be in `AUDITED_TABLES`), `actor` (uuid or `system`), `action` (in `AUDIT_ACTIONS`), `row` (uuid), `from`/`to` (`YYYY-MM-DD` in the org timezone → instants via `zonedLocalToInstant`, `to` = end of that day), `cursor`, and `org` (uuid or `platform`, only when `allowOrg`); unknown values are dropped, never thrown. `auditFiltersToSearchParams(filters)` for the reverse. Default date range: none on the org page; **last 7 days on `/admin/audit`** (there is no cross-org index — the default range bounds the scan; say so in a code comment and in `docs/RLS.md`). Table tests for every parameter, the timezone boundary (`from=2026-09-07` in `America/New_York` → `2026-09-07T04:00:00Z`) and the drop-not-throw rule.
3. **Diff rendering** `src/features/audit/diff.ts`: `diffAuditRow(row): AuditChange[]` where `AuditChange = { key, label, before: string | null, after: string | null }` — for `UPDATE` only keys whose JSON differs between `old_data` and `new_data`; for `INSERT` every key of `new_data`; for `DELETE` every key of `old_data`; for the two synthetic actions whatever the RPC stored. Format values with `formatAuditValue(key, value, tz)`: booleans → "Yes"/"No"; ISO timestamps (keys ending `_at`) → `formatInstantInZone`; `permission` / `permissions` arrays → `PERMISSION_LABELS`; uuids → shortened (`8 chars…`) with the full value in a `title`; nulls → "—"; objects → compact JSON. Column labels from a per-table map (`hide_from_fellowship` → "Hidden from fellowship", `congregation_status` → "Congregation status", `user_id` → "Linked account", `requires_password` → "Password required", …; unknown keys fall back to the column name). **Deny-list, defence in depth**: `NEVER_RENDER_KEYS = ['notes', 'birthdate', 'anniversary', 'password_hash', 'token_hash', 'token']` are dropped from every diff and from the Raw view even if a future trigger stores them (1.3a never does; 07's test asserts it). Special rendering: `org_membership_permissions` INSERT → "Granted <permission label>", DELETE → "Revoked <permission label>"; `invitations` → email + permission labels; `sermons` DELETE → title and media kind. Vitest: UPDATE keeps only changed keys, INSERT/DELETE sides, every deny-listed key is absent from the output of a row that contains them all, permission labels resolve, timestamps render in the given zone.
4. **Row links** `src/features/audit/links.ts`: `auditRowHref(row, { orgSlug, isSuperPage }): string | null` mapping `table_name` + ids to the routes listed under Inputs (`org_membership_permissions` uses `membership_id` from `new_data`/`old_data`; `sermon_share_links` uses `sermon_id`; `households`/`persons` link to the 5.1 directory route when present; `super_admins` → `/admin/super-admins`; `organizations`/`organization_settings` → `/o/<slug>/settings` on the org page, `/admin/churches/<orgId>` on the admin page); deleted rows return null. Unit-test the map; the test reads `apps/web/app` with `fs` to assert that every returned path prefix exists as a route directory (skip a mapping gracefully when 5.1's directory route is absent — say which in the test name).
5. **Components** `src/features/audit/`: `AuditFilters.tsx` (client; shadcn `Select` for table/action/actor/church, two date inputs, a row-id input, Apply → `router.replace` with the new search params, Clear; the actor list comes from `listAuditActors` plus "System"; the church select on the admin page from `listOrganizations` plus "Platform"); `AuditTable.tsx` (server-rendered rows: When (`formatInstantInZone` in the org tz — on the admin page use each row's church timezone from the organizations list, falling back to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`), Actor (display name → link to `/o/<slug>/users/<membershipId>` when the actor is a current member; "System" for null; "(profile not visible)" when unknown), Table label, Action label as a badge, Row (short id + link from `auditRowHref`), Summary (first change as "label: before → after", "+N more"); every row expands (`Collapsible`) into `AuditEntryDetail.tsx`: the full change list as a two-column before/after table, and a "Raw" toggle showing the deny-list-filtered `old_data`/`new_data` JSON); `LoadMore.tsx` (a link to the same URL with `cursor=nextCursor`; plain `<a>` so it works without JS); `AuditEmpty` states ("No audit entries match these filters" / "Nothing has been audited yet — permission, membership, privacy and sharing changes appear here").
6. **Pages**: `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit/page.tsx` — server component, `await params` and `await searchParams`, `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(ctx, 'org.settings')` (no `requireWritable`), `getSettings` for `timezone`, `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz, allowOrg: false })` forced to `orgId = ctx org id`, `listAuditLog`, `listAuditActors`, render filters + table + load-more + "Download CSV" button (href `/o/<slug>/audit/export?<same params>`); heading text: "Every permission, membership, privacy, sharing and settings change in <church name>. Entries are written by the database and cannot be edited or deleted." `app/(super)/admin/audit/page.tsx` — `requireSuperAdmin()`, `parseAuditFilters(searchParams, { tz: DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, allowOrg: true })` with the 7-day default when no `from`/`to`, `listOrganizations` for the church select and per-row church name/timezone, actor names via the profile merge (super admins read every profile), rows with `org_id null` show "Platform"; same components; CSV button → `/admin/audit/export`. Add "Audit log" to `NAV_ITEMS` in `src/features/org/nav.ts` with `requires: ['org.settings']` (after Settings) and to the `AdminShell` sidebar; on `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx` add a small "Changes in the last 7 days: N" tile (`countAuditSince`) linking to `/audit` for `org.settings` holders — additive, do not restyle the dashboard.
7. **CSV export** route handlers `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit/export/route.ts` and `app/(super)/admin/audit/export/route.ts` (`runtime = 'nodejs'`, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`): same guards as the pages, same `parseAuditFilters`, iterate `listAuditLog` pages (limit 200) up to **10,000 rows** then stop and append a final line `# truncated at 10000 rows — narrow the date range`, columns `created_at_utc, created_at_local, actor, table, action, row_id, changes` (`changes` = `label: before → after` joined by `; ` from `diffAuditRow`, deny-list applied), `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="audit-<slug or all>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Guards in the Route Handlers (`requirePerm`/`requireSuperAdmin` are written for pages and render or throw — do not call them here): org route `const ctx = await requireOrgMember(orgSlug); if (!hasPerm(ctx, 'org.settings')) return Response.json({ error: 'permission_denied' }, { status: 403 })` (use the permission helper 2.1b/3.1 exported — read `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` for its name); super route `const ctx = await getSuperAdminContext(); if (!ctx) return Response.json({ error: 'forbidden' }, { status: 403 })` (2.1b's null-returning variant). Anonymous callers are already redirected by `proxy.ts` because the routes sit under `(org)`/`(super)`.
8. **Tests and QA**: Vitest for `filters`, `diff`, `links`, the nav visibility change (`org.settings` → Audit log visible; a `users.create`-only leader → hidden), and a page-level test of the org page's guard with the mocked context (no `org.settings` → 403 via `requirePerm`; `suspended` org still renders). Playwright smoke (`apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`): anonymous `/o/any/audit`, `/o/any/audit/export`, `/admin/audit` → redirect to `/login?next=…`; with the smoke's mock session, if 3.7 provides one, the org page renders the filter form. Env-gated full E2E (`test:e2e:full`, 3.7's scenario file): after the existing "admin toggles permissions" step, open `/o/<slug>/audit?table=org_membership_permissions` → a row "Granted <label>" by the admin's display name appears; as the super admin open `/admin/audit?org=<orgId>&table=org_membership_permissions` → the same row; `/o/<slug>/audit` as the plain member → 403; as the provisioned church admin (not super) open `/admin/audit` → 403 (or the `requireSuperAdmin` redirect 2.1b chose — assert whichever it is) and `GET /admin/audit/export` → 403 JSON with no CSV body. Add a Vitest that every distinct `table_name`/`action` pair written by the SQL test fixtures (`grep -h "audit_log" supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` — 07's part (d) and 6.3a's `13_account_deletion.sql` if present) is contained in `AUDITED_TABLES`/`AUDIT_ACTIONS`, so a new audited action cannot be silently dropped by the filters.
9. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` — "Audit log" subsection: the ten audited tables and which columns of `households`/`persons` are captured, the synthetic actions, "never stores leader notes, birthdates or secrets" plus the UI deny-list, who can read (`org.settings` or super), the 7-day default and the missing cross-org index (a future `9996_*` migration may add `audit_log (created_at desc)` if `/admin/audit` becomes slow — do NOT add it now). `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` — an "Audit log" click-through (toggle a permission → find it; change a household's privacy → find the before/after; download the CSV; plain member → 403). `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md` — tick "audit rows on permission/privacy changes" with the URL where the founder can see them.

## Constraints
- User client only: no `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` import anywhere under `src/features/audit/`, `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/audit` or `app/(super)/admin/audit` — RLS decides what a viewer sees, the page guard is the first line. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components, pages or routes; every read goes through `@church/db` (add helpers additively, with tests).
- Never write to `audit_log` from the app, never add an "audit note" feature, never call an `srv_*` RPC here. No migrations: `9999_init.sql` may be frozen (check the ledger) and this step needs no schema change; if you find one is needed, record it under HANDOFF "Open questions" instead.
- Never render `notes`, `birthdate`, `anniversary` or any secret even if present in a jsonb payload (deny-list + test). Never read `persons`/`households` directly for names — actors are resolved through profiles/memberships; audited person rows show only the ids and the captured columns.
- Keep 3.5a/3.6a/6.1b code intact apart from the CSV extraction (item 8 of Inputs) and the nav/dashboard additions. Do not touch `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, the mobile app, `apps/web/vercel.json` or the cron. Do not build the notification status page or the scheduled-announcement polish — that is 6.2b.
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*`.
- No model names, no secrets, `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in tests and fixtures.

## Goal
When you finish, scheduled announcements are a first-class thing on the web: `/o/<slug>/announcements` has a Scheduled view sorted by publish time with "publishes in 2 days (Wed, Sep 9, 09:00)" captions, and `announcements.edit` holders can **Reschedule** or **Publish now** from the row; moving a publish time also moves the queued push (`notifications.scheduled_for`) so an announcement pulled forward is pushed at its new time instead of the old one — the gap 3.5a/3.6a left open. Leaders holding any `announcements.*` permission get a delivery status page at `/o/<slug>/notifications` listing every push the church has queued, sent, failed or cancelled across announcements, bulletins, events and surveys, with kind/status/date filters, delivery counts, Retry, and a detail page per notification that shows which recipients' devices received a ticket, the Expo receipt outcome and the error text — the place to look when "my push did not arrive". Docs tell the founder where to look; Playwright covers the pages.

## Inputs / prior state
- Database (1.2–1.4c, frozen if pasted — check the ledger): `notifications (id, org_id, kind notification_kind, ref_id, audience_group_id, title, body, data, status notification_status, scheduled_for default now(), claimed_at, sent_at, attempts default 0, last_error, created_at, updated_at)` with indexes `(status, scheduled_for)` and `(kind, ref_id)`; statuses `queued, claimed, sent, failed, cancelled`; kinds `announcement, event, survey, bulletin`. `notification_deliveries (id, notification_id fk cascade, user_id fk auth.users, device_id fk push_devices set null, expo_ticket_id, receipt_status, error, created_at, updated_at)`; `push_devices (id, user_id, expo_push_token, platform push_platform, device_name, enabled, last_seen_at, …)`. RLS: `notifications` select for `announcements.*` holders, no write policies for `authenticated` (`revoke insert, update, delete`); `notification_deliveries` select super admin only. `srv_claim_notifications(max_rows)` claims `queued` rows with `scheduled_for <= now()` and `attempts < 5` — a queued row whose `scheduled_for` is in the future is untouched until that instant, which is why a moved `publish_at` needs the outbox row moved too. `app.on_content_publish` inserts one row per publish-worthy announcement (`scheduled_for = publish_at`); `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete` cancels on delete.
- 3.5a: `src/features/announcements/actions.ts` (`createAnnouncementAction`, `updateAnnouncementAction`, `deleteAnnouncementAction`), `announcement-state.ts` (`deriveAnnouncementState` → `scheduled | active | expired`), `AnnouncementsTable.tsx` with `?show=active|scheduled|expired|all` for managers, `AnnouncementForm.tsx` with the notice "Push already queued — a moved publish time is re-checked by the dispatcher before sending" (3.6a wording), `src/lib/dates.ts` (`formatInstantInZone`, `zonedLocalToInstant`, `instantToZonedLocal` — the only date helpers). 3.5b: `/o/[orgSlug]/bulletins` Push column reusing `PushStatusBadge`. 5.3a: `/o/[orgSlug]/events` (+ `/events/pending`); 6.1b: `/o/[orgSlug]/surveys/[surveyId]`.
- 3.6a: `src/lib/push/after-publish.ts` (`afterContentPublish({ orgId })` → `AfterPublishResult`), `src/lib/push/dispatch.ts` (`dispatchQueued`), `src/lib/push/refs.ts` (`loadNotificationRef` → `future` state reschedules a claimed row to the content's publish time), `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts` (`retryPush(orgSlug, notificationId)` — permission follows the row's kind: `bulletins.upload` for bulletin rows, `announcements.edit` otherwise; `getDeliveryCounts(orgSlug, notificationIds)` — counts by `receipt_status` through the service client, org-checked), `PushStatusBadge.tsx` + `pushStatusLabel(status, row)`, `@church/db` service-only helpers `getNotificationById(svc, id)`, `resetNotificationForRetry(svc, id)`, `countDeliveriesByNotification(svc, ids)`, `listPendingReceipts`, `insertDeliveries`, plus user-client `listNotificationStatus(db, orgId, { kind? })` (1.7a/5.3a) in `queries/announcements.ts`. 3.6b: the service-client whitelist asserted by `git grep` (`src/lib/push/*`, `src/lib/cron/*`, `app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`, `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts`) and `docs/ENV.md` "Push & maintenance job".
- `@church/domain`: `urls.ts` `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` (mobile deep-link paths — do not reuse for web links), `schemas/enums.ts` (`notificationKindSchema`, `notificationStatusSchema`), `errors.ts` (`permission_denied`, `not_found`, `invalid_payload`, `organization_suspended`). Guards: `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember` → `OrgContext`; read the org-id field name), `require-perm.ts` (`hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm` any-of with an array, `requireWritable`), `src/features/org/nav.ts`, `src/lib/actions/result.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/*` (3.7).
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only" (`requireWritable` before Reschedule / Publish now / Retry; the status pages are read-only and work for every status); decision 6 — bulletin pushes exist (`push_on_bulletin`), so the status page must show `bulletin` rows; decision 4 — the mapping ships as the default: the status pages are for `announcements.*` holders (mirrors the `notifications` select policy), Retry on bulletin rows stays with `bulletins.upload` (3.6a). Orchestrator decision 7 fixed the 3.5/3.6 ordering; this step only polishes what they built.

## Build
1. **Outbox helpers in `@church/db`** (`packages/db/src/queries/notifications.ts`, additive, tests with the mocked client): user-client `listNotifications(db, orgId, { kind?, status?, from?, to?, cursor?, limit = 50 })` → `{ rows, nextCursor }` ordered `scheduled_for desc, id desc` with the same base64url keyset cursor pattern 6.2a used for the audit log (put the cursor codec in `packages/db/src/cursor.ts` if 6.2a inlined it, and re-point 6.2a's `audit.ts` at it); `countNotificationsByStatus(db, orgId, sinceIso)` → `Record<notification_status, number>` (one grouped query or five head counts — keep it simple); service-only `rescheduleQueuedNotification(svc, { kind, refId, scheduledFor })` → number of rows updated (`update … set scheduled_for, updated_at = now() where kind = … and ref_id = … and status = 'queued'`; `claimed`/`sent`/`failed`/`cancelled` rows are never moved); service-only `listDeliveriesForNotification(svc, notificationId)` → rows `id, user_id, device_id, expo_ticket_id, receipt_status, error, created_at` embedded with `push_devices(platform, device_name, enabled)` through the real `device_id` FK (embedding is allowed only through FKs that exist in `9999_init.sql` — this one does). Add `queryKeys.notifications.list(orgId, filters)` and `.notifications.detail(id)` to `keys.ts` with the uniqueness test.
2. **Reschedule and Publish now** — `src/features/announcements/schedule-actions.ts` (`'use server'`; the second sanctioned service-client file in `src/features/announcements/` next to `push-actions.ts`): `rescheduleAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id, publishAtLocal)` and `publishAnnouncementNowAction(orgSlug, id)`. Sequence for both: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')` → `requireWritable(ctx)` → `getAnnouncement(db, id)` with the USER client (`not_found` when missing or not visible — the org check is the RLS-scoped read plus an explicit `row.org_id === ctx org id` comparison) → the row must still be scheduled (`deriveAnnouncementState(row) === 'scheduled'`; otherwise `invalid_payload` with the message "This announcement is already published") → new instant: `zonedLocalToInstant(publishAtLocal, tz)` validated as **at least one minute in the future** (`invalid_payload` "Pick a time in the future") for Reschedule, `now()` for Publish now → `updateAnnouncement(db, id, { publish_at })` — plus whatever actor column 3.5a's `updateAnnouncementAction` already sets, if any; `announcements` has no documented `updated_by` column (PLAN §4) — with the USER client (0 rows → "You no longer have permission to edit announcements") → ONLY THEN, with `createServiceSupabase()`, `rescheduleQueuedNotification(svc, { kind: 'announcement', refId: id, scheduledFor })` (0 rows moved is fine: push was off or the row already left `queued`) → for Publish now additionally `afterContentPublish({ orgId })` so the push goes out in the same request → `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements')`, `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/notifications')` → `ActionResult` carrying `{ publishAt, pushMoved: boolean, dispatched }` for the toast ("Rescheduled — push moves with it" / "Rescheduled" / "Published — push sent to N devices" / "Published — push queued"). Then make the edit form consistent: in 3.5a's `updateAnnouncementAction`, after a successful update whose `publish_at` changed and whose new state is `scheduled`, call the same `rescheduleQueuedNotification` (factor a tiny `moveQueuedPush(svc, id, publishAt)` helper inside `schedule-actions.ts` and import it — do not duplicate the service call), and change the form notice to "Push notifications move with the publish time" (delete the 3.6a "re-checked by the dispatcher" sentence — `pushStatusLabel` keeps handling the `future` case for rows the cron rescheduled).
3. **Scheduled view polish** — `src/features/announcements/ScheduledAnnouncements.tsx` (server-rendered table used when `?show=scheduled`, and as a "Coming up" strip of at most 3 rows above the default `all` view when any scheduled rows exist): columns Publishes (`formatInstantInZone` + relative caption "in 2 days" computed server-side from `now` in the org zone — no client clock drift), Title, Audience, Push (`PushStatusBadge`: `queued` with a future `scheduled_for` now reads "Scheduled — sends at <time>" — extend `pushStatusLabel` additively), Actions: **Reschedule** (a `Popover` with a `datetime-local` input, minimum = next minute in the org tz, caption "Times are in <timezone>", Save → `rescheduleAnnouncementAction`), **Publish now** (`AlertDialog`: "Publish '<title>' now? Its push notification, if on, is sent immediately." → `publishAnnouncementNowAction`), Edit, Delete (existing). Sort ascending by `publish_at` (the soonest first) — the `all` view keeps 3.5a's `pinned desc, publish_at desc`. Empty state: "Nothing scheduled — pick 'Schedule for' when creating an announcement". `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx`: turn the announcements tile into two lines "Active: N · Scheduled: M (next <date>)" for managers — additive; read counts through existing `@church/db` helpers (add a `countAnnouncementsByState` head-count helper additively if none fits).
4. **Delivery status list** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/page.tsx` (server; `await params`/`searchParams`): `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(ctx, ['announcements.create', 'announcements.edit', 'announcements.delete'])` (any-of; mirrors the select policy — a `bulletins.upload`-only leader keeps seeing bulletin push status on `/bulletins`, 3.5b) → `getSettings` (timezone) → `parseNotificationFilters(searchParams, tz)` in `src/features/notifications/filters.ts` (`kind` ∈ the four kinds, `status` ∈ the five statuses, `from`/`to` dates in the org tz on `scheduled_for`, `cursor`; unknown values dropped) → `listNotifications` → `getDeliveryCounts(orgSlug, ids)` (3.6a, one call for the page) → `listAudienceGroups` for names. Render `src/features/notifications/NotificationsTable.tsx`: summary tiles for the last 7 days from `countNotificationsByStatus` ("Queued", "Sent", "Failed" — Failed links to `?status=failed`), filter bar (`NotificationFilters.tsx`, client, `router.replace`), rows: Kind badge, Title (link to the content when the route exists in the repo — `announcement` → `/o/<slug>/announcements/<ref_id>/edit`, `bulletin` → `/o/<slug>/bulletins`, `event` → `/o/<slug>/events`, `survey` → `/o/<slug>/surveys/<ref_id>`; check `ls apps/web/app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]` at build time and omit links whose route is absent — keep this map in `src/features/notifications/links.ts` with a unit test like 6.2a's), Audience (group name; "Everyone" for null), Scheduled for (`formatInstantInZone`), Status (`PushStatusBadge` with the counts; the failed label shows `last_error`), Attempts (`attempts`/5), Sent (`sent_at`), Actions: Retry (3.6a's `retryPush`, shown when `status = 'failed'` and the caller may retry that kind: `hasPerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')` for non-bulletin rows, `hasPerm(ctx, 'bulletins.upload')` for bulletin rows), Details → `/o/<slug>/notifications/<id>`. Load more via cursor link. Empty state: "No push notifications yet — publishing an announcement, bulletin, approved event or opened survey queues one".
5. **Delivery detail** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/notifications/[notificationId]/page.tsx`: same guard; the notification row through the USER client (`getNotificationForOrg(db, orgId, id)` — additive user-client helper selecting by `id` and `org_id`; `notFound()` when absent — RLS plus the explicit org filter); then `listDeliveriesAction(orgSlug, notificationId)` from `src/features/notifications/notification-actions.ts` (`'use server'`; the ONLY service-client file under `src/features/notifications/`): `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm(any announcements.*)` → `getNotificationById(svc, id)` (3.6a) → refuse with `not_found` unless `row.org_id` equals the ctx org → `listDeliveriesForNotification(svc, id)` → resolve recipient display names from `profiles` by `user_id` through a new service-only helper `listProfileNames(svc: ServiceDbClient, userIds: string[])` (explicit columns `user_id, display_name`; add it to `packages/db/src/queries/profiles.ts` or the file the 2.2b/3.2 merge helper lives in, with a mocked-client test — the existing helper takes the user-scoped `DbClient` and the service client is branded `ServiceDbClient`, so reuse would not typecheck and casting is forbidden; names only, never emails) → return `{ targeted: distinct user count, devices: row count, ok, error, pending (receipt_status null), rows: [{ displayName, platform, deviceName, enabled, ticket: boolean, receiptStatus, error }] }`. Render `src/features/notifications/DeliveryDetail.tsx`: header (kind, title, body excerpt, audience, scheduled/sent times, status, attempts, `last_error`), the summary numbers with one-line explanations ("Pending — Expo has not reported a receipt yet; receipts are fetched by the maintenance job about 15 minutes after sending", "Error — see the row; `DeviceNotRegistered` means the app was uninstalled and the device was disabled"), and the per-device table. Zero deliveries for a `sent` row → "Sent — but nobody in the audience had a registered device". Retry button as in item 4. Explain in a muted footer that a notification lists devices, not people who read it — there is no read receipt.

## Constraints
- The service client (`createServiceSupabase()`) appears ONLY in `src/lib/push/*`, `src/lib/cron/*`, `app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`, `src/features/announcements/push-actions.ts` (3.6a), `src/features/announcements/schedule-actions.ts` and `src/features/notifications/notification-actions.ts` (this step) — extend 3.6b's `git grep` whitelist in `docs/RLS.md` accordingly. Every service read/write is preceded by the user-client permission check and followed by an explicit `org_id` comparison; `srv*`/service helpers require the `ServiceDbClient` brand — never cast.
- The user-client update of `announcements.publish_at` happens BEFORE the service-side outbox move, never the other way round (if the user update fails, nothing moves). Never move `claimed`/`sent`/`failed`/`cancelled` rows; never set `scheduled_for` in the past through Reschedule (Publish now uses `now()`).
- No migrations (`9999_init.sql` may be frozen); no changes to `srv_claim_notifications`, the dispatcher's claiming logic, `refs.ts`, the cron phases, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, `apps/web/vercel.json`, or the mobile app. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components, pages or actions — helpers go in `@church/db` additively with tests. No `persons`/`households` reads — recipient names come from `profiles` only.
- Do not build the audit pages (6.2a), account deletion (6.3) or anything mobile. Keep 3.5a/3.5b/5.3a/6.1b tables intact except the one-line `detailHref` pass-through and the notice text.
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, Playwright 1.62. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` (`popover`, `alert-dialog` if absent).
- No model names, no secrets; `<slug>@example.test` addresses only in tests.

Second half of skeleton step 6.2 (see 6.2a notes for the split). The real fix in this step: 3.5a/3.6a left a queued push at the OLD `scheduled_for` when `publish_at` was moved earlier (`srv_claim_notifications` claims by `scheduled_for <= now()`; the dispatcher only reschedules rows it has already claimed), so Reschedule/Publish now and the edit form now move the outbox row through `rescheduleQueuedNotification` — a service-client write, because `notifications` has no write policies for `authenticated`; it is confined to `schedule-actions.ts` and runs only after the user-client update succeeded. Names chosen because the docs do not name a delivery status page: routes `/o/[orgSlug]/notifications` and `/notifications/[notificationId]`, feature dir `src/features/notifications/`, helpers `listNotifications`, `countNotificationsByStatus`, `rescheduleQueuedNotification`, `listDeliveriesForNotification`, `getNotificationForOrg`, Server Actions `rescheduleAnnouncementAction`, `publishAnnouncementNowAction`, `listDeliveriesAction`. The detail page exposes which members' devices got a ticket (display names and platforms, never emails or tokens) to `announcements.*` holders — `notification_deliveries` is super-only in RLS, so this is a deliberate, org-checked widening recorded for the founder to veto. Web content links come from a repo-checked map, not `notificationTargetPath` (mobile paths). Depends on 6.2a for the shared cursor codec and links-test pattern and on 3.6b for the cron/receipts semantics the docs describe.

Mobile screens and the Play Data Safety worksheet follow in 6.3c.

2. **Account state hook** — `src/features/account/useAccountState.ts`: TanStack Query over `getMyAccountState(supabase)` keyed `queryKeys.account.state()`, `staleTime: 0`, `meta: { persist: false }`, and add the `queryKeys.account` prefix to `shouldPersistQuery`'s deny list (additive, with a test) so another person's archive state never survives in the cache. `useDeactivateAccount()`, `useRequestAccountDeletion()`, `useRestoreMyAccount()` mutations built on injected deps `{ rpc, signOut, navigate }` exactly like `registerForPush`'s tests: success order rpc → signOut → navigate for the two destructive ones, rpc → invalidate → navigate for restore; rpc failure → no sign-out, error surfaced (`account_archived_by_admin` → the `@church/domain` message; network failure → inline error, nothing signed out; `organization_suspended` cannot occur — the RPCs have no org).
3. **Screens at the ROOT of `apps/mobile/app`** (outside `(app)`, because a signed-in person with no active church — and an archived one — must reach them; Play requires deletion for every user): `app/account/deactivate.tsx` → `src/features/account/DeactivateAccountScreen.tsx` (explanation from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.deactivate` + `DELETION_POLICY_COPY` deactivate sentence, checkbox "I understand I will be signed out and hidden from my church until my account is restored", button "Deactivate my account" → `Alert.alert` confirm → mutation → `signOutEverywhere()` (runs 4.3's `registerBeforeSignOut` hook, so the `push_devices` row is deleted immediately — say so in the copy: "Notifications stop right away") → `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')` with a one-time inline message "Your account is deactivated — sign in again and choose Restore my account, or ask your church office"); `app/account/delete.tsx` → `DeleteAccountScreen.tsx` (explanation from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.delete`, the policy sentence, `whatTheChurchKeeps`, the exact date `now + graceDays` formatted in the device locale, `TextInput` for `DELETE` with `autoCapitalize="characters"`, the checkbox "I understand my church keeps its directory entry", a destructive "Delete my account" button → `Alert.alert` → mutation → sign out → sign-in with the message "Deletion request received. Your account will be deleted on <date> unless you sign in before then and choose Keep my account"); when `useAccountState` already shows a pending deletion, the screen instead shows "A deletion request is pending — your account will be deleted on <date>" with a **Keep my account** button (restore mutation); `app/account/restore.tsx` → `RestoreAccountScreen.tsx`: by `archiveReason` — `'user'` → "Restore my account" (restore → invalidate context → `router.replace('/(app)')`), `'deletion_request'` → "Keep my account" with the scheduled date and the note that restoring cancels the deletion, `'admin'` → the admin message and a "Sign out" button only. Every screen guards itself: no session → `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')`. Register the three in `app/_layout.tsx` with titles "Deactivate account", "Delete account", "Your account".
4. **Routing for archived users** — in the sign-in success path (4.1b) and in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx`'s membership check, read `useAccountState` before the no-church redirect: `archivedAt` set → `router.replace('/account/restore')` (an archived user has no active org, so without this they would land on no-church with no way back). Keep the check cheap (one query, no persist) and unit-test the decision as a pure function `routeForAccountState({ archivedAt, archiveReason, hasActiveOrg })` → `'restore' | 'no-church' | 'app'`.
5. **Entry points** — `MoreMenu.tsx`: a "Your account" section under the existing privacy/terms links with two rows — "Deactivate account" (secondary style, subtitle from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.deactivate` after the dash) and "Delete account" (destructive style, subtitle from `ACCOUNT_ACTION_COPY.delete` after the dash) — replacing 4.3's `TODO(6.x)` comment; `app/(auth)/no-church.tsx`: a small "Delete my account" text link below its explanation; all three `router.push('/account/…')`. Do not restyle More or no-church; add rows/links only.
6. **`docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`** — the Play Console "Data safety" worksheet, filled in from the schema: a table per Play category (Personal info: name, email, phone, address, other — birthdate, marital status, photos; Photos; Messages — none; App activity — survey responses; in-app search history/other content none; App info and performance — crash logs "none until step 6.3b enables error reporting; then diagnostics, optional"; Device or other IDs — Expo push token/device id) with columns Collected? / Shared? / Optional or required / Purpose(s) / Ephemeral? / Encrypted in transit (yes) / Deletion request mechanism (yes — URL). Then the form's direct questions with the answers: "Does your app collect or share any of the required user data types?" yes; "Is all of the user data collected by your app encrypted in transit?" yes; "Do you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted?" yes — account deletion URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` (redirects a signed-out visitor to sign-in — expected) and in-app path More → Delete account; the "Account deletion" App content page answer must describe **both** paths and the window in decision 15's words: deactivation (temporary, reversible — Google says this alone does NOT satisfy the requirement, which is why Delete exists) and deletion (account archived immediately, all account data permanently deleted 30 days after the request unless cancelled; directory entries the church created are the church's records — "some data is retained: church directory entries, survey answers without the account attached"); "Data deletion: are there any other data deletion methods?" contact the church office / `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` for directory entries; privacy policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; "Independent security review" no; target audience adults (no child accounts); "Families policy" not enrolled; the app contains no ads and no analytics SDK (4.4). Add "How this was derived" (pointing at the tables, `9999_init.sql` and decision 15) and "Re-check when" (Sentry enabled in 6.3b; a new table with personal data; the grace period changes). Link it from `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` and the README docs index.
7. **Docs** — `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`: a "Device checklist: account" section (throwaway member → More → Deactivate → signed out, `push_devices` row gone → sign in → Restore screen → Restore → home; More → Delete → `DELETE` → signed out → SQL Editor shows the request row ~30 days out → sign in → Keep my account → row gone; no-church screen shows the Delete link) — the founder runs it on a 4.5 preview build against the hosted project. `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md`: a one-line cross-reference. `docs/CHECKLIST_SECURITY.md`: the "account deactivation, restore and 30-day deletion work" row gains "mobile: MOBILE_BUILD.md device checklist". README route list: the three mobile account routes.

## Constraints
- User session only — never a service key in the app; deletion is executed only by the web cron. Mobile native modules unchanged (no `expo install` needed); Expo 57 / RN 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 exact; no new dependencies; versions of native packages only via `npx expo install` if ever needed.
- Strings must match the web module byte for byte (the test in Build 1 enforces it); do not paraphrase decision 15's two sentences. No real email, entity, price or address — placeholders only (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, `<DOMAIN>`). No analytics or tracking SDK (the worksheet says "none").
- Do not restyle More, no-church or sign-in; add rows, links and the archived-user redirect only. No web code changes except the README/docs lines named above. No model identifiers, no secrets.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (new tests: `deletion-copy.test.ts` source comparison, the three mutation hooks with injected deps, `routeForAccountState`, the `shouldPersistQuery` deny-list addition).
- `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo-doctor` and, from `apps/mobile`, `npx expo export --platform android` → clean; `grep -rn "Delete account\|Deactivate account" apps/mobile/src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx apps/mobile/app/(auth)/no-church.tsx` → More hits both rows, no-church hits Delete; `ls apps/mobile/app/account` → `deactivate.tsx delete.tsx restore.tsx`.
- `grep -n "<DOMAIN>/account/delete\|<DOMAIN>/privacy\|30 days" docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` → all three hit; `grep -c "analytics" docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` → ≥ 1 (stating none).
- Device checklist against the hosted project with a 4.5 preview/dev-client build (the local harness has no Auth/PostgREST, so the app cannot sign in locally): run the `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` "Device checklist: account" section from Build 7. If you cannot run it, write it into `session_log.md` for the founder.

- `HANDOFF.md`: State — tick "Account deactivation/deletion mobile + Play Data Safety (6.3c)"; feature table — row "Account deactivation + deletion (Play requirement)" Mobile done; Decisions — mobile routes `app/account/{deactivate,delete,restore}.tsx`, `routeForAccountState`; founder to-dos — run the device checklist on the next preview build, keep `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` for step 6.5, re-check it when 6.3b enables error reporting; "Deviations from plan" for anything that differed from decision 15 or 6.3a's names.

## 6.4 — iOS / TestFlight (founder, 2–3 hours of clicking plus Apple's enrolment and processing waits; an iPhone is required, a Mac is NOT)

Run the agent prompt's first pass first, `git pull`, then follow this list; the long form is `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` → "iOS (step 6.4)". Never put a `.p8` key, certificate, provisioning profile, Apple password or app-specific password into git, a prompt or chat — EAS stores them; copies go to the vault from 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. HANDOFF "Applied migrations" lists every file under `supabase/migrations/` as pasted (9999, and 9998/9997 if they exist — otherwise the production build talks to a database without the join-code or survey RPCs). 6.6 is done (`https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` live, no banner); 4.5 is done (EAS project `anacast`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID` in `apps/mobile/.env`); the EAS **production** environment variables exist (created in 6.5 item 13 — if 6.5 has not run, create them now exactly as 4.5 step B but for the environment `production`: `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<DOMAIN>`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID`; the `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` file variable is Android-only and harmless here). The reviewer/demo account from 6.5 item 3 exists (create it if not: demo church in `/admin`, `/o/<demo-slug>/users` → Create account → temporary password to the vault).
2. `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public | grep -E 'bundleIdentifier|package'` → both print `com.anacast.app` (orchestrator decision 18); write it down. It is immutable once App Store Connect has the app.

**A. Apple Developer Program (start early — approval takes 1–2 days for individuals, longer for organisations)**
3. developer.apple.com → Account → sign in with an Apple ID using `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and two-factor authentication → Join the Apple Developer Program → Enrol → choose Individual (your own name is the seller name shown in the App Store) or Organization (needs a D-U-N-S number and a legal entity — the one recorded in HANDOFF "Legal entity" by 6.6) → pay 99 USD per year → wait for the "Welcome" email. Then developer.apple.com → Account → Membership details → copy the **Team ID** (10 characters, not secret) into HANDOFF.md → "iOS / TestFlight" and into Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables as `APPLE_TEAM_ID` (Production) → Redeploy (this turns on the Universal Links file).

**B. Credentials and first build (EAS does the certificate work)**
4. `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` → "Do you want to log in to your Apple account?" **Yes** → Apple ID + password + the 2FA code (EAS uses the session once; nothing is stored in the repo) → let EAS **register the bundle identifier**, **generate a new Apple Distribution Certificate**, **create the provisioning profile**, and answer **Yes** to setting up **Push Notifications** (EAS creates the APNs key `AuthKey_….p8` in your developer account and keeps it) → the build queues (15–40 minutes on the free tier). If the Apple login fails, run `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios` → production → set up each item there, then rebuild.
5. When the build finishes, note the build id and the iOS build number from the build page in HANDOFF.

**C. App Store Connect record**
6. appstoreconnect.apple.com → My Apps → **+** → New App → Platforms iOS → Name `Anacast` → Primary language → Bundle ID: pick the one EAS registered → SKU `anacast` → User access Full → Create. Note the Apple ID number of the app ("App Information → General → Apple ID") in HANDOFF as the ASC app id.
7. App Information → Privacy Policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`; Category Primary "Lifestyle" (secondary optional); Content Rights → does not contain third-party content. Save.
8. App Privacy → Get started → answer from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (collects data: Yes; Contact Info, Identifiers, User Content; each "linked to identity: Yes", "used for tracking: No", purpose "App Functionality"; Diagnostics only if error reporting is on) → Publish.
9. Age Rating → questionnaire with the answers from `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` (all "None"; result 4+) → Done.
9b. App Store → 1.0 Prepare for Submission → upload the screenshot sets listed in `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` → "Assets" (6.7" and 6.5" iPhone, at least 3 each, taken from the TestFlight build in step 14 — the app's real palette, no mock-ups); the 1024×1024 icon is taken from the build automatically. Not needed for internal TestFlight testers, but required before external testers or review.
10. TestFlight tab → Test Information → Beta App Description (one paragraph), Feedback email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`, Privacy Policy URL again; Sign-in required → **Yes** → the reviewer account email + password from item 1; Review notes: "Church members are invited by their church; use the password, ignore the one-time code option. Account deletion: More → Delete account (30-day grace) or https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete". (Needed only when you later add external testers, but fill it now.)

**D. Upload to TestFlight**
11. `npx eas-cli submit -p ios --profile production --latest` → log in with the Apple ID again, or — recommended for repeat use — first create an App Store Connect API key: App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys → **+** → name `eas-submit`, access **App Manager** → Download the `.p8` ONCE → `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios` → production → **App Store Connect API Key** → Upload → provide the `.p8`, Key ID and Issuer ID → then move the `.p8` to the vault and delete the download. Submit again with `--latest`.
12. App Store Connect → TestFlight → iOS builds: the build shows "Processing" (10–30 minutes), then "Ready to Test" (no "Missing Compliance" prompt thanks to the agent's `usesNonExemptEncryption: false`; if it appears anyway, answer "None of the algorithms mentioned above" / "No").
13. TestFlight → Internal Testing → **+** → group "Church leaders" → add testers: Users and Access → **+** → invite yourself and up to 100 App Store Connect users with the role Developer or Marketing (internal testers must be ASC users; no Beta App Review is needed). Enable automatic distribution → the build appears in the group.

**E. Device checklist (iPhone with the TestFlight app from the App Store)**
14. Open the TestFlight email/invite → Accept → Install Anacast → open it → sign in with a 6-digit code (or password) as an active member of the first church (4.5 item 2 — Invite + accept on the web, not Create account, if you use your super-admin email).
15. Accept the push explainer → iOS permission prompt "Anacast Would Like to Send You Notifications" → Allow → in Supabase SQL Editor `select platform, device_name from public.push_devices;` shows an `ios` row.
16. On the web publish an announcement with push on → the notification arrives on the locked iPhone → tapping opens the announcement; upload a bulletin → its push arrives; turn the Bulletins preference off in the app → the next bulletin push is suppressed.
17. Play an uploaded mp3 sermon → lock the phone → audio continues → the lock screen shows play/pause (and title/speaker if the agent could set them); play a YouTube-linked sermon → inline, stops when backgrounded (expected); a Drive-linked sermon → opens the in-app Safari view.
18. Open a bulletin PDF → renders in the in-app Safari view with the share icon → "Share" → Save to Files works; an image bulletin renders inline.
19. More tab: Privacy Policy / Terms open in Safari view; Deactivate account and Delete account rows exist and show their explanations (do not confirm them on your real account); Sign out → the `push_devices` row is gone; reopen → sign in again keeps working. If the directory (5.2b) exists: pick a household photo → the photo-library permission prompt shows the Anacast purpose sentence.
19b. If surveys (6.1c) exist: open a survey push → answer a `date` and a `multi_choice` question → "Answer saved"; as head of house answer for a child without an account.
19c. If events (5.3b) exist: submit an event → it shows as pending.
19d. Tap an invite link `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` from Mail → opens in Anacast (Universal Links; falls back to Safari when `APPLE_TEAM_ID` is unset — note which happened).
19e. With a throwaway account: More → Deactivate account → signed out → sign in again → "Restore my account" → the account and its church are back.
20. Note keyboard/safe-area problems (field hidden by the keyboard, content under the notch, tab bar under the home indicator).

**F. Hand back**
21. Paste into the agent prompt's second pass: pass/fail per item 14–20, iPhone model + iOS version, build number, any `eas build` error excerpt, any email from Apple (ITMS codes). Record in HANDOFF → "iOS / TestFlight": Team ID, bundle id, ASC app id, build number, EAS build id, TestFlight date, tester count, results.

## Goal
Two agent passes around the founder's checklist. First pass (Build 1–8): make the project build and behave correctly on iOS without a Mac — configuration, iOS branches that Phase 1 left "untested until Phase 3", the App Store privacy worksheet and docs — so the founder's `npx eas-cli build -p ios --profile production` succeeds on the first try. Second pass (Build 9): triage the TestFlight device results and Apple's emails the founder pastes, fix iOS-only bugs (PDF viewer, background audio and lock-screen controls, push permission flow, safe areas, keyboard) and fill the HANDOFF TestFlight ledger. Nothing in this step changes Android behaviour.

## Inputs / prior state

## Build
1. **`app.config.ts` iOS block.** Keep `ios.bundleIdentifier` = `android.package` = `com.anacast.app` (orchestrator decision 18, confirmed lowercase; immutable once App Store Connect has the record). Add `ios.config: { usesNonExemptEncryption: false }` (the app uses only HTTPS/TLS → exempt; this answers App Store Connect's export-compliance question in every build and skips the "Missing Compliance" prompt in TestFlight). Do not write `UIBackgroundModes` into `ios.infoPlist` by hand — the `expo-audio` plugin owns it (Build 5 proves it). Store assets from the brand palette (orchestrator decision 17 — the token file `apps/mobile/src/theme.ts` is the single source: `ink` Prussian Blue `#00072d`, `primaryDark` Deep Navy `#001c55`, `primary` Imperial Blue `#0a2472`, `accent` Bright Marine `#0e6ba8`, `tint` Icy Blue `#a6e1fa`): Apple requires an opaque 1024×1024 PNG without alpha, so generate `assets/icon-ios.png` by flattening `assets/icon.png` (6.5's palette icon if it ran, else the current icon) onto `theme.colors.ink` with a small Node script that uses only dependencies already installed in the workspace (`sharp` if present, else `pngjs`; if neither exists, write an SVG at `assets/icon-ios.svg` from the palette and put the exact export instructions for the founder into `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`), set `ios.icon` to it, and confirm `splash.backgroundColor` and `android.adaptiveIcon.backgroundColor` read the token values (`ink` and `primary`). List under a new "Assets" section of `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` the screenshot sets App Store Connect requires (6.7" and 6.5" iPhone, at least 3 each) and which screens to capture (Home, Sermon playing, Announcement, Bulletin, Directory, Survey — whichever exist), all in the app's real theme. Ensure `ios.buildNumber` is absent (remote versioning bumps it). If `expo-image-picker` is installed (5.2b), give its plugin entry purpose strings: `['expo-image-picker', { photosPermission: 'Anacast uses your photo library so you can choose a household or profile photo for your church directory.', cameraPermission: 'Anacast uses the camera so you can take a directory photo.' }]` — Apple rejects generic or missing `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` / `NSCameraUsageDescription`. `expo-notifications` needs no purpose string on iOS.
2. **`eas.json`.** `build.production.ios` needs nothing beyond the defaults (store distribution, `autoIncrement` with remote versioning); add `build.preview.ios: { simulator: false, distribution: 'internal' }` ONLY as documentation of the ad-hoc alternative in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` — the founder uses TestFlight, which needs no device UDIDs. Leave `submit.production.ios` as an empty object (no `ascAppId`, no `appleId`) and document that `eas submit -p ios` resolves the app from the bundle id after the founder logs in or uploads an App Store Connect API key through `npx eas-cli credentials -p ios`; never commit `appleId`, `ascAppId` or a key path. HANDOFF: an "iOS / TestFlight" block (Team ID — not secret, bundle id, ASC app id, ledger: build number, EAS build id, TestFlight date, tester count, device/iOS version results) and the founder to-dos in checklist order. 9. **Second pass — TestFlight results (run when the founder pastes them).** Triage like 4.5's helper: build failures (`npx eas-cli build:view <id>` excerpt) → credentials (founder: `eas credentials -p ios`), CocoaPods/native errors (usually a version mismatch → `npx expo install --fix`, never a manual pin), or config; device failures → the layer that owns them (push permission prompt never shown → capability/handler; no lock-screen controls → Build 5's deviation; PDF opens blank → signed URL expired, re-mint (4.2a's `remint()`), or the `pageSheet` presentation; keyboard hides the OTP field → `KeyboardAvoidingView` with `behavior: 'padding'` on iOS in the auth screens; content under the notch/home indicator → `SafeAreaView` edges from `react-native-safe-area-context` (already a dependency of expo-router) in the affected screen; tab bar overlapped → expo-router `Tabs` `tabBarStyle` safe-area inset). ## Constraints
- No Mac is assumed anywhere: builds run on EAS, `expo prebuild --no-install` is used only to inspect the generated `Info.plist` and its output is deleted, never committed. Do not add native modules; native versions only via `npx expo install`; no `react-native-pdf`, `react-native-track-player`, `expo-av`.
- Never commit or paste an APNs key (`.p8`), App Store Connect API key, distribution certificate, provisioning profile, Apple ID password or app-specific password; EAS holds them. `prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim.
- Do not change `android.package`, the Android PDF path, the push dispatcher on the web, migrations (never `supabase db push`), or Phase 1/2 screens beyond the iOS-specific fixes named above. Keep every change guarded by `Platform.OS === 'ios'` where it would otherwise alter Android.
- `ios.bundleIdentifier` becomes immutable once App Store Connect has the record — read HANDOFF first; if the founder already created the ASC app with a different id, use that one and record the deviation.
- Do not build a "Sign in with Apple" flow; do not add In-App Purchase (churches pay on the web through Stripe — Apple's guideline 3.1.3(b) treats a multi-tenant organisational subscription bought outside the app by the organisation as acceptable; the app must not link to the Stripe checkout — confirm no mobile screen links to `/settings/billing` or `/api/billing/*`, and record the guideline reference in `docs/APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md` "Review notes").

- Prebuild proof: the grep commands from Build 5 print `audio`, the purpose strings and `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` false; afterwards `git status` shows no `ios/` or `android/` directory.
- `git ls-files | grep -Ei '\.p8$|\.mobileprovision$|\.p12$'` → no output; `pnpm --filter web build` → green; `curl -s http://localhost:3000/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` → 404 without `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, JSON with it (local dev server).

**Founder checklist**

## 6.5 — Google Play Console: internal testing (founder, 2–4 hours of clicking spread over several days of Google verification; agent first pass before, agent second pass after)

Run the agent prompt's first pass (Build 1–6) first, `git pull`, then follow this list. Follow `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` → "Google Play (step 6.5)" for the long form. Never put a key file, `google-services.json` or the Play service-account JSON into git, a prompt or chat; they go to the vault from 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. HANDOFF "Applied migrations" lists every file under `supabase/migrations/` as pasted (9999, and 9998/9997 if they exist — otherwise the production build talks to a database without the join-code or survey RPCs). 6.6 is done: `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` shows the approved policy without a banner and `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` redirects a signed-out visitor to sign-in (Google's reviewer opens both). 4.5 is done: the `preview` APK runs on your phone and pushes arrive. `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` is open next to you.
2. Print the package id — `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public | grep '"package"'` — and write it on paper; it is immutable from the first upload.
3. Create a demo church in `/admin` holding only fictional data, and in it a reviewer account via `/o/<demo-slug>/users` → Create account (temporary password shown once — put it in the vault). Sign in with it once in the Android app to confirm the password path works.

**A. Developer account (start early — identity verification takes 1–7 days)**
4. play.google.com/console → Create developer account → choose Personal or Organization (an organization account needs a D-U-N-S number; a personal account created after November 2023 must run a closed test with 20 testers for 14 days before it may publish to production — internal testing, which is all this step needs, is not gated). Pay the one-time 25 USD, complete identity verification, turn on 2-step verification on the Google account. Record the developer account name and date in HANDOFF.md → "Google Play".

**B. Create the app**
5. All apps → Create app → App name `Anacast` → Default language → App: "App" → Free (irreversible; keep Free) → accept the declarations → Create app. Note the Play app id from the URL (`…/app/<id>/…`) in HANDOFF.

**C. App content (Dashboard → "Set up your app" → each task, in this order)**
6. Privacy policy → `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy` → Save.
7. App access → "All or some functionality is restricted" → Add instructions → name "Reviewer account", the demo email + temporary password from item 3, note "Sign in with email and password; ignore the one-time code option" → Save.
8. Ads → "No, my app does not contain ads" → Save.
9. Content rating → Start questionnaire → email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → category "All other app types" → answer No to every violence/sexual/drugs/gambling item; "Does the app allow users to interact or exchange content" → Yes (announcements, surveys, directory within a closed church group); "Does the app share user-provided personal information" → Yes, with other users within the church (as the questionnaire words it) → Save → Submit. Expected rating: Everyone / PEGI 3 or Teen — either is fine.
10. Target audience and content → age groups "18 and over" only (children have no accounts) → "Could your app unintentionally appeal to children" → No → Save.
11. News apps → No. COVID-19 contact tracing and status apps → No. Government apps → No. Financial features → "My app doesn't provide any financial features" (churches pay on the web through Stripe; the app never takes payments). Health → none.
12. Data safety → Start → copy each answer from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` (collection & security: yes collects, encrypted in transit, provides a way to request deletion → the URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete`; data types per the worksheet table; purposes "App functionality" and "Account management"; no sharing with third parties except service providers; no ads/analytics). The **Account deletion** question: choose "Provides a way for users to request that their account is deleted" → URL `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` → in the free-text, state the 30-day window and that deactivation is separate. Save → review summary → Submit.

**D. Production build and first upload (by hand)**
13. expo.dev → project → Environment variables → environment **production** → create the same variables as 4.5 step B (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<DOMAIN>`, `EAS_PROJECT_ID`, and the secret **File** variable `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` from the same `google-services.json`).
14. `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` → reuse the keystore EAS created in 4.5 → wait → Download the `.aab` from the build page. Record the EAS build id and version code (shown on the build page) in HANDOFF.
15. Play Console → Testing → Internal testing → Create new release → if asked, "Use Google-generated key" for Play App Signing (Google keeps the signing key; your EAS keystore becomes the upload key) → upload the `.aab` → Release name (prefilled) → Release notes "First internal build" → Next → fix any listed error (agent second pass if it is not a form) → Save → Go to Testers.
16. Testers → Create email list "Church testers" → add your email and a few members' Google-account emails (≤ 100) → Save → copy the **opt-in link** → Save release → Review release → Start rollout to Internal testing. Internal testing needs no Google review.
17. On your phone (signed into a Google account on the tester list): open the opt-in link → Become a tester → Download it on Google Play → install → sign in → run the 4.5 Checkpoint C device list once more (OTP sign-in, a push from a web announcement, background audio, bulletin PDF, Deactivate and Delete rows present on More). Then the production-only checks: if 5.7 built App Links — Play Console → Setup → App integrity → copy the **App signing key certificate** SHA-256 and paste it into the agent's second-pass prompt (Play re-signs the bundle, so the preview keystore's fingerprint in `assetlinks.json` no longer matches); after the agent redeploys, tap `https://<DOMAIN>/invite/<token>` from Gmail → opens in Anacast. If surveys (6.1c) exist: answer one from a push. If the directory (5.2b) exists: pick a household photo → the permission prompt appears. Uninstall the sideloaded preview APK first if the install fails with "package conflicts".

**E. Later uploads by command (optional but recommended)**
18. Google Cloud console (the project Play created, or Firebase's) → IAM & Admin → Service accounts → Create → name `eas-submit` → Keys → Add key → JSON → download. Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite new users → the service account's email → App permissions → Anacast → "Release to testing tracks", "Manage testing tracks" → Invite. Then `cd apps/mobile && npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → select the production profile → Google Service Account → the **Play Store submissions** entry (not the FCM push key) → upload the JSON. Move the JSON to the vault and delete the download. From now on: `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production` then `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest`.

**F. Pre-launch report and hand-back**
19. Play Console → Testing → Pre-launch report (appears ~30 minutes after the upload) → copy the summary (crashes, accessibility, security, performance) and any policy email you receive, plus your device results from item 17, and paste them into the agent prompt's second pass. Record in HANDOFF → "Google Play": app id, package id, track "internal", version name/code, build id, upload date, opt-in link, number of testers.

**Done when**: the developer account is verified; the Anacast app exists with the package id from `app.config.ts`; App content is complete (green ticks) including Data safety with the deletion URL; a production `.aab` is on the Internal testing track and installed from the opt-in link on at least one phone; the pre-launch report has no crash or the agent fixed it; HANDOFF has the Play block filled in.

## Build
1. **`apps/mobile/eas.json`.** Confirm `cli.appVersionSource` is `"remote"` (4.1a set it; keep 4.1a's `cli.version` — EAS stores the Android `versionCode` and `autoIncrement` on the production profile bumps it per build) and remove any `android.versionCode` from `app.config.ts` so the two never fight. Fill `submit.production.android` with `{ "track": "internal", "releaseStatus": "completed", "changesNotSentForReview": false }`. For the key, prefer the credential store: document that the founder uploads the Play service-account JSON with `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → "Google Service Account" → the entry for **Play Store submissions** (a different key from the FCM v1 push key uploaded in 4.5); `eas submit` then finds it without a local path. Keep `serviceAccountKeyPath` OUT of the committed file; document the fallback `"serviceAccountKeyPath": "./play-service-account.json"` for a one-off local run only. Add `play-service-account.json` and `*service-account*.json` to `apps/mobile/.gitignore` and the root `.gitignore`. Also add `submit.production.ios: {}` as a placeholder for 6.4 with a comment-free note in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (JSON has no comments).
2. **`app.config.ts` release hygiene.** Ensure `version` is `1.0.0` (or the value HANDOFF records), `android.versionCode` is absent (remote), `android.permissions` stays the explicit minimal list (`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is added by `expo-notifications`; `RECORD_AUDIO` must not appear — 4.1a's `expo-audio` plugin has `recordAudioAndroid: false`; check `npx expo config --type introspect | grep -i permission`), `android.allowBackup: false` (no app data in Google backups — the session is in SecureStore), and `android.adaptiveIcon` plus `icon` point at real files under `apps/mobile/assets/` generated from the brand palette (orchestrator decision 17; the token file `apps/mobile/src/theme.ts` is the single source): `assets/icon.png` 1024×1024 and `assets/adaptive-icon.png` (foreground = a neutral "A" monogram in Icy Blue `#a6e1fa` on an Imperial Blue `#0a2472` background, `android.adaptiveIcon.backgroundColor` = `theme.colors.primary`), `splash.backgroundColor` = `theme.colors.ink` (Prussian Blue `#00072d`) — regenerate the PNGs from the token values with a small Node script that uses only dependencies already installed in the workspace (`sharp` if present, else `pngjs`; if neither exists, commit an SVG source and exact export instructions for the founder in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md`), commit them, and record in HANDOFF that the glyph is a placeholder monogram the founder may replace with a designed logo using the same palette.
3. **`docs/PLAY_STORE_LISTING.md`.** Write the listing the founder pastes into Play Console → Main store listing: app name `Anacast`; short description (≤ 80 characters) and full description (≤ 4000 characters) describing sermons, announcements with notifications, bulletins, directory, calendar and surveys for a congregation, stating that an invitation or join code from the church is required (no public sign-up — 4.1b/5.6); category "Lifestyle" (alternative "Communication" — founder decides); tags; contact email `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and website `https://<DOMAIN>`; privacy-policy URL `https://<DOMAIN>/privacy`. Asset specification with exact sizes: app icon 512×512 PNG (32-bit, no alpha per Play rules — derive it from `assets/icon.png`, flattened; generate it with the same Node script as Build 2 and commit it under `apps/mobile/store/`), feature graphic 1024×500 PNG (generate it too: an Imperial Blue `#0a2472` field with the Anacast wordmark in white — contrast 13.9:1 — from the palette in `theme.ts`), phone screenshots 2–8 at 16:9 or 9:16 with min 320 px and max 3840 px on the long side taken from the real app theme (list which screens to capture: Home, Sermon playing, Announcement, Bulletin, Directory, Survey — whichever exist), optional 7-inch and 10-inch tablet screenshots (skip; `supportsTablet` is false on iOS and the Android app is phone-first — say so). Add a "Test account for reviewers" block: how to create it on the web (`/o/<slug>/users` → Create account → temporary password shown once; put the person in a demo church that holds only fictional data) and what to write in App access ("Sign in with the email and password below; a one-time code is also offered but the reviewer should use the password").
4. **`docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` → "Google Play (step 6.5)".** A numbered section that follows the founder checklist exactly: developer account (25 USD one-time, identity verification, and the note that personal accounts created after November 2023 must run a closed test with 20 testers for 14 days before they can apply for production access — internal testing is not gated, which is why this step stops there); creating the app with the exact package id; the App content pages in order (Privacy policy, App access, Ads, Content rating questionnaire, Target audience, News apps, COVID-19 contact tracing, Data safety, Government apps, Financial features, Health, Account deletion) with the answers taken from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` and this step; EAS `production` environment variables (same five as `preview`, incl. the `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` file variable — the founder re-creates them for the `production` environment); `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile production`; the first upload done by hand in the Console (Google requires the first bundle to come through the UI before the API can be used); the Play App Signing enrolment on that first upload (the EAS keystore becomes the upload key; Google holds the app signing key); service account for later `eas submit` runs (Google Cloud service account, JSON key, invited in Play Console → Users and permissions with "Release to testing tracks" on the app); `npx eas-cli submit -p android --profile production --latest`; internal testers (email list ≤ 100, opt-in link); the pre-launch report location; the HANDOFF ledger row; a "Production-only checks" sub-list (App Links fingerprint after Play App Signing, survey push, directory photo permission) mirroring founder item 17. Add a troubleshooting list: "Version code already used" → remote versioning not enabled or a build was uploaded by hand — bump via `npx eas-cli build:version:set -p android`; "The Android App Bundle was signed with the wrong key" → the app was created with a different upload key; "Data safety form incomplete" blocks even internal releases after the deadline; "App access: credentials invalid" → the test account was archived/deleted or the church suspended.
5. **CI.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` add, next to the existing `expo export --platform android`, a step `pnpm --filter mobile exec expo config --type public` with `EAS_PROJECT_ID` mocked and a `node -e` check that the printed JSON has `android.package` equal to the expected id and no `android.versionCode`; and `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('apps/mobile/eas.json','utf8'))"` plus an assertion that `submit.production.android.track === 'internal'` and no key contains `serviceAccountKeyPath`. Keep CI non-blocking and EAS-free.
6. **HANDOFF and hand-over.** Add a "Google Play" block under "Mobile (Phase 1)": package id (immutable from the first upload on), Play app id (to fill), track, versions ledger (version name, version code, EAS build id, date), the tester opt-in link (to fill), and the founder to-dos in the checklist order. Commit and push (Finish below), then tell the founder to run the checklist.
7. **Second pass — pre-launch report and device check (run when the founder pastes results).** Triage each finding: crashes or ANRs → reproduce from the stack trace (the report shows the JS stack when source maps are uploaded; otherwise ask for the `adb logcat` excerpt) and fix in the app; accessibility warnings (touch targets < 48 dp, missing content descriptions) → fix in the affected component with `accessibilityLabel`/`hitSlop`; security warnings (cleartext traffic — must already be off via `expo-build-properties` `usesCleartextTraffic: false`; outdated dependency — only through `npx expo install --fix`); performance flags on the 50 MB sermon download → note as known (Free-plan cap, 4.2b's signed-URL streaming). App Links (if 5.7 built them): Play App Signing re-signs the bundle with Google's app signing key, so the `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` fingerprint from the preview keystore no longer matches — add the **App signing key certificate** SHA-256 the founder copies from Play Console → Setup → App integrity next to the upload-key fingerprint in the assetlinks route (both fingerprints stay listed) and redeploy; then the founder re-tests the invite link. Policy rejections: "Account deletion" → check `https://<DOMAIN>/account/delete` is reachable signed-out (redirects to `/login?next=`) and the in-app path exists on More; "Login credentials not working" → the demo account; "Privacy policy" → the URL must be live and reachable without sign-in. Record every fix under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and the Play ledger row for the build that carries it.

## Constraints
- Mobile native versions only via `npx expo install`; do not add packages for this step. No EAS build or submit in CI; EAS builds/submits are the founder's commands on their machine with their credentials.
- Never commit `google-services.json`, the FCM key, the Play service-account JSON or a keystore; never paste any of them into a prompt (`prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim). The `.gitignore` entries from Build 1 are mandatory.
- Never change `android.package` — it is `com.anacast.app` (orchestrator decision 18) everywhere (Firebase app, Play app, `app.config.ts`) and cannot change once an `.aab` has been uploaded.
- Do not touch the web app except the docs; do not touch migrations (never `supabase db push`); do not change the `preview` profile the founder already uses; no Supabase plan wording other than Free (decision 10).
- The Data safety answers come from `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md`; if you find the worksheet wrong while writing the Play section, fix the worksheet (the schema is the source of truth) and say so in the final message — the founder must re-check the form.

- `cd apps/mobile && EAS_PROJECT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 npx expo config --type public | grep -E '"package"|"versionCode"|"version"'` → shows the package id and `version`, no `versionCode`.
- `git check-ignore -q apps/mobile/play-service-account.json && echo ignored` → `ignored`; `git ls-files | grep -i "service-account\|google-services.json"` → no output.

Two agent passes: config/docs before the founder's clicking, findings after — the prompt says when to tick the step.
